112.x: India rose from 5th to 3rd in nanoscience publications.

113.s: Out of the following, ____ is used for linear measurements
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
113.x: An invar tape (nickel-steel alloy that hardly expands with heat) gives the most accurate linear measurements in surveying, for example base lines. Chains and cloth tapes are less precise.

113.s: The human eye forms the image of an object at its –
113.x: The eye's lens focuses light to form the image on the retina, which holds the photoreceptors. The cornea, iris and pupil do not form the image.

113.s: In a Sitar, which type of sound vibrations are produced?
113.x: Plucking a sitar string sets up a transverse wave that reflects from the fixed ends, forming a stationary (standing) transverse wave.

113.s: In human eye, image of object forms at :
113.x: The cornea and lens focus light so that the image forms on the retina, which sends it to the brain through the optic nerve.

113.s: The lens of the eye is behind the
113.x: Light enters through the pupil and then passes through the lens, so the lens lies just behind the pupil. The retina is at the back of the eye.

113.s: A person is unable to read a newspaper without his glasses. He is most probably suffering from
113.x:
Most books and keys: presbyopia. Some keys give hypermetropia, which also blurs near objects; presbyopia (age-related loss of accommodation) is the usual reason a person needs glasses only to read.
Needing glasses only to read a newspaper is the typical sign of presbyopia, the age-related loss of accommodation corrected with convex (reading) lenses. Myopia blurs distant objects.

113.s: Retina of the eye is comparable to which of the following parts of a traditional camera?
113.x: The retina is the light-sensitive surface on which the image forms, like the film in a camera. The lens of the eye corresponds to the camera lens.

113.s: The ………… helps in equalising the pressure on either sides of the eardrum.
113.x: The eustachian tube connects the middle ear to the pharynx and equalises air pressure on both sides of the eardrum. Malleus and incus are ossicles that transmit vibrations.

113.s: For a colourblind person, red colour appear as
113.x: In common red–green colour blindness red and green are confused, so red appears greenish; it is not seen as yellow, blue or violet.

113.s: In which medical condition is the eye’s optic nerve damaged and the condition worsens over time?
113.x: Glaucoma damages the optic nerve and worsens progressively, usually due to raised eye pressure. Cataract affects the lens.

113.s: ……… helps the eye to adjust the focal length of the lens.
113.x: The ciliary muscles of the ciliary body change the curvature of the lens and so its focal length (accommodation). The retina only receives the image.

113.s: Rajat has hypermetropia. What type of lens will the ophthalmologist recommend to correct his vision?
113.x: Hypermetropia is corrected by a convex (converging) lens, while concave lenses correct myopia.

113.s: The human eye is like a camera and hence It contains a system of lens. The eye lens forms
o: a straight or upright, real image of the object on the retina.
an inverted virtual image of the object on the retina.
an inverted, real image of the object on the retina.
a straight or upright, real image of the object on the iris.
113.x: The eye lens acts like a convex lens in a camera and forms a real, inverted image on the retina, which the brain interprets as upright.

113.s: The focal length of the lens of a normal human eye is about
113.x: The eye lens forms images on the retina about 2.5 cm behind it, so the focal length of a normal eye is about 2.5 cm.

113.s: The change in focal length of an eye lens is caused by the action of the ……… .
113.x: The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the eye lens, which alters its focal length (accommodation). The pupil and iris control only the amount of light entering, and the retina receives the image.

113.s: Person who is colourblind can not distinguish between
113.x: The commonest colour blindness is red-green, caused by a defect in the cone cells that detect red or green light.

113.s: A colour-blind person cannot differentiate between the colours
113.x: The commonest colour blindness is red-green, caused by a defect in the cone cells that detect red or green light.

113.s: The person is suffering from far-sightedness face difficulties in–
o: To see both close and distant object clearly
113.x: A far-sighted (hypermetropic) person sees distant objects clearly but has difficulty with close objects.

113.s: In long-sightedness, images are formed at following :
113.x: In long-sightedness the image of a near object falls behind the retina.

113.s: A person with vision defect ‘Myopia’ can see –
o: Nearby as well as distant objects clearly
Neither nearby nor distant objects clearly
113.x: A myopic (short-sighted) person sees near objects clearly but not distant ones.

113.s: Myopia is the disorder of which organ?
113.x: Myopia is a defect of the eye.

113.s: A man cannot see objects distinctly at a distance less than one metre. He is suffering from
113.x: Not seeing near objects clearly (near point beyond 25 cm, here 1 m) is hypermetropia.

113.s: In a transformer, which winding has more cross-section area?
o: Neither; it depends on the core material
113.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
113.x: The low-voltage winding carries the larger current, so it has a larger conductor cross-section (fewer turns).

113.s: The common TV remote control makes use of which of the following waves?
113.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
113.x: TV remotes send infrared pulses from an IR LED to a sensor on the TV.

113.s: What is the range of sound frequency audible to human ears?
113.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
113.x: Humans hear about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz; below is infrasound, above ultrasound.

113.s: RADAR stands for
113.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer in Sainik Welfare Service
113.x: RADAR = Radio Detection And Ranging.

113.s: Which of the following is NOT from the family of Electromagnetic waves?
113.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
113.x: Sound waves are mechanical waves needing a medium; infrared, UV and radio waves are electromagnetic.

113.s: Photons are?
113.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
113.x: Photons are particles (quanta) of light.

113.s: Phonons are?
113.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
113.x: Phonons are quanta of vibration (sound) in solids – 'sound particles'; photons are light particles.

113.s: Bats are able to find out direction for flying because they can produce?
113.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
113.x: Bats emit ultrasonic sound and use the echoes to navigate (echolocation).

113.s:
What is/are not true among the following?
(i) Audible range of sound for human beings is approximately 20 Hz to 10 kHz.
(ii) Sound waves with frequencies higher than 10 kHz are called ultrasound.
(iii) In earthquake, ultrasounds are produced before main shock waves.
113.x: All three are false: hearing is 20 Hz–20 kHz, ultrasound is above 20 kHz, and earthquakes give infrasound, not ultrasound, before the main shock.

113.s: A 3-phase slip-ring induction motor is always started with
o: Full external resistance in rotor circuit
113.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
113.x: A slip-ring motor is started with full external resistance in the rotor circuit to limit starting current and raise starting torque; it is cut out as speed rises.

113.s: The starting torque of the slip ring induction motor can be increased by
113.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
113.x: Adding external resistance to the rotor circuit raises the starting torque of a slip-ring induction motor (max torque at start when R2 = X2).

113.s: Which of the following is responsible for carrying electromagnetic energy?
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Mains Paper-I General Studies & M
113.x: The photon is the carrier (quantum) of electromagnetic energy. Gluons carry the strong force, the graviton is the hypothetical carrier of gravity, and the neutrino is a lepton, not a force carrier.

113.s: What converts sound waves into electrical energy or the audio signals?
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
113.x: A microphone converts sound waves into electrical (audio) signals; a loudspeaker does the reverse. A dynamic microphone works by electromagnetic induction.

113.s: Which of the following is the most important safety method used for protecting home appliances from short-circuiting or overloading?
113.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
113.x: A fuse (or MCB) in series melts and breaks the circuit on overloading or short-circuit. Earthing protects people from shocks, a stabiliser only steadies voltage and a meter only measures.

113.s: A small weight put on the hole of the pressure cooker increases the pressure of steam because?
o: Pressure builds up with no weight also
113.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
113.x: The weight sits on the vent and seals it, so the cooker is airtight and steam cannot escape until its pressure exceeds weight ÷ vent area; that is why the pressure (and boiling point) rises. The small vent area is why even a small weight is enough.

113.s: Which among the following principles is used for wireless charging of modern mobile phones?
113.x: Wireless charging uses Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction: an alternating current in the pad's coil induces a current in the phone's coil. Lenz's rule only gives the direction of the induced current.

113.s: A pressure cooker greatly reduces cooking time. How?
o: Because the heat is distributed very evenly
It cooks the food with higher heat throughout
Because the boiling point inside the cooker is higher
Because the stove flame is made larger
113.x: A pressure cooker raises the pressure, which raises the boiling point of water to about 120 °C, so food cooks faster. It does not spread heat more evenly or use a bigger flame.

113.s: Why does a pressure cooker reduce the cooking time?
o: Because the heat is more evenly distributed
Because the high pressure tenderises the food
Because the boiling point inside is elevated
Because a larger flame is used by the stove
113.x: Higher pressure inside raises the boiling point of water above 100 °C (about 120 °C), so food cooks faster. The pressure itself does not tenderise the food.

113.s: The working principle of a washing machine is
113.x: A washing machine spin-dries by centrifugation: the fast-spinning drum flings water out through its holes. Dialysis, reverse osmosis and diffusion are membrane or molecular processes.

113.s: Fuse wire used for safety of household have :
113.x: A fuse wire must have a low melting point so that it melts when excess current heats it. It also has fairly high resistivity, but the low melting point is the defining property the key asks for.

113.s:
Consider the following statements with reference to osmosis :
(1) If the semipermeable membrane is placed between the solvent and solution, the solvent molecules will flow through the membrane from pure solvent to the solution.
(2) The process of flow of solvent is called as reverse osmosis.
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
113.x: Statement 1 is osmosis: solvent flows through the membrane from pure solvent into the solution. That flow is osmosis, not reverse osmosis (RO needs applied pressure to push solvent the other way), so only 1.

113.s: By which process the sea water can be converted into pure water?
113.x: Reverse osmosis pushes sea water through a semi-permeable membrane under pressure, leaving salts behind (desalination). Deliquescence and efflorescence are about salts gaining or losing water.

113.s: Food gets cooked faster in a pressure cooker because –
o: Water starts boiling at a lower temperature due to high
Water starts boiling at a higher temperature due to high
Water boils only at 100°C but the heat content is higher
Convection currents are set inside the cooker
113.x: The high pressure raises the boiling point of water to about 120 °C, so food cooks faster at the higher temperature. Water does not boil at a lower temperature in a cooker.

113.s:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Generally an alloy of lead and tin is used as a material of the fuse wire.
Reason (R): Alloy of lead and tin has a higher melting point than copper and aluminium.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
113.x: Fuse wire is a tin-lead alloy precisely because it has a low melting point, lower than copper or aluminium. So A is true and R, which says higher, is false.

113.s: The process used for transforming salty water into pure water is called –
113.x: Reverse osmosis applies pressure on the salty side so that pure water passes through the membrane and salts stay behind (desalination).

113.s: Why does water boil at a temperature below 100 °C at higher altitudes ?
o: The atmospheric pressure decreases and hence boiling
Because of heavy winds in mountains
None of the above is correct
113.x: At high altitude the atmospheric pressure is lower, so water boils below 100 °C. Gravity and wind have no such effect.

113.s: Principle of fuse is
113.x: A fuse works on the heating effect of current: excess current heats the low-melting wire until it melts and breaks the circuit.

113.s: After cutting cucumber if salt is added, then water comes out due to :
113.x: Salt makes the outside more concentrated than the cucumber's cell sap, so water leaves the cells by osmosis. Diffusion is solute movement, and active transport needs energy.

113.s: Food is cooked faster in a pressure cooker because
o: Heat cannot escape from the cooker
Steam is colder than the boiling water
Due to high pressure, the boiling point of water is
Water starts boiling at a lower temperature
113.x: The high pressure raises the boiling point of water (~120 °C), so food cooks faster. Water does not boil at a lower temperature in a cooker.

113.s: Water passes from the soil into the roots by a physical process called :
113.x: Root hairs take in soil water by osmosis, because the cell sap is more concentrated than soil water. Transpiration is water loss from leaves.

113.s: The device which works on the principle of electromagnetic induction is
113.x: A dynamo (generator) works on electromagnetic induction, turning motion into current. An electric motor works on the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field (the reverse), and ammeters/voltmeters measure.

113.s: Why does food cook faster in a pressure cooker?
o: The increased pressure increases the boiling point
The food is cooked quickly by steam
The water boils at constant temperature
113.x: The higher pressure raises the boiling point, so water stays liquid at about 120 °C and food cooks faster. Saving steam is not the reason.

113.s: In microwave oven, the microwave tube used is –
o: A combination of klystron and magnetron tubes
113.x: A microwave oven uses a magnetron tube to produce ~2.45 GHz microwaves. Klystrons and travelling-wave tubes are used in radar and communications amplifiers.

113.s: The ‘Choke’ used with a tube light is basically
113.x: The choke of a tube light is an inductor (a coil on an iron core). It gives a high-voltage surge to start the discharge and then limits the current.

113.s: Which one of the following statement regarding a thermo flask is not correct?
o: The walls of flask are separated by vacuum and made of glass which is a poor conductor of heat.
The glass walls themselves have shiny surfaces.
The surface of inner wall radiates good amount of heat and the surface of outer wall absorbs some of the heat that is radiated from the inner wall.
The cork supports are poor conductors of heat.
113.x: In a thermos flask the silvered (shiny) walls reflect heat, so the inner wall radiates very little. The statement that it radiates a good amount of heat is the incorrect one.

113.s:
What is the role of Ultraviolet (UV) radiation in the water purification systems?
I. It inactivates/kills the harmful microorganisms in water.
II. It removes all the undesirable odours from the water.
III. It quickens the sedimentation of solid particles, removes turbidity and improves the clarity of water.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: UV radiation only inactivates or kills microbes by damaging their DNA. It does not remove odours, and it does not speed sedimentation or reduce turbidity.

113.s: If a refrigerator’s door is kept open, then
o: room may get cooled or heated depending upon the weather.
113.x: A refrigerator only moves heat from inside to the coils outside, and the compressor adds heat of its own. With the door open both ends are in the room, so the room heats up.

113.s: In the pressure cooker, cooking is fast because the increase in vapour pressure
113.x: The higher vapour pressure in the cooker raises the boiling point of water (~120 °C), so food cooks faster. Specific heat is unchanged.

113.s: What precaution should be taken to avoid the overloading of domestic electric circuits?
o: Fuse should be connected in the circuit.
Too many appliances should not be connected in single circuit.
Faulty appliances should not be connected in the circuit.
113.x: Overloading is prevented by a fuse in the circuit, by not putting too many appliances on one circuit and by keeping faulty appliances out, so all options are correct.

113.s: A fuse wire must be
o: conducting and of low melting point.
conducting and of high melting point.
insulator and of high melting point.
insulator and of low melting point.
113.x: A fuse wire must conduct and have a low melting point, so that it melts and breaks the circuit when the current is excessive.

113.s: The fuse in an electric circuit is connected in
113.x: A fuse is connected in series with the live wire, so all the current passes through it and the appliance is cut off from the supply when it blows.

113.s: The direction of heat flow between two body depends on which of the following?
113.x: Heat flows from the body at higher temperature to the body at lower temperature, so the direction depends only on their temperatures.

113.s: Blowing air with open pipe is an example of
113.x: Blowing air through an open pipe keeps the gas at the constant atmospheric pressure, so it is an isobaric process.

113.s: A cycle tyre bursts suddenly. This represents an
113.x: A tyre bursts so suddenly that there is no time for heat exchange with the surroundings, so the expansion is adiabatic.

113.s: When oil floats on water, the surface tension of water
113.x: When oil spreads over water it forms a film that considerably lowers the surface tension of the water surface, so the surface tension decreases considerably.

113.s: When the short circuit condition occurs, the current in the circuit
113.x: In a short circuit the resistance becomes almost zero, so by Ohm's law the current rises very sharply.

113.s: A lemon kept in water in a glass tumbler appears to be larger than its actual size. It is because of
113.x: Light from the lemon bends (refracts) as it passes from water to air through the glass, so the lemon appears magnified.

113.s: The splitting of different colours of light in a prism is
113.x: Splitting of white light into its colours in a prism is dispersion, caused by different wavelengths refracting by different amounts.

113.s: A soap bubble shows colours when illuminated with white light. This is due to ……… .
113.x: Colours in a soap bubble come from interference of light reflected from the front and back surfaces of the thin film.

113.s: A fan produces a feeling of comfort during hot weather, because
o: our body radiates more heat in air.
113.x: A fan speeds up evaporation of perspiration, and evaporation takes heat from the body, so we feel cool. The fan does not supply cool air.

113.s: In negative acceleration, the velocity of a body ............ .
113.x: Negative acceleration (retardation) means velocity decreases with time.

113.s: Whether an object will float or sink in a liquid, depends on
o: mass of the object and density of liquid only.
difference in the densities of the object and liquid.
mass and shape of the object only.
113.x: Floating or sinking depends on whether the object's density is less or more than the liquid's, i.e. on the difference in densities, not on mass or shape alone.

113.s: Of the two bulbs,one glows brighter than the other. Which bulb has a higher resistance?
113.x:
Most keys: the dim bulb (bulbs on the same voltage, P = V²/R). Strictly: in series (same current, P = I²R) the brighter bulb has the higher resistance (NCERT Class 10 Electricity).
Two bulbs glowing differently imply they are on the same voltage, so P = V²/R: the bulb with higher resistance draws less power and glows dimmer. (If the bulbs were in series, P = I²R and the brighter one would have the higher resistance.)

113.s: Which of the following devices can be used to detect radiant heat?
113.x: A thermopile is made of thermocouples and detects radiant heat by the voltage generated when radiation heats its junctions.

113.s: Why do water droplets always take a round shape when dropped onto plane surfaces?
o: Due to the presence of Eddy current in the air
Due to exertion of surface tension by the molecules
113.x: Surface tension pulls the surface molecules inward, which minimises surface area, so a droplet takes a round shape.

113.s: Thermal capacity of a body depends on the
o: mass and shape of the body only.
mass, shape and temperature of the body.
113.x: Thermal capacity (C = m·s) depends on the body's mass (and material), not on its shape or temperature, so of the listed options only 'mass of the body only' fits.

113.s: We feel cool when we sit near the fan, this is because
o: air vapourises the sweat on our body.
we feel cool when air touches the body.
113.x: Moving air from the fan evaporates sweat, and evaporation absorbs heat from the skin, causing the cooling feeling. The fan does not cool the air.

113.s: Curie point is the temperature at which
113.x: The Curie point is the temperature above which a ferromagnetic metal loses its magnetic properties and becomes paramagnetic.

113.s: A ball balanced on a vertical rod is an example of
113.x: A ball balanced on top of a vertical rod is in unstable equilibrium: a small displacement lowers its potential energy, so it moves further away from its position instead of returning.

113.s: A stone tied to a string is whirled in a circular path. As it was revolving, the rope suddenly snaps. Then
113.x: When the string snaps, the centripetal force vanishes, so by Newton's first law the stone continues in the direction of its velocity at that instant, which is tangential to the circle.

113.s: Specific gravity is defined as the ratio of
o: density of the substance to the density of water.
density of the substance to the density of water at 0°C.
density of water at 4°C to the density of the substance.
density of the substance to the density of water at 4°C.
113.x: Specific gravity (relative density) is the density of a substance divided by the density of water at 4°C, where water's density is maximum (1 g/cm³).

113.s: A glass vessel is filled with water up to the brim and a lid is fixed to it tightly. Then it is kept inside a freezer for hours. What is expected to happen?
o: The water freezes to ice and the level of ice comes down.
The water in the glass vessel freezes to ice.
The glass vessel breaks due to expansion as water freezes to ice.
The water does not freeze at all.
113.x: Water expands by about 9% on freezing. In a tightly sealed, full glass vessel it cannot expand, so the pressure breaks the vessel.

113.s: What is the distance between a crest and a consecutive trough in a transverse wave?
113.x: The wavelength is the distance between two consecutive crests or troughs. A crest and the adjacent trough are half a wavelength apart.

113.s: Which one of the following is not true for an electromagnetic wave?
o: Electromagnetic wave transports energy and momentum.
Electromagnetic wave can be polarised and reflected.
Electromagnetic wave propagation is described by the varying electric and magnetic fields.
113.x: Electromagnetic waves are transverse, with electric and magnetic fields perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel. So the claim that they are longitudinal is not true.

113.s: The unit of the force constant k of a spring is
113.x: From Hooke's law F = kx, k = F/x, so its unit is newton per metre (N/m).

113.s: A conducting wire is dropped along East-West direction, then
o: induced current flows from West to East.
induced current flows from East to West.
113.x: A wire falling vertically in an East-West line cuts the Earth's horizontal magnetic field (south to north). By Fleming's right-hand rule (motion down, field north) the induced current flows from West to East. An emf is induced, so 'no emf' is wrong.

113.s: If an object moves with constant velocity, then which one of the following statement is not correct?
o: Its motion is along a straight line.
Its displacement increases linearly with time.
113.x: Constant velocity means constant speed and direction, so motion is in a straight line, acceleration is zero and displacement grows linearly. Speed changing with time is therefore not correct.

113.s: The refractive index of fused quartz is 1.46 and that of sapphire is 1.77. If vq is the speed of light in quartz and vs is the speed of light in sapphire, then which one of the following relations is correct?
113.x: Speed of light in a medium is v = c/n. Quartz has the lower refractive index (1.46 vs 1.77), so light travels faster in quartz: vq > vs.

113.s: Surface water of a lake is about to freeze. What will be the temperature (in °C) of water at the bottom of the lake?
113.x: Water is densest at 4 °C, so the densest water sinks to the bottom. The bottom stays at about 4 °C while ice forms at 0 °C on the surface.

113.s: A body is floating in a liquid partly immersed. The body and the liquid are taken to moon. The body
o: will continue to float as before.
113.x: Floating depends on the densities of the body and the liquid, not on g. The weight and the buoyant force both scale with g, so on the moon the body floats as before.

113.s: At low temperature, lead behaves as a
113.x: Lead becomes a superconductor at very low temperature, about 7.2 K.

113.s: Maxwell is the unit of which one of the following?
113.x: The maxwell is the CGS unit of magnetic flux (1 Mx = 10^-8 Wb).

113.s: Which one of the following is a non-dimensional quantity?
113.x: Strain is a ratio of change in length to original length, so it has no dimensions. The other quantities have dimensions.

113.s: The blackboard seems black because it
113.x: A blackboard appears black because it absorbs all colours and reflects none. Black is the absence of reflected light.

113.s: In the absence of the earth’s atmosphere, sky would appear
113.x: The sky looks blue because air molecules scatter sunlight. Without an atmosphere there is nothing to scatter light, so the sky would look black, as it does from the Moon or space.

113.s: Which of the following is not a characteristics of a solid?
113.x: Solids have negligible compressibility because their particles are tightly packed, so high compressibility is not a characteristic of solids.

113.s: A car undergoes a uniform circular motion. The acceleration of the car is
113.x: In uniform circular motion the speed is constant but the velocity direction keeps changing, so there is a centripetal acceleration of constant magnitude but changing direction. Hence it is non-zero and not constant as a vector.

113.s: A wheel-barrow is an example of
113.x: In a wheelbarrow the load lies between the fulcrum (wheel) and the effort, which is a class II lever.

113.s: Steel is more elastic than rubber because it
113.x: Elasticity is the ability to resist deformation and regain shape. Steel needs a larger deforming force for the same strain (higher Young's modulus) than rubber, so it is more elastic.

113.s: The threshold frequency of material is
o: the minimum frequency of light which can emit photoelectrons from materials.
the maximum frequency of light which can emit photoelectrons from materials.
The minimum energy required for the emission of photoelectron from a material.
113.x: Threshold frequency is the minimum frequency of incident light that can eject photoelectrons from a material. Option 3 describes the work function (an energy), not the frequency.

113.s: Thermal conductivity of aluminium, copper and stainless steel increases in the order
113.x: Copper is the best conductor of heat, aluminium is next, and stainless steel is a poor conductor. So the order is stainless steel < aluminium < copper.

113.s: Which one of the following statement about gravitational force is not correct?
o: It is experienced by all bodies in the universe.
It is a dominant force between celestial bodies.
It is a negligible force for atoms.
It is same for all pairs of bodies in our universe.
113.x: Gravitational force depends on the masses and the distance between the bodies (F = Gm1m2/r²), so it differs for different pairs of bodies.

113.s: Which one of the following statements about bar magnet is correct?
o: The pole strength of the North pole of a bar magnet is larger than that of the South pole.
When a piece of bar magnet is bisected perpendicular to its axis, the North and South poles get separated.
When a piece of bar magnet is bisected perpendicular to its axis, two new bar magnets are formed.
The poles of a bar magnet are unequal in magnitude and opposite in nature.
113.x: Cutting a bar magnet perpendicular to its axis gives two smaller complete magnets, each with its own N and S poles. Poles cannot be isolated, and the two poles have equal strength.

113.s: When you walk on a woolen carpet and bring your finger near the metallic handle of a door, an electric shock is produced. This is because
o: charge is transferred from your body to the handle.
a chemical reaction occurs when you touch the handle.
the temperature of the human body is higher than that of the handle.
the human body and the handle arrive at thermal equilibrium by the process.
113.x: Walking on a carpet builds up static charge on the body by friction; touching the metal handle discharges it, so charge is transferred from the body to the handle.

113.s: If electric resistance is to be decreased, then the number of resistances should be connected in … .
113.x: In parallel, the reciprocals of resistances add, so the equivalent resistance is lower than the smallest resistance; series increases it.

113.s: The …… is connected in parallel in an electric circuit.
113.x: A voltmeter is connected in parallel across the component; fuse and ammeter are in series.

113.s: The SI unit of luminous emittance is
113.x: Luminous emittance (luminous flux per unit area) has SI unit lux (lumen per square metre); candela is luminous intensity and lumen is flux.

113.s: Which one of the following wave does not belong to the category of the other three?
113.x: X-rays, microwaves and radio waves are electromagnetic waves; sound waves are mechanical and need a medium.

113.s: The loudness of sound depends upon the
o: velocity of sound waves in the medium.
frequency and velocity of the sound waves.
113.x: Loudness depends on the amplitude of the sound wave (pitch depends on frequency).

113.s: Sound of frequencies below 20 Hz are called ……… .
113.x: Sound below 20 Hz is infrasound.

113.s: Bats detect obstacles in their path by receiving the reflected
113.x: Bats use ultrasound, receiving reflected ultrasonic waves to detect obstacles.

113.s: Which of following property of a proton cannot change while it moves freely in magnetic field?
113.x: Magnetic force is perpendicular to velocity so it does no work; speed and kinetic energy stay constant, while direction (velocity and momentum) changes.

113.s: Flemings “Left hand Rule” is associated with the effect of
113.x: Fleming's left hand rule gives the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field, i.e. the effect of magnetic field on current.

113.s: What is the net force experienced by a bar magnet placed in a uniform magnetic field?
o: Depends upon length of the magnet
113.x: In a uniform field the forces on the two poles are equal and opposite, so net force is zero (only a torque acts).

113.s: Which one among the following waves carries the maximum energy per photon?
113.x: Photon energy E=hf is proportional to frequency; X-rays have the highest frequency among the options.

113.s: Which of the following represents a relation for heat lost = heat gained?
113.x: Heat lost by the hot body equals heat gained by the cold body is the principle of calorimetry; thermal equilibrium only means equal temperatures.

113.s: Which of the following has the lowest electrical resistivity?
113.x: Silver has the lowest resistivity of all metals, lower than aluminium, while nickel and nichrome (a heater alloy) have high resistivity.

113.s: A Galvanometer can be converted into a voltmeter by connecting with it a
113.x: A galvanometer becomes a voltmeter when a high resistance is connected in series, so most of the voltage drops across the resistance and little current flows through the galvanometer.

113.s: The phenomena of electromagnetic induction is ……… .
o: the process of charging a body
the process of generating magnetic field due to a current passing through a coil
induced current in a coil due to relative motion between a magnet and the coil
the process of rotating a coil of an coil electric motor
113.x: Electromagnetic induction is the production of an induced current/emf in a coil due to relative motion between a magnet and the coil (change in magnetic flux).

113.s: Which one of the following metal is used in the filaments of photoelectric cells that converts light energy into electric energy?
113.x: Photoelectric cells use alkali metals with low work function, such as rubidium or caesium, which emit electrons easily when light falls on them; tungsten is used for bulb filaments.

113.s: Net movement of water from a dilute to a concentrated solution through a selectively permeable membrane is called
113.x: Osmosis is the net movement of water from a dilute to a concentrated solution through a selectively permeable membrane. Diffusion is movement of any particles without needing a membrane.

113.s: The movement of water molecules through the plasma membrane is called
113.x: Water molecules move across the plasma membrane (a selectively permeable membrane) by osmosis. Transpiration is water loss from leaves, and sedimentation and precipitation are not membrane processes.

113.s: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
113.x: Electrostatic potential has magnitude only, so it is a scalar. Velocity, force and angular momentum are vectors.

113.s: Identify the unit of measuring intensity of sound
113.x: Sound intensity level is measured in decibels (dB). Knot is a speed unit, ampere is current and candela is luminous intensity.

113.s: What is the unit of the physical quantity, Momentum?
113.x: Momentum = mass × velocity, with unit kg m/s, which equals newton second (N·s), since 1 N = 1 kg m/s².

113.s: Which one of the following physical quantities has the same unit as that of pressure?
113.x: Stress is force per unit area, so it has the same unit as pressure (pascal, N/m²). Strain is dimensionless.

113.s: The resistivity of a material may be expressed in unit of
113.x: Resistivity ρ = RA/l, so its unit is ohm × length: ohm-metre in SI, ohm-cm in CGS. Ohm is the unit of resistance itself.

113.s: Which one of the following is not the unit of energy?
113.x: Joule, watt-hour and newton-metre are all units of energy. Kg·m/s² is the unit of force (newton), so it is not an energy unit.

113.s: The unit of momentum is
113.x: Momentum = mass × velocity, so its SI unit is kg m s⁻¹.

113.s: Which one of the following is the unit of Force?
113.x: The newton is the SI unit of force. The other options are units of pressure (pascal), power (watt) and energy (joule).

113.s: The symbol of SI unit of inductance is H. It stands for
113.x: The henry (H) is the SI unit of inductance.

113.s: The SI unit for electrical resistivity is
113.x: Resistivity ρ = RA/l, so its SI unit is the ohm-metre (Ω m). Tesla is magnetic field; V/m is electric field.

113.s: Newton-metre (Nm) is the SI unit of which of the following physical quantity?
113.x: Torque = force × perpendicular distance, so its unit is N m. Force is in N, power in W and acceleration in m/s².

113.s:
Consider the following statements.
I. Microwave oven uses microwaves to heat food.
II. Microwave oven is highly efficient in the foodstuff containing water, fats and sugar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: A microwave oven heats food with microwaves (~2.45 GHz) that agitate water molecules, and fats and sugars also absorb them well, so both statements are correct.

113.s: The cooling by a desert Cooler is based on
113.x: A desert cooler works by evaporative cooling: evaporating water takes latent heat from the air. It does not dehydrate the air (it adds moisture).

113.s:
Consider the following statements.
I. During the pressure of osmosis, the solvent travels from the concentrated solution to the dilute solution.
II. In the reverse osmosis, external pressure is applied to the dilute solution.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
113.x: In osmosis the solvent moves from the dilute to the concentrated solution (I false), and in reverse osmosis pressure is applied to the concentrated solution (II false).

113.s: Weight of L.P.G. in Kilogram filled in non-domestic gas cylinder is :
113.x: In India a non-domestic (commercial) LPG cylinder holds 19 kg; the domestic cylinder holds 14.2 kg.

113.s: Opening the door of refrigerator kept in the room –
o: You can cool the room to some degree
You can cool the room to the temperature of
You can warm the room a little
You can neither cool nor warm the room
113.x: A refrigerator only pumps heat from inside to the condenser outside, and its motor adds heat; with the door open, the room warms slightly.

113.s:
Consider the following statements:
1.
Assertion (A): The main constituent of the Liquefied Petroleum Gas is methane.
2.
Reason (R): Methane can be used directly for burning in homes and factories where it can be supplied through pipelines.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both (A) and (R) are individually true and R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
113.x: LPG is mainly propane and butane, not methane (A false). Methane, the main component of natural gas, is piped (PNG) to homes and factories (R true).

113.s:
Assertion (A) : The handle of pressure cooker is made up of ebonite.
Reason (R) : Ebonite is a hard material.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
113.x: Pressure-cooker handles are made of ebonite (hard rubber), and ebonite is hard, but it is used because it is a poor conductor of heat. Both true, R not the explanation.

113.s:
Consider the following statements –
Assertion (A) : If Ice collects in the freezer, the cooling in the refrigerator is affected adversely.
Reason (R) : Ice is a poor conductor.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
113.x: Ice in the freezer insulates the cooling coils because ice is a poor conductor of heat, so cooling suffers. Both true and R explains A.

113.s: Tea will cool most easily in:
113.x: Metal is the best heat conductor among the options, so tea in a metal cup loses heat fastest. Glass, clay and porcelain are poor conductors.

113.s: Quartz is extensively used as a piezo-electric material. It contains
113.x: Quartz is crystalline silicon dioxide (SiO2), so it contains silicon. It is piezoelectric and is used in quartz clocks.

113.s: What are 'liquid crystals'?
o: Neither Solid nor liquid phase of matter
113.x: Liquid crystals are a phase between solid and liquid: they flow like liquids but keep some crystal-like molecular order. LCD screens use them.

113.s: Which of the following mirrors is best suited for use in a solar cooker?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: A concave mirror converges sunlight to its focus, so it suits solar cookers. Convex mirrors diverge light, and flat mirrors do not focus.

113.s: The rear view mirror of a motorcycle shall be a
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
113.x: A convex mirror is used as a rear-view mirror because it gives an erect, diminished image over a wide field of view.

113.s: The Hydraulic press used to lift a car is based on the following principle:
113.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
113.x: A hydraulic press/lift works on Pascal's principle: pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally in all directions.

113.s: Hydraulic Brakes work on which principle?
113.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
113.x: Hydraulic brakes work on Pascal's principle: pressure on the brake fluid is transmitted equally to all wheel cylinders.

113.s: A vacuum cleaner can be suitable for all, EXCEPT ______.
o: removing dirt and dust from floors made of hard wood
removing dirt and dust from upholstery
113.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
113.x: A vacuum cleaner suits dust on floors, cars, stairs and upholstery, but sharp glass pieces can damage the hose and bag, so they are swept up instead.

113.s: The material filled in the breather of a transformer is
113.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
113.x: The breather of a transformer is filled with silica gel, which absorbs moisture from the air drawn in so the insulating oil stays dry.

113.s: Name the type of mirror used in the headlights of a car.
113.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
113.x: Car headlights use a concave mirror: with the bulb at the focus it gives a strong parallel beam.

113.s: Which of the following is the principle cause for a passenger to bend forward when the driver of a bus applies brakes to stop the bus?
113.src: APPSC Deputy Inspector of Survey, Technical Assistant in AP
113.x: When the bus brakes, the passenger's body tends to keep moving because of inertia of motion, so the passenger bends forward.

113.s: Which of the following is the principle cause for dust particles to fall off a carpet when the carpet is beaten with a stick?
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
113.x: When the carpet is beaten, it moves but the dust stays at rest by inertia of rest and falls off.

113.s: The generation of electricity by flow of water through dams is an example of which of the following?
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
113.x: Hydroelectricity converts the potential energy of stored water into kinetic and then electrical energy, an example of conservation of energy.

113.s: Which of the following is correctly matched pair of physical quantity and its unit?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
113.x: Pressure is measured in pascal. Temperature is in kelvin, sound level in decibel, and depth in metres (watt is power).

113.s: Passengers sitting in train lean in the opposite direction if the train starts suddenly from rest. This happens due to the:
o: inertia of the body of the passengers
mass of the passengers being significantly less in comparison to the mass of train
113.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
113.x: When the train starts suddenly, the passengers' bodies tend to stay at rest by inertia, so they lean backward.

113.s: Angstrom is a unit of
113.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
113.x: The angstrom (1 Å = 10⁻¹° m) is a unit of length used for wavelengths and atomic sizes.

113.s: One hydraulic horsepower is equal to
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
113.x: One horsepower (including hydraulic horsepower) is about 746 W.

113.s: Which lenses are used by people having short-sightedness?
113.src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
113.x: Short-sightedness (myopia) is corrected with a concave (diverging) lens.

113.s: Under normal conditions, when a current through a Nichrome wire increases, the voltage difference across the wire?
113.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
113.x: By Ohm's law V = IR; nichrome's resistance stays nearly constant, so the voltage rises linearly with current.

113.s: What is the principle behind working of RADAR?
113.src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning
113.x: RADAR works by reflection of radio waves from objects; the echo's delay gives distance.

113.s: Which is the fourth state of matter?
113.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
113.x: Plasma, an ionised gas, is the fourth state of matter after solid, liquid and gas.

113.s: Which of the following microscopes can image individual atoms?
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Mains Paper-I General Studies & M
113.x: The atomic force microscope (like the scanning tunnelling microscope) can image individual atoms by scanning a sharp tip over the surface. Ordinary electron microscopes cannot, though high-resolution TEM can resolve atomic columns, and X-ray and 'radio' microscopes cannot.

113.s: What will happen if a conducting coil of wire is moved through a magnetic field?
113.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
113.x: Moving a coil through a magnetic field induces a current (Faraday's electromagnetic induction).

113.s: Which of the following waves are used by the common TV remote control?
113.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
113.x: TV remote controls use infrared waves (an IR LED).

113.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correct with regard to measurable quantity and their respective unit?
113.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
113.x: Weight is a force and is measured in newtons; pascal is the unit of pressure. The other pairs are correct.

113.s: Myopia and Hypermetropia can be corrected by ____ and ____ lens, respectively.
113.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
113.x: Myopia is corrected with a concave lens and hypermetropia with a convex lens.

113.s:
Which of the following explains the given situation?
When a swimmer pushes the water backwards with his/her hands, in return the water pushes the swimmer forward
113.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
113.x: The swimmer pushes water back (action) and the water pushes the swimmer forward (reaction): Newton's third law.

113.s: What type of lens is prescribed for a person suffering from myopia?
113.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
113.x: Myopia is corrected with a concave (diverging) lens.

113.s: Rocket operates on the principle of
113.x: A rocket works on conservation of momentum (and Newton's third law): exhaust gases go backward and the rocket forward.

113.s: The working of rockets is based on the principle of
113.x:
Printed key: Newton's law (third law). Conservation of momentum (option D) is an equally valid statement of the same principle.
A rocket is propelled by Newton's third law: exhaust is pushed back and the rocket goes forward. 'Conservation of momentum' describes the same effect and is equally right.

113.s: The unit used for measuring the Speed in oceanic navigation is
113.x: Speed at sea is measured in knots (1 knot = 1 nautical mile/h ≈ 1.852 km/h). Fathom is depth, ohm resistance and horsepower power.

113.s: X-rays can be detected by using
113.x: X-rays darken photographic plates, which is how they were discovered and how they are recorded.

113.s:
Match the following The final image formed by different optical instruments
List-I -
List-II
a. Simple Microscope - i. virtual, erect and small
b. Terrestrial telescope - ii. virtual, inverted and small
c. Compound Microscope - iii. virtual and enlarged
d. Astronomical telescope - iv. magnified, virtual and inverted
113.x: Simple microscope: virtual, enlarged (iii). Terrestrial telescope: erect image (i). Compound microscope: magnified, virtual, inverted (iv). Astronomical telescope: virtual, inverted, small (ii).

113.s: A fathometer is an instrument that measures
113.x: A fathometer is an echo sounder that measures the depth of the sea from sound echoes. It uses travel time but does not measure it as such.

113.s: Pressure is measured in:
113.x: Pressure (force per unit area) is measured in pascal (N/m²).

113.s: The hydraulic breaks used in automobiles is a direct application of
113.x: Hydraulic brakes apply Pascal's law: pressure on an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally.

113.s: In a Doctor's stethescope, the sound is intensified because of
113.x: In a stethoscope, sound is carried along the tube by multiple reflections from its walls, so it reaches the ear without spreading out.

113.s: If a table-fan rotating at 50 rpm is placed under an electric lamp (AC supply), it would appear to be
o: rotating slowly, both forwards and backwards
113.x: Stroboscopic effect: the lamp's flicker samples the blade positions at intervals, and the fan can seem to turn slowly backwards. This is the answer the books give.

113.s: Which of the following is considered by scientists as the 'fourth state of matter'?
113.x: Plasma is the fourth state of matter.

113.s: An air bubble in water will act like a
113.x: An air bubble in water is a convex-shaped region of lower refractive index, so it diverges light and acts as a concave lens.

113.s: A myopic eye can be corrected by using a :
113.x: A myopic eye is corrected with a concave (diverging) lens.

113.s: The type of mirror used in the headlight of a car is:
113.x: Car headlights use a concave mirror; the bulb at its focus gives a parallel beam.

113.s: The formation of glittering colours in thin foam of soap is the result of which of the following phenomenon –
113.x: Soap-film colours come from thin-film interference of light reflected from the two surfaces of the film; the standard key reads 'total reflection and interference'.

113.s: Decibel is used to measure :
113.x: The decibel measures sound (intensity) level.

113.s: Which of the following is a cause of echo?
113.x: An echo is sound reflected from a hard surface.

113.s:
Assertion (A) : The boiling point of water decreases as the altitude increases.
Reason (R) : The atmospheric pressure increases with altitude.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
113.x: Boiling point falls with altitude because atmospheric pressure decreases (not increases) with height, so A is true and R false.

113.s: Which mirror is used as a rear view mirror in vehicles ?
113.x: Vehicles use a convex mirror as the rear-view mirror: an erect, diminished image and a wide view.

113.s: A person standing in front of a mirror finds his image larger than himself. This implies that the mirror is :
113.x: Only a concave mirror gives an enlarged (erect, virtual) image when you stand within its focus. Plane mirrors give same-size images and convex mirrors smaller ones.

113.s: Relative humidity is measured by :
113.x: A hygrometer measures relative humidity. A hydrometer measures liquid density, and a lactometer milk density.

113.s: Two glass lenses of same focal length, one being convex and the other concave, are kept in contact, the combination will act as :
113.x: Powers +1/f and −1/f add to zero, so the pair acts like a plane glass sheet.

113.s: Which of the following cannot travel in vacuum?
113.x: Sound needs a material medium and cannot travel in a vacuum; light, heat radiation and EM waves can.

113.s: One important characteristic of sound is 'Pitch', which depends upon :
113.x: Pitch depends on frequency: higher frequency, higher pitch. Loudness depends on amplitude/intensity, and quality (timbre) on the waveform.

113.s: Which of the following lens is used to minimize Myopia?
113.x: Myopia is corrected with a concave lens.

113.s: Sound waves do not travel in :
113.x: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a medium, so it cannot travel through a vacuum.

113.s: Which of the following is used by the dentist to see the image of teeth of a patient?
113.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Concave mirror); it is added as option 5.
Dentists use a concave mirror: with the tooth inside its focus it gives an enlarged, erect image. A concave lens is not a mirror and gives diminished images, a convex mirror diminishes, and a plane mirror gives no magnification. The printed key 'concave lens' is wrong.

113.s: Which instrument is used for measuring humidity in the air?
113.x: A hygrometer measures humidity. A hydrometer measures liquid density, and a eudiometer gas volumes.

113.s: Reading glasses are made from which type of lenses?
113.x: Reading glasses (for hypermetropia/presbyopia) use convex lenses.

113.s: Myopia is corrected by using :
113.x: Myopia is corrected with a concave lens of negative power. Mirrors are not used in spectacles.

113.s: As the diameter of objective lens of a telescope increases, the resolution of telescope :
o: Depends on focal length of lens
113.x: Resolving power of a telescope is proportional to the objective's diameter (θ ≈ 1.22λ/D), so a larger objective gives better resolution.

113.s: The total resistance of a circuit having two parallel resistors is 1.403 kilo-ohm. If one of the resistors is 2.0 kilo-ohm, then the other resistor will be
In automobile hydraulic brakes work on –
113.x: Automobile hydraulic brakes work on Pascal's law.

113.s: What type of lens is used in magnifying glass?
113.x: A magnifying glass is a convex lens with the object placed within its focus.

113.s: Pressure-cooker cooks food in lesser time because
o: The temperature of boiling water decreases due to
Air has no effect as it is closed from all sides
Temperature of boiling water increases due to high
Evaporation of the water used is very small
113.x: The higher pressure in a cooker raises the boiling point of water (~120 °C), so food cooks faster.

113.s: Myopia or short sightedness is corrected by :
113.x: Myopia is corrected with a concave lens.

113.s: Sound wave in air is –
113.x: Sound in air travels as compressions and rarefactions, i.e. a longitudinal mechanical wave. It is not electromagnetic, and only transverse waves can be polarised.

113.s: Rocket works on the principle of the following :
113.x: A rocket throws hot gases backward and moves forward – conservation of linear momentum (Newton's third law). Bernoulli's theorem explains lift, not rocket thrust.

113.s: A dentist mirror is a –
113.x: Dentists use a concave mirror: held close to a tooth it gives an enlarged, erect image. Convex mirrors diminish.

113.s: The power of a lens is measured in :
113.x: Power of a lens P = 1/f (f in metres) and is measured in dioptres (D). Lumen and candela are units of light, not lens power.

113.s: Which one of the following types of the mirror is used to see the traffic behind the car?
113.x: Drivers use a convex mirror: it always gives an erect, diminished image and a wide field of view of the traffic behind.

113.s: In Stethoscope, the sound of the patient's heartbeat reaches the doctor's ears by :
113.x: In a stethoscope the sound of the heartbeat travels along the tube by multiple reflection of sound to the doctor's ears.

113.s:
Which of the following statements is/are true in relation to sound waves?
Statement I : Speed of sound decreases when we go from solid to gaseous state Statement II : In any medium as we decrease the temperature, the speed of sound increases Statement III : Speed of sound is less in aluminium medium than in glass medium
o: Statement I, II and III all are true
Only Statement I and II are true
Only Statement II and III are true
113.x: Statement I is true – sound is fastest in solids and slowest in gases. II is false: speed of sound falls as temperature falls. III is false: sound is faster in aluminium (~6420 m/s) than in glass (~5640 m/s).

113.s: Microwaves are electromagnetic waves having frequencies in range of :
113.x: Microwaves span about 300 MHz–300 GHz, so the option 1 GHz–300 GHz is the one that fits; 3–300 MHz is radio/VHF and 300 GHz–400 THz is infrared.

113.s: On which principle, a Jet Engine works?
113.x: A jet engine expels gases backwards at high speed and gets an equal forward push – conservation of linear momentum (Newton's third law). Angular momentum concerns rotation.

113.s: Large number of thin strips of black paint are made on the surface of a convex lens of focal length 20 cm to catch the image of a white horse. The image will be:
o: More than one of the above
113.x: Each part of a lens forms the whole image; blacking out strips only cuts the light, so the image is a full horse of less brightness, not a striped one.

113.s: Myopia and Hypermetropia can be respectively corrected by :
113.x: Myopia (short sight) is corrected by a concave (diverging) lens and hypermetropia (long sight) by a convex (converging) lens. Cylindrical lenses correct astigmatism.

113.s: In driving a car which type of mirror would you like to use for observing traffic at your back ?
113.x: A convex mirror is used for seeing traffic behind: erect, diminished images and a wide field of view.

113.s: What will be the nature of image formed by a convex mirror when the position of object is between infinity and pole P of the mirror?
113.x: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image behind it, whatever the object distance.

113.s: The density of milk is measured by?
113.x: A lactometer measures the density (specific gravity) of milk to judge its purity. Hydrometer is for liquids in general, hygrometer for humidity, barometer for pressure.

113.s: An air bubble inside water behaves as a:
113.x: An air bubble in water is optically rarer than its surroundings, so its convex shape spreads light – it behaves as a diverging (concave) lens.

113.s: For the myopic eye, the defect is cured by :
113.x: Myopia (image in front of the retina) is corrected by a concave lens of suitable negative power.

113.s: An ice cube is floating in a glass of water. What happens to the water level when the ice melts? It –
113.x: Floating ice displaces its own weight of water; on melting it gives exactly that volume of water, so the level remains the same.

113.s: A distance of 1 km. means –
In a pressure cooker food is cooked in shorter time because –
o: The boiling point of water increases
The boiling point of water decreases
113.x: Raised pressure in a pressure cooker raises the boiling point of water (~120 °C), so food cooks faster.

113.s: Dispersion of light is possible by :
113.x: A prism splits white light into its seven colours (dispersion) because the refractive index differs for each wavelength.

113.s: To remove the defect of long sightedness one uses :
113.x: Long-sightedness (hypermetropia) is corrected with a convex lens, which converges the rays onto the retina.

113.s: An air bubble in water will act like a :
113.x: An air bubble in water acts as a concave (diverging) lens, because air is optically rarer than water.

113.s: Which one of the following statement is not true for a person suffering from hypermetropia?
o: The person can see far objects distinctly
The focal length of the lens is large
The image of the close objects is focused behind the
A concave lens is used to correct this defect
113.x: Hypermetropia is corrected by a convex lens, not a concave lens, so statement (d) is the false one. The person sees far objects clearly, the eye-lens focal length is too long and near images form behind the retina.

113.s: 'Joule' is related to energy in the same way as 'Pascal' is related to :
113.x: Joule is the SI unit of energy and pascal (N/m²) the SI unit of pressure.

113.s: Density of water is
113.x: Water has its maximum density at 4 °C (anomalous expansion), which is why lakes freeze from the top.

113.s: A man standing close to the platform at a railway station experiences a pulling force towards a fast moving train because of ………
o: gravitational force between train and man
pressure difference due to fast moving air in between
113.x: Fast-moving air between the train and the man lowers the pressure there (Bernoulli), so the higher pressure behind pushes him toward the train.

113.s: Which among the following is not a conductor of electricity?
113.x: Ebonite (hard vulcanised rubber) is an insulator; mercury, manganese and iron are metals and conduct electricity.

113.s: Which of the following waves can not be polarised?
113.x: Only transverse waves can be polarised. Ultrasonic waves are sound – longitudinal – so they cannot be polarised; radio, UV and IR are electromagnetic.

113.s: Which of the following is the SI unit of temperature?
113.x: The SI unit of temperature is the kelvin. Candela is luminous intensity and ampere current; Réaumur is an old scale.

113.s: The movement of a horse drawn carriage is an example of which principle of physics.
113.x: The horse pushes the ground back and the ground pushes it forward – action and reaction, Newton's third law.

113.s: The impulse on a particle due to a force acting on it during a given time interval is equal to the change in its
113.x: Impulse = force × time = change in momentum.

113.s: Which one of the following statement about the refractive index of a material medium with respect to air is correct?
o: It can be either positive or negative.
It is unity for all materials.
It is always greater than one.
113.x: Light is slower in any material than in vacuum/air, so the refractive index n = c/v is greater than one. (Strictly, exotic metamaterials and X-rays aside.)

113.s: Bose-Einstein condensate is a
113.x: The Bose–Einstein condensate, near absolute zero, is called the fifth state of matter (after solid, liquid, gas and plasma).

113.s: Nuclear sizes are expressed in a unit named
113.x: Nuclear sizes are expressed in fermi (1 fm = 10⁻¹⁵ m). Angstrom (10⁻¹° m) suits atomic sizes.

113.s: A conductor having some appreciable resistance is called a
113.x: A conductor with appreciable resistance used in a circuit is a resistor.

113.s:
A liquid is kept in a glass beaker.
Which one of the following statement is correct regarding the pressure exerted by the liquid column at the base of the beaker ?
o: The pressure depends on the area of the base of the beaker.
The pressure depends on the height of liquid column.
The pressure does not depend on the height of liquid column.
The pressure neither depends on the area of the base of the beaker nor on the height of liquid column.
113.x: Liquid pressure p = hρg depends on the height of the column (and density), not on the base area.

113.s: In respect of the difference of the gravitational force from electric and magnetic forces, which one of the following statements is true?
o: Gravitational forces is stronger than the other two.
Gravitational force is attractive only, whereas the electric and the magnetic forces are attractive as well as repulsive.
Gravitational force has a very short range.
Gravitational force is a long range force, while the other two are short range forces.
113.x: Gravity is only attractive, while electric and magnetic forces attract and repel. It is the weakest force and, like electromagnetism, long-range.

113.s: Which one of the following statements about energy is correct?
o: Energy can be created as well as destroyed.
Energy can be created but not destroyed.
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed.
Energy cannot be created but can be destroyed.
113.x: Law of conservation of energy: energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only changed from one form to another.

113.s: The energy of a photon, whose momentum is 10 Me V/c, where c is the speed of light, is given by
113.x: For a photon E = pc, so momentum 10 MeV/c gives energy 10 MeV.

113.s:
Statement I Sound waves cannot propagate in vacuum. Statement II Sound waves are elastic waves and require a medium to propagate.
Codes
o: Both the statements are true and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.
Both the statements are true, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
113.x: Sound is an elastic (mechanical) wave needing a medium, which is exactly why it cannot travel in vacuum – II explains I.

113.s:
Statement I The pitch of sound wave depends upon its frequency. Statement II The loudness of the sound wave depends upon its amplitude.
Codes
o: Both the statements are true and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.
Both the statements are true, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
113.x: Pitch depends on frequency and loudness on amplitude – both true, but the loudness fact does not explain pitch.

113.s:
Statement I Sound waves can travel through vacuum. Statement II Light is an electromagnetic wave and can travel through vacuum.
Codes
o: Both the statements are true and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.
Both the statements are true, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
113.x: Sound cannot travel through vacuum (I false); light is an electromagnetic wave and can (II true).

113.s: Statement I While putting clothes for drying up, we spread them out. Statement II The rate of evaporation increases with an increase in surface area.
o: Both the statements are individually true and statement II is the correct expalanation of statement I.
Both the statements are individually true, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true
113.x: Spreading clothes increases the exposed surface area, and evaporation rises with surface area – II explains I.

113.s: The correct relation between the radius of curvature R and focal length f of a spherical mirror is
113.x: For a spherical mirror the focus lies midway between pole and centre of curvature: R = 2f.

113.s: This is not a use of a concave mirror
113.x: Rear-view mirrors are convex, not concave. Torches, headlights and shaving mirrors use concave mirrors.

113.s: Which one of the following is the value of 1 nanometre?
113.x: 1 nm = 10⁻⁹ m = 10⁻⁷ cm.

113.s: At 20°C, the speed of sound in water approximately
113.x: Sound travels at about 1480–1500 m/s in water at 20 °C (330–343 m/s in air).

113.s: If x the temperature of a system in Kelvin and y is the temperature of the system in °C, then the correct relation between them is
The absolute zero, i.e. temperature below which is not achievable, is about
113.x: Absolute zero is 0 K = −273.15 °C, i.e. about −273 °C. '−273 K' is meaningless – kelvin has no negative values.

113.s: The frequency (in Hz) of a note that is one octave higher than 500 Hz is
113.x: One octave higher means double the frequency: 2 × 500 = 1000 Hz.

113.s: If a body is whirled in a circle the work done on it …………
113.x: In circular motion the centripetal force is perpendicular to the displacement, so the work done is zero.

113.s: How many watts are there in metric horse power?
113.x: Metric horsepower = 735.5 W ≈ 736 W (the British/mechanical hp is 746 W).

113.s: A current I flows through a resistor. A source maintains a potential difference of V across the resistor. The energy supplied by the source in time t is
113.x: Energy = power × time = V × I × t.

113.s: Insulators have resistivity of the order of
113.x: NCERT gives insulators resistivities of about 10¹² to 10¹⁷ Ω m (metals 10⁻⁸–10⁻⁶).

113.s: ........ states that the total current entering a junction is equal to the total current leaving the junction.
113.x: Kirchhoff's first (junction) law: total current entering a junction equals the total current leaving it (conservation of charge).

113.s: .......... .is not related to gases.
113.x: Boyle's, Avogadro's and Charles's laws are gas laws; Joule's law (H = I²Rt) concerns heating by electric current.

113.s: How much calories are there in a Joule?
113.x: 1 cal = 4.186 J, so 1 J ≈ 0.24 cal.

113.s: The motion of a freely falling body is an example of ........... accelerated motion.
113.x: A freely falling body has a constant acceleration g, so its motion is uniformly accelerated.

113.s: Why does a cannon recoil after firing?
113.x: Firing pushes the shell forward and the cannon back by an equal and opposite reaction – Newton's third law (equivalently, momentum conservation).

113.s: A body is acted upon by two unequal forces in opposite directions, but not in one line. The effect is that the body will have
o: neither the rotational nor the translational motion.
rotational as well as translational motion.
113.x: Two unequal opposite forces not in one line give a net force (translation) and a torque (rotation), so both motions result.

113.s: Boiling point of water is .... .
113.x: Water boils at 100 °C = 212 °F at standard pressure.

113.s: The absolute zero temperature is 0°K. In °C unit, which one of the following is the absolute zero temperature?
Which finger shows the direction of current in Fleming’s left hand rule?
113.x: In Fleming's left-hand rule the forefinger shows the field, the middle finger the current and the thumb the force (motion).

113.s: The heat produced by current in wire during time t is determined by ……… .
113.x: Joule's law of heating: H = I²Rt.

113.s: As the object covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time, it is said to be in ......... motion.
113.x: Unequal distances in equal intervals of time = non-uniform motion.

113.s: The sensation of sound persists in the human brain for about
113.x: The sensation of a sound persists in the brain for about 0.1 s – why an echo needs a 0.1 s delay (17.2 m distance).

113.s: More density of the particles in the medium through which sound travels, creates more ……… and vice versa.
113.x: Where particles are crowded (compressions) the density and pressure are high; rarefactions have low pressure.

113.s: If an object is at rest, then the time (X-axis) versus distance (Y-axis) graph
113.x: At rest the distance does not change with time, so the distance–time graph is a horizontal line parallel to the time axis.

113.s: The angle in which a cricket ball should be hit to travel maximum horizontal distance is
113.x: Range R = u² sin2θ / g is maximum when sin2θ = 1, i.e. θ = 45°.

113.s: Magnetic meridian is an imaginary
113.x: The magnetic meridian is the vertical plane through the magnetic axis of a freely suspended magnet (the magnetic N–S direction).

113.s:
Statement I A compass needle placed near a current-carrying wire will get deflected. Statement II A current-carrying wire creates magnetic field around it.
Codes
o: Statement I and statement II are correct and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I
Statement I and statement II are correct, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I
Statement I is correct, but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, but statement II is correct
113.x: A current-carrying wire produces a magnetic field around it, which is why a nearby compass needle deflects – II explains I.

113.s: Two identical solid pieces, one of gold and other of silver, when immersed completely in water exhibit equal weights. When weighed in air (given that, density of gold is greater than that of silver),
o: the gold piece will weigh more.
the silver piece will weigh more.
Both silver and gold pieces weigh equal.
weighing will depend on their masses.
113.x: Apparent weight in water = W(1 − ρw/ρ). Equal apparent weights mean the less dense silver loses a bigger share, so its true (air) weight is larger.

113.s: A person is standing on a frictionless horizontal ground. How can he move by a certain distance on this ground?
113.x: On frictionless ground he cannot push the ground backward; expelling air by sneezing (or throwing anything) gives him an opposite push – momentum conservation.

113.s: When the direction of motion of coil is perpendicular to the electromagnetic field, then the value of induced current is ……… .
113.x: Induced current is maximum when the coil moves perpendicular to the magnetic field (maximum rate of flux cutting) and zero when it moves parallel.

113.s:
A spring can be used to determine the mass m of an object in two ways : I by measuring the extension in the spring due to the object and II by measuring the oscillation period for the given mass.
Which of these methods can be used in a space-station orbiting the earth?
113.x: In orbit everything is in free fall (weightless), so the object stretches the spring by nothing; the oscillation period T = 2π√(m/k) does not depend on g and still works.

113.s: When temperature difference between liquid and its surroundings is doubled, the rate of loss of heat will
113.x: Newton's law of cooling: rate of heat loss ∝ temperature difference, so doubling the difference doubles the rate.

113.s: Which one of the following force is non-central and non-conservative?
113.x: Friction acts against motion along the surface, not along a line joining centres (non-central), and its work depends on path (non-conservative). Electric and gravitational forces are central and conservative.

113.s: If a physical quantity has the units- ampere meters per second squared, then what are it’s dimensions?
113.x: Ampere → [I], metre → [L], per second squared → [T⁻²]: the dimensions are [I L T⁻²].

113.s: A rectangular coil of copper wire is rotating in a magnetic field. The direction of the induced current changes once in each?
113.x: In a coil rotating in a magnetic field the induced current reverses direction once every half revolution, giving alternating current.

113.s: Ability to distinguish two closely placed objects is
113.x: Resolving power is an instrument's ability to show two close objects as separate. Magnifying power only enlarges the image; 'video' and 'distinguish' power are not terms.

113.s: Which of these travels in glass with minimum velocity?
113.x: Violet has the highest refractive index in glass, so it travels slowest (v = c/n). Red light is the fastest of the colours in glass.

113.s: Which of the following is not a unit of speed?
113.x: Speed is distance per time, so m/s, km/h and cm/s are speed units. m²/h is area per time, not speed.

113.s: For a body moving with uniform acceleration its final velocity equals ........... .
113.x: With uniform acceleration the average velocity is (u + v)/2, so v = 2 × average velocity − u. The other combinations do not follow from this relation.

113.s: The first equation of motion gives the relation between
113.x: The first equation v = u + at links velocity and time. The second (s = ut + ½at²) links position and time, the third links position and velocity.

113.s: The second equation of motion gives the relation between
113.x: The second equation s = ut + ½at² gives position (displacement) against time. Velocity–time is the first equation and position–velocity the third.

113.s: The rate of change of displacement with time is called as ...... .
113.x: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, and force is not a rate of displacement.

113.s: In a vacuum, a five-rupee coin a, feather of sparrow bird and a mango are dropped simultaneously from the same height. The time taken by them to reach the bottom is t1, t 2 and t 3 , respectively. In this situation, we will observe that
113.x: With no air resistance every body falls with the same acceleration g, so all three take the same time (t1 = t2 = t3). Mass does not affect free-fall time.

113.s: At magnetic poles, the angle of dip is
113.x: At the magnetic poles the needle stands vertical, so dip is 90°. Dip is zero at the magnetic equator.

113.s: The temperature which has the same reading on both Fahrenheit and Celsius scales is
113.x: Setting F = C in F = 9C/5 + 32 gives C = −40. So −40 °C = −40 °F.

113.s: A man weighing 70 kg is coming down in lift. It the cable of the lift breaks sudden, the weight of the man would become
113.x: If the cable breaks, man and lift fall freely with g, so the floor pushes on him with no force and his apparent weight becomes zero.

113.s: The unit of pressure is
o: None of the above/More than one of the above
113.x:
Printed BPSC key: None of the above. Most books treat kg/cm² (as kgf/cm²) as a pressure unit, which would make (a) correct.
The printed BPSC 2019 key is 'None of the above/More than one of the above': kg/cm² is mass per unit area; the pressure unit is kgf/cm² (or the SI pascal, N/m²).

113.s: Pressure is a scalar quantity because
o: it is the ratio of force to area and both force and area are vectors.
it is the ratio of magnitude of force to area.
it is the ratio of component of force (normal to area) to area
113.x: Pressure is the normal component of force divided by area; it acts equally in all directions and has no direction of its own, so it is scalar.

113.s: One nanometer is equal to ……… meters.
113.x: One nanometre is 10⁻⁹ m. 10⁻⁶ is micro and 10⁻¹² is pico.

113.s: Magnetic keepers are used to protect magnets from
113.x: Soft-iron keepers close the magnetic circuit across the poles, which stops the magnet's own demagnetising field from weakening it. They do not shield heating or outside fields.

113.s: Ice is packed in saw dust because
o: saw dust will not get melted easily.
saw dust is poor conductor of heat.
saw dust is a good conductor of heat.
saw dust does not stick to the ice.
113.x: Sawdust is a poor conductor of heat (air trapped in it), so heat reaches the ice slowly. It is not a good conductor.

113.s: According to the Second Law of Motion, for a given force, acceleration is inversely proportional to the ……… of an object.
113.x: From F = ma, for a fixed force the acceleration is inversely proportional to the mass. Density and volume do not enter the law.

113.s: Acceleration due to gravity of planet decreases with ..... .
o: decrease in radius of the planet
increase in mass of the planet
decrease in mass of the body
increase in altitude from surface of the planet
113.x: g falls with altitude because distance from the centre grows. Smaller radius or larger planet mass would increase g, and the falling body's mass does not matter.

113.s: A liquid disturbed by stirring comes to rest due to
