Official key / most books: neutrino = zero mass. Strictly: neutrinos have a tiny non-zero mass (neutrino oscillations, Nobel Prize 2015); the photon is the truly massless particle (Rocket Physics p.3: 'Neutrino (near-zero)').
Neutrino – zero mass, quark – fractional charge, positron – half-integral (fractional) spin, photon – integral spin: 2 3 1 4.

113.s:
Match List I (Physical quantity) with List II (Unit) and select the correct answer using codes given below the lists.
List I (Physical quantity)
A. Distance
B. Amount of material
C. Amount of electrical charge
D. Energy
List II (Unit)
1. Mole
2. Coulomb
3. Light year
4. Watt-hour
Codes A B C D
113.x: Distance – light year, amount of substance – mole, charge – coulomb, energy – watt-hour: 3 1 2 4.

113.s: Which of the following is a mechanical wave?
113.x: Sound needs a material medium, so it is a mechanical wave; radio waves, X-rays and light are electromagnetic.

113.s:
If the amplitude or oscillation of a simple pendulum is very small, then its time period of oscillation
I. depends on the length of the pendulum, L.
II. depends on the acceleration due to gravity, g.
III. depends upon the mass of the bob of the pendulum, m.
IV. does not depend upon the amplitude of the pendulum, A.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
113.x: For small amplitude T = 2π√(L/g): it depends on L and g, not on the bob's mass or the amplitude. So I, II and IV.

113.s: The Leaning Tower of Pisa does not fall because
o: it is tapered at the top.
it covers a large base area.
its centre of gravity remains as the lowest position.
the vertical line through the centre of gravity of the tower falls within its base.
113.x: A body stays upright while the vertical line through its centre of gravity falls within its base, which is why the leaning tower stands.

113.s:
Consider the following statements X-rays
I. can pass through aluminium.
II. can be deflected by magnetic field.
III. move with a velocity less than the velocity of ultraviolet rays in vacuum.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
113.x: X-rays penetrate light metals such as aluminium (I true). Being uncharged electromagnetic waves they are not deflected by a magnetic field, and they travel at the speed of light like UV.

113.s:
With reference to the movement of molecules of fluid in plant, consider the following statements.
I. Diffusion is the movement of molecules of a substance from the region of their higher concentration to the region of their lower concentration.
II. Osmosis is a process in which the water molecules move through a semipermeable membrane from the region of their lower concentration to the region of their higher concentration.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct ?
113.x: I is the correct definition of diffusion. II is wrong: in osmosis water moves from the region of its higher concentration (dilute solution) to its lower concentration (concentrated solution).

113.s: Which one of the following scales of temperature does not have a negative value?
113.x: Kelvin is an absolute scale starting at absolute zero (0 K), so it has no negative values; Celsius, Fahrenheit and Reaumur do.

113.s:
Assertion (A) All liquids are conductors of electricity.
Reason (R) Under the condition of low pressure and high voltage, liquids can be made conducting.
Codes
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
113.x: A is false: pure water, oils and most organic liquids are insulators; only electrolytes and liquid metals conduct. R is a true statement in itself.

113.s:
Which of the following statement(s) about latent heat for a given substance is/are correct?
I. It is fixed at a given temperature.
II. It depends upon the temperature and volume.
III. It is independent of temperature and volume.
IV. It depends on the temperature but independent of volume.
113.x: Latent heat is fixed at a given temperature (I) and does not depend on volume, but it varies with temperature (latent heat of vaporisation of water falls as temperature rises and is zero at the critical point). So I and IV, not III.

113.s: The radius of curvature of the plane mirror is
113.x: A plane mirror is a sphere of infinite radius, so its radius of curvature (and focal length) is infinity.

113.s: Which one of the following is the natural phenomenon based on a simple periscope works?
113.x: A simple periscope has two plane mirrors at 45° and works by reflection of light; prism periscopes use total internal reflection.

113.s: What is the minimum distance (in metres) required to hear an echo?
113.x: An echo needs a 0.1 s gap; at ~344 m/s sound covers ~34 m out and back, so the reflector must be at least ~17 m away.

113.s: Transfer of heat by convection can take place in
113.x: Convection needs a medium that can flow, so it occurs only in fluids – liquids and gases; not in solids or vacuum.

113.s: The basic difference between an AC generator and a DC generator is that
o: AC generator has an electromagnet while a DC generator has permanent magnet.
AC generator has slip rings while the DC generator has a commutator.
DC generator will generate a higher voltage.
AC generator will generate a higher voltage.
113.x: An AC generator uses slip rings; a DC generator uses a split-ring commutator to give unidirectional current.

113.s:
Match the following.
Quantity SI Unit
A. Frequency
B. Force
C. Resistance
1. Ohm
2. Hertz
3. Newton
Codes A B C
113.x: Frequency – hertz, force – newton, resistance – ohm: 2 3 1.

113.s:
Consider the following sentences.
I. The phenomenon of emission of electrons from metals under the effect of light rays is called photoelectric effect.
II. The electron emitted by the photoelectron effect are called proton.
III. The phenomena like interference diffraction and polarisation were explained successfully on the basis of wave nature of radiation.
Which of the above sentence/sentences is/are correct?
113.x: I defines the photoelectric effect and III is right (wave nature explains interference, diffraction, polarisation). II is wrong: the emitted particles are photoelectrons, not protons.

113.s: Which of the following is not a vector quantity?
113.x: Speed has only magnitude (scalar); velocity, torque and displacement are vectors.

113.s: Which one of the following quantities does not have unit?
113.x: Strain is a ratio (change in length / original length), so it has no unit; stress and pressure (Pa) and force (N) have units.

113.s: The sound will have the highest velocity in
113.x: Sound is fastest in solids such as steel (~5,000 m/s), slower in water (~1,500) and air (~343) and cannot travel in vacuum.

113.s:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using codes given below the lists.
List I
A. Acceleration
B. Force
C. Work done
D. Impulse
List II
1. Joule
2. Newton second
3. Newton
4. Metre per second2
Codes A B C D A B C D
113.x: Acceleration – m/s², force – newton, work – joule, impulse – newton second: 4 3 1 2.

113.s: A hot body cools from 90°C to 75°C in 25 second. The same body in further cooling from 75°C to 60°C will take how much time?
113.x: By Newton's law of cooling the rate of cooling falls as the body approaches room temperature, so the next 15 °C drop takes longer than 25 s.

113.s:
After using for some time, big transformers get heated up. This is due to the fact that
I. current produces heat in the transformers.
II. hysteresis loss occurs in the transformers.
III. liquid used for cooling gets heated.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
113.x: Transformers heat up from copper (I²R) losses due to the current and from hysteresis and eddy-current losses in the core. The coolant getting hot is a result, not a cause.

113.s:
Consider the following four particles I. Alpha particle
II. Proton III. Electron
IV. Neutron
Which of the following is the correct sequence in which their rest masses increase?
113.x: Electron (lightest) < proton < neutron (slightly heavier) < alpha particle (2p + 2n): III-II-IV-I.

113.s:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using codes given below the lists.
List I
A. Watt
B. Knot
C. Nautical mile
D. Calorie
List II (Units) (Parametric quantities)
1. Heat
2. Navigation
3. Speed of a ship
4. Power
Codes A B C D A B C D
113.x: Watt – power, knot – speed of a ship, nautical mile – navigation (distance), calorie – heat: 4 3 2 1.

113.s: The speed of sound is faster in
113.x: Sound travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids, slowest in gases and not at all in vacuum.

113.s: Which one of the following pairs constitutes particle-antiparticle pair?
113.x: The positron (Anderson, 1932) is the antiparticle of the electron – same mass, opposite charge.

113.s: Which is not a primary colour?
113.x: Primary colours of light are red, green, blue (pigments: red, yellow, blue); black is the absence of light, not a primary colour.

113.s: Which one of the following statement is not correct?
o: The SI unit of charge is ampere- second.
Debye is the unit of dipole moment.
Resistivity of a wire of length I and area of cross-section A depends upon both I and A.
The kinetic energy of an electron of mass m kilogram and charge e coulomb, when accelerated through a potential difference of V volt is eV joule.
113.x: Resistivity ρ = RA/l is a property of the material (and temperature), not of the wire's length or area, so statement 3 is false. 1 C = 1 A·s, debye is the dipole-moment unit and KE = eV are true.

113.s: The minimum distance of clear vision for a normal healthy eye of human being is supposed to be
113.x: The least distance of distinct vision (near point) of a normal young eye is about 25 cm.

113.s: Which one of the following is not the unit of heat?
113.x: Calorie, erg and joule are units of heat/energy; centigrade (Celsius) is a temperature scale.

113.s: With the rise of temperature, the viscosity of liquid
o: may increase or decrease depending on nature of liquid
113.x: In liquids viscosity falls as temperature rises (cohesion weakens); in gases it rises.

113.s: Magnification produced by a rear view mirror fitted in vehicles —
113.x: A rear-view mirror is convex: it always forms a virtual, erect, diminished image (magnification < 1) and a wide field of view.

113.s: The velocity of sound is highest
o: In dry air at 0 degrees centigrade
In dry air at 30 degrees centigrade
In moist air at 0 degrees centigrade
In moist air at 30 degrees centigrade
113.x: Sound is faster at higher temperature and in humid air (moist air is less dense), so moist air at 30 °C.

113.s:
Given below are the two statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Analyze the statements and choose one of the given options.
Assertion (A): We see a blue sky most of the time.
Reason (R): Sunlight reaches Earth's atmosphere and is always concentrated. Blue light is concentrated more than the other colors as it travels in long, lazy waves.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
113.src: APPSC 2021 Medical Officer (Ayurveda) In Ayush Department
113.x: A is true. R is false: the sky is blue because air molecules scatter short-wavelength blue light most (Rayleigh scattering); blue light has short waves, not 'long, lazy' ones.

113.s:
Given below are the two statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Analyze the statements and choose one of the given options.
Assertion (A): Spirit is used in a thermometer to measure temperatures down to -70° C.
Reason (R): Spirit is less toxic and evaporates quickly.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
113.src: APPSC 2021 Medical Officer (Ayurveda) In Ayush Department
113.x: Alcohol (spirit) freezes at about −114 °C, so it can read down to −70 °C – that low freezing point is the reason. Lower toxicity and quick evaporation are true but do not explain it.

113.s:

Assertion (A): Spirit is used in a thermometer to measure temperatures down to -70° C.
Reason (R): Spirit is less toxic and evaporates quickly.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

113.x: Alcohol (spirit) freezes at about −114 °C, so it can read down to −70 °C – that low freezing point is the reason. Lower toxicity and quick evaporation are true but do not explain it.

113.s: If the cover of a book looks red when seen through a piece of red glass, then the cover will look like
113.x: Red glass passes only red light: a red cover reflects red and looks red, a white cover also sends red through, so it could be red or white.

113.s: The flying of birds is a proof of Newton's
113.x: Wings push air down and back (action); air pushes the bird up and forward (reaction) – Newton's third law.

113.s: The image formed by astronomical telescope is
113.x: In an astronomical telescope (two convex lenses) the final image is virtual, inverted and highly magnified.

113.s:
Assertion (A) : Radio waves bend in a magnetic field.
Reason (R) : Radio waves are electromagnetic in nature.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
113.x: Radio waves are electromagnetic (R true) and, being uncharged, are not bent by a magnetic field (A false).

113.s: The SI unit of electrical resistivity of conductor is –
113.x: The SI unit of resistivity is the ohm-metre, so 'ohm' is the option that fits.

113.s: What is the unit of atmospheric pressure?
113.x: The bar (10⁵ Pa) is a common unit of atmospheric pressure (SI unit pascal); knot – speed, joule – energy, ohm – resistance.

113.s: Which one of the following statements is not true about cosmic rays?
o: They are made of highly energetic charged particles
113.x: Cosmic rays are streams of highly energetic charged particles (mostly protons), not electromagnetic waves.

113.s: What is the unit of measure of magnetic field?
113.x: The SI unit of magnetic field (flux density) is the tesla.

113.s: Bats can fly during dark nights and also prey. This is because :
o: The pupil of their eyes is large
Their night vision is very good
They produce ultrasonic waves and are guided by
113.x: Bats emit ultrasonic waves and navigate and hunt by their echoes (echolocation).

113.s: By which one of the following an old written material which cannot be read easily, can be read?
113.x: Infrared photography/reflectography brings out faded or obscured old writing, so IR rays.

113.s: Which one of the following SI unit is not correctly matched?
113.x: The SI unit of pressure is the pascal; the dyne is the CGS unit of force, so 'Pressure – Dyne' is wrong.

113.s: Pressure inside a soap bubble is –
113.x: Surface tension makes the pressure inside a soap bubble higher than outside (excess pressure 4T/r).

113.s: The reverse effect of X-ray emission is
113.x: X-ray emission turns electron energy into photons; the photoelectric effect turns photon energy into ejected electrons – the reverse.

113.s:
Read the following statements–
Statement (A) : Ernest Rutherford said in Royal Society that a man will never be able to get nuclear energy.
Reason (R) : He was confident that the Law of Einstein will fail and the volume will not be converted to energy. Select your answer in the code given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (A) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(R) is correct but (A) is not correct
113.x: Rutherford did call atomic power 'moonshine' (British Association, 11 Sep 1933), so A is broadly true. R is false: he did not doubt Einstein's mass–energy law; he judged that splitting atoms consumed more energy than it released (official key: a).

113.s:
Consider the following statements :
Assertion (A) : Light coloured clothes are preferred in summer.
Reason (R) : Light colours are poor absorbers of heat. Select correct answer from the code given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) correctly explains
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) does not correctly
113.x: Light colours reflect most heat and absorb little, so light clothes keep us cooler in summer – R explains A.

113.s: An object weighs the most
113.x: In vacuum there is no buoyant upthrust, so the object shows its full weight; air, hydrogen and water all reduce it.

113.s: A convex mirror is used to correct which of the following?
113.x: The stem means a convex lens: a converging (convex) lens corrects long sight (hypermetropia); myopia needs a concave lens.

113.s: Which of the following types of matter is in ionic state?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
113.x: Plasma is ionised gas, i.e. matter in the ionic state, as in the Sun and lightning. Solids, liquids and ordinary gases are made of neutral atoms or molecules.

113.s:
Consider the following reaction. CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2 O
Which of the following about the reaction given above is/are correct?
I. Carbon is oxidised
II. Hydrogen is oxidised
III. Hydrogen is reduced
IV. Carbon is reduced
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
113.x: Carbon goes from −4 in CH4 to +4 in CO2, so it is oxidised. Hydrogen stays +1, so it is neither oxidised nor reduced; oxygen is reduced.

113.s: Identify the hormone that is found in the plants:
113.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
113.x: Cytokinin is a plant hormone that promotes cell division. Thyroxine, oestrogen and testosterone are animal hormones.

113.s: Aneurysms can be detected by using this technology
113.x:
Printed key: MRI. Strictly, CT angiography detects aneurysms as well and is often the first test; a catheter angiogram is the most sensitive (Barnes-Jewish Hospital, Brain Aneurysm Diagnosis).
MRI (MR angiography) shows the brain's blood vessels without ionising radiation and detects aneurysms. CT angiography also detects them and is often the first test, so CT is the tempting option; ECG records heart rhythm and plain X-ray does not show vessels.

113.s: A dehydrated person should not drink :
113.x: Sea water is far saltier than body fluids, so drinking it pulls more water out of the cells and worsens dehydration. Tea, coffee and alcohol are diuretics, but they still add water; sea water is the one that must not be drunk.

113.s: Scorpion venom contains toxins which are
113.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
113.x: Scorpion venom toxins are small proteins (peptides) that act on nerve ion channels. They are not vitamins, cyanides or alkalis.

113.s: Thalassemia disease is caused by ______
o: mutation in certain genes present in the X chromosome
the protein involved in the blood clotting is affected
accumulation of phenylalanine in the brain
reduced rate of synthesis of one of the globin chains
113.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
113.x: Thalassemia is an autosomal recessive disorder with a reduced rate of synthesis of one of the globin chains (α or β) of haemoglobin. X-linked inheritance is haemophilia, a clotting-protein defect is also haemophilia, and phenylalanine build-up is PKU.

113.s: Pepsin is produced in
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: In ruminants, the abomasum is the true glandular stomach that secretes pepsin and HCl. The rumen, reticulum and omasum produce no gastric juice.

113.s: Which of the following hormones contains Iodine?
113.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
113.x: Thyroxine (T4) contains iodine, which is why iodine deficiency causes goitre. Insulin, testosterone and adrenaline contain no iodine.

113.s: Dialysis differs from the kidney in which of the following functions?
o: Maintaining proper water balance in the body
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Dialysis filters wastes and excess water from blood, but cannot reabsorb useful nutrients as the kidney tubules do. Waste removal, water balance and stopping toxic build-up are things it does.

113.s: Satish was injured while playing kabaddi and started bleeding. When he was taken to the doctor, he was diagnosed with a genetic disorder that prevents blood from clotting. What disease is Satish suffering from?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Haemophilia is an inherited (X-linked) disorder in which blood does not clot. Anaemia and thalassemia lower haemoglobin, and blood cancer is leukaemia.

113.s: Viruses contain?
113.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
113.x: A virus is nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) inside a protein coat. It has no metabolism of its own, so the defining content is nucleic acid, not enzymes, carbohydrates or vitamins.

113.s: Which one of the following is not an genetic disease?
113.x: Night blindness is mostly due to vitamin A deficiency, a nutritional disease. Albinism, haemophilia and colour blindness are inherited (genetic) disorders.

113.s: Recently scientists discovered protein which is responsible for hazardous neural disease Alzheimer’s. Which of the following is that protein?
113.x: Amyloid-beta plaques of Alzheimer's come from the amyloid precursor protein (APP); the other names are not real proteins.

113.s: Which one of the following is not a genetic disorder?
113.x: Xerophthalmia is caused by vitamin A deficiency, not by genes. Colour blindness, Down's syndrome and haemophilia are genetic disorders.

113.s: Intake of which one of the following food components should be minimised by patients having Gouty Arthritis due to elevated serum uric acid level?
113.x: Uric acid comes from breakdown of purines of nucleic acids, so gout patients cut purine-rich (nucleic acid) foods. Fibre, lipids and carbohydrates do not raise uric acid directly.

113.s: Which gland is associated with Diabetes?
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
113.x: Diabetes is due to low insulin or insulin resistance; insulin comes from the beta cells of the pancreas. Thyroid, spleen and liver do not secrete it.

113.s: Which of the following controls body temperature in humans?
113.src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
113.x: The hypothalamus works as the thermostat, controlling body temperature. Liver, thyroid and heart produce or move heat but do not regulate it.

113.s: Presence of albumin in urine is an indication of malfunctioning of following organ
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Healthy glomeruli hold back albumin, so albumin in urine (albuminuria) shows kidney damage; heart, lung and brain are not the filter.

113.s: The accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity is termed as
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Ascites is fluid collected in the peritoneal (abdominal) cavity. Hydrothorax is fluid in the pleural cavity, hydroamnion excess amniotic fluid and oedema fluid in tissues.

113.s: With respect to digestion in the human body, what are mucous, chief and parietal cells?
o: Major types of cells in gastric glands
Types of intestinal mucosal goblet cells
Major types of cells in pancreas
Major cells in lobes of liver
113.src: APPSC Executive Officer Gr-III Endowment Paper-I General Stu
113.x: Gastric glands of the stomach have mucous cells (mucus), chief cells (pepsinogen) and parietal cells (HCl). They are not intestinal, pancreatic or liver cells.

113.s: Which blood group is a universal recipient?
113.src: APPSC Deputy Inspector of Survey, Technical Assistant in AP
113.x: AB has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies, so it can receive any ABO group – the universal recipient; O is the universal donor.

113.s: Which among the following is the primary stress hormone?
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
113.x: Cortisol from the adrenal cortex is the primary stress hormone (long-term stress response). Adrenaline is the quick 'fight or flight' hormone, so it is tempting; dopamine and serotonin are neurotransmitters.

113.s: Which of the following is not a type of a Salivary Gland?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
113.x: Parotid, submandibular and sublingual are the three salivary glands; the pineal gland is an endocrine gland in the brain (melatonin).

113.s: Which among the following is the largest organ of human body is
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
113.x: Skin is the largest organ of the human body (about 16% of body weight); the liver is the largest internal organ and gland.

113.s: The Average blood pressure of a human is
113.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
113.x: Normal adult blood pressure is about 120/80 mm Hg (systolic/diastolic).

113.s: What is the expected systolic - diastolic blood pressure in case of normal human beings in mm Hg?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
113.x: Normal blood pressure is 120 mm Hg systolic over 80 mm Hg diastolic; systolic is always the higher number and 140 is the hypertension mark.

113.s: Insulin Controls?
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
113.x: Insulin from the pancreas lowers blood sugar by moving glucose into cells; it does not control salts, reflexes or heart pumping.

113.s: What is the function of liver in human body?
o: All the given answers are correct
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
113.x: The liver does all three: it metabolises drugs, regulates the chemical levels of blood and secretes bile.

113.s: Which part of the brain is called as the 'thermostat' of the human body?
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
113.x: The hypothalamus is the body's thermostat, regulating temperature. Cerebellum controls balance, hippocampus memory and frontal lobe reasoning.

113.s: Which part of the human body useful for organ transplantation?
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
113.x: The kidney is the organ most often transplanted (living or deceased donor); nose, tail bone and brain are not transplanted.

113.s: What is the major organic substance present in human urine?
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Urea, made in the liver, is the major organic waste in urine; uric acid and ammonia are minor, and glucose appears only in diabetes.

113.s: The Adam's apple in human beings is formed due to the growth of which structure?
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: The Adam's apple is the thyroid cartilage of the larynx, which grows larger in boys at puberty; it is not the thyroid gland, trachea or pharynx.

113.s: Identify the gland that secretes insulin
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas, not by the liver, thyroid or pituitary.

113.s: Name the Blood Group Which is known as Universal Recipient?
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
113.x: AB group has no anti-A/anti-B antibodies, so it is the universal recipient (strictly AB positive); O is the universal donor.

113.s: High blood sugar level in body is an indication of:
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
113.x: Persistently high blood sugar is the sign of diabetes mellitus (low insulin or insulin resistance).

113.s: The liver stores food in the form of
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: The liver stores excess glucose as glycogen; starch is the plant store, albumin a blood protein, and glucose is converted before storage.

113.s: The excretory unit of kidney is
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: The nephron is the structural and functional (excretory) unit of the kidney; a neuron is the nerve cell.

113.s: The liver and skeletal muscle in the body mainly stores ____, which is used as a source of energy.
113.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
113.x: Liver and skeletal muscle store glucose as glycogen for energy; pepsinogen is an enzyme precursor and the others are not energy stores.

113.s: Which is the largest gland of the human body?
113.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
113.x: The liver is the largest gland of the body (~1.5 kg); the pancreas is the second largest, stomach and kidneys are not the largest glands.

113.s: What is the number of chromosomes in a normal human body cell?
113.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
113.x: Human somatic cells have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs (44 autosomes + XX or XY); 45 or 47 indicate disorders such as Turner or Down syndrome.

113.s: Which type of blood group is known as universal donor?
113.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
113.x: Group O red cells carry no A or B antigens, so O (strictly O negative) is the universal donor; AB is the universal recipient.

113.s: Which type of blood group is a universal recipient?
113.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
113.x: AB blood has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies, so AB is the universal recipient; O is the universal donor.

113.s: The cells of which organ in the human body are known as hepatocytes?
113.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
113.x: Hepatocytes are the main functional cells of the liver (Greek hepar = liver). Brain cells are neurons, heart cells cardiomyocytes.

113.s: When the kidneys in a human body fail to function which procedure is recommended by the doctors?
113.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
113.x: When kidneys fail, dialysis removes wastes and excess water from blood. Angiography images vessels; sigmoidoscopy and colonoscopy examine the bowel.

113.s: Which of the following hormones is secreted by "Beta cells" of pancreas.
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
113.x: Beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin; alpha cells secrete glucagon.

113.s: Which blood group is called universal donor?
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
113.x: Group O red cells carry no A or B antigen, so O (strictly O negative) is the universal donor; AB is the universal recipient.

113.s: The largest gland in human body is?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
113.x: The liver is the largest gland of the human body; the pancreas is second. The spleen is not a gland and the pituitary is pea-sized.

113.s: If Kidneys of a person are not working, he would undergo?
113.src: Technical Asst. (Hydrology), Laboratory Assistants in AP Gro
113.x: When the kidneys fail, blood is cleaned artificially by dialysis (haemodialysis or peritoneal). Radiolysis, pyrolysis and hydrolysis are chemical breakdown processes, not treatments.

113.s: Scientists have developed an artificial muscle to treat which of the body part?
113.x: Artificial muscles have been developed to help a failing heart pump (e.g. a soft robotic sleeve around the heart), so heart is keyed; the source news item behind this question was not traced.

113.s: Pace-maker is related to:
113.x: A pacemaker is a device that regulates the heartbeat (the heart's own pacemaker is the SA node), so it is related to the heart.

113.s: Which of the following human body organs behaves like the endocrine as well as exocrine glands?
113.src: APPSC 2019 Various non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
113.x: The pancreas is both endocrine (insulin from Islets of Langerhans) and exocrine (digestive enzymes). Liver, testis and pituitary are not described this way.

113.s: Which of the following glands in humans is located on the kidney?
113.x: The adrenal glands sit above the kidneys, so the adrenal gland is the one on the kidney. The pituitary, thyroid and hypothalamus are in the brain or neck.

113.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the functions of Glucagon?
o: Glucagon is essential for your health. It supports cell growth, immune function, fetal development and vision.
Glucagon triggers your liver to convert stored glucose (glycogen) into a usable form and then release it into your bloodstream. This process is called glycogenolysis.
Glucagon helps your body make glucose from other sources, such as amino acids.
Glucagon can also prevent your liver from taking in and storing glucose so that more glucose stays in your blood.
113.x: Glucagon raises blood glucose through glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis from amino acids, and reduced hepatic glucose uptake; the statement about cell growth, immunity, fetal development and vision describes vitamin A, not glucagon.

113.s: Which of the following glands in humans is located on the kidney?
113.x: The adrenal glands sit above the kidneys, so the adrenal gland is the one on the kidney. The pituitary, thyroid and hypothalamus are in the brain or neck.

113.s: Which gland in the human body continuously supplies tear fluid that is wiped across the surface of the eyes each time the eyelids are blinked?
113.x: The lacrimal gland secretes tear fluid that is spread over the eye by blinking. The thyroid, salivary and pituitary glands have no such role.

113.s: Which live-cut human organ has the ability to grow back to nearly 85 percent of its original capability within 2-3 weeks?
113.x: The liver is renowned for its regenerative capacity, restoring a large proportion of lost mass and function within a few weeks after partial removal.

113.s: Which hormone stimulates the thyroid gland to secrete thyroxine?
113.x: The hormonal output from the thyroid is regulated by thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) produced by the anterior pituitary.

113.s: Average blood pressure of a human is –
113.x: The normal average blood pressure of human is 120/80 mm Hg. This means that systolic pressure around 120mm Hg and diastolic pressure should be around 80 mm Hg.

113.s: The normal temperature of the human body is –
113.x: Normal human body temperature is about 37°C (98.6°F). 98°C is far too high; 367 K is about 94°C, not 37°C (310 K).

113.s: In a patient of Thalassemia, the body is unable to synthesise –
113.x: Thalassemia is a genetic blood disorder. In a patient of Thalassemia, the body is unable to synthesise enough haemoglobin, which causes severe anaemia.

113.s: The process by which blood is purified in human body is called :
113.x: Dialysis removes waste and excess water from the blood and replaces lost kidney function. Haemolysis is RBC breakdown and osmosis is water movement across a membrane.

113.s: Iodine containing hormone is –
113.x: Thyroxine (T4) and T3 from the thyroid contain iodine (T4 has four iodine atoms). Insulin, adrenaline and testosterone contain no iodine.

113.s: When kidneys fail to function, there is accumulation of–
o: Nitrogenous waste products in the blood
113.x: The kidneys remove urea and other nitrogenous wastes from the blood, so when they fail these wastes accumulate. Fats, proteins and sugar are not what builds up.

113.s:
A man having ‘A’ blood group met a serious road accident and the doctors advised for blood transfusion. The relatives were asked to donate blood, whose blood groups were found to be as follows :
(i) Wife – ‘O’
(ii) Brother – ‘AB’
(iii) Son – ‘A’
(iv) Daughter – ‘O’ Who among the above relations could donate blood to the injured man?
113.x: Blood group A individuals have the A antigen on the surface of their RBCs and blood serum containing IgM antibodies against the B antigen. Therefore, group A individual can receive blood only from individuals of groups A or O (with A being preferable) and can donate blood to individuals with type A or AB.

113.s: The dialyzer is used for the work of –
113.x: The treatment options for kidney failure are peritoneal dialysis (PD), hemodialysis and kidney transplant. A dialyzer is an artificial kidney designed to provide controllable transfer of solutes and water across a semipermeable membrane separating flowing blood and dialysate streams.

113.s: Which one of the following biotransformations provides maximum energy to the human body?
113.x: ATP → ADP + Pi releases the energy cells use (ATP is the energy currency). ADP → ATP stores energy rather than providing it.

113.s:
Consider the following statements :
Assertion (A) : During sleep, bright light is undesirable.
Reason (R) : In bright light, production of melatonin in the body is considerably increased. Select your answer using the codes given below.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not correct
113.x: Darkness raises melatonin and bright light suppresses it, so A is true (light disturbs sleep) but R is false.

113.s: Insulin is produced by :
113.x: Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the Islets of Langerhans in the pancreas, not by the pituitary, thyroid or adrenal glands.

113.s: The pituitary gland by virtue of its tropic hormones controls the secretion activity of other endocrine glands. Which one of the following endocrine gland can function independent of the pituitary gland ?
113.x: Parathyroid hormone is controlled by blood calcium, not by a pituitary tropic hormone, so the parathyroid works independently. Thyroid (TSH), adrenal cortex (ACTH) and gonads (FSH/LH) depend on the pituitary.

113.s: Which one of the following is a female sex-hormone?
113.x: Estrone is a weak postmenopausal estrogen and a minor female sex hormone. Estrogen (Oestrogen) is the actual female sex hormone.

113.s: The kidneys in human beings are a part of system for
113.x: In humans, kidneys are the main organ of the excretion system. Filtering the blood and removing unnecessary and waste products from the body is the basic function of kidney.

113.s: In human body, which one of the following hormones regulates blood calcium and phosphate ?
113.x: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) raises blood calcium and increases phosphate excretion, so it regulates both. Glucagon controls sugar; growth hormone and thyroxine do not mainly regulate calcium.

113.s: Where is urea separated from the blood?
113.x: The process, ultrafiltration occurs at the barrier between the blood and the filtrate in the renal capsule in the kidney. The kidneys remove urea and other toxic wastes from the blood, forming a dilute solution called urine in the process.

113.s: Which gland secretes the milk ejection hormone oxytocin?
113.x: Oxytocin is made in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary, so the pituitary is keyed. Thyroid, parathyroid and adrenal glands do not secrete it.

113.s: Which organ of the body is affected most on keeping fast for a long time ?
113.x:
Most books and keys: kidney. Strictly: the question is loose – prolonged fasting first drains liver glycogen and then muscle protein; the kidney is stressed by ketones and dehydration.
Most compilations key the kidney as the organ most affected by long fasting. The question is loose (see the dispute line), but kidney is the commonly taught answer.

113.s: If albumin is releasing with urine then the failure of which organ may occur?
113.x: In urine, there are about 91-96% water, about 2% unuseful salt ions, about 2.6% urea, about 0.3% creatinine and very small amount of uric acid and some other useless matter. The presence of albumin (a protein found in blood plasma) in it increases the chance of kidney failure.

113.s: Of the following which hormone is associated with ‘fight or flight’ concept ?
113.x: Adrenaline from the adrenal medulla prepares the body for 'fight or flight' – faster heartbeat, more blood to muscles. Insulin, estrogen and oxytocin have no such role.

113.s: Bright’s disease affects human body in the part –
113.x: Bright's disease is inflammation of the kidneys (nephritis) with albumin in the urine. It does not affect the spleen, heart or liver.

113.s: At the age of 20 years, the number of bones in human body is approximately-
113.x: An adult skeleton has 206 bones, so about 200 at age 20. A newborn has about 300, which is why that option tempts.

113.s: Production of which one of the following is a function of the liver?
113.x: The liver converts toxic ammonia into urea. Lipase comes from the pancreas, HCl from the stomach and mucus from many linings.

113.s: Which of the following is not correct regarding haemoglobin ?
o: It carries oxygen from lungs to cell.
It carries carbondioxide from tissues to lungs.
113.x:
Most books and keys: 'slightly acidic' is the wrong statement. Strictly: haemoglobin behaves as a weak acid (isoelectric pH ~6.8, so it is anionic at blood pH 7.4), so the statement is arguable; the other three are plainly true.
Haemoglobin is red and carries oxygen to the cells and some CO2 back to the lungs, so 'slightly acidic' is the statement keyed as not correct.

113.s: Which of the following is not connective tissue?
113.x: Connective tissues include bone, cartilage and blood. Skeletal muscle is muscular tissue, not connective tissue.

113.s: Muscles are connected to bones by connective tissue called as
113.x: Tendons connect muscle to bone. Ligaments connect bone to bone; neurons and adipose tissue do not join muscles to bones.

113.s: Where is the governing centre of reflex action located?
113.x: A reflex action is coordinated by the spinal cord, so the response occurs without waiting for the brain. The cerebrum handles voluntary action.

113.s: Which of the following part of blood carry out the function of body defence?
113.x: White blood cells such as neutrophils defend the body against infection. Red cells carry oxygen and platelets help clotting.

113.s: The Human skeleton consists of
113.x: An adult human skeleton has 206 bones. 200 is only an approximation, so 206 is the exact answer.

113.s: Which of these bones is not a part of the human ear?
113.x: The ear ossicles are the malleus, incus and stapes. The femur is the thigh bone in the leg, not part of the ear.

113.s: In a healthy person, rate of heart beat in one minute is
113.x: The normal resting heart rate of a healthy adult is about 72 beats per minute.

113.s: Which one of the following is an example of vestigial organ in man?
113.x: Ear muscles are vestigial in humans: they are reduced and functionless, though they are functional in other animals. Jaw, canine teeth and humerus are functional.

113.s: If father have blood group A and mother have blood group O, which one of following blood group may present in their son?
113.x: Mother O has genotype OO, and father A may be AO. The child can be A or O.

113.s: Which of the following roles is/are played by epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles and prostate in male reproductive system of human?
113.x: The epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles and prostate are accessory ducts and glands. They mature and carry sperms and provide fluid for motility.

113.s:
Read the following statements and select the correct option. Statement I Active immunity is developed when a person’s own cells produce antibodies in response to infection or vaccine. Statement II Injection of snake anti-venom against snake bite is an example of active immunisation.
Codes
o: Both statements I and II are correct.
Statement I is correct, but statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but statement II is correct.
Both statements I and II are incorrect.
113.x: Active immunity arises when the body's own cells make antibodies after infection or vaccination, so statement I is correct. Anti-venom gives ready-made antibodies, which is passive immunisation, so statement II is wrong.

113.s: Which one among the following is not correct about Down’s syndrome?
113.x: NCERT lists short stature, a furrowed tongue and mental retardation for Down's syndrome (trisomy 21), but not early ageing, so option 2 is the statement keyed as not correct.

113.s: In female, a small portion of oviduct in removed and cut end is ligated by surgical operation is called
113.x: Tubectomy is the surgical cutting and ligation of the fallopian tube (oviduct) in females. Vasectomy is the male procedure on the vas deferens.

113.s: Which one of the following is the special type of milk produced by a lactating mother, essential for the development of immune response of newborn body in human?
o: Breast milk produced after a month of childbirth
113.x: Colostrum is the first milk after childbirth. It is rich in antibodies and builds the newborn's immunity.

113.s: Which of the following natural substance contains iron (Fe) ?
113.x: Myoglobin is an iron-containing oxygen-storing protein in muscle. Chlorophyll contains magnesium, while collagen and carotene contain no iron.

113.s:
Oxygen transportation in a human body takes place through
I. Blood
II. Lungs
III. Tissue The correct sequence of transportation is
113.x: Oxygen enters the lungs first, is carried by the blood, and is then delivered to the tissues: lungs, blood, tissue.

113.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
I. Coronary artery supplies blood to heart muscles.
II. Pulmonary vein supplies blood to lungs.
III. Hepatic artery supplies blood to kidneys.
IV. Renal vein supplies blood to kidneys.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
113.x: Only the coronary artery statement is correct. The pulmonary vein carries blood from the lungs to the heart, the renal artery supplies the kidneys, and the hepatic artery supplies the liver.

113.s:
Absorption of water in the human body can be found in
I. renal tubule in kidney
II. hepatic cells in liver
III. large intestine
IV. pancreatic duct
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
113.x: Water is reabsorbed in the renal tubules and the large intestine. Hepatic cells and the pancreatic duct do not absorb water.

113.s:
With reference to the human body, consider the following statements.
I. The production of somatotropin goes up when a person exercises.
II. Men’s testes produces progesterone.
III. Women’s adrenal gland secrete testosterone.
IV. Stress causes the adrenals to release very less amount of cortisol than usual.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
113.x: Somatotropin (growth hormone) rises with exercise, the testes make small amounts of progesterone, and the female adrenal secretes some testosterone, so I, II and III are correct. Stress raises cortisol, so IV is wrong.

113.s: The amount of which of the following component in the air does not change in the process of respiration?
113.x: Respiration changes the O2 (21% to 16%) and CO2 (0.04% to 4%) content of air, while nitrogen is not used and stays unchanged.

113.s: Which one of the following statements regarding haemoglobin is correct?
o: Haemoglobin present in RBCs can carry only oxygen, but not carbon dioxide.
Haemoglobin of RBC can carry both oxygen and carbon dioxide.
Haemoglobin of RBCs can carry only carbon dioxide.
Haemoglobin is only used for blood clotting and not for carrying gases.
113.x: Haemoglobin in RBCs carries mainly oxygen, and also some carbon dioxide (as carbamino-haemoglobin). It is not for clotting.

113.s: Which of the following cell secrete insulin?
113.x: Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the pancreas; alpha cells secrete glucagon.

113.s: Which one of the following salts is found in maximum amount in the human bones?
113.x: Bones consist mainly of calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite), so it is the salt found in maximum amount.

113.s: A surge of which hormone stimulates ovulation in human females?
113.x: A mid-cycle surge of luteinizing hormone triggers ovulation.

113.s: Which of the following is the primary sex organ in females?
113.x: The ovary is the primary sex organ in females since it produces ova and hormones. The uterus, vagina and fallopian tube are accessory organs.

113.s: Which one of the following is not a component of human male reproductive system?
113.x: The cervix is part of the female reproductive system (the neck of the uterus). The urethra, seminal vesicle and vas deferens are in the male system.

113.s: By which combination of chromosome, a child will be male?
o: X from male and X from female
X from male and Y from female
Y from male and X from female
Y from male and Y from female
113.x: A male child is XY. The Y chromosome can only come from the father and the X from the mother.

113.s: Which among the following is the food tube?
113.x: The oesophagus is the food pipe carrying food from the pharynx to the stomach. The larynx is the voice box, the aorta is an artery and the thymus is a gland.

113.s: The yellow colour of human urine is due to a pigment called
113.x: Urine is yellow due to the pigment urochrome, formed from the breakdown of haemoglobin.

113.s: Corpus luteum is a mass of cells found in
113.x: The corpus luteum forms in the ovary from the ruptured follicle after ovulation and secretes progesterone.

113.s: With which of the physiological process, thrombin is associated?
113.x: Thrombin is the enzyme that converts fibrinogen into fibrin during blood clotting; it has no role in excretion, reproduction or growth.

113.s: Person having blood group B can donate the blood to person having group
113.x: Group B donates to B and AB. AB is the universal recipient, so B can donate to AB.

113.s: The oxygenated blood from the lungs in received by the
113.x: Oxygenated blood returns from the lungs through the pulmonary veins to the left auricle (atrium), then passes to the left ventricle.

113.s: Haemophilia is a genetic disorder which lead to
113.x: Haemophilia is an X-linked disorder in which a clotting factor is missing, so the blood does not clot. It does not lower haemoglobin or WBC count.

113.s: Which of the following is not a symptom of Wilson’s disease?
o: Problems with speech, swallowing or physical coordination.
Fluid build-up in the legs or abdomen
113.x: Wilson's disease is copper accumulation, causing neurological symptoms, liver problems and fluid build-up. Night blindness is caused by vitamin A deficiency, so it is not a symptom.

113.s: Which one of the following is an X-linked, recessive disorder caused by the deficiency of functional plasma clotting factor VIII (FVIII), which may be inherited or arise from spontaneous mutation?
113.x: Haemophilia A is the X-linked recessive disorder caused by a deficiency of clotting factor VIII. The others are blood cancers or a clotting disorder (thrombosis), not factor VIII deficiency.

113.s: Bile is stored in
113.x: Bile is made in the liver but stored and concentrated in the gall bladder, which is why 'liver' is the tempting wrong option.

113.s: In which organ of the human body are the lymphocytes cells formed?
113.x: Lymphocytes form from stem cells in the red bone marrow of (long) bones; the spleen and lymph nodes store and activate them but are not where they are formed.

113.s: Which chamber of human heart pumps fully oxygenated blood to the aorta and hence to the body?
113.x: The thick-walled left ventricle pumps fully oxygenated blood into the aorta for the whole body. The right ventricle sends deoxygenated blood to the lungs.

113.s: Between which one of the following sets of bloods, in the transfusion possible?
113.x: AB is the universal recipient, so A can donate to AB. A cannot donate to O, B cannot donate to A, and AB cannot donate to O.

113.s: Which one among the following is the correct pathway for the elimination of urine?
113.x: Urine is made in the kidneys, flows down the ureters to the bladder and leaves through the urethra.

113.s: Which one of following is smallest gland of body?
113.x: Of the listed glands the pea-sized pituitary is the smallest; the liver is the largest gland and the thyroid the largest endocrine gland.

113.s: Name the gland that controls the functioning of other endocrine glands
113.x: The pituitary is the master gland and controls other endocrine glands through hormones such as TSH and ACTH.

113.s: Which of the following gland is present between the lungs?
113.x: The thymus lies behind the sternum, between the lungs, and trains T cells. The pituitary and pineal glands are in the brain.

113.s: Which one of the following hormones do not contains peptide chain?
113.x: Cortisol is a steroid hormone from the adrenal gland, so it has no peptide chain. Oxytocin, corticotropin (ACTH) and insulin are peptide hormones.

113.s: Thyroid gland produces a hormone called ‘Thyroxine’ which
113.x: Thyroxine (T4) from the thyroid regulates the metabolic rate. Blood glucose is controlled by insulin, not thyroxine.

113.s: Cretinism is a human disorder which is due to the under secretin of
113.x: Cretinism in children results from under-secretion of thyroxine by the thyroid. Adrenaline and cortisone are adrenal hormones and glycogen is not a hormone.

113.s: Life saving hormone is
113.x: The adrenal gland is called the life-saving gland because adrenaline and cortisol help the body survive stress and emergencies.

113.s: Which of the following hormone is called emergency hormone?
113.x: Adrenaline from the adrenal gland is the emergency hormone, used in fight-or-flight situations.

113.s: Which of the following is not a gland?
113.x: Gastrin is a hormone secreted by the stomach lining, not a gland. Thyroid, liver (the largest gland) and pancreas are all glands.

113.s: Which of the following gland is responsible for the secretion of insulin?
113.x: Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the Islets of Langerhans in the pancreas, so pancreas is correct.

113.s: Insulin is secreted by
113.x: Insulin comes from the Islets of Langerhans (beta cells) of the pancreas, not the spleen, gonads or liver.

113.s: Which of the following control blood pressure?
113.x: The adrenal glands secrete adrenaline and cortisol, which regulate blood pressure; parathyroid, thyroid and thymus do not primarily do so.

113.s: Which of the following endocrine glands in human is not found in pair?
113.x: The pituitary is a single gland at the base of the brain, while the adrenals, testes and ovaries occur in pairs.

113.s: A man suffering from diabetes mellitus drinks water more frequently as he has to eliminate from the blood extra
113.x: In diabetes mellitus blood glucose is high and excess glucose is excreted in urine, carrying water with it, so the person drinks more water to eliminate glucose.

113.s: Which of the following elements is needed in the human body to transfer electrical signals by nerve cells?
113.x: Sodium ions (Na+), with potassium, create the ion movements across nerve cell membranes that carry electrical signals. Lithium, rubidium and caesium are not needed for this.

113.s: Which of the following are the properties of neurons?
113.x: Neurons are specialised for excitability (responding to stimuli) and conductivity (transmitting impulses). Elasticity and flexibility are not their properties.

113.s: The pH of human’s slightly basic blood is normally around
113.x:
Official key / most books: 7.5-8.0 (the only basic range offered). Strictly: normal blood pH is 7.35-7.45, about 7.4 (NextGen Rocket Chemistry p.21).
Human blood is slightly basic, about pH 7.4; the only basic range offered, 7.5-8.0, is keyed. Ranges below 7 would be acidic and 8.5-9.0 is far too basic.

113.s: In an human brain memory power is found in
113.x: The cerebrum is the seat of memory, thinking and intelligence. The medulla and cerebellum control involuntary functions and balance.

113.s: Tachycardia is a condition characterised by
113.x: Tachycardia means an abnormally fast heart rate (above normal), whereas a slow rate is bradycardia.

113.s: The brain is responsible for
113.x: The brain handles thinking (cerebrum), heartbeat regulation (medulla) and body balance (cerebellum), so all of the above is correct.

113.s: Which of the following is not a part of the brain?
113.x: The pinna is the external part of the ear, not of the brain. Medulla, thalamus and pons are brain parts.

113.s: Largest part of human brain is
113.x: The cerebrum is the largest part of the human brain, much larger than the cerebellum and medulla oblongata.

113.s: Smooth muscles are likely to be found in
113.x: Smooth (involuntary) muscle is found in the walls of internal organs like the stomach. Leg and arm muscles are skeletal, and the heart has cardiac muscle.

113.s: After reaching the female genital tract, human sperms retain their fertilizing capacity for
113.x: Human sperms remain viable and capable of fertilising in the female genital tract for about one to two days.

113.s: The main thinking part of the brain is
113.x: The forebrain (cerebrum) is the seat of thinking, intelligence and memory, whereas the midbrain and hindbrain handle reflexes and coordination.

113.s: Which of the following cells secrete androgen?
113.x: Leydig (interstitial) cells of the testes secrete androgens such as testosterone, while Sertoli cells nourish the developing sperms.

113.s:
Consider the following statements with reference to human body.
I. The common bile duct releases its contents in stomach.
II. The pancreatic duct releases its contents into duodenum.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
113.x: The common bile duct and the pancreatic duct both open into the duodenum, not the stomach, so only statement II is correct.

113.s: In human body, what is the number of cervical vertebrae?
113.x: The human neck has 7 cervical vertebrae, the same number as in most mammals.

113.s: In human digestive system, the process of digestion starts in
113.x: Digestion starts in the buccal cavity, where salivary amylase begins breaking down starch. Protein digestion starts in the stomach, which is the tempting wrong option.

113.s: Which of the following is a vestigial organ?
113.x: The appendix is a vestigial organ with no significant function in humans. The heart, kidney and lungs are vital functioning organs.

113.s: Which one of the following statements regarding muscle contraction and relaxation is correct?
o: It involves movement of Zn+ + ion.
It involves Ca + + ion of blood.
It involves release of Ca + + from sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) and pumping Ca + + back in SR.
It involves exchange of Na and K.
113.x: Muscle contraction is triggered by Ca2+ released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, and relaxation occurs when Ca2+ is pumped back into it. It does not depend on Ca2+ from the blood or on Zn.

113.s: Tooth enamel is made up of which one of the following calcium compounds?
113.x: Tooth enamel is mainly calcium phosphate in the form of hydroxyapatite, the hardest substance in the body.

113.s: The acid in gastric juice is
113.x: The gastric juice contains hydrochloric acid, secreted by the parietal (oxyntic) cells; it activates pepsinogen to pepsin.

113.s: The acid in gastric jucie is
113.x: The gastric juice contains hydrochloric acid, secreted by the parietal (oxyntic) cells; it activates pepsinogen to pepsin.

113.s: If the radius of blood vessels decrease, the blood pressure will
o: increase in male but decrease in female
113.x: Narrower vessels increase resistance to blood flow, so blood pressure rises.

113.s: When kidneys fail to function, there is accumulation of
o: nitrogenous waste products in the blood.
113.x: The kidneys filter urea and other nitrogenous wastes out of the blood, so when they fail these wastes accumulate in the blood. This is why dialysis is needed.

113.s: Which of the following is the first enzyme mixing with food in digestive region?
113.x: Food first meets salivary amylase in the mouth, which begins starch digestion. Pepsin acts in the stomach and trypsin in the intestine, so both come later.

113.s: Which among the following is not a connective tissue?
113.x: Blood, bone and cartilage are connective tissues. Skin is an organ made of epithelial and other tissues, not a connective tissue.

113.s: Which one of the following types of tissues will have contractile proteins?
113.x: Muscle tissue contains the contractile proteins actin and myosin, which produce contraction.

113.s: Buildup of which acid in our muscles during sudden activity causes cramps?
113.x: During sudden strenuous activity muscles respire anaerobically and lactic acid builds up, causing cramps.

113.s: Sweat contains water and ………
113.x: Sweat is mostly water with dissolved salts (NaCl) and a little urea. Its salt content makes it taste salty.

113.s: Neutrophils and lymphocytes originate from
113.x: All blood cells, including neutrophils and lymphocytes, originate from stem cells in the bone marrow. Lymph nodes and the spleen only store or mature lymphocytes.

113.s: What is the name of the vessel that delivers the nutrient rich blood from the stomach and small intestine to the liver?
113.x: The hepatic portal vein carries nutrient-rich blood from the stomach and small intestine to the liver. The hepatic veins carry blood away from the liver and the hepatic arteries bring it oxygenated blood.

113.s: Which part of the body is responsible for the manufacture of red blood cells?
113.x: Red blood cells are made in the red bone marrow. The lungs, heart and brain do not make blood cells.

113.s: Which one of the following carries out the function in human beings similar to the one with Malpighian tubules perform in cockroaches and other insects?
113.x: Malpighian tubules are the excretory organs of insects, and the kidneys do the same job in humans by filtering waste such as urea from the blood.

113.s: Cerebrum is related to
113.x: The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain and controls thinking, memory and voluntary action. It is not part of the liver, heart or arteries.

113.s: Cartilage is not found in
113.x: The larynx, nose and external ear have cartilage in their walls. The urinary bladder is a muscular organ with no cartilage.

113.s: Which one of the following is the correct sequence in the order of decreasing length of the structural parts given below of small intestine in the human body?
113.x: The ileum is the longest part of the small intestine (~3.5 m), then the jejunum (~2.5 m); the duodenum (~25 cm) is the shortest.

113.s: The complete digestion of carbohydrates, proteins and fats occurs in
113.x: Carbohydrates, proteins and fats are completely digested in the small intestine by pancreatic and intestinal enzymes with bile. The stomach only begins protein digestion.

113.s: In human body most of the digestive process, takes place in
113.x: Most digestion takes place in the small intestine, where pancreatic juice, bile and intestinal juice act. The stomach digests only part of the protein.

113.s: The acidic, semidigested food coming out of the stomach is neutralised by
113.x:
Most books / NCERT and the NDA key: bile juice. Strictly: pancreatic juice bicarbonate does most of the neutralising, bile helps (NCERT Biology Class 11 ch.16).
NCERT (Class 10) says the acidic food from the stomach is made alkaline by bile juice so pancreatic enzymes can act. Physiologically, the bicarbonate of pancreatic juice does most of the neutralising.

113.s: How many pairs of nerves arise from the human spinal cord?
113.x: 31 pairs of spinal nerves arise from the spinal cord (12 pairs of cranial nerves arise from the brain).

113.s: Which one of the following depicts the correct circuit of a reflex arc?
o: Effector → sensory neuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → receptor
Receptor → sensory neuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → effector
Receptor → sensory neuron → brain → motor neuron → effector
Sensory neuron → receptor → brain effector → motor neuron
113.x: A reflex arc runs receptor → sensory neuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → effector; the spinal cord, not the brain, handles the reflex.

113.s: White blood cells act
o: as a medium for oxygen transport from lung to tissues
113.x: White blood cells defend the body against infection. Platelets clot blood and red cells carry oxygen.

113.s: Which one of the following statements about blood elements is correct?
o: Red blood cells number is same as that of white blood cells and platelets.
The number of white blood cell is more then red blood cells.
The number of red blood cells is the highest.
The number of red blood cells is lower then platelets.
113.x: Red blood cells are the most numerous (~5 million/mm³), then platelets (~1.5–4 lakh/mm³), then WBC (~4,000–11,000/mm³).

113.s: Which cells in our body are popularly called “soldiers of the human body”?
113.x: White blood cells are popularly called the 'soldiers of the body' because they fight infection. Eosinophils and basophils are only kinds of WBC.

113.s: What is the effect of antigen in an ill person?
o: It increases the production of WBC.
It increases the production of antibodies.
It increases the production of anti-serum against bacteria.
It prevents the growth of bacteria.
113.x: An antigen stimulates the immune system to produce specific antibodies against it.

113.s: In the human body, cowper’s glands form a part of which one of the following?
113.x: Cowper's (bulbourethral) glands are accessory glands of the male reproductive system.

113.s: Which one of the following is not a function of liver?
o: Destruction of dead and worn-out red blood cells.
Absorption of food and excess water from the undigested food.
113.x: The liver stores glycogen, makes urea and breaks down worn-out RBCs; absorbing food and water from undigested food is the work of the intestines.

113.s: Which one of the following body parts/organs of the human body does not have smooth muscles?
113.x: The biceps is a skeletal (striated, voluntary) muscle. Ureters, iris and bronchi have smooth (involuntary) muscle.

113.s: In our body, antibodies are formed against pathogens in
113.x:
Most keys: thymus by lymphocytes. Strictly: antibodies are made by B lymphocytes / plasma cells, mainly in lymph nodes and spleen; the thymus matures T cells (NCERT Biology Class 12 ch.8).
Antibodies are made by lymphocytes, so the lymphocyte option is the only one right; strictly B lymphocytes (plasma cells) in lymph nodes/spleen make them, while the thymus trains T cells.

113.s: Who performs the task of capturing oxygen in the blood?
113.x: Haemoglobin in red blood cells binds (captures) oxygen. RBC carry it, but the oxygen-binding molecule is haemoglobin; chlorophyll is in plants.

113.s: Number of chromosome in a normal human body cell is
113.x: A normal human body cell has 46 chromosomes (23 pairs).

113.s: Which one of the following parts of the human brain is the regulating centre for swallowing and vomiting?
113.x: The medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions such as swallowing, vomiting, heartbeat and breathing. The cerebellum controls balance.

113.s:
Consider the following statements regarding human brain.
I. Brain is responsible for controlling heart beat.
II. It is also responsible for maintaining body balance.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
113.x: The brain controls the heartbeat (medulla) and body balance (cerebellum), so both statements are correct.

113.s:
Select the correct statements regarding the characteristics of acquired immunity.
I. Cell-mediated immunity is responsible for acquired immunity.
II. It produces a primary response of low intensity.
III. Active and passive immunity are types of acquired immunity.
IV.Polymorphonuclear leucocytes and natural killer cells are involved in acquired immunity.
Codes
113.x: Acquired immunity (cell-mediated and humoral) has a low-intensity primary response and comes as active or passive immunity. PMN leucocytes and NK cells belong to innate immunity, so IV is wrong.

113.s: Light enters the eye through a thin membrane called
113.x: Light enters the eye through the cornea, the thin transparent front membrane. The pupil is the opening in the iris behind it.

113.s: Light enters the eye through a thin membrane called
113.x: The cornea is the thin transparent membrane through which light enters the eye; the iris and pupil lie behind it.

113.s: The blood pressure of an individual is 140 mm Hg. In this statement, ‘Hg’ refers to
113.x: Hg is the chemical symbol of mercury; blood pressure is measured in mm of mercury (sphygmomanometer).

113.s: Energy is stored in liver and muscles in the form of
113.x: The liver and muscles store energy as glycogen (animal starch).

113.s:
Match List I (Endocrine Gland) with List II (Hormone) and select the correct answer using codes given below the lists.
List I
A. Gonads
B. Pituitary
C. Pancreas
D. Adrenal
List II
1. Insulin
2. Progesterone
3. Growth hormone
4. Cortisol
Codes A B C D A B C D
113.x: Gonads – progesterone, pituitary – growth hormone, pancreas – insulin, adrenal – cortisol, giving 2 3 1 4.

113.s: The blood pressure (systolic and diastolic) of a healthy man is
113.x: Normal adult blood pressure is about 120/80 mm Hg (systolic/diastolic).

113.s: A healthy human being excretes the following litres of urine in 24 hours.
113.x: A healthy adult passes about 1.5 litres of urine a day.

113.s: Body temperature is regulated by
113.x: The hypothalamus is the body's thermostat; it also holds the hunger, satiety and thirst centres.

113.s: Which one of the following pair is not correctly matched?
113.x: Cowper's gland belongs to the male reproductive system, not the intestine; the other pairs are correct.

113.s: The amount of light entering into eye can be controlled and regulated by ……… .
113.x:
Most keys (SSC CGL 2019, Cracku/Testbook): iris. NCERT Class 10 wording: 'the pupil regulates and controls the amount of light entering the eye'.
The iris, a muscular diaphragm, controls the size of the pupil and so regulates the light entering the eye. NCERT words it as 'the pupil regulates and controls the amount of light', so pupil appears in some keys.

113.s: Which of the following is not the normal function of the human kidney?
o: Regulation of water level in the blood
Regulation of sugar level in the blood
113.x: The kidney regulates water and salts, filters urea and secretes hormones (erythropoietin, renin); blood sugar is regulated by insulin and glucagon of the pancreas.

113.s:
With reference to the work of human kidney, consider the following statements.
1. After the waste is removed in the kidney, the clean blood is sent back through renal artery.
2. From Bowman’s capsule, the filtered liquid passes through tiny tubes where much of the glucose is reabsorbed and sent back to the blood in the renal vein.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
113.x: Statement 1 is wrong: cleaned blood leaves the kidney by the renal vein, not the renal artery. Statement 2 is right: glucose is reabsorbed in the tubules and returns to the blood.

113.s: The temperature of the human body
o: Neither decreases in winters nor increases in summers
113.x: Human body temperature stays about constant (~37 °C) in all seasons – humans are warm-blooded and the hypothalamus regulates it.

113.s: Which one of the following human organs is responsible for detoxification of alcohol?
113.x: The liver detoxifies alcohol (alcohol dehydrogenase) and other poisons.

113.s: When there is a decrease in the concentration of oxygen in the blood, the rate of breathing
113.x: Low blood oxygen (and high CO2) is sensed by chemoreceptors and the breathing rate increases.

113.s: The strongest muscle in human body is found in
113.x: The masseter of the jaw is the strongest muscle by force it can exert.

113.s:
Consider the following statements
I. Pituitary gland is situated in brain.
II. The effect of over secretion of hormone from pituitary gland is increase growth in length.
III. Growth hormone is secreted from pituitary gland.
Which of the above are true about pituitary gland?
113.x: The pituitary lies at the base of the brain, secretes growth hormone, and its over-secretion in childhood causes gigantism (excess growth in length). All three are true.

113.s: The number of bones in human skull is
113.x:
Most keys: 28 (22 skull bones + 6 ear ossicles). Strictly: the skull proper has 22 bones (Gray's Anatomy).
The skull has 22 bones; with the 6 ear ossicles it is counted as 28 (29 with the hyoid), which is the figure keyed among these options.

113.s:
Assertion (A) In human body, the liver has an important role in fat digestion.
Reason (R) Liver produces two important fat-digesting enzymes.
Codes
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
113.x: The liver helps fat digestion through bile, which emulsifies fats, so A is true. Bile has no enzymes, so R is false.

113.s: What is arthroplasty in surgery?
113.x: Arthroplasty is surgical repair or replacement of a joint, such as hip or knee replacement.

113.s: Which of the following is known as master gland in man?
113.x: The pituitary is called the master gland because its tropic hormones control other endocrine glands.

113.s: In humans, Where does fertilization occur?
113.x: Fertilisation occurs in the oviduct (fallopian tube), at the ampulla, not in the uterus.

113.s: BMD testing is done to diagnose
113.x: BMD (bone mineral density) testing, usually a DEXA scan, diagnoses osteoporosis.

113.s: The heart of human embryo starts beating?
o: In the first week of development
In the third week of its development
In the fourth week of its development
In the sixth week of its development
113.x:
Most keys: 4th week. Strictly: the first beats appear around day 21–22, the end of the 3rd week (embryology texts).
The embryonic heart begins to beat at about day 22, i.e. the start of the 4th week (NCERT: heart formed after one month).

113.s: In human beings, normally in which one of the following parts, does the sperm fertilize the ovum?
113.x: The sperm fertilises the ovum in the fallopian tube (ampulla).

113.s: A man, who does not know when to stop eating, is suffering from
113.x: Bulimia is uncontrolled binge eating (often with purging); anorexia nervosa is refusing to eat.

113.s: In human body, leg bone is
113.x: Long bones such as leg bones are hollow – a marrow cavity inside a hard shell.

113.s: The total volume of blood in a normal adult human being is
113.x: A normal adult has about 5–6 litres of blood (about 7% of body weight).

113.s:
Consider the following statements about haemoglobin
I. It carries oxygen in the blood.
II. It is iron-containing compound.
III. It provides a immunity against certain diseases.
IV. It imparts a red colour to the blood.
The correct statements out of these are
113.x: Haemoglobin carries oxygen, contains iron and gives blood its red colour; immunity comes from WBC, so III is wrong.

113.s: ‘Satiety’ and ‘thirst’ centres in humans are located in which of the following parts of the brains?
113.x: The satiety (hunger) and thirst centres lie in the hypothalamus.

113.s: What amongst the following is responsible for the formation of stone in the human kidney?
113.x: Most kidney stones are calcium oxalate.

113.s:
Which of these are typical signs of heart attack?
I. Nausea
II. Severe perspiration
III. Headache
IV. Severe chest pain
Select the correct answer from the given
Codes
113.x: Typical heart-attack signs are severe chest pain, sweating and nausea; headache is not a typical sign.

113.s: Insulin is a kind of
113.x: Insulin is a peptide hormone from the beta cells of the pancreas.

113.s: With reference to the blood in a normal person, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Compared to arteries, veins are less numerous and holdless of the body’s blood at any given time.
Blood cells constitute about 70% of the total volume of the blood.
White Blood Cells (WBC) are made by lymphnodes only.
The blood has more platelets then WBCs.
113.x: Blood has far more platelets (1.5–4 lakh/mm³) than WBC (4,000–11,000/mm³). Veins hold most of the blood (~70%), blood cells are ~45% of volume, and WBC are made in bone marrow as well as lymph nodes.

113.s: In medical terminology ‘Golden Hour’ is related with
113.x: In medicine the 'golden hour' is the first hour after a heart attack or major trauma, when treatment saves most lives.

113.s: The average blood flow through kidneys per minute is
113.x: Renal blood flow is about 1,100–1,200 mL per minute (about a fifth of cardiac output).

113.s: The amount of light entering into eye can be controlled and regulated by
113.x:
Most keys (SSC CGL 2019, Cracku/Testbook): iris. NCERT Class 10 wording: 'the pupil regulates and controls the amount of light entering the eye' (printed key here: pupil).
The iris controls the size of the pupil and so regulates the light entering the eye (the SSC key for this question). NCERT says the pupil 'regulates and controls the amount of light', which is why pupil appears in some keys.

113.s: Which of the following is the smallest bone in the human body?
113.x: The stapes (stirrup) of the middle ear is the smallest bone; malleus and incus are the other ossicles.

113.s: Mammals respire by
113.x: Mammals breathe by lungs; fish use gills, insects trachea, frogs also the skin.

113.s: Maximum nutritive element absorbed by blood from which part of alimentary canal?
113.x: Most digested nutrients are absorbed into the blood in the small intestine (villi).

113.s: The following bone is not found in man
o: None of these (all are human bones)
113.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (None of these (all are human bones)); it is added as option 5.
All four printed bones are human: humerus (upper arm), carpals (wrist), astragalus (= talus, ankle) and atlas (first neck vertebra), so none is 'not found in man'. The printed key 'astragalus' is wrong – astragalus is another name for the human talus.

113.s: The adult human skeleton consists of
113.x: An adult human skeleton has 206 bones (about 300 at birth).

113.s: A man of AB blood group needs a transfusion. Who among the following (wife-A, son-AB, friend-O, daughter-B) could donate blood to him?
o: a, b and d (Wife, son and daughter)
113.x: AB is the universal recipient: it can receive A, B, AB and O blood, so all four can donate.

113.s:
This question consist of two statements –
Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer the question selecting the appropriate option given below:
Assertion (A): Persons with blood group ‘AB’ are called ‘universal recipients’
Reason (R): Group ‘O’ blood can be donated to persons with any other blood group.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
Both A and R are false.
113.src: APPSC 2023 Screening test (Online Mode) to the post of Deput
113.x: AB persons are universal recipients (no anti-A/anti-B antibodies) and O blood can go to any group; but R speaks of donors and does not explain A.

113.s: What is the average weight of the lungs of a healthy man?
113.x: The two lungs of an adult man weigh roughly 0.9–1.3 kg together, so 0.91 kg is the only near option; 0.5, 2.5 and 10 kg are clearly off.

113.s: If a colour-blind man marries a normal-visioned woman whose parents also had normal vision, what proportion of their children is likely to be colour-blind?
113.x: Colour blindness is X-linked recessive. With a non-carrier normal mother, sons get her normal X and daughters become carriers, so 0% of the children are colour-blind.

113.s: Tooth decay occurs when pH of the mouth is?
113.x: Tooth decay starts when mouth pH falls below 5.5 – bacterial acids dissolve the enamel.

113.s:
