Which of the following is/are secreted by the gastric glands present in the wall of the
I. Hydrochloric Acid
II. Pepsin
III. Casein
113.src: APPSC 2022 Various Non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
113.x: Gastric glands secrete HCl (parietal cells) and pepsin (as pepsinogen) with mucus; casein is a milk protein, not a secretion.

113.s:
Which of the following is/are secreted by the gastric glands present in the wall of the stomach?
I. Hydrochloric Acid
II. Pepsin
III. Casein
113.src: APPSC 2022 Various Non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
113.x: Gastric glands secrete hydrochloric acid and pepsin (pepsinogen); casein is the protein of milk.

113.s: The complete conversion of glucose in the presence of oxygen into carbon dioxide and water with release of energy is called
113.x: Complete breakdown of glucose to CO2 and water with oxygen, releasing energy, is aerobic respiration; glycolysis is only the first step.

113.s: What is the angle of vision for a normal healthy individual?
113.x:
Most keys: 60°. Strictly: the human visual field is about 150° per eye and ~180° binocular; 60° is the nasal/superior limit of one eye (NCBI NBK220).
The keyed answer is 60°. The full horizontal visual field is much wider (~150° per eye, ~180° with both eyes), and about 60° is the nasal/upper limit of each eye's field.

113.s: The ‘Pace Maker’ is also knows as –
113.x: The SA (sinoatrial) node in the right atrium is the heart's natural pacemaker.

113.s: Haemophilia is a genetic disorder which leads to
113.x: Haemophilia is an X-linked defect of a clotting factor, so blood does not clot.

113.s: Haemophilia is a hereditary disease which affects as –
113.x: Haemophilia is a hereditary lack of a clotting factor – blood fails to clot.

113.s: If by an unknown accident the acid secreting cells of the stomach wall of an individual are damaged. Digestion of which one of the following biomolecule will be affected to a greater extent?
113.x: Acid-secreting (parietal) cells give the HCl that activates pepsin, so protein digestion is hit most; carbohydrate and fat digestion happen mainly in the mouth and small intestine.

113.s: In the buccal cavity of human being digestion of which one of the following get started?
113.x: Carbohydrate digestion starts in the mouth with salivary amylase (ptyalin).

113.s: After menopause, production of which of the following hormones does not take place in women ?
113.x: After menopause, ovulation stops, so the corpus luteum no longer forms and progesterone production stops; oestrogen falls but some is still made from adrenal androgens in fat tissue.

113.s: Which type of image of an object is formed by eye lens of the retina?
113.x: The eye lens forms a real, inverted image on the retina.

113.s: The blood pressure in our body is –
113.x: Blood pressure is the pressure above atmospheric that pushes blood through the vessels, so it is greater than atmospheric pressure.

113.s: Blood is a type of _________.
113.x: Blood is a fluid connective tissue (plasma matrix with cells).

113.s: In human eye, light rays get transformed into neural impulses at :
113.x: The retina's rods and cones turn light into nerve impulses.

113.s: What function does blood perform in the body?
113.x: Blood carries oxygen to all parts of the body (with nutrients, hormones and wastes).

113.s: Blood pressure of four person is given below : Mrs. (X) – 90/60 Mr. (X) – 160/120 Mr. (Y) – 120/80 Mrs. (Y) – 140/100 Whose blood/pressure is normal in the following :
113.x: 120/80 mm Hg is normal, i.e. Mr. (Y); 90/60 is low, and 140/100 and 160/120 are high.

113.s: The fingerprints of Siamese (conjoined) twins are
113.x: Fingerprints are not identical even in identical or conjoined twins – they form from random pressures in the womb.

113.s: Which of the following is the largest part of the human brain?
113.x: The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain.

113.s: What is the pH level of blood of a normal person?
113.x: Normal blood pH is 7.35–7.45 (slightly alkaline).

113.s: The image formed on Retina is :
113.x: The retina image is real, inverted and smaller than the object.

113.s: The element that maintains balance between acidity and alkalinity in our body is
113.x: The keyed answer is phosphorus – phosphates form one of the body's acid-base buffers (with bicarbonate and proteins). Sodium and potassium also help, so books differ.

113.s:
Assertion (A) : Drinking of whiskey increases the frequency of urination.
Reason (R) : Alcohol intake speeds up the secretion of vasopressin in the body.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
113.x: Alcohol increases urination because it suppresses vasopressin (ADH), so A is true and R (speeds up vasopressin) is false.

113.s:
Assertion (A) : The person with diabetes insipidus feels thirsty.
Reason (R) : A person with diabetes insipidus suffers from excess secretion of vasopressin.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
113.x: Diabetes insipidus brings thirst from heavy urination, so A is true; it is due to a deficiency, not excess, of vasopressin, so R is false.

113.s: The disease with high levels of uric acid in the blood is characteristic of
113.x: High blood uric acid deposits urate crystals in joints – gout.

113.s:
Given below are two statements :
Assertion (A) : Human body is incapable of digesting cellulose.
Reason (R) : Starch degrading enzyme, diastase, is found in human body.
Choose the correct answer from the code given below:
Codes :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct
113.x: Humans lack cellulase, so cellulose is not digested (A true); salivary amylase (diastase) exists (R true) but does not explain A.

113.s: The bones are held together by elastic tissues are called–
113.x: Ligaments are the elastic connective tissues that join bone to bone; tendons join muscle to bone.

113.s: In human system, insulin controls the metabolism of :
113.x: Insulin mainly controls carbohydrate (glucose) metabolism – it lowers blood sugar.

113.s: Arteries supplying blood to the heart are called
113.x: Coronary arteries supply blood to the heart muscle.

113.s: Detoxification is
113.x: Unkeyed: 'detoxification' (removing a toxic substance under supervision) is the first stage of treating both drug and alcohol dependence, so options 1 and 2 are equally right and no official key was found.

113.s: A person affected by phenylketonuria disease suffers form :
113.x: Phenylketonuria (no phenylalanine hydroxylase) lets phenylalanine build up and causes mental retardation if untreated.

113.s: Which of the following is the basal part of diencephalon, forebrain?
113.x: The hypothalamus is the basal (floor) part of the diencephalon of the forebrain; the pons is in the hindbrain.

113.s: Instrument used for preparation of histopathological sections is
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: A microtome cuts the thin sections for histopathology; a microscope only views them.

113.s: Which among the following is not used for brain scanning?
113.x: The skull blocks most ultrasound, so routine brain scanning uses EEG, MEG, MRI or CT, not ultrasound.

113.s: What is not true with CT Scan?
113.x: A CT scan is painless; it combines many X-ray images into 3-D cross-sections that show normal and abnormal structures.

113.s: Which waves are used in sonography?
113.x: Sonography uses ultrasonic waves (above 20 kHz).

113.s: Which of the following rays/waves are used to know the growth of fetus in the womb?
113.x: Ultrasound tracks foetal growth – it uses no ionising radiation; X-rays would harm the foetus.

113.s: Which of the following was invented by Wilhelm Rontgen?
113.x: Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays (1895), the basis of the X-ray machine.

113.s: MRI is a diagnostic tool, which means –
113.x: MRI = Magnetic Resonance Imaging.

113.s: CT Scan is done by using –
113.x: CT scans use X-rays.

113.s: Amniocentesis is a method used to determine the :
o: Sequence of amino acids in protein
113.x: Amniocentesis tests the amniotic fluid for chromosomal disorders and can show the foetal sex (its misuse for sex determination is banned under the PCPNDT Act).

113.s: To diagnose the medical conditions, MRI technique is used. Which is not used in MRI?
113.x:
Keys usually: X-ray. Strictly: gamma rays are not used in MRI either; only magnetic field and radio waves are.
MRI uses a strong magnetic field and radio waves, not X-rays (that is CT); gamma rays are not used either, but X-ray is the contrast usually asked. The printed key 'radio wave' is wrong – radio waves are used.

113.s: Which one of the following statements regarding electrocardiogram is correct?
o: Electrocardiogram is graphical representation of electrical activity of cornea
Electrocardiogram is graphical representation of activity of kidney.
Electrocardiogram is graphical representation of activity of brain.
Electrocardiogram is graphical representation of electrical activity of heart.
113.x: An ECG records the electrical activity of the heart.

113.s: What is 'Bariatric Surgery'?
o: A kind of heart bypass surgery
113.x: Bariatric surgery is weight-loss surgery such as gastric (stomach) bypass.

113.s: C.T. in C.T. scan stands for
113.x: CT = Computerised (Computed) Tomography.

113.s:
This question consist of two statements –
Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer the question selecting the appropriate option given below:
Assertion (A): Laparoscopy allows a surgeon to use only small cuts and a camera for procedures inside the tummy or pelvis.
Reason (R): A laparoscopy is done under general anaesthetic condition.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
Both A and R are false.
113.src: APPSC 2023 Screening test (Online Mode) to the post of Deput
113.x: Laparoscopy is keyhole surgery with small cuts and a camera (A true), usually under general anaesthesia (R true), but the anaesthesia does not explain the small cuts.

113.s: Recently developed technique for monitoring foetal growth is :
113.x: Ultrasonics (sonography) is the technique for monitoring foetal growth.

113.s: An endoscope is a –
113.x:
Most keys: a narrow telescope. Some keys: none of these (it is an optical-fibre medical instrument, not strictly a telescope or camera).
An endoscope is a thin tube with optical fibres, light and lens/camera – a narrow 'telescope' to look inside the body. It is not a microscope.

113.s: A biotechnique in which ultrasonic sound is used :
113.x: Sonography uses ultrasonic sound; ECG and EEG record electrical activity and X-ray uses radiation.

113.s: Which of the following types is used by Computed Tomography employed for visualisation of the internal structure of human body ?
113.x: Computed tomography uses X-rays.

113.s: What is lithotripsy?
o: Breaking of kidney stone through rays
113.x: Lithotripsy breaks kidney stones with focused shock waves (the option's 'rays').

113.s: What is Jarvik-7?
113.x: Jarvik-7 was the first permanent artificial heart (Robert Jarvik, 1982).

113.s: An ECG test is conducted:
o: to measure electrical signals of our brain.
to measure retina power by electrical impulse.
to measure electrical signals of our heart.
113.src: APPSC Deputy Inspector of Survey, Technical Assistant in AP
113.x: An ECG (electrocardiogram) records the electrical activity of the heart. Brain signals are recorded by EEG and muscle activity by EMG.

113.s: What is tissue?
113.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
113.x: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform a particular function (e.g. muscle, nervous, blood tissue).

113.s: ____ is a special fluid connective tissue consisting of a fluid matrix, plasma, and formed elements.
113.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
113.x: Blood is the fluid connective tissue: plasma (fluid matrix) with formed elements (RBCs, WBCs, platelets). Serum is plasma without clotting factors, and bone is a solid connective tissue.

113.s: Which of the following procedures can be used to identify Down's Syndrome ?
113.src: Social Structure, Issues and Public Policies 2016
113.x: Amniocentesis tests foetal cells from amniotic fluid for chromosome number, so it detects the extra chromosome 21 of Down's syndrome. Ultrasound or a sonogram only shows markers, and MRI is not a chromosomal test.

113.s: Radar is used for :
o: Detecting objects by using light waves
Reflecting sound waves to detect objects
Determining the presence and location of objects with
113.x: RADAR (Radio Detection and Ranging) uses radio waves to detect the presence, range and direction of objects. Sound waves are used in SONAR and light in LIDAR.

113.s: SONAR is mostly used by–
113.x: SONAR uses ultrasonic waves under water to find depth, submarines and shoals; it is used mainly by navigators (ships, navies). Doctors use ultrasound scanning, not SONAR.

113.s: Which one of the following is a true fish as per the biological system of classification ?
113.x: The flying fish is a true fish (class Pisces) with gills and fins. Silverfish is an insect, jellyfish is a cnidarian and cuttlefish is a mollusc.

113.s: Which one of the following has a bilateral symmetry in its body organisation ?
113.x: Nereis (an annelid) is bilaterally symmetrical. Asterias and Echinus are echinoderms with radial symmetry as adults, and sea anemone is radially symmetrical.

113.s: Adamsia (sea anemone), Pennatula (sea pen), etc are examples of which Phylum?
113.x: Sea anemones (Adamsia) and sea pens (Pennatula) are cnidarians, formerly called Coelenterata, with a hollow gut cavity and tentacles.

113.s:
Assertion (A) Asexual reproduction required only female animals.
Reason (R) Male animals are not capable for asexual reproduction.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
113.x: Asexual reproduction does not need gametes, and it can occur in either sex, e.g. budding and fragmentation. Both the assertion and the reason are false.

113.s: In which of the following animals hooves are not found ?
113.x: Hooves are found in ungulates such as deer, zebra and horse. The jackal is a carnivore with claws and paws, so it has no hooves.

113.s: Which of the following is the smallest bird in the world ?
113.x: The bee hummingbird of Cuba is the smallest bird in the world, about 5-6 cm long.

113.s: Only male frog produce croacking sound because
o: female frog larynx but no vocal cord.
male frog have three pair of vocal cord.
male frog can magnify their voice with the help of sound box.
113.x: Male frogs have vocal sacs that act as resonating sound boxes that amplify the croak. Females lack these, though they do have a larynx.

113.s: In prokaryotic organisms, nuclear region is not surrounded by a membrane. This undefined nuclear region is known as
113.x: In prokaryotes the nuclear region without a membrane is the nucleoid. The nucleolus and nucleosome are structures in eukaryotic nuclei.

113.s: Sycon (Scypha), Spongilla (Fresh water sponge) and Euspongia (Bath sponge) are example of which Phylum?
113.x: Sycon, Spongilla and Euspongia are sponges, which belong to Phylum Porifera.

113.s: The scientific name of peacock is
113.x: The Indian peafowl (peacock) is Pavo cristatus. The other names refer to other birds.

113.s: What is the name of a group of similar cells performing a specific function?
113.x: A group of similar cells performing a specific function is called a tissue; organs are made of several tissues.

113.s: Genes are made up of
113.x: Genes are segments of DNA, which is a nucleic acid.

113.s: Which of the following is not a connective tissue?
113.x: Cardiac muscle is a muscular tissue. Adipose, bone and areolar tissues are connective tissues.

113.s: If cells are kept in some solution and the net result is that the cell swells up, then the solution is ………
113.x: In a hypotonic solution (lower solute concentration outside), water enters the cell by osmosis and the cell swells; in a hypertonic solution it shrinks.

113.s: A substance which is more than 80% in the cell is
113.x: Water is the most abundant component of the cell, making up more than 80% of it; protein, fat and minerals form much smaller fractions.

113.s: In cataract which part of the eye is affected?
113.src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
113.x: Cataract is clouding of the eye lens; the cornea, retina and iris are not affected.

113.s: Which of the following sound frequency cannot be heard by a normal human ear?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
113.x: The human ear hears about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz, so 30,000 Hz is ultrasonic and inaudible.

113.s: In eye donation, which part of the eye of the donor is utilized?
113.x: In eye donation the donor's cornea is used for corneal transplant (keratoplasty). Lens, retina and iris are not transplanted.

113.s: Which one among the following is blind (extremely poor eyesight)?
113.x:
Most books and keys: Bat. Strictly no bat is blind – all bats see, and fruit bats see well; they rely on echolocation (bats.org.uk / Britannica 'bat').
Of the options the bat is the one popularly called 'blind' (it navigates by echolocation); echidnas, flying squirrels and lorises rely on sight more.

113.s: Binary fission is a mode of
113.x: Binary fission – one cell dividing into two (Amoeba, bacteria) – is asexual reproduction.

113.s: Mendel’s principles of inheritance are based on
113.x: Mendel's laws come from cross-pollinating (sexually reproducing) pea plants – the segregation of factors happens through gametes.

113.s: What is the bond between two amino acids in a protein called ?
113.x: Amino acids in a protein are joined by peptide bonds. Glycosidic bonds join sugars and phosphodiester bonds join nucleotides.

113.s: Which of the following is not unicellular ?
113.x: Hydra is a multicellular cnidarian; Euglena, Amoeba and Paramecium are unicellular protists.

113.s: The site of cellular respiration in animal cell is
113.x: Cellular (aerobic) respiration happens in the mitochondria, the 'powerhouse' of the cell. Ribosomes make proteins and lysosomes digest.

113.s: Which of the following is not a mammal?
113.x: Fishes are cold-blooded with gills and scales; bats, whales and man are mammals.

113.s: Which one of the following contains powerful oxidative enzyme and helps in removing toxic substances from cells?
113.x: Peroxisomes hold oxidative enzymes such as catalase and remove toxic H2O2 and other substances. Lysosomes hold hydrolytic enzymes.

113.s: Statement I Two ATP molecules are produced during anaerobic respiration. Statement II Glucose is converted into pyruvic acid through a series of reaction with a net gain of 2 ATP molecules.
o: Both the statements are individually true and the statement II is the correct explanation of the statement I.
Both the statements are individually true, but the statement II is not correct explanation of the statement I.
The statement I is true, but the statement II is false.
The statement I is false, but the statement II is true.
113.x: In anaerobic respiration only glycolysis yields energy: glucose → pyruvic acid with a net gain of 2 ATP, which explains statement I.

113.s: The generic name of tusk shell or elephant tusk shell is
113.x: Tusk (elephant tusk) shells are the scaphopod molluscs of genus Dentalium. Chiton is a polyplacophoran.

113.s: Which of the following is monogamous?
113.x: Wolves are the classic monogamous mammals (a breeding pair for life); walruses, seals and deer are polygynous.

113.s: Crabs belongs to the Phylum
113.x: Crabs have jointed legs and an exoskeleton – phylum Arthropoda (class Crustacea).

113.s:
Consider the following statements.
I. Frogs can breathe by lungs as well as skin.
II. Gills are present in certain stages of life span of frogs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
113.x: Adult frogs breathe through lungs and moist skin, and tadpoles breathe through gills – both statements are correct.

113.s: Snails belong to Phylum
113.x: Snails have a soft body inside a shell – phylum Mollusca.

113.s: In the context of genetic disorder, consider the following. A women suffer from colour blindness, while her husband does not suffer from it. They have a son and a daughter. In this context, which one of the following statement is most probably correct?
o: Both children suffer from colour blindness.
Daughter suffer from colour blindness while son does not suffer from it.
Both children do not suffer from colour blindness.
Son suffers from colour blindness, while daughter does not suffer from it.
113.x: Colour blindness is X-linked recessive: a colour-blind mother gives her X to every son (affected); daughters also get the father's normal X and are carriers.

113.s: Who among the following first discovered cell?
113.x: Robert Hooke first saw and named cells (cork, 1665). Leeuwenhoek saw living cells, Robert Brown the nucleus, Virchow said cells come from cells.

113.s: Which of the following is warm blooded animal ?
113.x: Bats are mammals and warm-blooded; sharks, snakes and lizards are cold-blooded.

113.s: In terms of the evolution of organisms, which one among the following is the most avanced?
113.x: Mammals are the most advanced vertebrate class, so the bat (mammal) ranks above birds (pigeon, vulture) and fish (shark).

113.s:
Match the following List I
List II
A. Birds
B. Inheritance
C. Environment
D. Fossil
1. Palaeobiology
2. Ecology
3. Ornithology
4. Genetics
Codes A B C D A B C D
113.x: Birds – ornithology (3); inheritance – genetics (4); environment – ecology (2); fossils – palaeobiology (1): 3-4-2-1.

113.s: The wing of a bat and the wing of a bird are the examples of .............. limbs.
113.x:
Most books and keys: analogous (same function, flight). Strictly, as forelimbs bat and bird wings are homologous; only as wings are they analogous (NCERT XII Evolution).
As organs of flight, bat and bird wings are analogous (same function, flight evolved separately). As forelimbs with the same bone plan they are homologous.

113.s: Which among the following has segmented body ?
113.x:
Most books and keys: Annelida. Strictly Arthropoda also have segmented bodies (NCERT IX Diversity: arthropod 'body is segmented').
Annelida are the metamerically segmented worms (earthworm, leech) – the textbook answer. Arthropod bodies are also segmented, but the phylum is defined by jointed legs; molluscs and coelenterates are unsegmented.

113.s: ………being a higher category, is the assemblage of families which exhibit a few similar characters.
113.x: An order is the assemblage of families with a few similar characters (above family, below class).

113.s: Which of the following is the correct sequence of levels of hierarchy of classification of organisms from higher to lower ?
113.x: Hierarchy from higher to lower: Phylum – Class – Order – Family – Genus.

113.s: The term ‘Meiosis’ was coined by
113.x: The term meiosis was coined by J.B. Farmer and J.E.S. Moore (1905).

113.s: Which statement is incorrect for animals belonging to class of Chondrichthyes ?
o: Notochord is persistent only at larval stage, after that it disappears.
113.x: In Chondrichthyes (sharks, rays) the notochord persists throughout life; they have placoid scales, a cartilaginous skeleton and no air bladder – so (d) is the incorrect statement.

113.s: Magnification is
o: observed size of specimen actual size.
113.x: Magnification = observed (image) size ÷ actual size of the specimen.

113.s: On what basis Greek thinker Aristotle classified the animals for the first time ?
113.x: Aristotle, the first to classify animals, grouped them by habitat – land, water and air (NCERT).

113.s: Where does Amoeba digests its food ?
113.x: Amoeba engulfs food with pseudopodia and digests it inside a food vacuole. The nucleus and cell membrane do not digest food.

113.s: Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER) looks rough under the microscope because of the attachment of which one of following cell organelles to its surface?
113.x: RER is studded with ribosomes, which make proteins; smooth ER lacks them. Centrioles, plastids and lysosomes are not attached to the ER.

113.s: Which one of the following pairs of animals is warm blooded ?
113.x: Birds (peacock) and mammals (camel) are warm-blooded. Each other pair contains a cold-blooded reptile or fish (crocodile, tortoise, hagfish, dogfish).

113.s: In artificial insemination process, which of the following is/are introduced into the uterus of the female?
113.x: In artificial insemination only semen from a selected male is introduced; fertilisation happens in the female. Placing a fertilised egg is embryo transfer after IVF.

113.s: Crossing over occurs during meiosis at
113.x: Crossing over between non-sister chromatids happens at pachytene of prophase I. Chiasmata become visible at diplotene; leptotene and diakinesis are other stages.

113.s: What is the definition for the term ‘hibernation’ ?
o: A state of hyperactivity in spring time among birds.
Building of habitat (nests) by birds to save themselves in rainy season.
A state of reduced metabolic activity during winter season among some animals.
A habit of food conservation during summer season for winter among animals.
113.x: Hibernation is a state of reduced metabolic activity during winter (bears, frogs). Summer dormancy is aestivation.

113.s:
Consider the following cell organelles of the organisms.
I. Mitochondria
II. Chloroplasts
III. Endoplasmic Reticulum
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are semi-autonomous organelle(s)?
113.x: Mitochondria and chloroplasts have their own DNA and ribosomes, so they are semi-autonomous. The endoplasmic reticulum has no genome.

113.s:
Which of the following is an example of unicellular organism ? I. Euglena
II. Amoeba III. Paramecium
113.x: Euglena, Amoeba and Paramecium are all single-celled protists, so all three are correct.

113.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct ?
I. Viruses lack enzymes necessary for the generation of energy.
II. Viruses can be cultured in any synthetic medium.
III. Viruses are transmitted from one organism to another by biological vectors only.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
113.x: Viruses have no enzymes of their own for energy metabolism (I). They cannot be grown in synthetic media, only in living cells, and spread by many routes, not only vectors.

113.s:
Which of the following statements about DNA is/are correct?
I. DNA is the hereditary material of all living organisms.
II. All segments of DNA code for synthesis of proteins.
III. Nuclear DNA is double helical with two nucleotide chains which run anti-parallel.
IV. DNA is also found in mitochondria.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
113.x: Statements I, III and IV are correct (key c). Large parts of DNA are non-coding, so II is false.

113.s: Which one of the following functions is not carried out by smooth endoplasmic reticulum?
113.x: Smooth ER synthesises lipids and steroid hormones and transports materials, but protein synthesis occurs on ribosomes of rough ER.

113.s: Darwin’s theory of natural selection is based on
113.x: Darwin's theory of natural selection includes overproduction, struggle for existence, variation and survival of the fittest, so all of these are correct.

113.s: Jellyfish are an example of which type of phylum ?
113.x: Jellyfish belong to phylum Cnidaria (coelenterates), which have stinging cells.

113.s: Wall lizard creep over the vertical wall and ceiling with the help of
o: adhesive pad found on their digits.
ventral side of body is adhesive.
113.x: Wall lizards (geckos) have adhesive pads on their digits that let them cling to vertical walls and ceilings.

113.s: Among the following respiration is which type of process ?
113.x: Respiration oxidises glucose and releases energy as heat and ATP, so it is an exothermic process.

113.s: The full form of SONAR is
113.x: SONAR stands for Sound Navigation And Ranging. It uses ultrasound echoes to detect and locate objects underwater.

113.s: Barr body is absent in somatic cell of
113.x: A Barr body is an inactivated X chromosome. Turner syndrome (XO) has only one X, so it has no Barr body.

113.s: For which one of the following snakes the diet is mainly composed of other snakes ?
113.x: The king cobra is ophiophagous, feeding mainly on other snakes.

113.s: The snake who make their nest
113.x: The king cobra is the only snake that builds a nest for its eggs.

113.s: Which one of the following groups of cellular organelles contains DNA?
113.x: Mitochondria, chloroplasts and the nucleus contain DNA. Golgi bodies, plasma membrane and ribosomes do not.

113.s: Generally insects respire through
113.x: Insects breathe through tracheae that open to the outside by pores called spiracles.

113.s: Which one of the following statements about proteins in mammalian cells is corrects?
o: Proteins in mammalian cells are synthesised in cell membrane.
Proteins in mammalian cells are not synthesised in cell membrane but directly absorbed from food.
Proteins in mammalian cells are synthesised in rough endoplasmic reticulum.
Proteins in mammalian cells are synthesised in Golgi apparatus.
113.x: Proteins are synthesised by ribosomes on the rough endoplasmic reticulum, not in the cell membrane or Golgi, and they are not absorbed directly from food.

113.s: Which one of the following organelle is not found in prokaryotic cells?
113.x: Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria, but have a cell wall, plasma membrane and ribosomes.

113.s: A plant cell differ from animal in having
113.x: Every plant cell has a cellulose cell wall, which animal cells lack, so the cell wall is the safest answer. Chloroplasts are also plant-only but are absent from roots and other non-green cells, and cell membrane and nucleus occur in both.

113.s: Which one of the following cell organelles does not possess nucleic acid?
113.x: The plasma membrane is made of lipids and proteins and has no nucleic acid; the nucleolus, chloroplast and ribosome contain RNA or DNA.

113.s: Which one of the following is considered as a cell within a cell?
113.x: Chloroplasts have their own DNA and ribosomes and divide independently, so they are called a cell within a cell (the same is said of mitochondria, which are not offered). Ribosomes, lysosomes and Golgi bodies have no DNA of their own.

113.s: In a living cell, what is the site of ribosome formation?
113.x: The nucleolus is the site where ribosomal RNA is made and ribosomes are assembled; the Golgi bodies, ER and plasma membrane do not form ribosomes.

113.s: Which of the following is not a multicellular organism ?
113.x: Paramecium is a unicellular protozoan; fungi (mostly), Spirogyra and Hydra are multicellular.

113.s: The grasshopper’s ears are located at his ………
113.x: A grasshopper's hearing organs (tympana) are on the sides of the first abdominal segment, i.e. the abdomen, which the options call 'stomach'. Crickets and katydids have them on the front legs, not grasshoppers.

113.s: Which is the oldest organism on earth
113.x: Blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) are among the earliest life forms, appearing about 3.5 billion years ago.

113.s:
Match the following list of animals with their level of organisation ? Level of Animal Organisation
A. Organ level
B. Cellular
C. Tissue level
D. Organ system
1. Pheretima
2. Fasciola aggregate level
3. Spongilla
4. Obelia level
Codes A B C D A B C D
113.x: Fasciola is at organ level, Spongilla at cellular level, Obelia at tissue level and Pheretima at organ-system level, giving the code 2 3 4 1.

113.s: The scientific study of a cell is called
113.x: Cytology is the scientific study of cells. Histology studies tissues and taxonomy deals with classification.

113.s: Which of the following creature is oviparous ?
113.x: A frog lays eggs, so it is oviparous. Rabbit, mouse and squirrel are mammals that give birth to young.

113.s: Which of the following is not vertebrate?
113.x: A snail is a mollusc, an invertebrate with no backbone. Mammals, fish and birds are vertebrates.

113.s: Which of the following animal has three chambered heart?
113.x: Amphibians such as salamanders have a three-chambered heart. Scoliodon (fish) has two chambers, while pigeon and human have four.

113.s: Panthera pardus is the scientific name of
113.x: Panthera pardus is the leopard; the tiger is Panthera tigris and the lion is Panthera leo. Panther is a general term for leopards/black panthers.

113.s: Which one of the following animals is cold blooded ?
113.x: Shark is a fish and therefore cold-blooded (poikilothermic), whereas dolphins, whales and porpoises are mammals and warm-blooded.

113.s: Which of the following processes makes direct use of oxygen?
113.x: Oxygen is directly used as the final electron acceptor in the electron transport chain; glycolysis and fermentation are anaerobic, and the citric acid cycle uses oxygen only indirectly.

113.s: What is the ultimate product of Glycolysis?
113.x: Glycolysis breaks down glucose into two molecules of pyruvic acid (pyruvate). Ethanol and CO2 form only afterwards in fermentation.

113.s: Which one of the following cell organelles is known as ‘suicidal bags’ of a cell?
113.x: Lysosomes are called 'suicidal bags' because their hydrolytic enzymes can digest the cell itself when the cell is damaged or dies.

113.s: Amoeba belongs to which of the following kingdom?
113.x: Amoeba is a unicellular eukaryote, so it belongs to Kingdom Protista, not Monera, which holds prokaryotes.

113.s: Which one of the following organelles of mammalian cell is rich in hydrolytic enzymes?
113.x: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic (digestive) enzymes that break down macromolecules and worn-out cell parts.

113.s: Which one of the following is wrong for fungi ?
o: All fungi possess a purely cellulosic cell wall.
They are both unicellular and multicellular.
113.x: Fungal cell walls are made mainly of chitin, not purely cellulose, so the statement that all fungi have a purely cellulosic wall is wrong.

113.s: Which one of the following cell organelles mainly functions as storehouse of digestive enzymes?
113.x: Lysosomes store digestive enzymes, and this is why they are called 'suicidal bags'. Ribosomes make proteins, and desmosomes are cell junctions.

113.s: Which of the following is in monera group ?
113.x: Bacteria are prokaryotes and belong to Monera. Mushrooms and yeast are fungi, and moss is a bryophyte.

113.s: Which organelles in the cell, other than nucleus contains DNA?
113.x: Mitochondria contain their own small circular DNA, apart from nuclear DNA. Centrioles, Golgi apparatus and lysosomes do not carry DNA.

113.s: Mitochondria are able to produce their own
113.x: Mitochondria have their own DNA and ribosomes, so they can synthesise some of their own proteins. They cannot make a nucleus, chloroplasts or digestive enzymes.

113.s: The main factor of evolution is
113.x: Natural selection, proposed by Darwin, is the main driving mechanism of evolution. Mutation only supplies variation, and acquired characters are not inherited.

113.s:
Living things are grouped into subgroups like plant kingdom/animal kingdom.
Which one of the following is not correct for animal kingdom?
o: Migrate from one place to another
113.x: Animal cells have no cell wall, so animal bodies do not contain cellulose; cellulose is a plant feature. Animals cannot make their own food, lack chlorophyll and can move about.

113.s: ……… are called the ‘Powerhouses’ of the cell.
113.x: Mitochondria release energy as ATP by cellular respiration, so they are called the powerhouses of the cell.

113.s: Organs having different structure and components but perform similar functions are called .................. .
113.x: Analogous organs have different structure and origin but perform similar functions, such as the wings of a bird and an insect. Homologous organs have the same structure but different functions.

113.s: Substances which are used to bring down the temperature in high fever condition are called
113.x: Antipyretics such as paracetamol reduce high fever. Antiseptics act on living tissue against microbes and antibiotics kill bacteria.

113.s: Which one of the following organs is the main respiratory organ of whale ?
113.x: A whale is a mammal living in water, so it breathes air with lungs and not gills.

113.s: ‘Metastasis’ is the process by which
o: cells divide rapidly under the influence of drugs.
cancer cells spread through the blood or lymphatic system to other sites or organs.
the chromosomes in cells nuclei are attached to the spindle before moving to the anaphase poles.
cancer cells are successfully inhibited to divide any further.
113.x: Metastasis is the spread of cancer cells through blood or lymph to other organs.

113.s: In which one of the following types of connective tissues in animals does fat get stored?
113.x: Adipocytes are the fat-storing cells of adipose connective tissue. Chondrocytes are in cartilage and osteocytes in bone.

113.s: Select the mismatched pair (Name of plant – Plant part – Drug obtained).
o: Erythroxylum coca – Leaves and young twigs – Cocaine
Claviceps purpurea – Fruiting bodies – Lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD)
Cannabis sativa – Leaves, resin and inflorescence – Bhang, hashish
113.x: Mescaline comes from the peyote cactus, not from Thea chinensis (tea), whose leaves yield caffeine. So the pair is mismatched.

113.s: Cyanide poisoning causes death in seconds because
o: it breaks the electron transport chain
it denatures enzymes of the heart muscle.
it causes lysis of red blood cells.
113.x: Cyanide inhibits cytochrome c oxidase, which blocks the electron transport chain. Cells then cannot make ATP, so death is very quick.

113.s: Red worms have a structure named………which helps them in grinding their food.
113.x: Earthworms (red worms) have a muscular gizzard that grinds food with the help of small stones.

113.s: Which drug is used as an Anti-Diabetic drug?
113.x: Metformin is a standard oral anti-diabetic drug (it lowers blood glucose); zolpidem is a sleep aid, promethazine an antihistamine and hydralazine an antihypertensive.

113.s: The drugs used to get relief from pain are called
113.x: Analgesics are pain-relieving drugs; antipyretics reduce fever, antibiotics kill bacteria and antiseptics are applied on living tissue to prevent infection.

113.s:
Match the following columns. Column I Column II
A. Physalia
B. Taenia
C. Fasciola
D. Scypha
1. Liver fluke
2. Sycon
3. Tapeworm
4. Portuguese man of war
Codes A B C D A B C D
113.x: Physalia is the Portuguese man of war (4), Taenia is a tapeworm (3), Fasciola is the liver fluke (1) and Scypha (Sycon) is a sponge (2), giving 4 3 1 2.

113.s: Which of the following multiplies very slowly in comparison to others ?
113.x: Bacteria, viruses and fungi multiply rapidly in large numbers, whereas worms reproduce sexually and much more slowly.

113.s: Which one among the following statements is not true for mammals ?
o: They possess hair on the body.
113.x: Mammals have a four-chambered heart; a three-chambered heart is found in amphibians and most reptiles. The other statements hold (hair, egg-laying monotremes, aquatic whales).

113.s:
Match List I (Source) with List II (Medicinal Product) and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists.
List I
A. Poppy plant
B. Bacterium
C. Cinchona bark
D. Fungus
List II
1. Quinine
2. Morphine
3. Penicillin
4. Tetracycline
Codes A B C D A B C D
113.x: Morphine comes from the poppy plant, tetracycline from bacteria (Streptomyces), quinine from cinchona bark and penicillin from the fungus Penicillium, giving 2 4 1 3.

113.s: The phenomena in which one gene controls two or more different characters simultaneously is called
113.x: Pleiotropy is when a single gene affects two or more characters; apomixis is seed formation without fertilisation, polyploidy is extra chromosome sets and polyteny is repeated DNA strands in giant chromosomes.

113.s: Latest ancestor of modern human is
113.x: Cro-Magnon man was the most recent of these and was essentially anatomically modern Homo sapiens; Java, Peking and Neanderthal men were earlier.

113.s: Study of Zoology deals with
113.x: Zoology is the study of animals, both living and dead (fossils, preserved specimens); botany deals with plants.

113.s: With reference to the evolution of living organism, which one of the following sequence is correct?
113.x: Evolutionary order of appearance: amphibian (salamander), then reptile (python), then mammal (kangaroo). The other sequences are not in evolutionary order.

113.s: Poisonous fanges of a snake are modified form of
113.x: Venomous snake fangs are modified maxillary teeth, borne on the maxilla of the upper jaw. They are not mandibular (lower jaw), palatine or canine teeth; snakes have no canines.

113.s:
Assertion (A) : In human being, the females play a major role in determining the sex of the offspring.
Reason (R) : Women have two `X' chromosomes.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not a correct
113.x: A is false because the father's sperm (X or Y) decides the child's sex. R is true: women are XX and give only an X.

113.s: Which molecule serves as the primary energy currency of cells and is involved in storing and transferring energy within the cell?
113.src: APPSC 2022 Various posts under Group-IV Services(Limited Rec
113.x: ATP is the cell's energy currency; it releases energy when it becomes ADP. ADP is the low-energy form, and RNA and DNA carry genetic information.

113.s: A married couple adopted a male child. A few years later, twin boys were born to them. The blood group of the couple is AB positive and O negative. The blood group of the three sons is A positive, B positive, and O positive. The blood group of the adopted son is?
o: Cannot be determined on the basis of the given data
113.x: An AB parent passes A or B and an O parent passes O, so their own children can only be A or B. The O-positive son must therefore be the adopted one.

113.s:
Consider the following statements about ultrasonic waves :
1. They can destroy insects.
2. They can clean clothes by removing dust.
3. They can be used to treat diseases.
4. They can control automatic doors. Of the above statements
113.x: Ultrasonic waves kill insects and bacteria, clean clothes and delicate parts, treat diseases (physiotherapy, kidney stones) and run door sensors. So all four are correct.

113.s: Synovial fluid is present in
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Synovial fluid fills the cavities of movable joints and lubricates them. The heart has pericardial fluid; the liver and kidney have none of this kind.

113.s:
Consider the following statements.
I. Some species of turtles are herbivores.
II. Some species of fish are herbivores.
III. Some species of marine mammals are herbivores.
IV. Some species of snakes are viviparous.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
113.x: All four are true: green sea turtles, parrotfish and dugongs/manatees are herbivores, and many snakes (boas, most vipers, sea snakes) are viviparous.

113.s: Achaeopteryx is
o: most ancient bird of Jurassic age.
reptile of both Triassic and Jurassic period.
113.x: Archaeopteryx (Solnhofen, Germany) is the oldest known bird, from the Jurassic, with reptilian teeth, tail and claws.

113.s:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding common differences between plant and animal cells?
I. Plant cells have cellulose cell wall, while animal cells lack it.
II. Plant cells lack plasma membrane, while animal cells have it.
III. Mature plant cell have a large vacuole, while animal cells have numerous small vacuoles.
113.x: Plant cells have a cellulose wall and a large central vacuole; animal cells lack the wall and have small vacuoles. Both have a plasma membrane, so II is wrong.

113.s: Chromosome number in any species
113.x: Each species has a fixed (constant) chromosome number (humans 46); it does not change with age or weight.

113.s: Mammoth is the ancestor of
113.x: Mammoths are extinct proboscideans closely related to modern elephants, so the expected answer is the elephant (strictly a cousin rather than a direct ancestor).

113.s: Which of the following statement is incorrect ?
o: Hydra have only a sexual reproduction.
Most frogs are an oviparous animals.
Internal fertilisation takes place in hens.
113.x: Hydra reproduces asexually by budding and also sexually, so 'only sexual reproduction' is the incorrect statement. Most frogs are oviparous and hens have internal fertilisation.

113.s:
Assertion (A) Whale is a mammal.
Reason (R) Whale has abundant hairs on the body and is a viviparous animal.
Codes
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
113.x: The whale is a viviparous mammal (A true), but it has almost no body hair, so R is false.

113.s: Which of the following has the largest brain in proportion to its body size ?
113.x: Ants have the largest brain relative to body size among the options (about 15% of body mass in some species), far above humans (~2%).

113.s: Which one of the following are useful in the detection of landmines
113.x: Honey bees can be trained to detect explosive vapour from landmines through their sense of smell.

113.s: In which one of the following kind of organisms is the phenomenon found where the female kills the male after copulation ?
113.x: In many spiders (e.g. black widow) the female kills and eats the male after mating (sexual cannibalism).

113.s: Which among the following animals excretes solid urine ?
113.x: The desert kangaroo rat conserves water by producing extremely concentrated, near-solid urine and can live without drinking water.

113.s: Which one of the following is the principal structural elements of a living cell?
113.x: Carbon forms the backbone of all organic biomolecules, so it is the principal structural element of living cells (oxygen is most abundant by mass).

113.s: ‘Archaeopteryx’ is a connecting link between which of the following classes of animal?
113.x: Archaeopteryx had feathers and wings (bird) plus teeth, a long bony tail and clawed fingers (reptile): link between Reptilia and Aves.

113.s: Crocodiles have a ...... chambered heart.
113.x: Crocodiles are the only reptiles with a four-chambered heart; other reptiles have three chambers.

113.s: Which of the following is not an insects?
113.x: Spiders are arachnids (8 legs, two body parts), not insects (6 legs, three body parts). Bed bugs, house flies and mosquitoes are insects.

113.s: Among the following which one lays eggs and does not produce young ones directly ?
113.x: The echidna (spiny anteater) is a monotreme – an egg-laying mammal, like the platypus.

113.s:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using codes given below the lists.
List I
A. Photosynthesis
B. Mineral uptake
C. Respiration
D. Protein synthesis
List II
1. Plasma membrane
2. Chloroplast
3. Mitochondria
4. Ribosomes
Codes A B C D
113.x: Photosynthesis – chloroplast, mineral uptake – plasma membrane, respiration – mitochondria, protein synthesis – ribosomes: 2 1 3 4.

113.s: Which one of these belong to the family in which Panda belong ?
113.x: The giant panda belongs to the bear family Ursidae (the red panda has its own family).

113.s: The cellular and molecular control of programmed cell death is known as
113.x: Apoptosis is genetically controlled programmed cell death; necrosis is uncontrolled death from injury.

113.s: Which of the following organisms has White blood ?
113.x: Cockroach blood (haemolymph) has no haemoglobin and looks colourless/whitish.

113.s: A bacteriophage is a
113.x: A bacteriophage is a virus that infects bacteria (usually double-stranded DNA).

113.s: Which of the following cell organelles play the most significant role in protein synthesis?
113.x: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis and the rough ER carries them, so ER and ribosomes.

113.s: Which one of the following is a membrane that protects the developing embryo from desiccation?
113.x: The amnion encloses the embryo in amniotic fluid and protects it from desiccation and shock; allantois – excretion/respiration, chorion – outer membrane, yolk sac – food.

113.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
I. Coelenterates, ctenophores and echinoderms have radical symmetry kind of body plan.
II. Sponges are mostly asymmetrical.
o: Both I and II are correct
Both I and II are not correct
113.x: Coelenterates, ctenophores and (adult) echinoderms are radially symmetrical and sponges are mostly asymmetrical, so both are correct (NCERT wording).

113.s: What does the following sign indicate? (a cross symbol)
113.x: A cross (plus) sign is the standard first-aid symbol.

113.s: Ants are social insects because
113.x: Ants are social insects because they live in organised colonies with division of labour (queen, workers, soldiers).

113.s: Which of the following creatures are stone-deaf?
113.x: Snakes have no external ear or eardrum, so they are deaf to airborne sound and sense ground vibrations.

113.s: Which one of the following instrument is used for locating submerged objects in an ocean ?
113.x: SONAR sends ultrasonic pulses and times their echoes to locate submerged objects.

113.s: Viagra is the brand name of the drug that improves sexual energy in men. What is its chemical name?
113.x: Viagra's active ingredient is sildenafil citrate, a PDE-5 inhibitor (PDE-5 is the enzyme it blocks, not the drug).

113.s: Which one of the following is a secretion from the body of an insect ?
113.x: Lac is the resinous secretion of the lac insect (Kerria lacca). Pearl comes from molluscs, coral from coral polyps' skeletons, gum from plants.

113.s: The synthesis of Urea occurs in:
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
113.x: Urea is made in the liver through the ornithine (urea) cycle and excreted by the kidneys.

113.s: Which of the following is a plant hormone?
113.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
113.x: Cytokinins are plant hormones that promote cell division and delay ageing. Insulin, thyroxin and oestrogen are animal hormones. (Off-topic: plant physiology.)

113.s: Which of the following does not have any enzyme in its cells?
113.x: Viruses are acellular and have no metabolic enzymes of their own; lichens, bacteria and algae are cellular organisms with enzymes.

113.s: Which blood group is known as the universal recipient?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Group AB is the universal recipient: its plasma has neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies, so it can receive red cells of any ABO group. O is the universal donor (its red cells carry no A or B antigen).

113.s: Which one among the following hormones stimulates the plant cells to grow in a manner such that the plant are to be bent towards light ?
113.x: Auxin accumulates on the shaded side and promotes cell elongation there, so the plant bends towards light (phototropism).

113.s: Which one of the following is a plant hormone ?
113.x: Cytokinin is a plant hormone promoting cell division; insulin, thyroxine and estrogen are animal hormones.

113.s: Which of the following procedures is used to produce phenol industrially from isopropylbenzene?
o: By treatment of cumene hydroperoxide with dilute acid
113.src: APPSC 2023 Lecturers in Government Degree Colleges
113.x: In the cumene process, cumene (isopropylbenzene) is oxidised by air to cumene hydroperoxide, which dilute acid splits into phenol and acetone. Hydrogenation, benzene oxidation and propane cracking do not give phenol this way.

113.s:
Consider the following statements about acetylene:
I. It is used in welding industry.
II. It is raw material for preparing plastics.
III. It is easily obtained by mixing silicon carbide and water. Of these statements:
o: I, II and III are correct
113.x: Acetylene (ethyne) is used in oxy-acetylene welding and as a feedstock for plastics such as PVC. It is made from calcium carbide and water, not silicon carbide, so III is wrong.

113.s: Which of the following statement is not true :
o: Boiling point of any water solution is higher than pure
Addition of solute to a solution increases its water
Water vapour pressure of any solution is lower than
When a solution is separated with the help of
113.x: Adding a solute lowers the water potential of a solution; it does not raise it, so (b) is the untrue statement. A solute does raise the boiling point and lower the vapour pressure, and water can be separated from a solution by distillation.

113.s: What is the main product formed when ethanol reacts with sodium?
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Ethanol reacts with sodium to give sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas. Sodium acetate, ethanoic acid and ethyl acetate need oxidation or esterification instead.

113.s: Which of the following is not a Natural polymer?
113.x: Nylon was the first fully synthetic fibre (Carothers, 1935). Wool, silk and leather are natural protein polymers.

113.s: Which of the following is an example of colloidal solution of liquid in solid?
113.x: Cheese is a gel, a colloid of a liquid dispersed in a solid. Milk is an emulsion (liquid in liquid), mud a suspension and rubber a polymer.

113.s: Charcoal which is used in decolouring raw sugar is :
113.x: Animal (bone) charcoal is used to decolourise raw sugar in refining because it adsorbs the coloured impurities. Wood, sugar and coconut charcoal are not the standard answer.

113.s: Milk is an example of
113.x: Milk is an emulsion, fat droplets dispersed in water (oil-in-water). A gel is liquid in solid, a foam gas in liquid, and milk is not a suspension.

113.s: Select the incorrect statement out of the following :
o: Cotton is suitable for use as clothing in summer
Polycarbonate is used for making CDs
Acrylic is also called artificial silk as it is prepared
Teflon is used for coating non-stick kitchenwares
113.x: Rayon, made from wood-pulp cellulose, is called artificial silk; acrylic is 'artificial wool', so (c) is the incorrect statement. Cotton suits summer, polycarbonate makes CDs and Teflon coats non-stick pans.

113.s: The cleaning action of soap primarily depends on
o: Formation of micelles that trap grease and dirt
Conversion of soap into fatty acid anions in water
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Soap molecules form micelles: the oily tails trap grease and the ionic heads face water, so dirt washes away.

113.s: Which of the following materials is used to remove permanent hardness of water?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: Sodium aluminium silicate (zeolite/permutit) removes permanent hardness by ion exchange of Ca/Mg for Na.

113.s: Why are tungsten filaments used in incandescent bulbs?
o: High specific resistance and high melting point
Low specific resistance and high melting point
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
113.x: Tungsten has high resistivity (heats up) and a very high melting point (3,422 °C), so the filament glows without melting.

113.s: What type of soap is generated when soap is dissolved in ethanol and then the surplus solvent is evaporated?
113.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
113.x: Dissolving soap in ethanol and evaporating the extra solvent gives transparent soap (NCERT Chemistry Class 12, 'Chemistry in Everyday Life').

113.s: The aromatic solvent widely used in the manufacturing of reinforced plastics and resins is ____.
113.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
113.x: Styrene is the aromatic monomer-solvent used with unsaturated polyester resins in reinforced plastics (fibreglass).

113.s: Which of the following Gas is produced when Baking soda is heated?
113.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
113.x: On heating, baking soda (NaHCO3) decomposes into sodium carbonate, water and carbon dioxide; the CO2 is what makes cakes rise. No CO, nitrogen or hydrogen is formed.

113.s: The wire in an electric iron is mainly made up of ____.
113.src: APPSC Sample Taker General Studies & Mental Abilities 2023
113.x: The heating element of an electric iron is nichrome (Ni-Cr alloy): high resistivity and a high melting point, and it does not oxidise when red-hot. Brass, bronze and steel are not heating-element materials.

113.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the chemical process in baking a cake?
A. Baking soda is used to chemically leaven doughs and batters when it is mixed with an acid.
B. Cream of Tarter is one of the powdery acids used in baking powder to help leaven products.
C. Baking powder makes cakes rise by releasing carbon dioxide gas.
113.src: APPSC Executive Officer Gr-III Endowment Paper-I General Stu
113.x: All three are true: baking soda leavens when it meets an acid, cream of tartar (potassium bitartrate) is the dry acid in baking powder, and baking powder releases CO2 that makes the cake rise.

113.s: The Statute of Liberty in USA is Green in colour because of?
o: Every 30 years colour polish is applied
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
113.x: The copper skin of the Statue of Liberty oxidised (with CO2, moisture and sulphur compounds) into a green patina of basic copper carbonate. It is not paint and is not repolished.

113.s: Application of soap cleans dirty clothes through the process of
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
113.x: Soap molecules surround oily dirt and form micelles, an emulsion that is washed away by water. Soap lowers the surface tension of water, not of the dirt, and it forms no compound with dirt.

113.s: Which of the following materials is not a better absorber of sound compared to other given materials?
113.src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning
113.x: A hard, smooth steel sheet reflects sound; porous materials such as glass wool, polyvinyl foam and wood panels absorb it.

113.s: Which of the following materials has the highest melting point?
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
113.x: Tantalum carbide melts at about 3,880 °C, above tungsten (3,422 °C, the highest-melting metal). Glass and bauxite melt far lower.

113.s: Which of the following chemicals is normally used as 'anti freeze' in cars?
113.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: Ethylene glycol is mixed with radiator water as antifreeze: it lowers the freezing point. Hexane and benzene are not used, and ethyl alcohol evaporates too easily.

113.s: Which of the following salts does not contain water of crystallisation?
113.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
113.x: Baking soda (NaHCO3) has no water of crystallisation. Blue vitriol is CuSO4·5H2O, washing soda Na2CO3·10H2O and gypsum CaSO4·2H2O.

113.s: Sodium bicarbonate is the chemical name of which one of the following household items?
113.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
113.x: Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) is baking soda. Detergents are sulphonates, sanitisers are alcohol-based and talc is a magnesium silicate.

113.s: Diamonds are crystals of?
113.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
113.x: Diamond is a crystalline form of pure carbon (each C bonded to four others). Quartz is silica, and glass is non-crystalline.

113.s: Type metal used to make printing types contains?
113.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
113.x: Type metal is an alloy of lead with antimony and tin (Pb + Sb + Sn); lead is the main metal. Steel, nickel and bismuth are not in it (bismuth is in Rose/Wood's metal).

113.s: Non-Stick Cookware is coated with
113.src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
113.x: Non-stick pans are coated with PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene, Teflon). PVC and polystyrene would melt or stick.

113.s: With what is non-stick kitchenware coated?
113.x: Non-stick kitchenware is coated with Teflon (polytetrafluoroethylene), a slippery, heat-resistant polymer. Graphite, silicon and glass are not non-stick coatings.

113.s: The Statue of Liberty is green because of
113.x: The Statue of Liberty is made of copper sheets, which oxidised over time into a green patina. It is not paint, algae or bronze.

113.s: The tubes used for dialysis and blood transfusion are made of
113.x: Dialysis and transfusion tubes and blood bags are made of PVC (poly vinyl chloride), which is flexible and can be sterilised.

113.s: Which kind of glass is used in the production of electric bulbs and optical instruments?
113.x: Flint (lead) glass has a high refractive index and dispersion, so it is used for lenses, prisms and electric bulbs. Pyrex is heat-resistant labware and hard glass is for chemical apparatus.

113.s: Milk of magnesia used as anti-acid is
113.x: Milk of magnesia is a suspension of magnesium hydroxide, Mg(OH)2, which neutralises excess stomach acid. The acetate, chloride and nitrate are not antacids.

113.s: Why is Sodium normally kept immersed in kerosene oil?
o: Kerosene oil is a good preservative
To prevent Sodium to absorb moisture in atmosphere
In open air Sodium explosively reacts with oxygen
113.x: NCERT: sodium reacts so vigorously that it catches fire in open air, so it is kept under kerosene. Avoiding moisture is part of the reason, but the vigorous reaction with oxygen is the answer the key gives.

113.s: PVC is a polymer used in a variety of applications in building and construction, health care, electronics, automobile and other sectors, in products ranging from piping and siding to blood bags and tubing. The full form of PVC is:
113.x: PVC stands for poly vinyl chloride, the polymer of vinyl chloride. The other expansions are not real polymers.

113.s: TEFLON is a polymer used for making non-stick cooking utensils. It is chemically known as:
113.x: Teflon is PTFE, polytetrafluoroethylene, the polymer of tetrafluoroethene (ethylene). The propylene, butylene and pentylene names are distractors.

113.s:
Which of the following statements are NOT true about gold?
a) soft metal
b) high density, 2.5x iron
c) pure gold ornaments cannot be made
d) not easily scratched
e) 18-carat gold has 25% copper
f) 1 carat = 100/24 percent
113.x: Untrue: (d) – gold is soft and easily scratched – and (c), since pure 24-carat ornaments can be made (they are merely soft). Gold's density (19.3) is about 2.5 times iron's (7.9), 18-carat gold has 25% other metal such as copper, and 1 carat = 100/24 %.

113.s: Some aircraft and car parts are made of the alloy 'dow metal'. What are the constituents of 'dow metal'?
113.x: Dow metal is a light magnesium alloy with a few per cent aluminium (Mg + Al), used in aircraft and car parts.

113.s: Baking soda is –
113.x: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO3. Sodium chloride is common salt and sodium hydroxide is caustic soda.

113.s: How much percentage of silver is found in German Silver?
113.x: German silver (nickel silver) is copper + zinc + nickel and contains no silver at all, so none of the percentages is right.

113.s: Phenol is used in the manufacture of which one of the following ?
113.x: Bakelite is made by condensing phenol with formaldehyde (Baekeland, 1907). PVC, nylon and polystyrene do not use phenol.

113.s: Bauxite, is an ore of which of the following metals?
113.x: Bauxite (hydrated aluminium oxide) is the main ore of aluminium. Iron ores are haematite and magnetite.

113.s:
Assertion (A) : Sodium metal is stored under kerosene.
Reason (R) : Metallic sodium melts when exposed to air.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct
113.x: Sodium is stored under kerosene because it reacts violently with oxygen and moisture of the air, not because it melts in air; so A is true and R false.

113.s: Which of the following polymer is NOT a thermoplastic?
113.x: Neoprene (polychloroprene) is a synthetic rubber, an elastomer, not a thermoplastic. Teflon, polystyrene and polythene soften on heating and can be remoulded.

113.s:
Consider the following statements –
1. Anhydrous sodium carbonate is commonly known as baking soda.
2. Baking soda is used as a fire extinguisher.
3. Bleaching powder is produced in Hasenclever plant. Which of these statements is right :
113.x: Statement 1 is wrong: anhydrous Na2CO3 is soda ash (washing soda), while baking soda is NaHCO3. Baking soda is used in soda-acid fire extinguishers, and bleaching powder is made in the Hasenclever (or Bachmann) plant, so 2 and 3.

113.s: The chemical formula of baking soda is :
113.x: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO3. Na2CO3 is washing soda, CaCO3 limestone and Ca(OH)2 slaked lime.

113.s: Non-stick frying pans are coated with :
113.x: Non-stick frying pans are coated with Teflon (PTFE). Orlon is an acrylic fibre, and polystyrene and polypropylene are ordinary plastics.

113.s: The chemical used as a 'fixer' in photography is –
113.x: Hypo, sodium thiosulphate (Na2S2O3), is the photographic fixer: it dissolves the unexposed silver bromide. Sodium sulphate and borax are not fixers.

113.s: Teflon is a polymer of which of the following monomers?
113.x: Teflon (PTFE) is the polymer of tetrafluoroethylene. Vinyl chloride gives PVC and chloroprene gives neoprene.

113.s: Full form of PHBV biodegradable polymer:
o: Poly hydroxy butyric acid veratric acid
113.x: PHBV is poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate), a biodegradable copolymer of 3-hydroxybutanoic and 3-hydroxypentanoic acids.

113.s: The chemical formula of washing soda is :
113.x: Washing soda is sodium carbonate, Na2CO3 (as decahydrate). NaHCO3 is baking soda, NaOH caustic soda and Ca(OH)2 slaked lime.

113.s: The formula of baking soda is :
113.x: Baking soda is NaHCO3, sodium hydrogen carbonate. KHCO3 and K2CO3 are potassium salts and Na2CO3 is washing soda.

113.s:
With reference to Baking Soda, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is Sodium hydrogen carbonate.
2. It is used in fire extinguishers.
Select the correct answer from the code given below:
Code :
113.x: Baking soda is sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO3), and it is used in soda-acid fire extinguishers, where it releases CO2. Both statements are true.

113.s:
Check these statements :
(i) Brass is an alloy of Copper and Zinc.
(ii) Magnetite is the main ore of Aluminium.
(iii) Amalgams are that substances which mainly involve mercury.
(iv) Potassium Nitrate (KNO3) is a chemical used in photography. Which of the above are true ? Code :
113.x: (i) Brass = copper + zinc and (iii) amalgams are mercury alloys are true. Magnetite (Fe3O4) is an iron ore, and photography uses silver bromide, not KNO3, so (i) and (iii).

113.s: Which chemical compound is present in Bleaching Powder?
113.x: Bleaching powder is calcium oxychloride, CaOCl2. Calcium hydroxide is only the slaked lime that is chlorinated to make it.

113.s: The important metal used with iron to produce stainless steel, is :
113.x: Stainless steel is iron alloyed with chromium (at least 10.5%, often with nickel); chromium's oxide film stops rusting. Carbon is in all steel, but it is not what makes it stainless.

113.s: Which one of the following polymers is used for making bullet-proof windows?
113.x: Bullet-resistant windows use tough, transparent polycarbonate laminated with glass. Polyurethane is used in foams and paints, polystyrene in packaging and polyamides in nylon fibres.

113.s: Solder used in soldering metal pieces is an alloy of :
113.x: Solder is a low-melting alloy of tin and lead. Bronze is tin + copper, and zinc is not in common solder.

113.s: Baking Soda is –
113.x: Baking soda is NaHCO3, sodium hydrogen carbonate. Sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) is washing soda.

113.s: Which one of the following materials contains calcium?
113.x: Gypsum is calcium sulphate dihydrate, CaSO4·2H2O. China clay (kaolin) and corundum contain aluminium, and talc is a magnesium silicate.

113.s: Baking soda is –
113.x: Baking soda is NaHCO3 (anhydrous). Na2CO3 is washing soda (decahydrate Na2CO3·10H2O), and the other formulae do not exist.

113.s: The important metal used with iron to make it rust free–
113.x: Chromium is alloyed with iron to make stainless steel, which resists rusting. Carbon is in all steel, but it does not stop rust.

113.s:
Consider the following statements :
1. Teflon and Dacron are polymers
2. Neoprene is synthetic rubber
3. Polythene is polyethylene polymer
4. Natural rubber is chloroprene
Which of the above statements are correct :
113.x: 1, 2 and 3 are true: Teflon and Dacron are polymers, neoprene is a synthetic rubber, and polythene is polyethylene. Natural rubber is polyisoprene, not chloroprene (that is neoprene).

113.s: Bakelite is formed by the condensation of :
113.x: Bakelite is formed by condensing phenol with formaldehyde. Urea-formaldehyde and melamine-formaldehyde are different resins.

113.s: What is untrue for bleaching powder?
o: It is more soluble in water
It is powder of light yellow colour
It releases chlorine after reaction with dilute acid
113.x: Bleaching powder is only partly soluble in water (it leaves a residue of lime), so 'more soluble' is the untrue claim. It is a pale-yellowish powder, an oxidant, and gives chlorine with dilute acid.

113.s: A polymer used for making nonstick surface coating for utensils is –
113.x: Teflon (PTFE) gives the non-stick coating of utensils. PVC, polystyrene and polypropylene are not non-stick and soften on heating.

113.s: Which one of the following polymers is used for the production of non-stick pans?
113.x: Teflon (PTFE) is the non-stick polymer used to coat pans. Neoprene is a synthetic rubber, PVC softens with heat, and gutta-percha is a natural latex.

113.s:
Consider the following statements : Hard water is not suitable for
1. Drinking
2. Washing clothes with soap
3. Use in boilers
4. Irrigating crops Which of these statements are correct ?
113.x:
Most books and keys: 1, 2, 3 and 4. Strictly: hard water is fit for drinking and is used in agriculture (PMF General Science Part 7 table: 'Domestic use ..., agriculture'); it is unsuitable mainly for washing with soap and for boilers, i.e. 2 and 3.
Hard water wastes soap (scum) and forms boiler scale, and books add drinking and irrigation, so the key is all four (1, 2, 3 and 4).

113.s: Stainless Steel is an alloy in which following is added along with iron:
113.x: Stainless steel is iron with chromium (plus some nickel), which makes it rust-resistant. Zinc is used for galvanising, tin for tin-plating.

113.s: The hair dye available in the market contains two bottles, one containing dye and other containing hydrogen peroxide. The bottles are mixed before applying the dye. The function of hydrogen peroxide is
o: to oxidise the dye to give desired colour.
to reduce the dye to give desired colour.
113.x: Hydrogen peroxide is an oxidising agent: it oxidises the dye precursors to develop the colour (and lightens natural pigment). It does not dilute, reduce or acidify the dye.

113.s: The advantage of detergents over soaps is
o: detergents could not give much lather.
detergents give lather even with hard water.
soaps give lather with only soft water.
113.x: Detergents form no scum with calcium and magnesium ions, so they lather even in hard water, which soaps cannot. Soap also dissolves in water, so 'soluble' is no advantage.

113.s: Soaps clean surfaces on the principle of based on
113.x: Soap cleans by lowering the surface tension of water, so it wets the surface and lifts grease into micelles. Viscosity, floatation and elasticity are not the principle.

113.s: Soaps clean surface on the principle is based on
113.x: Soap cleans by lowering the surface tension of water, so it wets the surface and lifts grease into micelles. Viscosity, floatation and elasticity are not the principle.

113.s:
Which of the following are fabrics that may contain polyester ? I. Polycot
II. Polywool III. Terrycot
113.x: Polycot (polyester + cotton), polywool (polyester + wool) and terrycot (terylene polyester + cotton) are all polyester blends.

113.s:
Which of the following statements are correct?
I. The soap molecules form structures called micelles.
II. Soap micelles cannot scatter light.
III. Only dirt gets collected in the centre of the micelle.
113.x: Soap molecules form micelles, and the oily dirt collects in the centre of the micelle (NCERT), so I and III. Micelles are colloid-sized and do scatter light, so II is wrong.

113.s: Cement is made hard with
113.x: Cement sets and hardens by hydration: its silicates and aluminates react with water to form hydrated gels and crystals. The key's wording 'hydration and dissociation of water' is the printed answer.

113.s: Brightness of the bulb decreases gradually with its period of use because of
o: evaporation of metal from filament of bulb.
decrease in electric supply to the bulb.
113.x: The hot tungsten filament slowly evaporates (sublimes), so it thins and the metal blackens the glass, and the bulb dims. Resistance actually rises as the filament thins.

113.s: Which of the following metal (shown by its symbol) is generally used for making filaments of bulb?
113.x: Tungsten (W) has the highest melting point of the metals, so it is used for bulb filaments. Fe is iron and Ag silver.

113.s: Which one of the following is used in the preparation of antiseptic solution?
113.x: Iodine (tincture of iodine, iodine in alcohol) is a standard antiseptic. Potassium nitrate, potassium chloride and iodine chloride are not.

113.s: What is the product formed when sodium bicarbonate is heated strongly?
113.x: On strong heating, sodium bicarbonate decomposes into sodium carbonate, water and CO2 (2NaHCO3 → Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2).

113.s: Which of the following is the chemical name of baking soda?
113.x: Baking soda is NaHCO3, sodium hydrogen carbonate. Sodium carbonate is washing soda.

113.s: What is the chemical name of slaked lime?
113.x: Slaked lime is calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)2, made by adding water to quicklime (CaO).

113.s: Which one among the following chemicals is used as washing soda?
113.x: Washing soda is sodium carbonate, Na2CO3·10H2O. Sodium bicarbonate is baking soda.

113.s: Which of the following properties is true for a tooth paste?
o: It is made up of Calcium phosphate, the material of tooth enamel.
113.x: Toothpaste is basic (alkaline) and neutralises the acid made by mouth bacteria, preventing tooth decay. Enamel is calcium phosphate, but toothpaste is not made of it.

113.s: A sample of ‘soft soap’ contains
113.x: Soft soaps are potassium salts of fatty acids (made with KOH); hard soaps are sodium soaps.

113.s: Which of the following is slaked lime?
113.x: Slaked lime is calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)2. CaO is quicklime, CaCO3 limestone and CaCl2 calcium chloride.

113.s: Which of the following is not correct about baking soda?
o: It is used in soda-acid fire extinguisher.
It is added for faster cooking.
It neutralises excess acid in the stomach.
113.x: Baking soda is a mild, non-corrosive base, so 'corrosive base' is the wrong statement. It is used in soda-acid extinguishers, added for faster cooking and as an antacid.

113.s: Soap solution used for cleaning purpose appears cloudy. This is due to the fact that soap micelles can
113.x: Soap micelles are colloid-sized and scatter light (Tyndall effect), so soap solution looks cloudy.

113.s: A fuse wire is made of
o: an alloy of tin and copper.
an alloy of tin and lead.
an alloy of tin and aluminium.
an alloy of nickel and chromium.
113.x: Fuse wire is a tin-lead alloy, which has a low melting point. Nichrome is for heater coils.

113.s: Filament in traditional incandescent bulb is made up of which metal?
113.x: The filament of an incandescent bulb is tungsten, which has the highest melting point of the metals.

113.s: Tungsten is used for the construction of filament in electric bulb because of its
113.x: Tungsten's very high melting point (~3,420 °C) lets the filament glow white-hot without melting.

113.s: The material used in electric heater is
113.x: Electric heaters use nichrome coils (high resistivity, high melting point, no oxidation). Tungsten is used for bulb filaments.

113.s: The coil wire in the electric room heater or electric cooking heater is called ……… .
113.x: The nichrome coil of a heater is called the heating element. 'Filament' is the word for a bulb's wire.

113.s: Which one of the following is used as an anti-freezer, which effectively depresses the freezing point of water in an automobile ?
113.x: Ethylene glycol is added to radiator water as antifreeze because it depresses the freezing point of water.

113.s: When items of jewellery made of metals such as copper or nickel are placed in a solution having a salt of gold, a thin film of gold is deposited by
113.x: A thin film of gold is deposited by electroplating: an electric current is passed through the gold salt solution with the jewellery as the cathode.

113.s: Sodium calcium silicate is called .......
113.x: Sodium calcium silicate is soft (soda-lime) glass. Hard glass is potassium calcium silicate; borosilicate (Jena/Pyrex) contains boron.

113.s: What is the dominant chemical present in detergent powder?
113.x:
Official key / most books: sodium carbonate (the main builder in detergent powder). Strictly: the cleansing agent of a detergent is the surfactant, a sodium alkyl sulphate / alkylbenzene sulphonate (NextGen Rocket Chemistry).
Answer keys take sodium carbonate, the builder that makes up most of a detergent powder by weight. Calcium carbonate is only a filler and HCl is never used.

113.s: What is the common name of CaOCl 2 ?
113.x: CaOCl2 (calcium oxychloride) is bleaching powder. Baking soda is NaHCO3 and washing soda Na2CO3.

113.s:
Match List I with List II.
List I
A. German silver
B. Solder
C. Bleaching powder
D. Hypo
List II
1. Tin
2. Nickel
3. Sodium
4. Chlorine
Codes A B C D A B C D
113.x: German silver contains nickel (A-2), solder tin (B-1), bleaching powder chlorine (C-4) and hypo is sodium thiosulphate (D-3), giving 2 1 4 3.

113.s: Which are the materials generally employed as solder in soldering operation in electronics?
113.x: Electronic solder is a tin-lead alloy (now often lead-free tin alloys). Iron and aluminium are not used.

113.s: Which alloy has bismuth, lead and tin?
113.x: Rose metal is a low-melting alloy of bismuth, lead and tin. Solder has only tin and lead, bell metal is copper + tin and German silver copper + zinc + nickel.

113.s: Bronze is often used to make statues and medals whereas brass is used in making utensils, scientific apparatus and cartridges. Both brass and bronze are copper containing alloys, yet they differ in their chemical composition for additionally containing.
o: zinc in brass and tin in bronze.
chromium in brass and nickel in bronze.
nickel in brass and tin in bronze.
iron in brass and nickel in bronze.
113.x: Brass is copper + zinc and bronze is copper + tin.

113.s: Natural rubber is a polymer of
