113.x: Natural rubber is cis-polyisoprene, a polymer of isoprene. Styrene gives polystyrene and propene polypropylene.

113.s: Soap, removes grease by
113.x: Soap removes grease by emulsification: micelles break the grease into tiny droplets that stay dispersed in water and are rinsed away.

113.s: Soap helps in better cleaning of clothes because
o: it reduces the surface tension of solution.
113.x: Soap lowers the surface tension of water, so it wets the fabric and lifts dirt better. It is not a catalyst and does not absorb dirt.

113.s: Which of the following statements is not true for soap?
o: Soaps cannot be used in acidic medium.
Soaps form a white curdy precipitate with hard water.
Soaps are relatively stronger in their cleaning action than synthetic detergents.
113.x: Soaps are biodegradable, fail in acidic water and form a curdy scum with hard water, so the untrue claim is that soaps clean more strongly than synthetic detergents.

113.s: Which one of the following types of glasses is used for making optical instruments?
113.x: Flint (lead) glass, with its high refractive index and dispersion, is used for lenses and prisms of optical instruments. Pyrex is used for labware and soft glass for windows and bottles.

113.s: Which one of the following statements about glass is not correct?
o: Glass is often said to be a supercooled liquid.
Glass has no definite melting point.
Soda glass is harder than pyrex glass.
Boron is present in pyrex glass.
113.x: Pyrex (borosilicate, contains boron) is harder and more heat-resistant than soda glass, so 'soda glass is harder than Pyrex' is the incorrect statement. Glass is a supercooled liquid with no definite melting point.

113.s:
Consider the following statements.
I. Glass wool has tensile strength greater than steel.
II. Glass wool is fire proof.
III. Glass wool has high electrical conductivity and absorbs moisture.
IV. Glass wool is used to prepare fibre glass.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
113.x: Glass wool (fine glass fibres) has very high tensile strength, is fireproof and is used to make fibre glass. It is an electrical insulator and does not absorb moisture, so III is wrong.

113.s: What is full form of PVC?
113.x: PVC is poly vinyl chloride, the polymer of vinyl chloride.

113.s: Iodine can be separated from a mixture of iodine and potassium chloride by
113.x: Iodine sublimes on heating while KCl does not, so sublimation separates them. Filtration and sedimentation only work for insoluble solids and distillation for liquids.

113.s:
Which of the following is an example of sublimation?
I. Dry ice
II. Camphor
III. Ice
113.x: Dry ice (solid CO2) and camphor change directly from solid to gas, so they sublime. Ice melts to liquid water, so it is not an example.

113.s: The pH of water at 25° C is 7. When it is heated to 100° C, the pH of water
o: decreases up to 50° C and then increases
113.x: On heating, water ionises more, so [H+] increases and pH falls below 7 (about 6.1 at 100°C), although the water stays neutral.

113.s: Which is a natural colloid?
113.x: Blood is a natural colloid in which proteins and cells are dispersed in plasma. Urea, cane sugar and sodium chloride dissolve to form true solutions, not colloids.

113.s: Glycol is added to aviation gasoline because it
113.x: Glycol (ethylene glycol type) is an anti-freeze additive. It lowers the freezing point of aviation fuel at high altitude, so the petrol does not freeze.

113.s: Which one of the following salts when dissolved in water makes the solution basic?
113.x: Sodium acetate is a salt of a strong base (NaOH) and a weak acid (acetic acid). Its acetate ion hydrolyses to give OH-, so the solution is basic. NaCl is neutral; CuSO4 and FeCl3 are acidic.

113.s: Which chemical was an important symbol in our struggle for freedom?
113.x: Salt (sodium chloride) was the symbol of the freedom struggle through Gandhi's Dandi March and Salt Satyagraha (1930) against the salt tax.

113.s: Which one of the following is used as a mordant in dyeing and tanning industry?
113.x: Magnesium sulphate is used as a mordant in the dyeing and tanning industry. The other magnesium compounds are not used for this purpose.

113.s: Which one among the following is not a property of salt?
o: Salts have ordered packing arrangements called lattices.
Salts have low melting points but high boiling points.
Salts conduct electricity when dissolved in water or even in the molten state.
113.x: Salts are ionic compounds with strong ionic bonds, so they have high melting and high boiling points. The statement that they have low melting points is false.

113.s: ………… is one of the most important technique for the separation of a mixture by passing it in solution or suspension through a medium in which the components move at different rates.
113.x: Chromatography separates mixture components because they move at different rates through a medium (stationary phase) carried by a solvent. Filtration, distillation and evaporation do not work this way.

113.s: Which of the following compounds is used as drying agent?
113.x:
Most keys: calcium oxide. Strictly: anhydrous calcium chloride is also a common drying agent, so two options fit (NCERT Class 11 Chemistry).
Calcium oxide (quicklime) absorbs water readily and is used as a drying agent, e.g. for ammonia gas. Gypsum and calcium hydroxide are not drying agents.

113.s: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
113.x: Non-metal oxides such as CO2 and SO2 are acidic, forming acids with water. Metal oxides are generally basic.

113.s: Which one among the following contains the most neutrons?
113.x: Neutrons = mass number minus atomic number. Fe-59: 33; Cu-61: 32; Zn-61: 31; Zn-60: 30. So Fe-59 has the most.

113.s: Which of the following cannot be beaten into Sheets?
113.x: Gold, silver and aluminium are malleable and can be beaten into sheets. Potassium is a soft, reactive alkali metal that is not beaten into sheets.

113.s: Which one of the following is an oxidation-reduction reaction?
113.x: In 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO, Mg is oxidised and O2 is reduced, so it is a redox reaction. The other options are neutralisation, combination and double displacement with no change in oxidation state.

113.s: Nitric acid does not react with
113.x: Gold is a noble metal that dissolves only in aqua regia (3 HCl : 1 HNO3), so nitric acid alone does not react with it. Copper, zinc and iron react.

113.s: The manufacturing of iron from iron ore involves the process of
113.x: Iron is extracted by reducing its oxide ore with coke, which acts as the reducing agent. So the process is reduction.

113.s: Bronze is an alloy of
113.x: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin. Brass is copper and zinc.

113.s: Which of the following has the lowest melting point ?
113.x: Tin melts at about 232 °C, lower than lead (327 °C), zinc (420 °C) and silver (962 °C).

113.s: What is the chemical formula for Sodium Chloride (Salt)?
113.x: Common salt is sodium chloride, NaCl: one Na+ ion combined with one Cl- ion, so the formula has no subscripts.

113.s: An amalgam of metal has which other element?
113.x: An amalgam is an alloy of a metal with mercury (Hg), the only common liquid metal.

113.s: Which of the following metal is the heaviest?
113.x: Osmium is the densest naturally occurring metal, denser than iron, silver and nickel.

113.s: Which one among the following metals is used in fireworks to make a brilliant white light?
113.x: Magnesium burns with a dazzling white flame, so it is used in fireworks for brilliant white light. Sodium gives yellow.

113.s: Which is used in storage batteries?
113.x: Lead (lead-acid accumulators) is used in storage batteries, with lead plates in sulphuric acid.

113.s: Which among the following elements comes under metalloids?
113.x: Germanium is a metalloid (semiconductor) while zinc, silver and gold are true metals.

113.s: The solution of which one of the following will have pH less than 7?
113.x: FeCl3 is a salt of a strong acid (HCl) and a weak base Fe(OH)3, so it hydrolyses to give an acidic solution (pH<7). NaCl and KCl are neutral and NaOH is basic.

113.s: A copper substances when exposed to air gains a green coating due to the formation of
113.x: Copper exposed to moist air and CO2 slowly forms a green layer of basic copper carbonate, CuCO3·Cu(OH)2 (patina). CuO is black and the sulphate or nitrate do not form from air.

113.s: A substance acquired in the form of brownish film on a piece of iron left in the open for some time is
113.x: Iron exposed to air and moisture forms a brownish layer of hydrated iron oxide, called rust.

113.s: Which of the following is a natural fibre?
113.x: Silk is a natural protein fibre from silkworms. Rayon is semi-synthetic, and nylon and polyester are synthetic.

113.s: The number of angular and radial nodes for 4d orbital is respectively
113.x: For 4d, n=4 and l=2. Angular nodes = l = 2, and radial nodes = n-l-1 = 1.

113.s: Fabric made from ………does not get wrinkled easily.
113.x: Polyester is a synthetic fibre that resists wrinkling. Cotton, flax and silk crease easily.

113.s: Which of the following are amongst the few carbon-containing compounds not classified as organic?
113.x: Cyanides, along with oxides of carbon, carbonates and carbides, are carbon compounds traditionally treated as inorganic. Methane, propane and nucleic acids are organic.

113.s: Very small insoluble particles in a liquid may be separated it by using
113.x: Centrifugation spins the liquid so that very fine insoluble particles settle out. Decantation works only for larger particles that settle on their own.

113.s: What is formed when Magnesium is burnt?
113.x: Magnesium burns in air to form magnesium oxide, a white ash. It does not form baking soda, calcium carbonate or vinegar.

113.s: In the reaction between hydrogen sulphate ion and water HSO4− + H2O → H3O+ + SO42−, the water acts as
113.x: Water accepts a proton from HSO4- to form H3O+, so water acts as a Bronsted-Lowry base.

113.s: Which one of the following could be the melting point of iron ?
113.x: Iron is a solid with a high melting point of about 1538°C, so 1500°C is the only option close to it.

113.s: A combustible gas is liberated when caustic soda solution is heated with
113.x: Zinc reacts with hot NaOH to give sodium zincate and hydrogen gas, which is combustible. NH4Cl would give ammonia, which is not combustible.

113.s: Which one of the following is the number of water molecules that share with two formula unit in Plaster of Paris?
113.x: Plaster of Paris is CaSO4·½H2O, i.e. (CaSO4)2·H2O, so two formula units share one water molecule.

113.s: What is detergent?
113.x: A detergent is a cleansing (purifying) agent that removes dirt and grease even in hard water, so 'refining agent' is the intended answer. It is not soap (detergents are soap substitutes), a medicine or a catalyst.

113.s: Which of the following is used to make light weight, but strong plastic ?
113.x: Methyl methacrylate polymerises to PMMA (perspex, acrylic glass), a light but strong, shatter-resistant plastic. Nylon is a fibre, polythene is soft, and PVC is heavier.

113.s: Which of the following is used to remove the green colour from glass?
113.x: Manganese dioxide ('glassmaker's soap') is added to glass to remove the green tint of ferrous iron. SiO2 is the glass itself, TiO2 a white pigment and SO2 a gas.

113.s: The Soda-acid fire extinguisher contains
o: sulphuric acid and solution of sodium hydrogen carbonate.
nitric acid and solution of sodium hydrogen carbonate.
sulphuric acid and solution of sodium carbonate.
sulphuric acid and solution of potassium carbonate.
113.x: A soda-acid extinguisher holds sulphuric acid and sodium hydrogen carbonate (baking soda) solution, which react to release CO2. Nitric acid, sodium carbonate or potassium carbonate are not used.

113.s: Which one of the following is used for water softening?
113.x: Calgon (sodium hexametaphosphate, Na6P6O18) softens permanent hard water. Mg(HCO3)2 causes hardness, and the other phosphates are not water softeners.

113.s: Nail polish remover contains
113.x: Nail polish remover is mainly acetone, a volatile solvent. Benzene, formaldehyde and acetic acid are not used for this.

113.s: Antacids are commonly used to get rid of acidity in the stomach. A commonly used antacid is
113.x: Milk of magnesia, Mg(OH)2, is a common mild antacid. Calcium hydroxide is too caustic, and the others are not antacids.

113.s: Which one of the following is used in the manufacture of soaps?
113.x: Soap is made by saponification of vegetable oils or animal fats with alkali (NaOH/KOH). Mobil, kerosene and cutting oils are petroleum (mineral) oils, which cannot be saponified.

113.s: Which one of the following elements is alloyed with iron to produce steel which can resist high temperatures and also have high hardness and abrasion resistance?
113.x: Tungsten is alloyed with iron to make tungsten (high-speed tool) steel that keeps its hardness at high temperatures and resists abrasion. Chromium mainly gives corrosion resistance (stainless steel) and nickel toughness.

113.s:
Which statements are correct?
I. In early 1930’s Nylon was prepared from coal, water and air.
II. Nylon was the first synthetic fibre.
III. Nylon fibre was strong elastic and light.
113.x: NCERT: nylon, the first fully synthetic fibre, was prepared in the 1930s from coal, water and air; it is strong, elastic and light. All three statements are correct.

113.s:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer from the codes given below.
List I
A. Morphine
B. Sodium
C. Boric acid
D. German silver
List II
1. Antiseptic
2. Alloy
3. Analgesic
4. Kerosene oil
Codes A B C D A B C D
113.x: Morphine is an analgesic (3), sodium is stored in kerosene (4), boric acid is an antiseptic (1) and German silver is an alloy (2), giving 3-4-1-2.

113.s: What is deposited on iron in the process of galvanisation?
113.x: Galvanisation coats iron with zinc to prevent rusting. Tin plating is a different process.

113.s:
Consider the following statements.
I. Photochromic lenses are lenses that darken on exposure to ultraviolet light.
II. Photochromic properties is due to embedded microcrystalline of silver chloride in the glass.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
113.x: Photochromic lenses darken in UV light because of microcrystals of silver halide (silver chloride) embedded in the glass, so both statements are correct.

113.s:
Assertion (A) Cellulose is used in making shatter-proof glass.
Reason (R) Polysaccharides are not soluble in water.
Codes
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
113.x: Cellulose derivatives (cellulose acetate/nitrate) formed the plastic interlayer in early shatter-proof (safety) glass, and polysaccharides such as cellulose are insoluble in water, but insolubility is not why it is used. Both true, R not the explanation.

113.s: Which one of the following is used in making Bullet proof Jacket’?
113.x: Body armour has used layered glass-fibre (fibrous glass) and aramid fibres; laminated glass is rigid bullet-resistant glazing for windows, not a jacket. Gun metal and lead are too heavy.

113.s:
When hard water is evaporated completely the white solid remains in the container. It may be due to the presence of
I. Carbonates of Ca and Mg.
II. Sulphates of Ca and Mg.
III. Chlorides of Ca and Mg.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
113.x: Hard water carries Ca and Mg bicarbonates (which become carbonates on heating), sulphates and chlorides; all of them stay as a white residue when the water evaporates.

113.s: Which pair of following is of Copper alloys?
113.x: Brass (Cu + Zn) and bronze (Cu + Sn) are copper alloys. Invar is iron-nickel and nichrome is nickel-chromium.

113.s:
: Which of the following is a correct match of chemical compounds and their uses? Chemical Compound
I. Analgesics
II. Antibiotics
III. Antiseptics
o: I.c II.a III.b Use a. To treat infections b. To prevent the growth of microorganisms c. To reduce or abolish pain
113.x: Analgesics reduce pain (c), antibiotics treat infections (a), and antiseptics prevent the growth of microorganisms on living tissue (b).

113.s: Chemically, baking soda is
113.x: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3). Baker's yeast is a fungus, and sodium chloride is common salt.

113.s: Which of the following is a chemical reaction?
o: Ice melting in a glass of lemonade
An aluminium vessel melting at very high heat
Bleaching changing the colour of a T-shirt
113.x: Bleaching changes the colour by a chemical (oxidation) reaction. Melting ice, a melting aluminium vessel and solidifying coconut oil are physical changes of state.

113.s: The nonstick pans used in Kitchens are coated with:
113.x: Non-stick pans are coated with polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE, Teflon). PVC, polyethylene and polyamide (nylon) are not.

113.s: Which type of chemical reaction is involved when baking soda is added to vinegar?
113.src: APPSC 2023 Lecturers in Government Degree Colleges
113.x: Baking soda (a base) reacts with the acetic acid of vinegar in an acid-base (neutralisation) reaction that releases CO2.

113.s: Which one of the following substances is used in photography and also as an antichlor ?
113.x: Sodium thiosulphate (hypo) is the photographic fixer and also an antichlor (removes excess chlorine).

113.s: Doctors, Artists and Sculptors use Calcium Sulphate which is popularly known as –
113.x: Calcium sulphate hemihydrate is Plaster of Paris, used by doctors for casts and by artists and sculptors. Quicklime is CaO and limestone CaCO3.

113.s: Which of the following is an example of a non-cellulosic fibre?
113.x: Rayon, linen and jute are made of cellulose; nylon is a synthetic polyamide, a non-cellulosic fibre.

113.s: Which of the following cannot be put out with water?
o: Fires that rise with an explosion
113.x: Water is not used on oil fires: oil floats on water and the burning oil spreads. Such fires are put out with foam, CO2 or sand.

113.s:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : A solution of table salt in a glass of water is homogeneous.
Reason (R) : A solution having different compositions throughout is homogeneous.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct
113.x: Salt dissolved in water is a homogeneous solution (A true). A homogeneous solution has the same composition throughout, so R is false.

113.s: Which of the following are the constituents of a soda acid fire extinguisher ?
o: Conc. Sulfuric acid and aluminium sulphate
Dil. Sulfuric acid and sodium carbonate
Dil. Sulfuric acid and sodium bicarbonate solution
Conc. Sulfuric acid and sodium carbonate solution
113.x: A soda-acid extinguisher holds sodium bicarbonate solution and sulphuric acid, which react to give CO2. Aluminium sulphate is used in foam extinguishers, and sodium carbonate is not the usual charge.

113.s: The gas used in fire extinguishers is
113.x: CO2 is used in fire extinguishers because it does not burn and cuts off the oxygen supply. Hydrogen burns, and SO2 and H2S are toxic.

113.s:
Assertion (A) : Phenyl is used as a household germicide.
Reason (R) : Phenyl is phenol derivative and phenol is an effective germicide.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
113.x: Phenyl (phenol-derived disinfectant) is used as a household germicide because phenol is an effective germicide. Both true and R explains A.

113.s: Bullet-proof vests are made from a fabric of
113.x: Bullet-proof vests are made of tightly woven high-strength synthetic polyamide fibres, nylon (ballistic nylon) and the aramid Kevlar. Jute and cotton are too weak, and steel wire is not a fabric.

113.s: Which of the following is a super cooled liquid?
113.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
113.x: Glass is an amorphous solid often called a supercooled liquid. Ice cream, coke and liquid nitrogen are not.

113.s: What is the phenomenon of the scattering of light as a light beam passes through a colloid called?
113.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
113.x: The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles; true solutions show none.

113.s: Which of the following is a super cooled liquid?
113.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
113.x: Glass is an amorphous solid often called a supercooled liquid. Ice cream, gelatine and helium are not.

113.s: ' Chiral ' in Greek represents
113.x: 'Chiral' comes from the Greek 'kheir' = hand: a chiral molecule is not superimposable on its mirror image, like left and right hands.

113.s: Because of impurities the boiling point of a liquid –
113.x: Dissolved impurities raise the boiling point of a liquid (elevation of boiling point).

113.s: On adding common salt to water, the boiling point and freezing point of water will :
113.x: A dissolved solute such as salt raises the boiling point (elevation) and lowers the freezing point (depression) of water. So boiling point increases and freezing point decreases.

113.s: Which one of the following changes occurs when salt is added into the water?
o: Boiling point is increased and freezing point decreased
Boiling point is decreased and freezing point is
Both boiling point and freezing point are decreased
Both boiling point and freezing point are increased
113.x: Salt raises the boiling point and lowers the freezing point of water (colligative properties).

113.s: Who discovered the rubber making process through the vulcanisation method ?
113.x: Charles Goodyear (1839) discovered vulcanisation – heating rubber with sulphur to make it hard and elastic. Dunlop made the pneumatic tyre.

113.s: Who among the following proposed that atom is indivisible?
113.x: Dalton's atomic theory (1808) held that atoms are indivisible. Rutherford found the nucleus; Avogadro dealt with molecules in gases.

113.s: Which one among the following is not a chemical change?
113.x: Evaporation of water is a physical change (no new substance). Curdling, ripening and burning make new substances – chemical changes.

113.s: The passage of an electric current through a conducting liquid causes … .
113.x: Current through a conducting liquid (electrolyte) decomposes it – a chemical reaction (electrolysis, electroplating).

113.s: Through the reaction of benzene and chlorine in the presence of catalyst say iron. Which of the following would be obtained?
113.x: Benzene + Cl2 with iron (FeCl3) catalyst undergoes electrophilic substitution to give chlorobenzene. Benzene hexachloride needs UV light (addition).

113.s:
Statement I All compounds contain more than one element. Statement II All compounds are heterogeneous mixtures.
Codes
o: Both the statements are individually true and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.
Both the statements are individually true but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
113.x: Every compound has two or more elements chemically combined (I true), but compounds are pure, homogeneous substances, not heterogeneous mixtures (II false).

113.s:
Statement I Glass is not considered as a true compound. Statement II Glass does not have a definite melting point.
Codes
o: Both the statements are individually true and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.
Both the statements are individually true, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
113.x: Glass is an amorphous mixture of silicates (a supercooled liquid), so it is not a true compound and has no sharp melting point – the printed key takes II as the reason for I.

113.s: A thick paste of cement, sand and water is called
113.x: Cement + sand + water paste = mortar; concrete also has gravel, and RCC has steel bars.

113.s: Which of the following is a major component of German silver?
113.x: German silver is copper (~60%) + zinc + nickel; it has no silver. Copper is the major component.

113.s: What are the maximum numbers of electrons that can be present in a shell represented by shell number ‘n’?
113.x: Maximum electrons in shell n = 2n² (K 2, L 8, M 18, N 32).

113.s:
An acid is a substance which
I. is sour in taste.
II. turns red litmus paper into blue.
113.x: Acids are sour and turn blue litmus red; turning red litmus blue is a property of bases, so only I is correct.

113.s: Which of the following is an aldehyde?
113.x: The suffix '-al' marks an aldehyde: propanal (CH3CH2CHO). Propanol is an alcohol, propanone a ketone, propyne an alkyne.

113.s: The oxidation number of nickel in K4[Ni(CN)4] is
113.x: In K4[Ni(CN)4]: 4(+1) + x + 4(−1) = 0, so x = 0 – nickel is in the zero oxidation state.

113.s: Which one of the following oxides dissolves in water?
113.x: Na2O is a basic alkali-metal oxide that dissolves in water to form NaOH. CuO, Al2O3 and Fe2O3 are insoluble.

113.s: If formula of sodium salt of an anion X is Na 2X , then the formula of its aluminium salt would be
113.x: Na2X means X has valency 2 (X²⁻); with Al³⁺ the neutral formula is Al2X3.

113.s: According to which one of the following laws it is indicated that when two or more gases react with one another, their volumes bear a simple ratio?
113.x: Gay-Lussac's law of combining volumes: reacting gases and gaseous products bear simple whole-number volume ratios.

113.s: Which of the following is a heterogeneous mixture?
113.x: A suspension (e.g. muddy water) is a heterogeneous mixture; a solution is homogeneous.

113.s: Silver ware turns black after a period of time due to the formation of
113.x: Silver reacts with hydrogen sulphide in the air to form black silver sulphide (Ag2S) – tarnishing.

113.s: How many elements are there in the 5th Period of Modern Periodic Table?
113.x: The 5th period (Rb to Xe) has 18 elements; periods 2–3 have 8, 4–5 have 18, 6–7 have 32.

113.s: JJ Thomson’s proposed model of atom is generally called ………… model.
113.x: J.J. Thomson's atom – electrons embedded in a positive sphere – is the plum-pudding model.

113.s: The atomic weights are expressed in terms of atomic mass unit. Which one of the following is used as standard?
113.x: Atomic masses are expressed relative to carbon-12: 1 u = 1/12 the mass of a ¹²C atom (since 1961).

113.s: If we plot a graph between volume V and inverse of pressure p (i.e. 1/p) for an ideal gas at constant temperature T, the curve so obtained is a
113.x: Boyle's law V = k(1/p) at constant T, so V against 1/p is a straight line through the origin (V against p is a hyperbola).

113.s: Which of the following is the maximum number of electrons that can be present in M-shell?
113.x: The M shell is n = 3: 2n² = 18 electrons.

113.s: The number of maximum electrons in N shell is
113.x: The N shell is n = 4: 2n² = 32 electrons.

113.s: The bond which is present between water molecules is
113.x: Neighbouring water molecules are linked by hydrogen bonds, which give water its high boiling point. The O–H bonds within one molecule are covalent, not the bond between molecules.

113.s: Which one of the following is mono- atomic ?
113.x: Noble gases such as helium exist as single atoms. Hydrogen is diatomic (H2), phosphorus P4 and sulphur S8.

113.s: The proposition ‘equal volumes of different gases contain equal numbers of molecules at the same temperature and pressure’ is known as
113.x: Avogadro's hypothesis (1811) states that equal volumes of all gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules. Gay-Lussac's law is about combining volumes.

113.s: Which of the following is not a noble gas?
113.x: Hydrogen is a reactive non-metal, not a noble gas. Helium, neon and argon are noble gases with full outer shells, hence chemically unreactive.

113.s: Iron sheet kept in moist air covered with rust. Rust is
o: a mixture of iron and dust
a mixture of iron, oxygen and water
113.x: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, Fe2O3·xH2O, a chemical compound. It is not an element or a mere mixture.

113.s: Constantan is an alloy of copper and ......
113.x: Constantan is a copper-nickel alloy (about 55:45) with a nearly constant resistance. Tin, iron and aluminium are not its partners.

113.s: Which one of the following compounds does not exhibt a different oxidation number of the same element?
113.x: In Fe2O3 every iron is +3. Pb3O4 (Pb +2, +4), Fe3O4 (Fe +2, +3) and Mn3O4 (Mn +2, +3) are mixed-valence oxides.

113.s: Multiplication of equivalent weight and valency of an element is equal to …… .
113.x: Equivalent weight = atomic weight / valency, so equivalent weight × valency = atomic weight. Density and atomicity are unrelated.

113.s: The rusting of iron nail
o: does not affect weight but iron is oxidised.
does not affect weight but iron is reduced.
113.x: Rusting adds oxygen and water to iron (Fe2O3·xH2O), so the nail gains weight. Iron is oxidised, not reduced.

113.s: Which one of the following will not produce carbon dioxide on reacting with an aqueous solution of hydrochloric acid?
113.x: Limestone, chalk and marble are all CaCO3 and release CO2 with HCl. Quicklime (CaO) is an oxide, giving only CaCl2 and water.

113.s: Inert gases are
113.x: Inert (noble) gases have complete outer shells, so they are stable and chemically unreactive. They are not very active.

113.s: Ultra purification of a metal is done by :
113.x: Zone refining melts a narrow zone that carries impurities along, yielding ultra-pure metals. Smelting and leaching are extraction steps.

113.s:
Which of the following solutions will not change the colour of blue litmus paper to red?
I. Acid solution
II. Base solution
III. Common salt solution
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
113.x: Only acids turn blue litmus red. A base (blue stays blue) and neutral common salt solution do not change it.

113.s:
Which of the following is/are state function/functions ? I. q + W
II. q
III.W
IV. H − TS
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
113.x: q + W equals ΔU, and H − TS is the Gibbs energy G, both state functions. Heat q and work W separately depend on the path.

113.s: White Phosphorus glows in the dark due to
113.x: White phosphorus slowly oxidises in air and the reaction gives off light (phosphorescence/chemiluminescence). It has a low, not high, ignition temperature.

113.s: In which one of the following is the valence electronic configuration, ns2 np 3 found?
113.x: Nitrogen (1s² 2s² 2p³) has the valence configuration ns² np³. Carbon is 2p², oxygen 2p⁴ and argon 3p⁶.

113.s: The pH of fresh ground water slightly decreases upon exposure to air because
o: carbon dioxide from air is dissolved in the water.
oxygen from air is dissolved in the water.
the dissolved carbon dioxide of the ground water escapes into air.
the dissolved oxygen of the ground water escapes into air.
113.x: CO2 from the air dissolves to form weak carbonic acid, lowering pH slightly. Dissolved oxygen does not change pH.

113.s: Rust needs three components to occur i.e. .........
113.x: Rusting needs iron, oxygen and moisture together. Nitrogen and helium play no part.

113.s: Which of the following elements is found in all organic compounds?
113.x: Organic compounds are by definition carbon compounds. Oxygen and nitrogen are in many but not all, and calcium is not typical.

113.s: The product of equivalent weight and valency of an element is equal to
113.x: Equivalent weight = atomic weight / valency, so equivalent weight × valency = atomic weight.

113.s: Which one of the following properties changes with valency?
113.x: Equivalent weight = atomic weight / valency, so it changes when an element shows a different valency. Atomic weight, molecular weight and density do not.

113.s: Under which condition real gas can work as an ideal gas?
113.x: At low pressure and high temperature molecules are far apart and fast, so attractions and molecular volume matter little and the gas behaves ideally.

113.s: Water is a good solvent. This is due to high
113.x: Water's high dielectric constant (about 80) weakens attraction between ions, so ionic compounds dissolve easily. Surface tension and specific heat are unrelated.

113.s: Which chemical law proposes that ‘soft drinks and soda bottles are sealed under high pressure to increase the solubility of CO2?
113.x: Henry's law says gas solubility in a liquid increases with the pressure of the gas, so CO2 is dissolved in soft drinks under high pressure.

113.s: Which one of the following types of glass can cut off ultraviolet rays?
113.x: Crookes glass contains cerium oxide and absorbs ultraviolet rays, so it is used in protective spectacles. Soda, Pyrex and Jena glass transmit UV.

113.s: Two electrons in an orbital are differentiated by which of the following?
113.x: Two electrons in the same orbital have the same n, l and m values and differ only in spin quantum number (+1/2 and -1/2), per the Pauli exclusion principle.

113.s: Tyndall effect is related to the ……… of light.
113.x: The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles, which makes the beam's path visible.

113.s: ………are homogeneous mixtures of two or more components.
113.x: Solutions are homogeneous mixtures of two or more components; emulsions are colloids (heterogeneous), and enzymes are proteins.

113.s: An emulsion is a colloid of a
113.x: An emulsion is a colloid of one liquid dispersed in another liquid, e.g. milk (fat in water).

113.s: Glass is soluble in
113.x: Hydrofluoric acid reacts with the silica in glass to form silicon tetrafluoride, so it dissolves glass. The other acids do not.

113.s: A molecule of a substance is similar to its atom for
113.x: A monoatomic molecule consists of a single atom, so the molecule is the same as the atom, as in noble gases.

113.s: Phosphorus is kept in water because
o: its ignition temperature is very high.
its ignition temperature is very low.
113.x: White phosphorus has a very low ignition temperature and catches fire in air, so it is stored under water.

113.s: Which of the following is NOT an unsaturated carbon compound?
113.x: Butane is a saturated alkane (only single bonds), whereas acetylene, pentene and benzene contain double or triple bonds and are unsaturated.

113.s: Methyl propane is an isomer of
113.x: Methylpropane (isobutane) has formula C4H10, the same as n-butane but with a branched chain, so they are structural isomers.

113.s: The elements of group in the Periodic table
113.x: Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons and hence similar chemical properties.

113.s: Which one of the following is not a periodic property i.e., does not show any trend on moving from one side to the other in the Periodic Table?
113.x: Radioactivity depends on nuclear stability, not on electron arrangement, so it shows no periodic trend. Atomic size, valency and electronegativity vary periodically.

113.s: Which of the following is the symbol of the metal that occurs in liquid form at ordinary temperature?
113.x: Mercury (Hg) is the only metal that is liquid at ordinary temperature. K, Ag and Pb are solids.

113.s: Which of the following elements has the lowest melting point?
113.x: Radon is a noble gas with a very low melting point (about -71 C), far lower than sodium, tin or radium.

113.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
I. Metallic oxides are said to be basic oxides.
II. Non-metallic oxides are basic in nature.
III. All acids have similar chemical properties.
Codes
113.x: Metallic oxides are basic and all acids share similar properties (they give H+ ions), so I and III are correct. Non-metallic oxides are acidic, not basic, so II is false.

113.s: Which of the following is a sweet smelling substance?
113.x: Esters have sweet, fruity smells; ammonia is pungent and alcohols are not typically sweet-smelling.

113.s: Ammonia (NH3) obtained from different sources always has same proportion of nitrogen and hydrogen. It proves the validity of law of
113.x: A compound always has the same elemental proportion by mass regardless of source, which is the law of constant (definite) proportions.

113.s: Which one of the following is used for writing on glass?
113.x: Hydrogen fluoride attacks and etches glass (silicon dioxide), so it is used to write on glass; graphite and others do not.

113.s: Liquid water is denser than ice due to
113.x: Hydrogen bonding makes ice an open lattice, so ice is less dense than liquid water.

113.s: Which compound, when dissolved in water, conducts electricity and forms a basic solution?
113.x: NaOH is a strong base that dissociates into ions, conducting electricity and giving a basic solution; HCl and CH3COOH are acids, and CH3OH does not ionise.

113.s: To weld metals together, high temperature required such a high temperature is obtained by burning
113.x: The oxyacetylene flame (acetylene burning in oxygen) gives the highest flame temperature (~3000 °C), used for welding; nitrogen does not support burning.

113.s: In a reaction, what is the loss of hydrogen by substance called as?
113.x: By the OIL RIG rule oxidation is loss (of electrons, and of hydrogen), so loss of hydrogen is oxidation, not reduction.

113.s: When a substance loses oxygen during a reaction, it is called … .
113.x: Loss of oxygen from a substance is reduction, the opposite of oxidation (gain of oxygen); corrosion is a different process.

113.s: When a spoon is to be electroplated with nickel the spoon is
o: dipped in a nickel sulphate solution.
made anode and a pure nickel rod, the cathode.
made cathode and a pure nickel red, the anode.
coated with nickel sulphate and dried.
113.x: In electroplating the object to be plated (the spoon) is made the cathode and the plating metal (pure nickel) is the anode, so nickel dissolves from the anode and deposits on the spoon.

113.s: The normal butane and isobutane are
113.x: n-Butane and isobutane share the formula C4H10 but differ in carbon chain (straight vs branched), so they are chain isomers.

113.s: Which of the following reaction is an example of exothermic reaction ?
o: The decomposition of vegetable matter into compost
113.x: Burning of natural gas, respiration and composting all release heat, so all are exothermic reactions.

113.s: Combustion of a candle is
113.x: Burning a candle is combustion, which releases heat and light, so it is exothermic. It is also a chemical change, not a physical one.

113.s: What is an endothermic reaction?
o: Reaction in which heat is released.
Reaction in which heat is absorbed.
Reaction in which neither heat is released nor absorbed.
113.x: An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from its surroundings, such as the decomposition of calcium carbonate on heating. A reaction that releases heat is exothermic.

113.s:
Following statements are made in connection with Carbon dioxide (CO2).
I. CO2 is a poisonous gas.
II. CO2 is an acidic oxide.
III. CO2 turns lime water milky.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
113.x: CO2 is an acidic oxide (forms carbonic acid with water) and turns lime water milky due to calcium carbonate formation. It is not poisonous, only an asphyxiant at high concentration, so statement I is wrong.

113.s: Which of the following gas causes explosion in coal mines?
113.x: Methane (firedamp) mixes with air in coal mines and forms an explosive mixture; CO2 and nitrogen are not flammable.

113.s: In a periodic table, while moving from left to right in a period, number of remains same.
113.x: Moving left to right across a period, electrons and protons increase by one per element, but the number of shells (the period number) stays the same.

113.s: Which one of the following substances is not a mixture?
113.x: Ice is just solid water, a pure compound, so it is not a mixture; ice-cream, air and honey are mixtures of several components.

113.s: Which one of the following elements exists in liquid state at room temperature ?
113.x: Mercury is the only metal liquid at room temperature; lead, sodium and calcium are solids.

113.s: Which of the following metal remains in liquid form at room temperature?
113.x: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature; cadmium, germanium and tin are solids.

113.s: Which one of the following carbon compounds will not give a sooty flame?
113.x: Hexane is a saturated alkane with a low carbon percentage and burns with a clean flame. Benzene, naphthalene and anthracene are aromatic and carbon-rich, so they burn with a sooty flame.

113.s: Which one of the following reducing agents can also act as an oxidising agent?
113.x: SO2 has sulphur in the +4 state, so it can be oxidised to +6 or reduced to lower states and acts as both. H2 and HI act mainly as reducing agents, and H2S too.

113.s: The gas which turns lime water milky is
113.x: CO2 reacts with lime water (calcium hydroxide) to form insoluble calcium carbonate, which makes it milky.

113.s: Yellow colour of usual nitric acid is due to the presence of which one of the following?
113.x: Nitric acid decomposes in light to give brown NO2, which dissolves in the acid and gives it a yellow colour.

113.s: In which of the following pairs are the Isoelectronic ions?
113.x: Na+ and O2− both have 10 electrons, so they are isoelectronic. In the other pairs the electron counts differ.

113.s: Which one of the following is a reduction reaction?
113.x: In 2HgO → 2Hg + O2, mercury(II) oxide loses oxygen and Hg is reduced from +2 to 0. The other reactions are oxidation or combination reactions.

113.s: Which one of the following polymers is made of proteins ?
113.x: Wool is made of the protein keratin, whereas cotton and jute are cellulose and rubber is a hydrocarbon polymer.

113.s: Which of the following is the first man made plastic that is bad conductor of heat ?
113.x: Bakelite, made from phenol and formaldehyde, was the first fully synthetic plastic and is a poor conductor of heat and electricity, so it is used for handles and switches. Polythene, nylon and Teflon came later.

113.s: Which of the following has a strong fruity fragrance?
113.x: Ethyl acetate is an ester, and esters have sweet, fruity smells. Methyl chloride, methanoic acid and methanol do not smell fruity.

113.s: On exposure to moist air, copper gains a green coat on its surface due to formation of which one of the following compounds ?
113.x: In moist air copper reacts with CO2, oxygen and water to form a green coat of basic copper carbonate (the patina of the Statue of Liberty). Copper oxide is black and copper sulphate is blue.

113.s: In which among the following molecules is the distance between two adjacent carbon atoms largest?
113.x: Ethane has a C-C single bond (about 154 pm), longer than the double bond in ethene, the triple bond in ethyne or the intermediate bond in benzene.

113.s: Which one of the following is not a monoatomic element ?
113.x: Iodine exists as diatomic I2 molecules, whereas copper, helium and barium occur as single atoms (monoatomic).

113.s: Which one of the following is the hardest metal?
113.x: Among the options, tungsten is the hardest metal; it also has the highest melting point.

113.s: Laughing gas is
113.x: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is laughing gas, a mild anaesthetic. Nitric oxide is NO, and the other two are higher oxides.

113.s: Chemically Dry Ice is –
o: Mixture of ice and common salt
113.x: Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide, which sublimes without melting. It is not ice, a salt mixture or sulphur.

113.s: Which among the following is not a polymer ?
113.x: Caprolactam is the monomer from which nylon-6 is made, so it is not a polymer. Nylon, Teflon and polystyrene are polymers.

113.s: Which one of the following colours is supplied by Sodium Chromate?
113.x:
Official key / most books: Red. Strictly: sodium chromate is a yellow solid; the orange-red salt is sodium dichromate (Wikipedia, Sigma-Aldrich).
The UPPSC key and books give red for sodium chromate (Na2CrO4). Blue, green and black are not linked to it.

113.s: Which of the following is the main ingredient of cement?
113.x: Limestone (~75%) is the main ingredient of cement, with clay the smaller part. Gypsum is added only to slow setting.

113.s:
Which of the following are exothermic processes ?
(i) Evaporation of water.
(ii) Dilution of an acid (H2SO4).
(iii) Reaction of water with quick lime.
(iv) Sublimation of camphor (crystals).
113.x: Diluting sulphuric acid and slaking quicklime with water both give out heat. Evaporation and sublimation absorb heat, so options with (i) or (iv) are wrong.

113.s: The pH value of distilled water exposed to air is?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: Distilled water left open dissolves CO2 from the air and forms carbonic acid, so its pH falls slightly below 7. It is exactly 7 only when pure and sealed.

113.s: How many covalent bonds are present in a Chloropropane molecule having molecular formula C3H7Cl?
113.x: C3H7Cl has 2 C–C, 7 C–H and 1 C–Cl single bonds = 10 covalent bonds.

113.s: Silver gets corroded due to ……… in air.
113.x: Silver tarnishes black by reacting with hydrogen sulphide in air to form silver sulphide (Ag2S).

113.s: Regarding the atom of a chemical element, the magnetic quantum number refers to
113.x: The magnetic quantum number (m) gives the orientation of an orbital in space; shape = azimuthal (l), size = principal (n), spin = s.

113.s: Which one of the following materials is very hard and very ductile?
113.x: Tungsten is very hard yet ductile enough to be drawn into bulb filaments. Carborundum and cast iron are hard but brittle; nichrome is used as heating wire, not for hardness.

113.s: Which one of the following elements exist in liquid state at room temperature?
113.x: Bromine is the only non-metal liquid at room temperature (mercury is the liquid metal); H2, O2 are gases and iodine a solid.

113.s: Which of the following metals is most ductile in nature?
113.x: Gold is the most malleable and ductile metal (1 g can be drawn into ~2 km of wire); silver comes next.

113.s: Which of the following is an example of chemical change?
o: Dispersion of white light into the light of 7 colours when passed through a prism.
Wet soil lump, when dried, gets fragile.
113.x: Cooking softens vegetables through irreversible changes in their chemical composition – a chemical change. Dispersion, drying of soil and dissolving salt are physical changes.

113.s: Which one of the following noble gases is not found in the atmosphere?
113.x:
Official key / most books: radon is not found in the atmosphere. Strictly: radon is present in trace amounts, released from radium decay in rocks and soil (NCERT Chemistry XII ch.7).
Radon is the radioactive noble gas; books list it as not a constituent of the atmosphere, while argon, krypton and xenon are.

113.s:
Consider the following statements
I. The carat is a unit of purity for gold alloys.
II. 18 carat gold is 24 parts pure gold and 6 parts another metal.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
113.x: Carat measures gold purity (I true). 18 carat = 18 parts gold in 24 (75%), not '24 parts gold + 6 parts other metal', so II is false.

113.s: Heaviest metal of the following is made of
113.x: Uranium (density ~19 g/cm³) is far denser than silver (~10.5), copper (~9) and aluminium (~2.7).

113.s: Which is not a Lewis acid?
113.x: A Lewis acid accepts an electron pair. AlCl3, BF3 and FeCl3 are electron-deficient acceptors; NH3 donates its lone pair and is a Lewis base.

113.s:
Consider the following statements about mixture?
I. A substance can be separated into other kinds of matter by any physical process.
II. Dissolved sodium chloride can be separated from water by the physical process of evaporation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
113.x: I is wrong: only a mixture, not a pure substance, can be separated by physical means. II is right: evaporation leaves dissolved salt behind.

113.s: Which gas is known as ‘noble gas’?
113.x: Helium is a Group 18 noble (inert) gas with a full outer shell; hydrogen, oxygen and CO2 are not.

113.s: The number of valence electrons in the O2− ion is
113.x: Oxygen has 6 valence electrons; O2− gains 2 more, completing an octet of 8.

113.s: Which of the following is the electron configuration of a metallic element?
113.x: 2, 8, 8, 2 (calcium) has 2 valence electrons that are easily lost – a metal. 2, 8 and 2, 8, 8 are noble gases; 2, 8, 7 is chlorine.

113.s:
Which of the following causes the rusting of iron?
I. Oxidation
II. Reduction
III. Chemical reaction with oxygen
IV. Chemical reaction with CO2
113.x: Rusting is oxidation of iron by reaction with oxygen (and moisture): I and III. It is not reduction, and CO2 is not the cause.

113.s:
Which one of the following types of medicines is used for treating indigestion? I. Antibiotic
II. Analgesic III. Antacid
IV. Antiseptic
113.x: Antacids (milk of magnesia, baking soda) neutralise excess stomach acid and relieve indigestion; antibiotics, analgesics and antiseptics do not.

113.s: The pH value of water is
113.x: Pure water is neutral, pH 7 at 25 °C.

113.s: Aspirin is obtained from
113.x:
Official key / most books: obtained from a tree (willow bark). Strictly: modern aspirin is synthesised from salicylic acid made from phenol (Kolbe reaction), i.e. petrochemical feedstock (NCERT Chemistry XII ch.11).
Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) traces to salicin from willow-tree bark, so books key 'a tree'.

113.s: Which one of the following is used in the production of explosives?
113.x: Glycerol is nitrated to nitroglycerine, the explosive in dynamite.

113.s: The foul smell of dead fish is due to the compound
113.x: The smell of dead fish comes from amines, chiefly trimethylamine, formed by bacterial breakdown – amino compounds.

113.s: The most reactive among the halogen is
113.x: Halogen reactivity falls down the group; fluorine, the most electronegative element, is the most reactive.

113.s: What percentage of gold is there in 14 carat gold?
113.x: Pure gold is 24 carat, so 14 carat = 14/24 ≈ 58% gold (22 carat 91.6%, 18 carat 75%).

113.s:
Read the Assertion and select the Logical reason:
Assertion: Glucose is highly soluble in water
Reason: Glucose forms Hydrogen bonds with water
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
113.src: APPSC 2021 Medical Officer (Ayurveda) In Ayush Department
113.x: Glucose has five –OH groups that hydrogen-bond with water, which is why it is highly soluble: R explains A.

113.s: In an atom, the order of filling up of the orbitals is governed by –
113.x: The Aufbau principle sets the order of filling orbitals (lowest energy first, n+l rule); Hund's rule and Pauli's principle govern how electrons occupy them.

113.s: Which of the following has highest melting point?
113.x: Boron (about 2,350–2,450 K) melts far above iron (~1,808 K), silicon (~1,690 K) and aluminium (933 K).

113.s: For two liquids A and B to form an ideal solution :
o: Entropy of mixing must be zero
Free energy of mixing should be zero
Enthalpy of mixing should be zero
113.x: An ideal solution has ΔH(mix) = 0 and ΔV(mix) = 0 (and obeys Raoult's law); entropy of mixing is positive and free energy of mixing negative.

113.s:
Consider the following :
Assertion (A) : Alum is applied to stop bleeding from cuts.
Reason (R) : Blood is a colloidal system containing colloidal particles. The Aluminium ions of Alum have high coagulating power so the blood gets coagulated.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct
113.x: Blood is a colloid; the Al³⁺ ions of alum coagulate it, so alum stops bleeding – R explains A.

113.s: The amount of solute present per unit volume or per unit mass of the solution/solvent is known as ____ in Chemistry.
113.x: The amount of solute per unit volume or mass of solution/solvent is the concentration of the solution.

113.s: A pungent smell often present near the urinals is due to :
113.x: Bacteria break down urea in urine into ammonia, which gives the pungent smell near urinals.

113.s: Lead Pencil contains –
113.x: Pencil 'lead' is graphite (mixed with clay), a form of carbon – no lead metal.

113.s: An example of physical change –
113.x: Dissolving sugar in water is physical (no new substance, reversible by evaporation); tarnishing, burning and curdling are chemical.

113.s: When any one experiences acidity problem, he may get immediate relief by taking a glass of water in which, a tea spoon of the following substance is dissolved?
113.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
113.x: Acidity is neutralised by a weak base such as baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) or an antacid dissolved in water; a strong base would harm the body.

113.s: Which of the following is an example of colloid?
113.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
113.x: Milk is the classic colloid (an emulsion of fat in water); sugar solution is a true solution and muddy water a suspension. (Water-in-oil is also an emulsion, but milk is the textbook answer.)

113.s: The best source of iodine in our diet is:
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
113.x: Iodised salt is the main everyday dietary source of iodine and the chief way India prevents goitre. Seaweed is the richest natural source, but it is not a staple of our diet.

113.s: Which one of the following is not an essential micronutrient for plants?
113.x: Boron, zinc and copper are essential plant micronutrients; sodium is not required by most plants. So sodium is the answer.

113.s: Kjeldal method is used for the estimation of
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: The Kjeldahl method measures nitrogen, which is multiplied by 6.25 to give crude protein. Crude fibre, ether extract (fat) and ash have their own methods.

113.s: The presence of this vitamin in feed is compulsory to prevent cage layer fatigue in Chickens.
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Cage layer fatigue is a bone disorder of laying hens prevented by enough vitamin D, calcium and phosphorus in feed, so 'all of these' is right.

113.s: Rickets in chickens is caused due to deficiency of
113.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
113.x: Rickets in chickens is caused by vitamin D3 deficiency; birds use D3 (cholecalciferol) far better than D2. Vitamins A, B12 and E cause other disorders.

113.s: Sea weeds are the main and important source of the following element :
113.x: Seaweeds are the richest natural source of iodine. Chlorine and bromine are not what seaweeds are prized for.

113.s: Seaweeds are an important source of which one of the following?
113.x: Seaweeds (kelp) concentrate iodine from sea water and are the richest natural source of iodine; they are not a chief source of sulphur, chlorine or bromine in diet.

113.s:
Consider the following elements.
I. Cobalt
II. Phosphorus
III. Zinc
Which of the above elements are required for maintaining the healthy human body?
113.x: Phosphorus (bones, ATP), zinc (enzymes) and cobalt (in vitamin B12) are all needed by the human body.

113.s: Hypokalemia is caused by the deficiency of ……… .
113.x: Hypokalemia means low blood potassium (kalium); low iodine causes goitre, low iron anaemia and low calcium hypocalcaemia.

113.s: Which of the following are required for the formation of bones and teeth?
113.x: Bones and teeth are made of calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite), so calcium and phosphorus are needed; sodium and potassium are body-fluid ions and iron is for haemoglobin.

113.s: Which one of the following is a rich source of iron?
113.x: Spinach is the iron-rich food of the four (book key); carrot gives vitamin A, pea protein and rice carbohydrate.

113.s: Among the following which fruit is a rich source of iron?
113.x: Karonda (Carissa carandas) is noted for its high iron content and is used against anaemia; it also has vitamin C. Jamun, loquat and guava are not iron-rich fruits.

113.s: Besides proteins and carbohydrates, other elements of nutritional value found in milk, include :
113.x: Milk is rich in calcium and potassium but poor in iron, so 'calcium and potassium' is right; any option with iron is wrong.

113.s: Which one among these is related to the deficiency of potassium ?
113.x:
Book key: low blood pressure. Strictly, low potassium is better known for muscle weakness/paralysis and tends to raise blood pressure; hypotension is only an occasional sign (NORD, Hypokalemia; PMF General Science Part 3).
The book key is low blood pressure. Muscle weakness and paralysis are the best-known signs of potassium deficiency, so option (a) is tempting; anaemia is iron and blurry vision vitamin A.

113.s: Iodised salt is useful because it–
113.x: Iodised salt is table salt mixed with a minute amount of various salts of the element iodine. Iodine deficiency can cause thyroid gland problems.

113.s: Which of the following species possesses a corymb inflorescence?
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
113.x: Gulmohar (Delonix regia) bears flowers in corymbs, where lower flower stalks are longer so the flowers come to one level. Mango and teak have panicles; Gliricidia has racemes.

113.s: Which of the following is not a chemical fertilizer?
113.x: Urea (N), superphosphate (P) and potassium nitrate (K, N) are fertilisers. Sodium sulphate supplies no major plant nutrient, and sodium is not essential for most plants.

113.s: Gaseous exchange takes place in leaves through tiny pores for the purpose of photosynthesis. What are these pores ?
113.x: Stomata are the tiny pores in leaves through which gases are exchanged. Chloroplast and chlorophyll are involved in photosynthesis, and the vacuole is a storage sac.

113.s: The ultimate cause of water movement in a plant stem against gravity is
113.x: Transpiration from leaves creates a suction (transpiration pull) that draws water up the xylem against gravity, so it is the ultimate cause.

113.s: In which one of the following physiological processes, excess water escapes in the form of droplets from a plant ?
113.x: Guttation is the loss of excess water as liquid droplets from leaf margins. Transpiration loses water as vapour.

113.s: Which type of plants are very tall and have hard and thick brown stem?
113.x: Trees are very tall plants with a hard, thick, brown woody stem (trunk). Herbs have soft green stems and shrubs are shorter and bushy.

113.s: Who propounded the theory of evolution?
113.x: Charles Darwin propounded the theory of evolution by natural selection (On the Origin of Species, 1859). Wallace independently proposed a similar idea, but Darwin is credited.

113.s: What is the basis of classifying various plant tissues as meristematic tissue and permanent tissue?
113.x: Meristematic tissues are classified as such because their cells keep dividing, while permanent tissues have lost the capacity to divide. So the basis of classification is dividing capacity.

113.s: Which one among the following produces seeds but not flowers ?
113.x: Pine is a gymnosperm and bears naked seeds in cones without flowers. Cashew, coffee and groundnut are angiosperms that flower.

113.s: Who was written book named ‘Origin of Species’?
113.x: Charles Darwin wrote 'On the Origin of Species' (1859), presenting natural selection.

113.s: Smallest flowering plant is
113.x: Wolffia (duckweed) is the smallest flowering plant known.

113.s: Mangifera indica is the scientific name of
113.x: Mangifera indica is the binomial name of the mango; guava, amla and jackfruit have different scientific names.

113.s: In the names Mangifera Indica (mango), Solanum tuberosum (potato) and Panthera leo (lion). The terms Mangifera, Solanum and Panthera represent the higher level of
113.x: The genus names Mangifera, Solanum and Panthera are taxa, i.e. units of classification; the specific epithet is the second word (indica, tuberosum, leo).

113.s: Which one of the following denotes a ‘true’ fruit?
o: When only the thalamus of the flower grows and develops into a fruit.
When only the receptacle of the flower develops into a fruit.
When fruit originates only from the calyx of a flower.
When only the ovary of the flower grows into a fruit.
113.x: A true fruit develops only from the ovary of the flower; fruits that develop from other parts such as the thalamus or receptacle are false fruits.

113.s: If the xylem of a plant is mechanically blocked, which of the following functions of the plant will be affected?
113.x: Xylem conducts water and dissolved minerals (solutes) upward, so blocking it affects the transport of both.

113.s: Which one of the following is not a component of conducting tissue in plants?
113.x: Pericycle is a layer of cells just inside the endodermis and is not a conducting element; xylem (tracheids, fibres) and phloem (sieve tubes) are the conducting tissues.

113.s: What is the shape of the two guard cells which enclose stomata ?
113.x: Guard cells enclosing a stoma are kidney (bean) shaped in dicots.

113.s: The only living tissue in plant xylem is
113.x: Xylem parenchyma is the only living cell type in xylem; tracheids, vessels (trachea) and fibres are dead at maturity.

113.s: Which element is specifically required by plants for the synthesis of amino acids and proteins?
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Nitrogen is needed for amino acids, proteins, chlorophyll and nucleic acids. C, H and O are in all organic compounds, and iron is for chlorophyll synthesis.

113.s: Which of the following is not a Primary function of a green leaf?
113.x: Food making, gas exchange and transpiration are leaf functions; conduction of food and water is mainly done by the vascular tissue of the stem.

113.s: What is the yellow dust present in the middle of a flower called?
113.x: The yellow dust in the middle of a flower is pollen, made in the anthers of the stamens.

113.s: A Parenchyma cell which stores ergastic substance is known as
113.x: Idioblasts are specialised parenchyma cells that store ergastic substances such as crystals, tannins or oils.

113.s: What is thick vein present in the middle of the leaf called?
113.x: The thick central vein of a leaf is the midrib; venation is the pattern of veins.

113.s: Pollens are produced in
113.x: Pollen grains are produced in the anther of the stamen; the stigma only receives them.

113.s: In which part of the female flower, fertilisation take place?
113.x: Fertilisation takes place in the ovule inside the ovary; the pollen tube grows down from the stigma through the style.

113.s: Which among the following is a male part of a flower ?
113.x: The stamen (anther + filament) is the male part; stigma, style and the whole pistil are female.

113.s: Damage to the apical meristem of a growing young plant will affect the
113.x: The apical meristem at shoot and root tips causes growth in length, so damaging it affects the length of the plant.

113.s: Any one parameter is not good enough to demonstrate growth through the life of a flowering plant because
o: lateral meristems appear later in life.
apical meristems contribute to elongation while lateral meristems increase girth.
increase in protoplasm is difficult to measure directly.
113.x: NCERT: growth is basically an increase in protoplasm, which is difficult to measure directly, so proxies (weight, length, area, cell number) are used and no one of them suffices.

113.s: Which one of the following tissues is responsible for increase of girth in the stem of a plant?
113.x: The lateral meristem (vascular and cork cambium) adds girth; intercalary meristem adds length at internodes.

113.s: Which of the following pair represent the Correct pair of reproductive parts of a flower ?
113.x: The reproductive whorls are the stamens (male) and carpels (female); sepals and petals are accessory whorls.

113.s:
Statement I Complex tissue is made up of more then one type of cells. Statement II Meristems are examples of permanent tissue.
Codes
o: Statement I is correct, but statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.
Both Statements I and II are correct.
Both Statements I and II are incorrect.
113.x: Complex tissues (xylem, phloem) have more than one cell type (I correct); meristems are dividing tissues, not permanent tissues (II incorrect).

113.s: Arrangement of leaves in a plant is called as ……… .
113.x: The arrangement of leaves on a stem is phyllotaxy (alternate, opposite, whorled).

113.s: Which one of the following features is an indication for modification of stem of a plant?
113.x: Potato is a stem tuber – its 'eyes' are nodes with buds, proof it is a modified stem. Onion scales are leaves, pea tendrils are modified leaflets and carrot is a root.

113.s: Fruit of which of the following plant is found in the underground soil?
113.x: The peanut flower stalk (peg) pushes the ovary into the soil, so the fruit (pod) ripens underground. Potato and onion are stems, carrot a root – not fruits.

113.s: Flower in which pollination takes place through insect, their pollen grains are
113.x: Insect-pollinated flowers have rough, sticky pollen that clings to insects. Smooth, dry, light pollen is typical of wind pollination.

113.s: To study meiosis in plants, the best part would be
113.x: Meiosis occurs in reproductive tissue, so young anthers are best. Root and shoot apices and leaf cells divide by mitosis.

113.s: Intercalary meristems are found in
113.x: Intercalary meristems lie between mature tissues at the base of internodes (and leaves), as in grasses. Apical meristems occupy terminal and lateral buds.

113.s: Most of photosynthesis process occur in
o: blue and red region of light.
in the green and yellow region of light.
in the blue and orange region of light.
in the violet and orange region of light.
113.x: Chlorophyll absorbs mainly blue and red light, so most photosynthesis occurs there. Green and yellow light are largely reflected.

113.s:
Consider the following statements.
I. Annual rings are distinct in plants which grow in temperate region.
II. growing rings of plant is consist of spring wood and autumn wood.
Which of the statements given above is/ are correct about annual ring?
113.x: Both statements are true: annual rings are clear in temperate trees with marked seasons, and each ring has spring wood and autumn wood.

113.s: Which of the following plants is carnivorous ?
113.x: The Venus flytrap traps insects to get nitrogen. Cypress vine, amaryllis and hyacinth are ordinary flowering plants.

113.s:
Consider the following fuction of xylem.
I. Conduction of water
II. Conduction of minerals.
III. Mechanical support.
Which of the function (s) of xylem given above is/are correct?
113.x: Xylem conducts water and dissolved minerals, and its lignified cells give mechanical support. All three are correct.

113.s: Role of chlorophyll in photosynthesis is
113.x: Chlorophyll's role is to absorb light energy. Water is absorbed by roots and CO2 enters through stomata.

113.s: Which one of the following gas comes out during photosynthesis?
113.x: Photosynthesis takes in CO2 and gives out oxygen. Hydrogen and chlorine are not released.

113.s: The oxygen evolved during photosynthesis comes from splitting of
113.x: The oxygen given off in photosynthesis comes from splitting (photolysis) of water, as isotope (O-18) experiments showed, not from CO2.

113.s:
Match the structures given in column
(A) with the functions given in column (B). Column A Column B
A. Stomata
B. Xylem
C. Root hairs
D. Phloem
1. Absorption of water
2. Transpiration
3. Transport of food
4. Transportion of water
Codes A B C D A B C D
113.x: Stomata – transpiration (2), xylem – water transport (4), root hairs – absorption of water (1), phloem – food transport (3): code 2 4 1 3.

113.s: Which botanist is credited with creating one of the first widely used natural systems of plant classification ?
113.x:
Official key: August Wilhelm Eichler (wording from Britannica). NCERT Biology XI Ch3 credits the natural system of flowering plants to George Bentham and Joseph Dalton Hooker, so Hooker is also defensible.
Britannica describes August Wilhelm Eichler's system as one of the first widely used natural systems of plant classification (it was the first phylogenetic one and the base of Engler's system). Hooker, with Bentham, gave the other famous natural system, which is the tempting option; Robert Brown and Joseph Banks did not create such a system.

113.s: Which of these is the energy conversion that happens in the process called photosynthesis?
113.x:
In photosynthesis, plants convert light (solar) energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.
In photosynthesis, plants convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.

113.s: Which one of the following statements about transport mechanism in plants is correct?
o: Diffusion of ions and small molecules across cell membrane requires energy.
Active transport of ions and small molecules across cell membrane against concentration gradient requires energy.
Cells conserve energy and no energy is required for transport of ions and small molecules against concentration gradient.
Cells do not transport ions across their membrane as these are charged molecules.
113.x: Active transport moves ions against the concentration gradient and requires energy (ATP); diffusion is passive.

113.s: Which of the following is not a process of asexual reproductions?
113.x: Syngamy is the fusion of gametes, a feature of sexual reproduction; budding, gemmulation and fragmentation are asexual methods.

113.s: The corner of the cells of collenchyma tissue in plant are thickened due to deposition of
113.x: Collenchyma has cell corners thickened with cellulose and pectin, giving flexible support; lignin is characteristic of sclerenchyma.

113.s: Which one of the following is active transport?
o: It is the movement of a substance against a diffusion gradient with the use of energy from respiration.
It is the movement of a substance against a diffusion gradient without the use of energy.
It is the movement of a substance against a diffusion gradient with the use of energy from photosynthesis.
It is the movement of a substance along a diffusion gradient with the use of energy from respiration.
113.x: Active transport moves a substance against its concentration gradient using energy (ATP) from respiration; movement along the gradient or without energy is diffusion or passive transport.

113.s: Process by which plant prepare their food is
113.x: Plants prepare their food by photosynthesis, using light, CO2 and water in chlorophyll-containing cells.

113.s: Which of the following organelles of a cell is/are involved in photosynthesis ?
113.x: Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts, which contain chlorophyll; mitochondria are for respiration.

113.s: The increase in length of stems and roots in plants is due to
113.x: Apical meristems at the tips of stems and roots cause increase in length (primary growth); lateral meristem increases girth.

113.s: Which one of the following organisms has vascular tissues ?
113.x: Marsilea is a pteridophyte and has xylem and phloem. Cladophora and Anabaena are algae and Penicillium is a fungus, so none of them has vascular tissue.

113.s: Marsilea, fern and horse tail are examples of which one of the following plant groups ?
113.x: Marsilea, ferns and horsetails (Equisetum) are all seedless vascular plants, so they belong to Pteridophyta.

113.s: In the plant kingdom, ferns and fern allies belong to which group ?
113.x: Ferns and fern allies (horsetails, club mosses) make up the Pteridophyta.

113.s: Which of the following is/are the main absorbing organ/organs of plants?
113.x: Roots are the main absorbing organs of plants, taking up water and minerals from the soil through root hairs.

113.s: Which one of the following statements about classification of plants is correct?
o: Thallophytes have well differentiated body design.
Vascular system is not found among Bryophytes.
113.x: Bryophytes lack a vascular system (xylem and phloem). Thallophytes lack a differentiated body, Funaria is a moss, and pteridophytes are cryptogams, not phanerogams.

113.s: Pteridophytes are also known as
113.x: Pteridophytes have vascular tissue but no seeds or flowers, so they are called vascular cryptogams.

113.s: The nature of stele in primitive vascular plants was
113.x: Primitive vascular plants had a protostele, in which the xylem forms a solid core surrounded by phloem.

113.s: A flower is a modified
113.x: A flower is a modified shoot, formed from the shoot apical meristem, with its parts as modified leaves.

113.s: Gymnosperms are characterised by
113.x: Gymnosperms (e.g., pines, cycads) bear naked seeds not enclosed in an ovary or fruit; angiosperms have seeds inside fruits.

113.s: First compound which is fixed during photosynthesis is
113.x: In the Calvin cycle CO2 combines with RuBP to give 3-phosphoglyceric acid (PGA), the first stable product of carbon fixation. Glucose and starch form later.

113.s: Which one of the following is not used as fertiliser?
113.x: Ammonium nitrate, phosphate and sulphate supply nitrogen or phosphorus to crops and are fertilisers. Ammonium sulphide is not used as one.

113.s: An element present in Chlorophyll is
113.x: Chlorophyll has magnesium at the centre of its porphyrin ring.

113.s: Double fertilisation occurs among
113.x: Double fertilisation, in which one sperm fuses with the egg and the other with the polar nuclei, is unique to angiosperms.

113.s: The technique of the development of fruits without fertilisation is known as
113.x: Parthenocarpy is the development of fruit without fertilisation, giving seedless fruit. Parthenogenesis is the development of an embryo from an unfertilised egg, not of a fruit.

113.s: The development of a fruit without fertilisation is called …
113.x: Parthenocarpy is fruit development without fertilisation. Apomixis is seed formation without fertilisation, so it is not the answer.

113.s: Which of the following is correct sequence of the events occurring during sexual reproduction in plants?
o: Seedling, Embryo formation, Pollination, Fertilisation, Division of zygote
Embryo formation, seedling, Pollination, Fertilisation, Division of zygote
Pollination, Fertilisation, Division of zygote, Embryo formation, Seedling
Seedling, Embryo formation, Division of zygote, Pollination, Fertilisation
113.x: In plant sexual reproduction, pollination is followed by fertilisation, then division of the zygote, embryo formation and finally the seedling.

113.s: Which one of the following statements about meristematic tissue in plants is correct?
o: These are dead tissues and from wood.
They provide flexibility to plant due to their thickened walls.
These are present is the bark of a tree only.
Growth occurs in plants due to division of cells of these tissues.
113.x: Meristematic tissue is made of actively dividing cells, and its cell division drives plant growth. It is not dead and is not limited to bark.

113.s: Which one of the following plant tissues has dead cells?
113.x: Sclerenchyma cells have thick lignified walls and are dead at maturity. Epidermis, parenchyma and collenchyma are living tissues.

113.s: The hormone related to drought tolerance is
113.x: Abscisic acid is the stress hormone. It closes stomata and so helps the plant tolerate drought.

113.s: Which one of the following agents does not contribute to propagation of plants through seed dispersal ?
113.x: Seeds are dispersed by wind, water and animals. Fungi do not disperse seeds.

113.s: The maximum amount of water, which plants need to grow, is absorbed by the following?
113.x: Root hairs are the main water-absorbing part of the root; water enters them by osmosis from the soil, so they absorb the most water for the plant.

113.s: Which among the following is an example of dicot seed?
113.x: Pulses (legumes) have two cotyledons so they are dicots; rice, wheat and maize are monocot cereals.

113.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding vegetative propagation of plants ?
I. Vegetative propagation produces clonal population.
II. Vegetative propagation helps in eliminating the virus.
III. Vegetative propagation can be practised most of the year.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
113.x: Vegetative propagation gives clones (I) and can be done through much of the year (III). It does not eliminate viruses, since the virus passes on to the offspring, so II is wrong.

113.s: The by-product of photosynthesis is
113.x: In photosynthesis, water is split and oxygen is released as the by-product; sugar is the main product, and CO2 is a raw material.

113.s: Essential requirements for a seed to germinate
113.x: A seed needs water, air (oxygen) and a suitable temperature to germinate. Soil and sunlight are not essential; seeds sprout on wet cotton in the dark.

113.s: It is harmful to sleep under a tree at night because the tree releases :
113.x: At night trees cannot photosynthesise but keep respiring, so they release carbon dioxide. They do not give out carbon monoxide or sulphur dioxide.

113.s: Which light is most effective in photosynthesis?
113.x: Red light (~655 nm) gives the highest rate of photosynthesis. Blue is also absorbed, but green is mostly reflected.

113.s: Chlorophyll absorbs ____ wavelengths of the sunlight.
o: More than one of the above
113.x: Chlorophyll absorbs mainly red and blue light and reflects green, which is why leaves look green. Options with green are therefore wrong.

113.s: Which of the following has the shortest gestation period?
113.x: A goat carries its young about 150 days, less than a cow (~280), a buffalo (~310) or a camel (~390). The cow is the tempting option, but its gestation is nearly twice as long.

113.s: Which animal can not digest fibres properly ?
113.x: The pig is a monogastric omnivore and cannot digest fibre well. Goats and cows are ruminants, and elephants are hindgut fermenters, so their gut microbes break down cellulose.

113.s: Desert plants have longer root system because :
o: High temperature of the soil stimulates the growth of
Roots grow in search of water
Soil does not contain water, hence becomes compact
Roots moves opposite to the solar heat
113.x: Desert plants have long roots because roots grow towards water (hydrotropism), and in deserts the water lies deep. Soil heat does not cause it.

113.s: The range of pH of urine of herbivorous animals
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Herbivores have alkaline urine (pH about 7–8) because of their plant diet. Carnivores' urine is acidic, so the lower ranges are wrong.

113.s: In a bisexual flower, if androecium and gynoecium mature at different times, the phenomenon is known as
113.x: Dichogamy = anthers and stigma of a bisexual flower mature at different times, which favours cross-pollination. Herkogamy is a physical barrier between them.

113.s: Which of the following elements is not essential for plant growth ?
