113.x: Sodium is not essential for most plants; potassium, calcium and magnesium are essential macronutrients.

113.s: Eight nucleated female gametophyte is found in
113.x: The typical angiosperm embryo sac (female gametophyte) is 7-celled and 8-nucleate (Polygonum type).

113.s: Among living organisms, which one of the following is the most responsible factor for bringing about the origin of a new species?
113.x:
Official key / most books: mutation. Strictly: mutation supplies variation, while reproductive isolation is what actually completes speciation (NCERT Biology XII ch.6).
Books and keys give mutation (de Vries) as the source of new heritable variation that leads to new species.

113.s: World first Camel hospital is located in which city?
113.x: The Dubai Camel Hospital (opened 2017) is billed as the world's first dedicated camel hospital.

113.s: In the context of organic evolution, the loss of limbs in snakes is explained by the phenomenon of
113.x:
Official key / most books: use and disuse of organs (Lamarck). Strictly: modern biology explains it by natural selection; Lamarckism is rejected (NCERT Biology XII ch.6).
Books and the key explain limb loss in snakes by Lamarck's use and disuse of organs.

113.s: Which one of the following elements is present in the green pigment of leaves?
113.x: Chlorophyll has a magnesium atom at the centre of its porphyrin ring (haemoglobin has iron).

113.s: Solar energy is converted into ATP in
113.x: In chloroplasts the light reactions convert solar energy into ATP (photophosphorylation) and NADPH; mitochondria make ATP from food, not from sunlight.

113.s: World’s first camel hospital is located in which city?
113.x: The Dubai Camel Hospital (opened 2017) is billed as the world's first dedicated camel hospital.

113.s: The reason of large scale diversity among the organisms is
113.x:
Official key / most books: adaptation. Strictly: diversity results from long-term evolution – natural selection acting on variation that mutation creates (NCERT Biology XII ch.6; Byjus NEET answer 'long-term evolutionary change').
Books and the BPSC key give adaptation – organisms adapting to varied environments – as the reason for large-scale diversity.

113.s: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to stigma of another flower of the same plant is called ?
113.x: Geitonogamy = pollen to another flower of the same plant; autogamy – same flower; xenogamy – a different plant.

113.s:
Consider the following statements
I. Homologous organs are common origin with different functions.
II. Analogous organs are different origin but perform similar function in different organisms.
III. Vestigial organs are non-functional and rudimentary organs in an organism which are fully developed and functional in phylogenetically related organisms.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: All three are correct definitions: homologous – same origin, different function; analogous – different origin, same function; vestigial – rudimentary organs functional in relatives.

113.s: Which of the following is poisonous for dogs?
113.x: Chocolate contains theobromine, which dogs metabolise slowly, so it is toxic to them.

113.s: The broad, green part of the leaf is called
113.x: The lamina (leaf blade) is the broad green part where most photosynthesis occurs; midrib – central vein, petiole – stalk, stipules – basal outgrowths.

113.s: At what age does bamboo flower?
113.x:
Printed key / books: 30 years. Strictly: it depends on the species – Melocanna baccifera (Mizoram mautam) flowers about every 48 years; PMF Part 3 p.34 says 50–100 years.
Bamboos flower only once, after long, species-specific intervals; the key takes about 30 years (Melocanna bambusoides ~30–35 years).

113.s: To which group of plants does the Banyan Tree belong?
113.x: The banyan (Ficus benghalensis) is a flowering, fruit-bearing plant – an angiosperm.

113.s:
Identify the correct pair(s) from the given pairs with respect to minerals and their function and choose the correct option.
I. Zinc - For insulin production
II. Phosphorus - Development of strong bones and teeth
III. Fluoride - Makes enamel of teeth hard and prevents dental caries
113.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
113.x: Zinc is needed for insulin synthesis and storage, phosphorus (with calcium) builds bones and teeth, and fluoride hardens tooth enamel and prevents caries – all three pairs are correct. Off-topic (nutrition), moved.

113.s: Which one of the following are richest sources of calcium:
113.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
113.x: Ragi (finger millet), amaranth and milk are among the richest common sources of calcium. Off-topic (nutrition), moved to book 5.

113.s: Which of the following nuts has the highest potassium content per equal weight?
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
113.x: Per 100 g, almonds (about 730 mg) have more potassium than peanuts (~705 mg), cashews (~660 mg) and walnuts (~440 mg).

113.s: What is the primary function of calcium in plants?
113.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
113.x: Calcium (as calcium pectate of the middle lamella) is needed for cell wall formation and development. ATP synthesis and electron transport rely on phosphorus, iron and magnesium.

113.s: Which of the following is matched INCORRECTLY?
o: Protein - Needed for the building of antibodies and immune system cells.
Vitamin A - Helps regulate the immune system and protect the body by keeping skin and tissues in the mouth.
Vitamin C - helps the body build healthy skin.
Zinc - Helps to activate immune cells and properly regulate their function.
113.src: APPSC Assistant Conservator of Forests General Studies & Men
113.x: Protein builds antibodies; vitamin A keeps skin and the linings of mouth, gut and airways healthy; vitamin C helps build skin (collagen) and antibodies; the printed key marks the zinc statement as the mismatch.

113.s: Out of the below, which food is richer in Zinc?
113.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
113.x:
Printed key: chicken (animal foods give well-absorbed zinc). Strictly, per 100 g almonds and dry legumes hold about as much or more zinc than chicken (general knowledge, not checked).
Animal foods such as chicken give well-absorbed zinc, so the printed key is chicken; green leafy vegetables are poor zinc sources. (Off-topic: nutrition.)

113.s: Which of the following diseases is caused due to deficiency of Ascorbic acid?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: Ascorbic acid is vitamin C, and its deficiency causes scurvy. Kwashiorkor is protein deficiency, glossitis is B2 and beri-beri B1.

113.s: Golden rice is a genetically modified plant where the incorporated gene is meant for the biosynthesis of
113.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
113.x: Golden rice carries genes for beta-carotene, the precursor of vitamin A. It is not designed for vitamin B, C or omega-3.

113.s:
Vitamins are a group of substances that are needed for normal cell function, growth, and development. Match the following Vitamins with their chemical name.
Vitamin:
I. Vitamin B2
II. Vitamin B6
III. Vitamin B3
IV. Vitamin B7
Chemical name:
a. Niacin
b. Riboflavin
c. Biotin
d. Pyridoxine
113.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
113.x: B2 is riboflavin, B6 pyridoxine, B3 niacin and B7 biotin, so I-b, II-d, III-a, IV-c.

113.s: Which of the following vitamins decomposes easily on heating?
113.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
113.x: Vitamin C is the vitamin most easily destroyed by heat (and by oxidation). The B group is partly heat-stable, and A and E are fat-soluble and more stable in cooking.

113.s: In which of the following is Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) available?
113.x: Thiamine (B1) is in the bran and husk layer of rice, which is why polished rice causes beri-beri. Carrot and beetroot are not B1 sources, and sunflower seeds are not the answer here.

113.s: Select the correct match of the vitamins with the deficiency diseases.
o: Vitamin B1 (thiamine) - pernicious anaemia (RBC deficient in haemoglobin)
Vitamin B2 (riboflavin) - cheilosis (fissuring at corners of mouth and lips), digestive disorders and burning sensation of the skin
Vitamin E - increased blood clotting time
Vitamin K - increased fragility of RBCs and muscular weakness
113.x: Riboflavin (B2) deficiency causes cheilosis and digestive disorders. Pernicious anaemia is B12, vitamin E is not about clotting, and vitamin K deficiency prolongs clotting time.

113.s:
Match the columns.
Vitamin:
A. Vitamin A
B. Vitamin D
C. Vitamin C
D. Vitamin K
Deficiency disease:
1. Scurvy
2. Night blindness
3. Excessive bleeding due to injury
4. Rickets
113.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
113.x: Vitamin A – night blindness, D – rickets, C – scurvy, K – excessive bleeding, so A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3.

113.s:
Match the following diseases in Column I with their causes in Column II
Column I:
1. Malaria
2. Goiter
3. Rickets
4. Night Blindness
Column II:
a. Vitamin D deficiency
b. Vitamin A deficiency
c. Iodine deficiency
d. Mosquito bite
113.src: General Studies & Mental Ability (paper title page missing i
113.x: Malaria spreads by mosquito bite, goitre is iodine deficiency, rickets vitamin D deficiency and night blindness vitamin A deficiency, so 1-d, 2-c, 3-a, 4-b.

113.s: Find the incorrect match.
113.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
113.x: Biotin is vitamin B7, not B12 (B12 is cobalamin), so that pair is incorrect. Thiamin B1, riboflavin B2 and niacin B3 are correct.

113.s: Which of the following can be associated with Vitamin C?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
113.x: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid. Hydrochloric, sulphuric and acetic acids are not vitamins.

113.s: What is another name for Vitamin B12?
113.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
113.x: Vitamin B12 is cobalamin. Riboflavin is B2, pyridoxine B6 and pantothenic acid B5.

113.s: Which Vitamin is known as anti pernicious Anemia factor?
113.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
113.x: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is the anti-pernicious-anaemia factor; its deficiency causes pernicious anaemia.

113.s: Scurvy is a deficiency of
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
113.x: Scurvy is caused by deficiency of ascorbic acid (vitamin C).

113.s: The richest source of Vitamin 'C' is:
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
113.x: Amla (Indian gooseberry) is the richest common source of vitamin C; chilli is the richest among vegetables.

113.s: Which of the following disease may be caused due to deficiency of Vitamin C?
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
113.x: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy (bleeding gums, poor wound healing).

113.s: Which Vitamin has Cobalt?
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
113.x: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) contains cobalt. B1, B2 and B6 have no metal.

113.s: Out of the below, which is richer in Vitamin D?
113.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
113.x:
Printed key: none. Strictly, none of the four contains vitamin D naturally; orange counts only as fortified orange juice (WebMD, Foods High in Vitamin D).
None of these is a natural vitamin D source (fresh fruits and seeds have almost none); only orange juice, which is often fortified, supplies some, so orange is the best of the four.

113.s: What is the other name of Vitamin B2?
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
113.x: Vitamin B2 is riboflavin. Pyridoxine is B6, thiamine B1 and cyanocobalamin B12.

113.s: Out of the following which food contains the highest Vitamin A content per equal weight?
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
113.x: Cod-liver oil has by far the most vitamin A (retinol) per gram – many times more than carrots or pumpkin (beta-carotene) or egg.

113.s: Vitamin 'A' deficiency cause which type of disease?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness and xerophthalmia, leading to vision loss and blindness. Rickets is vitamin D, and clotting problems are vitamin K.

113.s: Which of the following is a major source of Vitamin C?
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
113.x: Gooseberry (amla) is the richest common source of vitamin C.

113.s: A deficiency of vitamin B3 can result in a condition called:
113.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
113.x: Niacin (B3) deficiency causes pellagra. Scurvy is C, rickets D and beri-beri B1.

113.s: Which of the following factors will NOT generally cause heart disease?
o: Deficiency of Vitamin A in diet
113.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
113.x: High blood pressure, high blood glucose and raised lipids are risk factors for heart disease; vitamin A deficiency is not, so it is the answer.

113.s: Damaged and dry skin, wounds healing slowly and easy bruising are some of the problems which can arise because of the deficiency of which vitamin?
113.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
113.x: Vitamin C is needed for collagen, so its deficiency gives dry damaged skin, slow wound healing and easy bruising (scurvy). Vitamins D, A and B12 cause bone, eye and anaemia problems.

113.s: The disease 'Osteomalacia' which causes softening of bones is caused by a deficiency of which nutrient in the human diet?
113.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
113.x: Osteomalacia, softening of adult bones, is caused by vitamin D deficiency. Carbohydrate, iodine and vitamin C are wrong.

113.s: When fruits are cut and exposed to air, Vitamin C is lost by
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
113.x: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is a strong reducing agent, so on cut fruit exposed to air it is lost by oxidation.

113.s:
Which of the following statement is/are not true about vitamins?
a. The term vitamin was coined by C Funk
b. Vitamins are organic compounds.
c. Vitamin K plays important role in clotting of blood.
d. Vitamin A, D, E and K are water soluble vitamins.
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
113.x: Statements a (Funk coined 'vitamine'), b (vitamins are organic) and c (K for clotting) are true; d is false because A, D, E and K are fat-soluble. So only d.

113.s: Thiamine is known to people as
113.x: Thiamine is vitamin B1, whose deficiency causes beri-beri.

113.s: Macrolytic anaemia is due to the deficiency of:
113.x: Macrocytic (megaloblastic) anaemia results from deficiency of folic acid (folacin) or B12. Biotin, niacin and pantothenic acid do not cause it.

113.s: Cyanocobalamin is a synthetic form of vitamin ______.
113.x: Cyanocobalamin is the synthetic, cobalt-containing form of vitamin B12.

113.s: Which vitamin is required for formation of bones and teeth?
113.src: APPSC 2018 Lecturers in Government Polytechnic Colleges (Eng
113.x: Vitamin D controls calcium and bone metabolism, so it is needed for bones and teeth; its deficiency causes rickets.

113.s: Which vitamin is known as the "sunshine vitamin" because the body can produce it when exposed to sunlight?
113.src: APPSC 2022 Various Non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
113.x: Vitamin D is made in the skin on exposure to sunlight, so it is called the sunshine vitamin. Vitamins A, C and K are not made this way.

113.s: The deficiency of which vitamin in human diet causes sore throat with swelling and redness of the mouth, cheilosis, stomatitis, glossitis and dermatitis?
113.x: Riboflavin (B2) deficiency causes sore throat, cheilosis, stomatitis, glossitis and dermatitis. Ascorbic acid is C (scurvy), retinol A and cyanocobalamin B12.

113.s: Which of the following is/are a source of Vitamin K?
113.x:
APPSC 2004 key: nuts, eggs, liver. Strictly, green leafy vegetables are the richest source of vitamin K (PMF General Science Part 3 p.14), but option (c) adds tomatoes and carrots, which are poor sources.
Nuts, eggs and animal liver supply vitamin K, which is the exam key. Green leafy vegetables are the best-known source, but tomatoes and carrots are poor, so option (c) is not a clean answer; shark-liver oil gives vitamins A and D.

113.s: Which of the following are water-soluble vitamins ?
113.x: B-group vitamins and vitamin C are water-soluble; A, D, E and K are fat-soluble, so every pair with A or D is wrong.

113.s: Golden Rice is a rich source of :
113.x: Golden Rice is genetically engineered to make beta-carotene, the precursor of vitamin A, in the grain.

113.s: Scurvy is a disease caused by the deficiency of :
113.x: Scurvy (bleeding gums, poor wound healing) is caused by lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid). B2 deficiency causes cheilosis and vitamin A deficiency night blindness.

113.s: Which of the following vitamins contains cobalt?
113.x: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is the only vitamin with a metal – cobalt – at its centre. K, B6 and B2 contain no cobalt.

113.s: A person will suffer from beri-beri, rickets and scurvy if he is not taking adequate amounts of :
113.x: Beri-beri = lack of B1 (thiamine), rickets = lack of D, scurvy = lack of C, so B1, D and C. The other sets include vitamins (A, E, K, B6) linked to other diseases.

113.s: Which of the following vitamin helps in blood clotting in humans?
113.x: Vitamin K is needed to make clotting factors (prothrombin), so it helps blood clot. A is for vision, D for bones.

113.s: Which of the following vitamins is essential for normal vision?
113.x: Retinol (vitamin A) forms the visual pigment rhodopsin, so it is essential for normal vision. Folic acid, riboflavin and niacin are B vitamins with other roles.

113.s: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
113.x: Tocopherol (vitamin E) deficiency causes sterility and muscle weakness; beri-beri is due to thiamine (B1). The other three pairs are correct.

113.s:
Consider the following pairs : Vitamin Deficiency disease
1. Vitamin C : Scurvy
2. Vitamin D : Rickets
3. Vitamin E : Night blindness Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
113.x: Vitamin C – scurvy and vitamin D – rickets are correct; night blindness is due to vitamin A, not E (E deficiency causes sterility/muscle weakness).

113.s: Which one of the following vitamins is helpful in keeping a dream in memory for a longer duration?
113.x: Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) was found (University of Adelaide study, 2018) to improve people's ability to recall their dreams. Vitamins A, D and C have no such link.

113.s: Which one of the following compounds is not a vitamin?
113.x: Thyroxine is a hormone of the thyroid gland, not a vitamin. Niacin (B3), riboflavin (B2) and pyridoxine (B6) are B vitamins.

113.s: Golden rice is a richer source of –
113.x: Golden Rice carries genes for beta-carotene (provitamin A), so it is a richer source of vitamin A; it was developed against vitamin A deficiency.

113.s: Which one of the following statements is not correct ?
o: Milk contains none of the B vitamins
Vitamin A (retinol) deficiency leads to the dry and
One of the symptoms of scurvy is pain in the joints
Vitamin B1 (thiamine) deficiency can lead to heart
113.x: Milk is a good source of riboflavin (B2) and B12, so 'milk contains none of the B vitamins' is wrong. Vitamin A lack causes dry eyes, scurvy causes joint pain and thiamine lack (wet beri-beri) can cause heart failure.

113.s: For which desirable character the transgenic crop ‘Golden Rice’ is produced ?
113.x: Golden Rice was engineered to produce beta-carotene (provitamin A) in the endosperm; it is not for amino acids, insulin or starch quality.

113.s: Which one of the following is an important source of vitamin E?
113.x: Wheat-germ oil is the richest natural source of vitamin E (tocopherol). Palm, coconut and mustard oil contain much less.

113.s: Which of the following vitamins is mainly responsible for blood coagulation in human being?
113.x: Vitamin K is needed for the liver to make prothrombin and other clotting factors; E, A and C have no direct role in coagulation.

113.s: Which of the following vitamin is effective in blood clotting?
113.x: Vitamin K (the 'koagulation' vitamin) makes blood clot; lack of it prolongs clotting time.

113.s: Which of the following vitamins contain cobalt –
113.x: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) contains cobalt; B1, B2 and B6 contain no metal.

113.s: Deficiency of which vitamin can cause night blindness?
113.x: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness; B1 causes beri-beri, C scurvy and E sterility.

113.s: Which of the following has the highest content of Vitamin C ?
113.x: Guava has about 200+ mg vitamin C per 100 g, about four times an orange; carrot and mango are known for vitamin A.

113.s: Which one of the following vitamins is formed in skin in the presence of sunlight?
113.x: Vitamin D is made in the skin when UV-B in sunlight acts on 7-dehydrocholesterol – the 'sunshine vitamin'.

113.s: The main source of Vitamin ‘C’ is –
113.x: Vitamin C comes mainly from fresh raw fruits (amla, guava, citrus); it is destroyed by heat and milk, ghee and pulses are poor in it.

113.s: Cyanocobalamin is –
113.x: Cyanocobalamin is the cobalt-containing form of vitamin B12. Vitamin C is ascorbic acid, B2 riboflavin, B6 pyridoxine.

113.s: Which of the following vitamins are fat soluble?
113.x: A, D, E and K are fat-soluble, so A and D is the pair; C and B12 are water-soluble.

113.s: Riboflavin deficiency causes which of the following diseases?
113.x: Riboflavin (B2) deficiency causes cheilosis (cracks at the lip corners). Pellagra is niacin (B3), scurvy vitamin C, beri-beri thiamine (B1).

113.s:
Assertion (A) : If somebody stops taking green vegetables hewill suffer from night blindness.
Reason (R) : He will suffer from vitamin A deficiency.
Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct
113.x:
UPPSC key: both true, R explains A. Strictly, stopping green vegetables causes night blindness only if no other vitamin A source (milk, liver, carrots, fruits) is eaten.
Green leafy vegetables are a main source of beta-carotene (vitamin A); without vitamin A one suffers night blindness, so the key is both true and R explains A.

113.s: The Deficiency of Vitamin D causes the disease :
113.x: Lack of vitamin D causes rickets in children (osteomalacia in adults). Beri-beri is B1, pellagra B3; osteoporosis is mainly age and calcium related.

113.s: The nutritional deficiency condition that needs to be given top priority for remedial action in India today is :
113.x: Vitamin A deficiency (xerophthalmia), the main preventable cause of child blindness, was India's priority deficiency, hence the vitamin A prophylaxis programme. Scurvy, rickets and pellagra are much rarer.

113.s: Which of the following vitamins is known as ergocalciferol?
113.x: Ergocalciferol is vitamin D2 (plant/fungal form); cholecalciferol is D3; B12 is cobalamin and B6 pyridoxine.

113.s:
Consider the statements :
Assertion (A) : Vitamin B12 remains stored in liver for about 3-5 years.
Reason (R) : Vitamin B12 is water-soluble.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
Codes :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
113.x: Both statements are true: B12 is water-soluble, yet the liver stores it for 3–5 years. Being water-soluble does not explain storage (water-soluble vitamins are usually excreted), so R is not the explanation.

113.s: If a person only takes milk, egg and bread in diet, so he may suffer from the disease :
113.x: Milk, egg and bread contain almost no vitamin C, so such a diet leads to scurvy. They give vitamin D, A and calories, so rickets, night blindness and marasmus are not the result.

113.s: Which of the following vitamins does not get stored in the body?
113.x: Vitamin C is water-soluble and not stored; excess is passed in urine. A, D and E are fat-soluble and stored in the liver and fat.

113.s: Which of the following facts is NOT correct about vitamins?
o: Some vitamins can be synthesized by intestinal
Some vitamins are stored in body
113.x: Vitamin K is fat-soluble, so that statement is false. Gut bacteria make K and B12, vitamin D acts as a hormone, and A, D, B12 are stored.

113.s: The richest source of Vitamin ‘C’ is –
113.x: Orange (citrus) is rich in vitamin C; potato has a little, sugarcane and sugar beet almost none.

113.s: Golden rice is rich in –
113.x: Golden Rice is rich in beta-carotene, the precursor of vitamin A.

113.s: Use of polished rice in human diet causes following disease :
113.x: Polishing removes the bran that holds thiamine (B1), so a polished-rice diet causes beri-beri. Rickets (D), anaemia (iron) and goitre (iodine) are not linked.

113.s: The vitamin available from sun rays is –
113.x: Vitamin D is made in the skin under sunlight (UV-B), so it is called the sunshine vitamin.

113.s: Which of the following vitamins is used as an antidote to anticoagulant poisons?
113.x: Warfarin-type anticoagulants block vitamin K; giving vitamin K restores the clotting factors, so it is the antidote. A, D and E have no such role.

113.s: Milk is a poor source of :
113.x: Milk is poor in vitamin C (and iron) but rich in calcium, protein and lactose (carbohydrate).

113.s: Which of the following is synthesized by intestinal bacteria?
113.x:
Book answer: (a) & (c) – B12 and K both. Strictly, vitamin K2 from gut bacteria is the part humans actually absorb; colonic B12 is largely not absorbed (it is made beyond the ileum).
Gut bacteria synthesise both vitamin B12 and vitamin K, and the book answer gives B12 (with K). Vitamins C and A are not made by bacteria in the gut.

113.s: Which vitamin is soluble in water?
113.x:
Printed key: (b) Vitamin B; the book answer reads '(b) & (c)'. Strictly both vitamin B and vitamin C are water-soluble (NextGen Rocket Biology vitamin table).
Vitamin B (the B-complex) is water-soluble; vitamin C is also water-soluble, while A and D are fat-soluble. The printed key gives B.

113.s: The vitamin which is found in citrus fruits and is necessary for maintaining healthy skin is –
113.x: Vitamin C, found in citrus fruits, is needed for collagen and so for healthy skin and gums.

113.s: Which one of the following is not formed in our body?
113.x: Vitamin A must come from food (retinol, or carotene converted in the gut/liver); proteins, enzymes and hormones are all synthesised in the body.

113.s: The common name of the chemical compound 'Cholecalciferol' is :
113.x: Cholecalciferol is vitamin D3, the form made in the skin under sunlight.

113.s: The vitamin which is effective in blood clotting is :
113.x: Vitamin K is needed for clotting factors; lack of it prolongs clotting.

113.s: Which of the following is the richest source of vitamin A?
113.x: Among the fruits given, mango is the richest in beta-carotene (vitamin A); papaya is close, while apple and guava are poor in it.

113.s: Use of polished rice in human diet causes the following disease
113.x: Polished rice has lost its thiamine-rich bran, so it causes beri-beri; goitre is iodine and night blindness vitamin A deficiency.

113.s: Some vitamins are fat soluble while others are water soluble. Which of the following are water soluble :
o: Vitamin A, D, E and K
113.x: Vitamins B and C are water-soluble; A, D, E and K are fat-soluble, so any set with A, D or K is wrong.

113.s: Among the following vegetables, the maximum Vitamin C is found in :
113.x: Green chilli has about 100+ mg vitamin C per 100 g, the most among these vegetables; pumpkin, pea and radish have far less.

113.s: Which of the following vitamin's deficiency causes disease of slow blood coagulation ?
113.x: Vitamin K deficiency increases clotting time (slow coagulation). C, D and E deficiencies cause scurvy, rickets and sterility.

113.s: Which one of the following contains more vitamin A content ?
113.x: Carrot is the richest in beta-carotene (vitamin A) of these vegetables, ahead of spinach; cabbage and cauliflower have little.

113.s: In countries where polished rice is the mean cereal in their diet, people suffer from –
113.x: Polished rice lacks thiamine (B1), so people eating it as the main cereal suffer beri-beri. Pellagra is a maize-diet (niacin) disease.

113.s: Which of the following is the richest source of Vitamin C?
113.x: Amla (Indian gooseberry) is the richest common source of vitamin C (~600 mg/100 g), far above orange; apple and carrot are poor.

113.s: The chemical name of Vitamin C is –
113.x: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid; thiamine is B1, while citric and tartaric acids are fruit acids, not vitamins.

113.s: Which one of the following is useful in the treatment of scurvy disease?
113.x: Aonla (amla, Indian gooseberry) is the richest vitamin C source, so it treats scurvy; mango and papaya have less and ber is moderate.

113.s: Which of the following statement regarding vitamin is not correct?
o: Some vitamins can be synthesised by intestinal microbes.
Some vitamins are stored in body.
vitamin K is a water soluble vitamin.
113.x: Vitamin K is fat-soluble, so that statement is wrong. Gut microbes make K and B12, vitamin D acts as a hormone, and fat-soluble vitamins and B12 are stored.

113.s: Vitamin C is also known as …………
113.x: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid; tartaric (tamarind), malic (apple) and acetic (vinegar) acids are not vitamins.

113.s: The deficiency of which nutrient causes night blindness?
113.x: Vitamin A (retinol) deficiency causes night blindness; K, C and protein deficiency do not.

113.s: Vitamin B12 deficiency causes pernicious anaemia. Animals cannot synthesise vitamin B12. Humans must obtain all their vitamin B12 from their diet. The complexing metal ion in Vitamin B12 is
113.x: Vitamin B12 has a cobalt ion (Co3+) at the centre of its corrin ring. Mg2+ is in chlorophyll, Fe2+ in haemoglobin.

113.s: Which of the following is a fat soluble vitamin that plays a role in blood clotting, bone metabolism and regulating blood calcium levels?
113.x: Vitamin K is fat-soluble and needed for clotting and bone metabolism (osteocalcin). C and B are water-soluble; A is for vision.

113.s: Pernicious anaemia is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin ……
113.x: Pernicious anaemia is due to vitamin B12 deficiency (lack of intrinsic factor). B2, B6 and B1 are not the cause.

113.s: Deficiency of ………… causes rickets disease.
113.x: Rickets is caused by vitamin D deficiency; C causes scurvy, A night blindness, B beri-beri/pellagra.

113.s: Which mineral element is present in Vitamin B-12?
113.x: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) contains cobalt; iron is in haemoglobin, magnesium in chlorophyll.

113.s: Which one of the following is not a natural source of Vitamin A ?
113.x:
Book key: milk. Strictly, whole milk does contain preformed vitamin A (retinol) in its fat, while mango, papaya and carrot give only provitamin A (beta-carotene).
Mango, papaya and carrot are rich carotene (provitamin A) sources; milk has comparatively little vitamin A, so the book key is milk.

113.s: The best source of Vitamin C is :
113.x: Gooseberry (amla) is the best source of vitamin C; apple and mango have less and milk almost none.

113.s: Vitamin 'C' help in absorption of which of following elements?
113.x: Vitamin C reduces dietary iron to the ferrous form and increases its absorption; it does not mainly aid calcium, iodine or sodium.

113.s: The source of vitamin D is –
113.x: Sun rays let the skin make vitamin D; lemon and orange give vitamin C and cashew nut has almost no vitamin D.

113.s:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and other as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Human body synthesizes all the Vitamins required by it.
Reason (R) : Vitamins are essential for proper growth of the body.
Choose the correct answer from the code given below.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct
113.x: A is false: the body makes only a few vitamins (D, some K, niacin), so most must come from food. R is true – vitamins are essential for growth.

113.s:
Assertion (A) : Vitamins are invigorating elements, whose small amount is required for good health.
Reason (R) : Vitamins helps to keep the body healthy by killing harmful bacteria.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but R is not the correct
113.x: Vitamins are organic compounds needed in small amounts for health, so A is true. They do not kill bacteria (that is antibodies or antibiotics), so R is false.

113.s: In human body, vitamin A is stored in –
113.x: Vitamin A is largely stored in the liver in the human body. Its chemical name is retinol whose deficiency causes night blindness.

113.s: In human body, Vitamin A is stored in –
113.x: Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin that is stored in the liver, so the liver is the correct answer.

113.s: The vitamin which can be synthesized under the skin in the presence of the uv light of sun is?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
113.x: Vitamin D (the sunshine vitamin) is made in the skin under the sun's UV light.

113.s: In which season Vitamin A is required in higher quantities?
113.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
113.x:
Official key: Winter. Strictly no authority gives a season-dependent vitamin A requirement for humans ('No seasonal dependence'); deficiency peaks in the hot pre-harvest season (NERC/Cambridge study on India).
The APPSC 2017 key is winter (option A in the paper as printed in Vijeta previous papers). No nutrition authority gives a season-specific vitamin A requirement: ICMR-NIN RDAs depend on age and life stage only.

113.s:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: The Haber process is an industrial method used to produce ammonia by reacting nitrogen and hydrogen gases under high temperature and pressure in the presence of an iron catalyst.
Statement II: The Contact process is an important industrial method used to manufacture sulphuric acid, which involves the catalytic oxidation of sulphur dioxide to sulphur trioxide using vanadium pentoxide (V2O5) as a catalyst.
o: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both statement I and statement II are true.
Both statement I and statement II are false.
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
113.x: Both are true: the Haber process makes ammonia from N2 and H2 over an iron catalyst, and the Contact process makes sulphuric acid by oxidising SO2 to SO3 over V2O5.

113.s: In periodic table helium is placed at
113.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
113.x: Helium is a noble gas in Group 18, period 1, so it sits at the top right corner of the periodic table.

113.s: Planets revolve around the sun due to gravitational force. Similarly, electrons revolve around the nucleus due to ____.
113.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
113.x: Electrons are held in orbit round the positive nucleus by electrostatic (Coulomb) attraction, just as gravity keeps planets round the Sun.

113.s: Which of the following has the same atomic number and atomic weight?
113.x: Ordinary hydrogen (protium) has one proton and no neutron, so its atomic number and mass number are both 1; helium is 2 and 4.

113.s: Which of the following is a noble gas?
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
113.x: Helium is a noble (inert) gas of Group 18; hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen are reactive.

113.s: Saponification is the reaction between
o: A fat and a strong acid
A fat and a strong base
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Saponification is the hydrolysis of a fat (or oil) with a strong base such as NaOH, giving soap and glycerol. An acid-base reaction is neutralisation.

113.s: Which of the following forces is responsible for all the nucleons to be concentrated in the nucleus?
113.src: APPSC Deputy Inspector of Survey, Technical Assistant in AP
113.x: The strong nuclear force, short-range and far stronger than electrostatic repulsion, binds protons and neutrons in the nucleus. Off-subject (physics).

113.s: The most malleable metal is
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: Gold is the most malleable (and ductile) metal; it can be beaten into leaves a few atoms thick. Silver is next; aluminium and iron are far less malleable.

113.s: When an iron nail gets rusted, its weight?
o: Increase or decrease depends on temperature and pressure
113.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
113.x: Rust is hydrated iron oxide; the iron combines with oxygen and water, so the weight increases. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: Which of the following is an inorganic lubricant?
113.src: APPSC 2018 Special Qualifying Test for Appointment by Promot
113.x: Graphite is an inorganic layered form of carbon used as a solid lubricant; lanolin, mineral oil and PTFE are organic. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: A soap molecule has two ends, one of which is an ionic end and the other is a carbonic chain end. Which part of the soap molecule interacts with oily dirt to enable cleansing?
o: The end that is closer to the oil molecule
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: The hydrocarbon (carbon-chain) tail dissolves in oil and grips the dirt, while the ionic end faces water, forming micelles. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: Why alum is used in the process of purifying drinking water?
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
113.x: Alum (potash alum) supplies Al3+ ions that neutralise the charge on suspended clay particles so they coagulate and settle. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s:
Match the following from table A to Table B - Use of Salts
Table A:
I. Sodium Carbonate
II. Sodium Benzoate
III. Calcium Carbonate
IV. Calcium Phosphate
Table B:
1. Extraction of Metals
2. As Washing Soda, Manufacturing of Glass
3. As a Fertilizers
4. As a Food preservative for Pickles
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Sodium carbonate is washing soda used in glass-making, sodium benzoate is a food preservative, calcium carbonate is a flux in metal extraction and calcium phosphate is a fertiliser. Moved.

113.s: Out of the below, what is the example of a chemical reaction?
113.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
113.x: Rusting forms a new substance (iron oxide), so it is a chemical change; freezing, glowing of a lamp filament and dissolving salt are physical changes. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: Which type of chemical process is tarnishing of silver?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
113.x: Tarnishing of silver (black silver sulphide from H2S in air) is a form of corrosion. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: Which reaction demonstrate the chemical property of alcohols as reducing agent?
o: Reaction with sodium to release hydrogen
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Alcohols are oxidised to aldehydes or ketones, so they act as reducing agents (they are themselves oxidised); esterification, reaction with sodium and dehydration are not redox reactions of this kind. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: Which gas is evolved when an acid reacts with a metal?
113.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
113.x: A metal reacting with an acid gives a salt and hydrogen gas (e.g. Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2). Off-topic (general science), moved.

113.s: Formation of Carbon dioxide gas from Carbon and Oxygen is a/an?
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
113.x: Burning carbon in oxygen to CO2 gives out heat – an exothermic (combination) reaction. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: Which one of the following is pure water?
113.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
113.x: Rain water is the purest natural water (natural distillation); well, river and sea water carry dissolved salts.

113.s: Which of the following substances is invariably formed, whenever an acid combines with a base?
113.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
113.x: An acid and a base always react to form a salt (and water). Off-topic science PYQ, moved.

113.s: What happens to the weight of Iron when it rusts?
113.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
113.x: Rust is iron combined with oxygen and water (hydrated iron oxide), so the rusted iron weighs more. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: Out of the following, which would not indicate occurence of a chemical reaction?
113.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
113.x: Evaporation is only a change of state (physical change); gas evolution, colour change and heat absorption can signal a chemical reaction. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: An 'aerosol' is a fine dispersion of
o: Tiny droplets of liquid in the air
Chalk and sand particles in water
113.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
113.x: An aerosol is a fine dispersion of liquid droplets (or solid particles) in air/gas, e.g. fog, mist, sprays. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: When you are facing the periodic table, on which side of the table the non-metals are present?
o: On the right-hand side of the periodic table
In the middle column of the periodic table
On the left-hand side of the periodic table
In the bottom most row of the periodic table
113.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
113.x: In the modern periodic table metals lie on the left, metalloids along a zigzag line and non-metals on the right-hand side.

113.s: Which of the following chemicals is generally used for purifying muddy water?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
113.x: Alum (potash alum) coagulates suspended clay so it settles, purifying muddy water. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: Which of the following is a mixture?
113.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
113.x: Sea water is a mixture of water and many dissolved salts in no fixed ratio; table salt, sugar and lime are compounds. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: Which of the following is used in glass industry?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
113.x: Sodium carbonate (soda ash) is a main raw material of glass. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: Which of the following is antidote for cyanide poisoning
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Sodium thiosulphate is an antidote for cyanide poisoning (it turns cyanide into less toxic thiocyanate). Off-topic (chemistry/medicine), moved.

113.s: Percentage of sodium chloride present in normal saline is
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Normal saline is 0.9% (w/v) sodium chloride, isotonic with blood. Off-topic (science), moved; the question had no printed key.

113.s: Fill in the blanks: Gunpowder, also known as black powder is made of Sulphur (S), Charcoal (C), and ______.
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: Gunpowder (black powder) is sulphur, charcoal and potassium nitrate (saltpetre). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: Out of the following, which compound has highest solubility in Water?
113.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
113.x: Glucose dissolves about 90 g per 100 mL water at 25°C, far more than table salt (~36 g), ammonium chloride (~38 g) or alum (~14 g). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: If Limestone (Calcium Carbonate) kept in a test tube is heated with a spirit lamp and a burning match stick is kept near the mouth of the test tube
o: The stick will glow with higher brightness
The stick will glow with same brightness
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
113.x: Heating limestone (CaCO3) decomposes it into quicklime (CaO) and carbon dioxide; CO2 does not support burning, so the flame goes out. Off-topic (chemistry), moved to book 5.

113.s: What happens when calcium oxide reacts vigorously with water?
o: Calcium Hypochlorite is produced and a large amount of heat is released
Calcium Oxyacid is produced and a precipitate is formed that settle down in the test-tube
Calcium Carbonate is produced and hydrogen gas is released
Calcium Hydroxide is produced and a large amount of heat is released
113.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
113.x: Calcium oxide (quicklime) reacts vigorously with water to form calcium hydroxide (slaked lime), releasing a lot of heat. Off-topic (chemistry), moved to book 5.

113.s: Unsaturated hydrocarbons add hydrogen in the presence of catalyst such as _____ to give saturated hydrocarbons.
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Hydrogenation of unsaturated hydrocarbons uses a nickel (or Pd/Pt) catalyst. Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: The strike plate of a match box is made up of
113.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
113.x: The striking surface of a safety-match box carries red phosphorus (with powdered glass); the match head has potassium chlorate. (Off-topic: moved to science.)

113.s: The strike plate of a match box is is made up of
113.x: The striking surface of a safety-match box carries red phosphorus (with powdered glass); the match head has potassium chlorate. (Off-topic: moved to science.)

113.s: Which of the following is used in titration
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: A burette delivers measured volumes of titrant in a titration; a pipette transfers a fixed volume.

113.s: The thermite process is used to weld railway tracks; it involves a reaction between
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: The thermite reaction is between iron oxide and aluminium; aluminium reduces the oxide and the molten iron produced welds rail joints.

113.s: What happens when a dry litmus paper is exposed to Anhydrous hydrochloric acid vapor?
o: Colour changes from blue to red
113.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
113.x: Dry HCl gas does not ionise without water, so dry litmus paper shows no colour change.

113.s: The Elements of Group IA are called:
113.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
113.x: Group IA (Group 1) elements – lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, caesium, francium – are the alkali metals. Off-topic (chemistry).

113.s: Galvanization is a method of protecting iron from corrosion by coating the iron with a thin layer of which of the following element?
113.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
113.x: Galvanisation coats iron with a thin layer of zinc. Off-topic (chemistry).

113.s: In Wurtz reaction, alkyl halides on treatment with-metal in dry ethereal (free from moisture) solution give higher alkanes.
113.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
113.x: The Wurtz reaction couples alkyl halides with sodium in dry ether to give higher alkanes. Off-topic (chemistry).

113.s: Which metal coating is used in Galvanization process to protect Steel and Iron from rusting?
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Galvanisation coats steel and iron with zinc to stop rusting. Off-topic (chemistry).

113.s: Which of the following metal is the best conductor of electricity?
113.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
113.x: Silver is the best conductor of electricity, ahead of copper and aluminium. Off-topic (physics).

113.s: Which of the following is a toxic material found in automotive batteries?
113.src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning
113.x: Lead in lead-acid automotive batteries is the toxic material. Off-topic (pollution / chemistry).

113.s: A solution reacts with crushed-egg shells to give a gas that turns lime water milky. The solution contains
113.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
113.x: Hydrochloric acid reacts with egg shells (calcium carbonate) to release CO2, which turns lime water milky. Off-topic (chemistry).

113.s: Which of the following metals can be easily cut with a knife?
113.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: Potassium, a soft alkali metal, can be cut with a knife; lead, aluminium and selenium cannot be cut easily. Off-topic (chemistry).

113.s: The head of a matchstick is generally made of
113.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
113.x:
Most books and keys: phosphorus. Strictly, a safety-match head is mainly potassium chlorate with antimony trisulphide; the red phosphorus is on the striking strip (only old 'strike-anywhere' heads carried phosphorus sesquisulphide) (general knowledge, not checked).
Exam keys answer phosphorus for the match head; see the dispute for what a safety-match head is actually made of.

113.s: In vulcanization of natural rubber, the following is used?
113.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
113.x: Vulcanisation heats rubber with sulphur to make it strong and elastic (Goodyear, 1839).

113.s: Which of the following substances can be used as an acid-base indicator?
113.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
113.x: Turmeric turns reddish-brown in bases and back to yellow in acids, so it works as a natural acid-base indicator; tamarind, sugar and salt do not change colour.

113.s: Which of the following can be prepared using Methyl Alcohol?
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
113.x: Perspex is PMMA, whose monomer methyl methacrylate is made by esterifying methacrylic acid with methanol (methyl alcohol); neoprene comes from chloroprene and Bakelite from phenol and formaldehyde.

113.s: How many moles of Oxygen are required for combustion of one mole of Propane?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: C3H8 + 5O2 → 3CO2 + 4H2O, so one mole of propane needs 5 moles of oxygen.

113.s: A spectral line is emitted when an electron
o: jumps from lower orbit to higher orbit
jumps from higher orbit to lower orbit
113.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
113.x: A spectral (emission) line is emitted when an electron jumps from a higher orbit (energy level) to a lower one, giving out a photon. Jumping up absorbs energy.

113.s: Which element is common to all acids?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: All acids contain hydrogen, which they release as H+ ions in water.

113.s: What is the meaning of pH?
o: To measure the pressure of liquid
To measure the density of a solution
To measure the pressure of a blood
113.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
113.x: pH = 'potential of hydrogen' (power of hydrogen), a measure of hydrogen-ion concentration.

113.s: Which of the following is not necessary for combustion to occur?
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Combustion needs fuel, oxygen and the ignition temperature (the fire triangle); water is not needed.

113.s: An organic compound must contain?
113.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
113.x: An organic compound must contain carbon.

113.s: Ammonia is a compound of
o: Nitrogen and sodium hydroxide APPSC PYQS "
113.x: Ammonia (NH3) = one nitrogen + three hydrogen atoms.

113.s: Which of the following elements does not contain neutrons?
o: None of the above/More than one of the above
113.x: Protium (ordinary hydrogen, 1H1) has no neutron; oxygen and nitrogen nuclei contain neutrons.

113.s: Approximately how many different chemical elements exist on the Earth?
113.x: 118 elements are known and about 94 occur naturally on Earth, so 'about 100' is nearest; 200–300 elements do not exist.

113.s: Which of the following is the most common element in the Universe?
113.x: Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the Universe (about 3/4 of matter); oxygen leads in the Earth's crust.

113.s: An iron nail dipped into Copper sulphate solution turns into the following colour?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: Iron displaces copper from copper sulphate; the nail gets a reddish-brown copper coating (solution turns pale green).

113.s: Into which colour will the yellow silver bromide turn when exposed to sunlight?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
113.x: Silver bromide decomposes in sunlight to grey silver metal (photolytic reaction).

113.s: The catalyst used in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils is
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Finely divided nickel is the catalyst for hydrogenating vegetable oils into vanaspati.

113.s: What happens when dilute hydrochloric acid is added to iron fillings?
o: Chlorine gas and iron hydroxide are produced
Hydrogen gas and iron chloride are produced
Iron salt and water are produced
113.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
113.x: Iron reacts with dilute HCl to give iron(II) chloride and hydrogen gas.

113.s: Which of the following has 1 as its atomic number?
113.x: Hydrogen has one proton, so its atomic number is 1; ammonia is a compound.

113.s: The bright colour of fire crackers containing Magnesium is due to?
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
113.x: The dazzling white light of magnesium in crackers comes from burning, i.e. oxidation of magnesium to MgO. Reduction and 'explosion of metal' are wrong; 'redox' is too general.

113.s: Which of the following happens during the electro refining of copper?
o: Pure copper from anode deposits at the cathode
Pure copper from anode deposits in the electrolytic solution
Pure copper from the electrolytic solution deposits at the anode
Pure copper from the electrolytic solution deposits at the cathode
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: In electrolytic refining the impure anode dissolves into the electrolyte and an equivalent amount of pure copper from the solution deposits at the cathode. Copper does not pass directly from anode to cathode, and nothing deposits at the anode.

113.s:
Identify the correct pairs of organic chemical reactions and their mechanisms.
1. Gatterman-Koch Reaction - The formation of cyclopropanes from alkenes using methylene carbene.
2. Friedel-Crafts Acylation Reaction - The conversion of carboxylic acids into esters using acids and alcohols.
3. Etard Reaction - The direct oxidation of an aromatic or heterocyclic bound methyl group with an aldehyde using chromyl chloride.
4. Stephen Reaction - The conversion of nitriles to aldehydes in the presence of hydrochloric acid, using tin chloride.
Select the correct answer from the options given below:
113.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
113.x: Etard reaction oxidises an aromatic methyl group to an aldehyde with chromyl chloride, and Stephen reaction reduces nitriles to aldehydes with SnCl2/HCl, so 3 and 4 are right. Gattermann-Koch is formylation of benzene (CO + HCl), not cyclopropanation, and Friedel-Crafts acylation adds an acyl group to an aromatic ring, not esterification.

113.s: Which of the elements is used as fungicide?
113.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
113.x: Sulphur (wettable or dusting sulphur, lime-sulphur) is a widely used fungicide; calcium, phosphorus and carbon are not used as fungicides.

113.s: The reaction of sodium Hydroxide with Hydrochloric acid leading to formation of salt and water is a?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H2O is a neutralisation, a double displacement reaction (ions exchange partners).

113.s: In the Haber's process, X moles of nitrogen react with Y moles of hydrogen to form Z moles of ammonia. What are the values of X, Y and Z?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Haber process: N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3, so X = 1, Y = 3, Z = 2.

113.s: Which of the below is a physical change?
113.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
113.x: Dissolving salt in water is a physical change: no new substance forms and evaporation recovers the salt. Burning wax or wood and curdling milk make new substances, so they are chemical changes.

113.s: Name the non-metal which exists in liquid state at room temperature.
113.src: APPSC Deputy Inspector of Survey, Technical Assistant in AP
113.x: Bromine is the only non-metal liquid at room temperature. Mercury is liquid but a metal; silicon and lithium are solids.

113.s: Which of the following is a non-metal that remains liquid at room temperature?
113.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
113.x: Bromine is the non-metal that is liquid at room temperature. Helium and chlorine are gases.

113.s: Which of the following can be used as Tear Gas?
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Tear gas CN is alpha- (omega-) chloroacetophenone, i.e. 2-chloro-1-phenylethanone. Plain acetophenone is not a lachrymator.

113.s: Which of the following noble gases is NOT present in the air?
113.x:
Most books: all noble gases except radon occur in air. Strictly, radon is present in trace amounts near the ground (decay of radium in soil).
Argon, neon and helium are constituents of air. Radon is radioactive and short-lived, so it is taken as the noble gas not present in air. (Off-topic: chemistry.)

113.s: Name the homologous series with an -OH functional group.
113.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
113.x: Alcohols form the homologous series with the -OH (hydroxyl) functional group. Hydroxide is the OH- ion of bases, not a functional group.

113.s: When an alcohol is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid at about 170°C, it undergoes dehydration. What is the major product formed?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Heating an alcohol with concentrated H2SO4 at about 170°C removes water (dehydration) and gives an alkene, e.g. ethanol → ethene.

113.s: Dry ice is used for packing Covid-19 vaccines for transportation. What is dry ice?
113.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
113.x: Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide (sublimes at -78.5°C), used to keep vaccines cold.

113.s: What is the process of extracting metals from their ores called?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
113.x: Smelting is extracting a metal from its ore by reduction at high temperature in the fused state; refining purifies the metal and mining removes the ore.

113.s: Identify the functional group responsible for the characteristic smell of fruits.
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Esters (RCOOR') give the characteristic fruity smell of fruits and are used in perfumes and flavouring; aldehydes, ketones and carboxylic acids are not the answer.

113.s:
C2H5OH + alkaline KMnO4 + Heat → X
X + C2H5OH (acid) → Y
What are the products X and Y, respectively?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Alkaline KMnO4 oxidises ethanol to ethanoic (acetic) acid (X); the acid reacts with ethanol in acid medium to form an ester, ethyl acetate (Y).

113.s: Which of the following reactions does not occur in a blast furnace during the extraction of iron?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: In the blast furnace, coke burns to CO, limestone decomposes to CaO + CO2 and CO reduces Fe2O3 to iron; decomposition of FeSO4 does not occur there.

113.s: Which of the following is incorrect about acids?
o: Aqueous solutions of acids are electrolytes
Acids can change the colour of certain acid-base indicators
Acids do not react with active metals
113.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
113.x: Acids do react with active metals (e.g. zinc, iron) to give hydrogen gas, so that statement is incorrect. Aqueous acids conduct electricity, taste sour and change indicator colours.

113.s: What is the colour of litmus solution when it is neither acidic or basic?
113.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: Litmus solution is purple in a neutral solution; it turns red in acid and blue in base.

113.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about chemicals and their popular names?
A. The chemical name of 'Alum' is Potassium aluminium sulphate dodecahydrate.
B. The chemical name of 'Aspirin' is Acetyl salicylic acid.
C. The chemical name of 'Chalk' is Hypochlorus acid.
113.src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
113.x: Alum (potash alum) is potassium aluminium sulphate dodecahydrate, KAl(SO4)2·12H2O, and aspirin is acetylsalicylic acid, so A and B are correct; chalk is calcium carbonate (CaCO3), not hypochlorous acid.

113.s: Tobacco plant contains the following alkaloid?
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
113.x: Nicotine is the alkaloid of the tobacco plant; morphine comes from the opium poppy and reserpine from Rauwolfia, and resin is not an alkaloid. (Off-topic: general science.)

113.s: What happens to the colour of litmus paper when you put a drop of acid on it?
o: Blue Litmus paper turns to red
Red Litmus paper turns to blue
Green Litmus paper turns to red
Red Litmus paper turns to green
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
113.x: Acids turn blue litmus red; bases turn red litmus blue. (Moved to 5:1.)

113.s: What is the role of Barium Nitrate (Ba(NO3)2) in fireworks and fountains?
o: It acts as a fuel for combustion.
It produces a blue color in the flames.
It is an oxidizer that produces a green color in the flames.
It produces a red color in the flames.
113.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
113.x: Barium nitrate is an oxidiser in fireworks that gives a green flame; strontium gives red and copper blue. (Moved to 5:1.)

113.s:
Which of the following statements are correct ?
a. Melamine polymer is used in the manufacture of unbreakable crockery
b. Enzymes are biocatalysts
c. DNA fingerprinting is used for identification of criminals
d. Tincture of iodine is an antiseptic
113.x: All four are correct: melamine makes unbreakable crockery, enzymes are biocatalysts, DNA fingerprinting identifies criminals and tincture of iodine is an antiseptic.

113.s:
Identify the compound described below:
- It is present in crude oil and gasoline.
- It can cause Leukemia, DNA Strand Breaks, Chromosomal damage, Cancer, and harmful effects on bone marrow.
- It is known to be carcinogenic to humans.
113.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
113.x: Benzene, found in crude oil and petrol, is a known human carcinogen causing leukaemia and bone-marrow and chromosome damage.

113.s: Which property of ammonia explains why it turns red litmus into blue?
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Ammonia turns red litmus blue because it is a weak base (NH3 + H2O gives NH4+ and OH-); being a reducing agent, soluble or covalent does not explain the colour change. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

113.s: Atoms are composed of
113.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
113.x: An atom is a small nucleus (protons and neutrons) surrounded by electrons. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

113.s: The smallest ketone has ____ carbon atom/s.
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: The smallest ketone is acetone (propanone, CH3COCH3) with 3 carbon atoms, since the C=O must be bonded to two carbons. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

113.s: Which of the following could be the molecular formula of an alcohol?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: C2H6O is ethanol (C2H5OH), a saturated alcohol CnH2n+2O; C2H4O is acetaldehyde, C3H6O acetone or propanal, and CH2O formaldehyde. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

113.s: What substance is added to water to dissolve shellac and create a water-based varnish?
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
113.x: Shellac dissolves in water when borax (an alkali) is added, giving a water-based shellac varnish; spirit (alcohol) gives the ordinary spirit varnish, not a water-based one.

113.s: Which group of elements generally form coloured compounds?
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Transition (d-block) metals form coloured compounds because of d-d electron transitions in partly filled d orbitals; alkali-metal and non-metal compounds are mostly colourless.

113.s: Which of the following methods is suitable for preventing cast iron cookware from rusting?
113.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
113.x: Seasoning (coating with fat or oil and heating) forms a protective layer that keeps cast iron from rusting; soap and abrasives strip that layer.

113.s: Which of the following is an emulsion?
113.src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning
113.x: Butter is an emulsion (water droplets dispersed in fat); vinegar, sugar solution and honey are solutions.

113.s: Sulphur is used in vulcanization. This process is mainly associated with
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Vulcanisation is heating natural rubber with sulphur, which cross-links it and makes it harder, stronger and more elastic and wear-resistant (tyres, footwear). Steel, glass and cement making do not use it.

113.s: The ignition temperatures of four substances P, Q, R and S are 95°C, 98°C, 105°C and 108°C, respectively. Which substance/s will catch fire when they are exposed to a temperature of 100°C?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: A substance catches fire only when its temperature reaches its ignition temperature. At 100°C, P (95°C) and Q (98°C) are above their ignition temperatures and burn; R (105°C) and S (108°C) stay below theirs, so only P and Q catch fire.

113.s: Goiter is characterized by:
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
113.x: Goitre is the enlargement of the thyroid gland, mostly due to iodine deficiency.

113.s:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: The axial skeleton consists of the skull, vertebral column, rib cage and sternum, providing structural support and protection to vital organs.
Statement II: The tibia is the longest and strongest bone in the human body, located in the upper arm.
o: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both statement I and statement II are false.
Both statement I and statement II are true.
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
113.x: Statement I is true (skull, vertebral column, ribs and sternum form the axial skeleton). Statement II is false: the femur (thigh) is the longest and strongest bone, and the tibia is in the lower leg, not the arm.

113.s: The Right Hemisphere of the brain handles?
113.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
113.x: The right cerebral hemisphere is dominant for spatial abilities (also face recognition, visual imagery); language is mainly left-hemisphere. Off-topic (psychology).

113.s: Which of the following is a diuretic
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Furosemide (loop diuretic), mannitol (osmotic diuretic) and acetazolamide (carbonic anhydrase inhibitor) all increase urine output, so all of these are diuretics.

113.s: Which is the most abundant element by mass in human body?
113.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
113.x: Oxygen is the most abundant element by mass in the human body (~65%), followed by carbon and hydrogen. Off-topic (general science), moved.

113.s: Commonly used absorbable suture material is
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Catgut, made from animal intestine (collagen), is the classic absorbable suture. Silk and nylon are non-absorbable, and fascia lata is a tissue graft.

113.s:
When it comes to the digestive system, which statements are true?
I. The pancreas produces digestive enzymes and insulin.
II. The small intestine is where most nutrient absorption occurs.
III. The gallbladder stores bile produced by the liver.
113.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon, Group-IV and Other Posts Gene
113.x: The pancreas makes digestive enzymes and insulin, most absorption is in the small intestine, and the gall bladder stores bile – all three true. Off-topic, moved.

113.s: What is the resting rate heart for a normal person?
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
113.x: A normal adult resting heart rate is 60 to 100 beats per minute (American Heart Association); about 72 is the textbook average.

113.s: A process of deposition of calcium and other minerals on the surface of the cartilage is called.
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: Deposition of calcium and other minerals that turns cartilage into bone is ossification. Off-topic (biology), moved.

113.s: The production of tears when dust particles hit the human eye; is an example of which of the following?
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
113.x: Tears flushing dust from the eye are part of the body's first-line (innate) defence – immunity; they contain lysozyme. Off-topic (biology), moved.

113.s: What is a characteristic feature of a first-degree burn?
o: Minor epithelial damage, presence of redness
Partial thickness burn and scalds, may be painful
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
113.x: A first-degree (superficial) burn damages only the epidermis, with redness and pain; partial-thickness is second degree and full-thickness/necrosis third degree. Off-topic (first aid), moved.

113.s: Which instrument is used to measure blood pressure?
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Blood pressure is measured with a sphygmomanometer. Off-topic (biology/health), moved.

113.s: In case of heat stroke, the body temperature?
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
113.x: In heat stroke the body's cooling fails and core temperature rises quickly (above 40°C). Off-topic (health), moved.

113.s: The weight of a brain of a normal human adult is about
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
113.x: An adult human brain weighs about 1.3-1.4 kg, i.e. about 3 pounds.

113.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the excretory system in humans?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
113.x: Nissl's granules are in the cell body of a neuron (nervous system), not the excretory system; the glomerulus, Bowman's capsule and Henle's loop are parts of the nephron. Off-topic (human biology), moved to book 5.

113.s: An abnormal cavity containing pus is called as
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: An abscess is a localised cavity filled with pus; a hematoma is collected blood, a cyst a fluid sac, a tumour a mass of cells. Off-topic (health), moved to book 5.

113.s: Tooth enamel is made up of which of the following?
113.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
113.x: Tooth enamel, the hardest substance in the body, is made of calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite). Off-topic (biology), moved to book 5.

113.s:
Which of the following statements is/are NOT correct with respect to definition of anatomy and physiology?
I. Physiology focuses on the physical arrangement of parts in the body.
II. Anatomy studies the inner functioning of cells, tissues and organs.
o: Only statement I is not correct
Only statement II is not correct
Both statements I and II are not correct
Both statements I and II are correct
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer (FRO) Paper-I General Studies & M
113.x: Both statements swap the definitions: anatomy studies the structure (physical arrangement) of body parts, physiology studies how cells, tissues and organs function – so both are not correct.

113.s: Which of the following is a procedure used to save an abscessed tooth in which the pulp chamber is cleaned out, disinfected, and filled with a permanent filling?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
113.x: Root canal therapy cleans, disinfects and fills the pulp chamber of an abscessed tooth; gum grafts and gingivoplasty treat gums. Off-topic (biology), moved.

113.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the human female reproductive system?
113.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
113.x: The vas deferens carries sperm in the MALE reproductive system; fimbriae (of the fallopian tube), cervix and endometrium (uterine lining) are female parts.

113.s: Which of the following is not a part of the female reproductive system in human beings?
113.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
113.x: The vas deferens carries sperm in the male reproductive system; ovary, uterus and fallopian tube are female organs. (Biology; moved.)

113.s:
Match Table-I with Table-II and choose correct code.
Table-I - Table-II
A. Lipase -
1. Breaks lactose
B. Amylase -
2. Breaks fat
C. Trypsin -
3. Breaks starch
D. Lactase -
4. Breaks Protein
113.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
113.x: Lipase breaks fat, amylase breaks starch, trypsin breaks protein and lactase breaks lactose: A-2, B-3, C-4, D-1.

113.s: In humans, Milk Teeth generally fall off at what age?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
113.x:
Most books and keys: between 6 and 8 years. Strictly: shedding starts at about 6 and is complete by about 12 (incisors 6-8, canines and molars 9-12) (AAP healthychildren.org; Wikipedia 'Deciduous teeth').
Milk (deciduous) teeth begin to fall at about 6 years, and the incisors are shed by about 6-8 years, so most keys give 6-8. Shedding of canines and molars continues until about 12, which is why 10-12 is only the end of the process.

113.s: The classical example for closed wound is
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: A contusion (bruise) is the classic closed wound, with the skin unbroken; lacerated, penetrating and incised wounds are open.

113.s: One of the following is not administered through rectum
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x:
Key: ecbolic (a drug class, usually injected), since suppositories and enemas are by definition rectal preparations. Strictly, one ecbolic (misoprostol) can also be given rectally (Wikipedia, Uterotonic).
Ecbolics (drugs such as oxytocin that stimulate uterine contraction) are given by injection, not per rectum, whereas suppositories and enemas are rectal preparations. (Off-topic: moved to general science.)

113.s: In a healthy adult, what is the approximate percentage of white blood cells in total blood volume?
113.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
113.x: White blood cells (with platelets) form well under 1% of blood volume (the thin buffy coat), so 'one percent' is the nearest figure.

113.s: The tube that connects the pharynx with the stomach is the
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: The oesophagus (food pipe) connects the pharynx to the stomach; the duodenum and jejunum are parts of the small intestine and the pylorus is the stomach's outlet.

113.s: Which cranial nerve in humans is the largest and has both, sensory and motor functions?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Engineers General Studies & Mental Ability 2
113.x: The trigeminal (5th) nerve is the largest cranial nerve and has both sensory and motor fibres.

113.s: It is always better to eat/drink the following foods in case of heat stroke?
113.src: APPSC Asst. Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper
113.x: Fluids such as lemon water or buttermilk restore water and salts in heat stroke; proteins, meat and dry fruits add heat load.

113.s: Which of the following is not a solid form of medicine
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Syrup is a liquid dosage form; tablets, capsules and boluses are solid.

113.s: Calcium along with which mineral is required for the strength of skeletal muscle?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
113.x: Calcium phosphate gives bones (the skeleton that muscles pull on) their strength, so phosphorus goes with calcium; the stem's 'skeletal muscle' means the skeletal system.

113.s: The gaseous exchange in humans takes place in
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: Gas exchange in the lungs takes place in the alveoli, across their thin walls into the capillaries. Off-topic (biology), moved.

113.s: The longest fibre on the cell body of a neuron is called:
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
113.x: The axon is the single long fibre that carries impulses away from the neuron's cell body; dendrites are short and branched.

113.s: What is the immediate first aid that can be administered to a victim of burns?
o: Wetting the burnt part in cold water
Removing stuck cloth on the burnt part
113.x: Immediate first aid for a burn is to cool the part in cool or cold running water. Stuck cloth must not be pulled off, butter or ointment should not be applied, and water should not be poured with force.

113.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the human respiratory system?
113.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
113.x: Schwann cells form the myelin sheath of peripheral nerves (nervous system); trachea, bronchi and larynx are parts of the respiratory tract.

113.s: Number of Incisors, Canines, Premolars and Molars in humans is respectively
113.src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
113.x: Human adult dentition (32 teeth) = 8 incisors, 4 canines, 8 premolars, 12 molars (dental formula 2123 per half-jaw).

113.s: The visual acuity of 20/200 is characteristic feature of
113.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
113.x: Visual acuity of 20/200 (seeing at 20 feet what a normal eye sees at 200 feet) in the better eye with correction is the usual threshold of legal blindness.

113.s: Which of the following are parts of the excretory system?
113.x: Bowman's capsule and Henle's loop are parts of the nephron in the kidney; colon, rectum, appendix and ileum belong to the digestive system.
