113.s: Which of following is NOT a part of the human excretory system?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
113.x: Alveoli are air sacs of the lungs (respiratory system); nephrons, Bowman's capsule and ureters belong to the excretory system.

113.s: Which of the following is a voluntary muscle that you can control consciously?
113.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon, Group-IV and Other Posts Gene
113.x: Skeletal (striated) muscle is voluntary; smooth and cardiac muscles are involuntary.

113.s: The capsules that contain medicines taken by us are normally made of
113.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
113.x: Medicine capsule shells are normally made of gelatin (from collagen), which dissolves in the stomach.

113.s: Which of the following is used to control Mange
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Sulphur ointment (sulphur, often with lime) is the classic remedy for mange, a mite infestation of animal skin.

113.s: What is range of the pH value of the human blood?
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Human blood is slightly alkaline, pH 7.35-7.45.

113.s: Which of the following assist the eye lens to adjust its focus for viewing bodies at different distances?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
113.x: The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the eye lens (accommodation) to focus near and far objects. The pupil only controls light entry; rods and cones are retinal receptors.

113.s: Hyper Natrimia is excess presence in blood of?
113.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
113.x: Hypernatraemia means too much sodium in the blood (natrium = sodium).

113.s: Which of the following are the main constituents of Dettol, a commonly used antiseptic in homes?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
113.x: Dettol's main constituents are chloroxylenol and alpha-terpineol (with pine oil); it has no iodine.

113.s: The gap between two neurons is called a
113.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
113.x: The junction between two neurons is a synapse; dendrites and axons are parts of a neuron, and an impulse is the signal it carries.

113.s: What is the average lung capacity of an adult human being (choose nearest figure)?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: Total lung capacity of an adult is about 6 litres (vital capacity ~4.5–4.8 L).

113.s: For the examination of skin scrapings which of the following is required
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Skin scrapings are cleared with 10-20% potassium hydroxide (KOH mount) so that fungal elements and mites can be seen. Heparin is an anticoagulant, and HCl and dichromate are not used for this.

113.s: If a person closes one eye and looks with the other eye only, he would see?
113.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: With one eye we lose binocular depth perception, so the world looks flat, i.e. two-dimensional (the usual key). Colour vision is not lost.

113.s: What is the primary function of the human digestive system?
o: To break down food and absorb nutrients
To provide Oxygen to the body
113.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
113.x: The digestive system breaks food down into simple absorbable molecules and absorbs the nutrients; temperature control, blood circulation and oxygen supply belong to other systems.

113.s: How many valves are present in a human heart?
113.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
113.x: The human heart has four valves: tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral (bicuspid) and aortic. (Off-topic: human biology.)

113.s: Which blood vessels have the smallest diameter?
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
113.x: Capillaries are the narrowest blood vessels (about 5–10 micrometres), one cell thick. (Off-topic: biology.)

113.s: Which of the elements found in human body has functional requirement?
113.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
113.x:
Official key: Arsenic. Strictly: arsenic's essentiality in humans is unproven (it is a toxic element); none of the options is an established essential element.
Among the options only arsenic is treated as a (possibly essential) ultra-trace element with a functional role; titanium, caesium and aluminium have no known requirement.

113.s: Which part of the eye gives it a distinctive colour?
113.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
113.x: The iris is the pigmented muscular ring around the pupil and gives the eye its colour. The cornea is transparent, the pupil is an opening and the retina lies at the back.

113.s: The human saliva has an average pH of____.
113.src: APPSC Assistant Conservator of Forest (General Studies & Men
113.x: Human saliva is slightly acidic to near-neutral, pH about 6.2-7.6 with an average of about 6.7 (salivary amylase works best near this); 5.5 is the enamel-dissolving critical pH, and 7.8 and 9.1 are too alkaline.

113.s: Which enzyme helps in the digestion of fats in the gut of humans?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Engineers General Studies & Mental Ability 2
113.x: Lipase digests fats (pancreas, intestine); amylase digests starch, lactase lactose, and helicase unwinds DNA.

113.s: Which of the following enzymes found in saliva is responsible for digestion?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
113.x: Saliva contains salivary amylase (ptyalin), which digests starch; pepsin acts in the stomach, trypsin from the pancreas.

113.s: Of the following bacteria, ____ causes pneumonia.
113.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
113.x: Haemophilus influenzae causes pneumonia (as does Streptococcus pneumoniae); S. thermophilus and Lactobacillus are curd/yoghurt bacteria and E. coli is a gut bacterium.

113.s: Which enzyme is found in tears?
113.src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
113.x: Tears contain lysozyme, an antibacterial enzyme that breaks down bacterial cell walls. Ptyalin is in saliva, pepsin in the stomach, and sebum is skin oil. (Off-topic: human physiology.)

113.s: Which body fluid plays an important role in transporting digested fats in humans?
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Digested fats are absorbed into the lacteals (lymph vessels) of the villi and carried by lymph, not directly by blood.

113.s: What is the main function of the kidneys in the human body?
o: To filter waste products and excess of water from the blood
Help the body to absorb nutrients from the food
To pump the blood throughout the body
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: The kidneys filter waste products and excess water from the blood and form urine; digestion, absorption and pumping are other organs' jobs.

113.s: Which of the following is the longest part of the alimentary canal?
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
113.x: The small intestine (about 6-7 m) is the longest part of the alimentary canal.

113.s: Fat in the food eaten by us is completely digested in?
113.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: Fats are completely digested in the small intestine by bile (emulsification) and pancreatic and intestinal lipase.

113.s: The duodenum is a part of the
113.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
113.x: The duodenum is the first part of the small intestine.

113.s: Nerves of the brain responsible for sending and receiving information
113.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
113.x: Neurons (nerve cells) send and receive information in the brain and nerves.

113.s: If all the alveoli in a human lung are separated and spread, they will occupy the size of a typical?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
113.x: The roughly 300-500 million alveoli have a surface area of about 70 m² – about a tennis court.

113.s: Identify the gland, which release HCl in human digestive tract.
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Gastric glands of the stomach wall release HCl.

113.s: Leucocytes are also known as ____ as they are colourless due to the lack of haemoglobin.
113.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
113.x: Leucocytes are white blood cells – colourless because they lack haemoglobin.

113.s: The ____ in the iris that make pigment are called melanocytes.
113.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
113.x: Melanocytes are the cells that make melanin pigment in the iris.

113.s: Red blood cells are formed in
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
113.x: Red blood cells are formed in the red bone marrow.

113.s: Which drugs are used to lower the body temperature?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
113.x: Antipyretics (e.g. paracetamol) lower raised body temperature; analgesics relieve pain.

113.s: Which of the following carries Carbon dioxide rich blood from heart to lungs in humans?
113.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated (CO2-rich) blood from the right ventricle to the lungs; pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood.

113.s: The largest artery in the human body
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: The aorta, leaving the left ventricle, is the largest artery of the body.

113.s: A blood vessel which pumps the blood from the heart to the entire body
113.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
113.x: Arteries carry blood from the heart to the body (the aorta from the left ventricle); veins return it and capillaries exchange materials.

113.s:
Match the given organs with the arteries which supply blood to them.
Organ:
I. Kidney
II. Liver
III. Heart
Arteries which supply blood:
a. Renal arteries
b. Hepatic arteries
c. Coronary arteries
113.src: APPSC Sample Taker General Studies & Mental Abilities 2023
113.x: Renal arteries supply the kidney, hepatic arteries the liver and coronary arteries the heart: I-a, II-b, III-c.

113.s: Alimentary canal runs from mouth to?
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
113.x: The alimentary canal is the continuous tube from the mouth to the anus (mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small and large intestine, rectum, anus).

113.s: Which of the following systems of the human body is responsible when a person sneezes?
113.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
113.x: Sneezing is a reflex of the respiratory system: irritants in the nasal lining trigger a forceful expulsion of air through the nose and mouth. It is controlled by the medulla, but the system involved is respiratory, not immune (printed key: immune system).

113.s: Anorexia and bulimia are types of ____ disorders.
113.x: Anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa are eating disorders (self-starvation; binge eating with purging).

113.s: A cardiac portion, a fundic region and a pyloric portion are parts of which of the following organs/body parts?
113.src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
113.x: The stomach has a cardiac part (near the oesophagus), a fundic region and a pyloric part (opening into the duodenum).

113.s:
In the context of human physiology, match the blood components with their respective names.
Blood components:
1. Erythrocytes
2. Leukocytes
3. Thrombocytes
Names:
A. White blood cells
B. Platelets
C. Red blood cells
113.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
113.x: Erythrocytes are red blood cells, leukocytes white blood cells and thrombocytes platelets: 1-C, 2-A, 3-B.

113.s: Anorexia nervosa is a ....disorder.
113.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
113.x: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder (self-starvation from fear of weight gain).

113.s: Which of the following is NOT a region of the human stomach?
113.x: Serosa is the outermost layer of the wall of the alimentary canal, not a region of the stomach. The stomach's regions are the cardiac part (where the oesophagus opens), the fundus, the body and the pyloric part (which opens into the duodenum).

113.s: All of the following are tests for brain, spinal cord, and nerve disorders, EXCEPT ______
113.x: Bronchoscopy examines the airways and lungs, not the nervous system. Myelography (spinal cord imaging), electroencephalography (EEG – brain's electrical activity) and echoencephalography (ultrasound of the brain) are nervous-system tests.

113.s: The part of the brain that controls involuntary actions such as blood pressure, salivation and vomiting
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: The medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions – heartbeat, blood pressure, breathing, salivation, swallowing and vomiting. The cerebrum handles voluntary action and thought, the cerebellum balance, and the diencephalon (hypothalamus) temperature, hunger and thirst.

113.s: Which part of the brain controls the process of Breathing?
113.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
113.x: Breathing is controlled by the respiratory centre in the medulla oblongata (with the pons). The cerebellum controls balance, the hypothalamus temperature/hunger, the cerebrum voluntary actions.

113.s: Which of the following represents the gap between two neurons?
113.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
113.x: A synapse is the junction (gap) between two neurons across which the impulse passes, usually by neurotransmitters. The dendrite receives and the axon carries the impulse; the impulse is the signal itself, not a gap. (Biology PYQ: moved to book 5 row 1.)

113.s: Suppose you have four test tubes labelled as ‘A’, ‘B’, ‘C’ and ‘D’. ‘A’ contains plain water, ‘B’ contains solution of an alkali, ‘C’ contains solution of an acid, and ‘D’ contains solution of sodium chloride. Which one of these solutions will turn phenolphthalein solution pink?
113.x: Phenolphthalein turns pink in basic (alkaline) solution. Tube B has an alkali, while water, acid and NaCl solution are neutral or acidic and leave it colourless.

113.s: Which of the following metals is the most reactive metal?
113.x: In the reactivity series calcium lies far above zinc, iron and copper, so it is the most reactive of these.

113.s: Zinc is used to protect iron form corrosion because zinc is
o: a good conductor of heat and electricity.
113.x: Zinc is more electropositive (more reactive) than iron, so it corrodes in preference to iron and protects it (galvanisation, sacrificial protection).

113.s: Which one of the following gives the highest amount of hydrogen ions (H+)?
113.x: Gastric juice contains HCl (pH ~1.5-3.5), so it is the most acidic and has the highest H+ concentration; lemon juice is a weaker acid and the others are basic.

113.s: Which of the following acids is present in ant bites?
113.x: Ant bites inject formic acid (methanoic acid), as the notes state.

113.s: Chemical used for preserving the serum is
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Merthiolate (thiomersal), a mercury compound, is the classic preservative for serum and vaccines. Heparin and oxalates are anticoagulants that stop blood clotting, and formaldehyde is a tissue fixative, not a serum preservative.

113.s: What is Bisphenol A (BPA)?
o: A medical test for detecting cancer
A test for testing the use of drugs to improve performance by athletes
A chemical used for the development of food-packaging materials
A special type of alloy steel
113.x: Bisphenol A is an industrial chemical used to make polycarbonate plastics and epoxy food-can linings, i.e. food-packaging materials. It is not a medical test, a doping test or an alloy steel.

113.s: What is Bisphenol A (BPA)?
o: A medical test for detecting cancer
A test for testing the use of drugs to improve
A chemical used for the development of food-
A special type of alloy steel
113.x: BPA is used in polycarbonate plastics and food-can linings, so it is a chemical used for food-packaging materials. The other options (medical test, doping test, alloy steel) do not describe it.

113.s: Gold is dissolved in –
o: Mixture of Sulfuric and Nitric Acid
Mixture of hydrochloric acid and nitric acid (aqua regia)
113.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Mixture of hydrochloric acid and nitric acid (aqua regia)); it is added as option 5.
Gold dissolves only in aqua regia, a 3:1 mixture of concentrated hydrochloric and nitric acids. No single acid dissolves it, and a sulphuric–nitric mixture does not either, so the printed key (c) is wrong.

113.s: Mustard gas is used –
o: As a source of mustard oil
113.x: Mustard gas (sulphur mustard) is a blistering chemical-warfare agent. It has nothing to do with mustard oil, fuels or deodorants.

113.s: During the first world war, which of the following gas was utilised as the chemical weapon?
113.x: Mustard gas (sulphur mustard) was used as a chemical weapon in World War I, along with chlorine and phosgene. Carbon monoxide and hydrogen cyanide were not the typical battlefield agents.

113.s: What is the chemical name of the deadly poison ‘cyanide’?
113.x: Prussic acid is hydrocyanic acid (HCN), whose salts are the cyanides. Sulphuric, hydrochloric and nitric acids are mineral acids, not cyanide.

113.s: Stinging hair of nettle leaves inject the following acid causing burning pain?
113.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
113.x: Nettle leaf hairs inject formic (methanoic) acid, causing the burning pain. Acetic acid is vinegar, phosphoric acid is in colas and sulphuric acid is a mineral acid.

113.s: Which of the following materials in normally used in a breath analyzer test to ascertain whether a person is drunk or not?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
113.x: In the breath analyser, orange acidified potassium dichromate turns green as it oxidises the alcohol in the breath. Permanganate, silica gel and baking soda are not used.

113.s: What is the dominant acid in a 'bee sting'?
113.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
113.x: School books and Rocket list formic (methanoic) acid as the acid of a bee sting. Lactic, malic and citric acids come from muscles, apples and lemons.

113.s: Hard coffee stains on clothes can be properly removed by?
113.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
113.x: Sodium hypochlorite (bleach) is an oxidising agent that breaks down the coloured compounds of tea and coffee stains on white cloth. Water and lemon juice only lighten fresh stains, and petrol removes grease, not coffee.

113.s: Cola type soft drinks contain:
113.x: Cola drinks are acidified with phosphoric acid, which gives their tangy taste. Formic, lactic and acetic acids are not cola ingredients.

113.s:
Consider the following statements
1.
Assertion (A): Formic acid is a stronger acid than acetic acid.
2.
Reason (R): Formic acid is an organic acid.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
113.x: Formic acid is stronger than acetic acid because acetic acid's CH3 group pushes electrons and weakens it. Formic acid is also an organic acid, but that does not explain why it is stronger, so both are true and R is not the explanation.

113.s: When ants bite, they inject:
113.x: Ants inject formic acid (from Latin formica, ant), which causes the burning sensation. Acetic acid, methanol and stearic acid are not involved.

113.s: Chlorination is a process used for water purification. The disinfecting action of chlorine is mainly due to:
o: The formation of hydrochloric acid when chlorine is added to water
The formation of hypochlorous acid when chlorine is added to water
The formation of nascent oxygen when chlorine is added to water
The formation of hydrogen when chlorine is added to water
113.x: Chlorine reacts with water to form hypochlorous acid (HOCl) and HCl; HOCl is the strong disinfectant that kills microbes. HCl does not disinfect, and 'nascent oxygen' is an older textbook explanation.

113.s: Which is the most reactive metal ?
113.x: Potassium is at the top of the reactivity series (K > Na > Ca > Fe), so it is the most reactive of the four metals.

113.s: Soft drinks such as colas contain significant quantities of :
113.x: Colas contain significant caffeine, a stimulant alkaloid. Nicotine is in tobacco, tannin in tea and renin is a kidney enzyme.

113.s: Which acid is mainly find in lemons?
113.x: Lemon contains citric acid. Acetic acid is in vinegar, ascorbic acid is vitamin C and nitric acid is a mineral acid.

113.s: When ants bite, they inject :
113.x: Ants inject formic acid, a simple carboxylic acid. Glacial acetic acid, methanol and stearic acid are wrong.

113.s: What is the dominant chemical present in vinegar?
113.x: Vinegar is dilute acetic acid, whose IUPAC name is ethanoic acid. Formic acid is the ant-sting acid and malic acid is in apples.

113.s: Food cans are coated with tin but not with zinc because
o: zinc has a higher melting point than tin.
zinc is more reactive than tin.
tin is more reactive than zinc.
113.x: Zinc is more reactive than tin, so it would react with food acids and form harmful salts; tin is less reactive and safe. Cost and melting point are not the reason.

113.s: Citric acid is present in free form in
113.x: Lemon contains citric acid in free form. Tamarind mainly has tartaric acid, apple malic acid and milk lactic acid.

113.s: Sodawater obtained by passing carbon dioxide in water is
113.x: CO2 dissolves in water to form carbonic acid, so soda water is acidic. It is not basic, and it is neither an oxidising nor a reducing agent.

113.s: Which one of the following acids is used in the manufacturing of baking powder ?
113.x: Baking powder is baking soda plus a mild edible acid, tartaric acid. Oxalic acid is toxic, and lactic and benzoic acids are not its acid component.

113.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Caffeine, a constituent of tea and coffee is a diuretic.
2. Citric acid is used in soft drinks.
3. Ascorbic acid is essential for the formation of bones and teeth.
4. Citric acid is a good substitution for ascorbic acid in our nutrition.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
113.x: Caffeine is a diuretic, citric acid is used in soft drinks and ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is needed for collagen in bones and teeth. Citric acid cannot replace ascorbic acid, so 1, 2 and 3 only.

113.s: Which one of the following does not contain COOH group?
113.x: Ascorbic acid is acidic because of an enol hydroxyl in a lactone ring and has no carboxyl group. Citric, lactic and tartaric acids are all carboxylic (–COOH) acids.

113.s: If a red litmus paper turns to blue when few drops of a liquid are poured on the paper, then the liquid is a/an?
o: Could be an acid or base
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
113.x: Bases turn red litmus blue; acids turn blue litmus red, and a neutral salt changes neither.

113.s:
Arrange the following solutions in the ascending order of pH value?
A. Lemon juice
B. Human blood
C. Milk of Magnesia
D. Sodium Hydroxide Solution
113.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
113.x: Lemon juice (~2) < human blood (~7.4) < milk of magnesia (~10) < NaOH solution (~14).

113.s: If Hydrochloric Acid is added to few pieces of Zinc in a beaker and a burning match stick is brought near the mouth of the beaker, then?
o: The gas inside the beaker catches fire
The match stick burns at original intensity
The match stick burns at reduced intensity
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
113.x: Zinc and dilute HCl give hydrogen gas, which catches fire with a pop when a burning match is brought near. The match is not put out, because hydrogen is combustible.

113.s: During winter in cold regions, bottles of vinegar are found to freeze. This happens because
o: Pure ethanoic acid has a high melting point
Pure ethanoic acid has a low melting point
Pure ethanoic acid is a strong acid
Pure ethanoic acid is a weak acid
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Pure (glacial) ethanoic acid melts at about 290 K (16.6 °C), well above winter temperatures in cold regions, so it freezes; that is why it is called glacial acetic acid (NCERT). A low melting point would keep it liquid, so the printed key 'low melting point' is wrong.

113.s: Bleaching action of chlorine is due to which reaction?
113.x: Chlorine bleaches by oxidation: with water it forms hypochlorous acid, which gives nascent oxygen that oxidises the coloured matter.

113.s: ‘Oil of Vitriol’ is the common name of which of the following?
113.x: Oil of vitriol is concentrated sulphuric acid (H2SO4), the 'king of chemicals'. Blue vitriol is copper sulphate.

113.s: Which one of the following is an organic acid?
113.x: Acetic acid (vinegar) is an organic (carboxylic) acid. HCl, HNO3 and H2SO4 are mineral acids.

113.s:
Which among the following is an incorrect pair? (Natural Source – Acid)
I. Vinegar – Acetic acid
II. Curd – Lactic acid
III. Tamarind – Citric acid
Codes
113.x: Tamarind's acid is tartaric acid, not citric acid, so only pair III is incorrect. Vinegar is acetic acid and curd is lactic acid.

113.s: Which one of the following was the first mineral acid discovered?
113.x:
Most keys (Testbook, NDA 2020): sulphuric acid. Some solution books: nitric acid. The history is not settled; the alchemists knew both early.
Sulphuric acid ('oil of vitriol') is usually given as the first mineral acid, known to the medieval alchemists. Some keys give nitric acid instead.

113.s: Which metal is generally used for coating of brass utensils to prevent copper contamination?
113.x: Brass and copper vessels are tinned ('kalai') so that food acids do not dissolve copper. Zinc and lead would themselves be toxic, and aluminium is not used for this.

113.s: Which acid is used in photography–
113.x: Oxalic acid (as ferrous oxalate developer and in toning) is the acid used in photography. Formic acid is in ant stings, citric acid in lemons and acetic acid in vinegar.

113.s: Which gas is used in the purification of drinking water?
113.x: Chlorine is used to disinfect drinking water; it forms hypochlorous acid, which kills germs.

113.s: Which one of the following organic acids is abundant in grapes, tamarind and banana?
113.x: Tartaric acid is abundant in grapes, tamarind and banana. Citric acid is in citrus fruits, and lactic acid in curd.

113.s:
Which of the following pairs is/are NOT correctly matched ? (Acid) (Acid found in)
1. Lactic acid – Curd
2. Tartaric acid – Grapes
3. Acetic acid – Potato
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Code :
113.x: Lactic acid–curd and tartaric acid–grapes are correct. Acetic acid is in vinegar, not potato, so only pair 3 is wrong.

113.s:
Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I
List-II (Natural Source) (Acid)
A. Vinegar i. Methanoic acid
B. Tamarind ii. Lactic acid
C. Sour milk (curd) iii. Acetic acid
D. Nettle sting iv. Tartaric acid
Codes :
113.x: Vinegar–acetic (iii), tamarind–tartaric (iv), sour milk–lactic (ii), nettle sting–methanoic/formic (i).

113.s: The alkaloid caffeine is present in :
113.x: Caffeine is the alkaloid of both tea and coffee (also colas). Lemon water has citric acid, not caffeine.

113.s: Which one among the following metals is more reactive than hydrogen?
113.x: Tin lies above hydrogen in the reactivity series (Pb, Sn above H), so it displaces hydrogen from dilute acids. Mercury, copper and silver lie below hydrogen.

113.s: Which one of the following represents the correct order of electron releasing tendency of metals?
113.x: Zinc is above copper and copper above silver in the reactivity series, so electron-releasing tendency is Zn > Cu > Ag.

113.s: Which of the following acid found in Apple?
113.x: Apples contain malic acid; nitric and sulphuric acids are strong mineral acids not found in fruits, and formic acid is found in ant stings.

113.s: ……… is the primary acid present in ripe bananas.
113.x: Ripe bananas contain malic acid as their main organic acid; formic acid occurs in ants and the others are mineral acids.

113.s: Acid turns blue litmus red and base turns red litmus blue. A student tested a liquid with a red litmus paper which remained red with no change. This shows that the liquid
o: is neither an acid nor a base.
must be pure water or acid.
113.x: Red litmus turns blue only with a base. No change means the liquid is not a base, but it could be an acid or neutral, so only option 1 must be true.

113.s: When we cut an onion, the synthase enzyme converts the amino acid sulfoxide of the onion into which acid?
113.x: Cutting an onion releases alliinase (synthase), which converts amino acid sulfoxides into sulfenic acids; these form the tear-inducing compound.

113.s: The pH of milk is 6. When it turns sour, the pH
113.x: Souring forms lactic acid by bacterial fermentation, so the acidity rises and the pH falls below 6.

113.s: Which one of the following elements will not react with dilute HCl to produce H2?
113.x: Mercury lies below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot displace hydrogen from dilute HCl. Al, Mg and Fe lie above hydrogen and release H2.

113.s: Which one among the following is the correct order of reactivity of the elements?
113.x: In the reactivity series the order is Na > Mg > Zn > Cu, with sodium most reactive and copper least.

113.s:
Match the following From Table A to Table B - Uses of Acids as Food
Table A:
I. Butyric Acid
II. Maleic Acid
III. Stearic Acid
IV. Oxalic Acid
Table B:
1. Fats
2. Wood Sorrel
3. Apples
4. Rancid Butter
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Butyric acid is in rancid butter, malic acid ('Maleic' in the stem) in apples, stearic acid in fats and oxalic acid in wood sorrel. Moved.

113.src: APPSC Sample Taker General Studies & Mental Abilities 2023
113.x: Orange - citric, tomato - oxalic, tamarind - tartaric: I-c, II-a, III-b.

113.s:
Match the following items with the acids found in them.
Natural source:
I. Orange
II. Tamarind
III. Tomato
Acid:
a. Tartaric Acid
b. Oxalic Acid
c. Citric Acid
113.src: APPSC Town Planning Building Overseers General Studies & Men
113.x: Orange - citric (c), tamarind - tartaric (a), tomato - oxalic (b): I-c, II-a, III-b (options 2 and 4 are printed identically).

113.s:
Which of the following acids are present in lemons?
(i) Citric acid
(ii) Tartaric acid
(iii) Malic acid
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
113.x: Lemons contain mainly citric acid with some malic acid; tartaric acid is the acid of tamarind and grapes.

113.s:
Match List-I (Acid) with List-II (Source):
List I
a. Citric acid
b. Oxalic acid
c. Lactic acid
d. Acetic acid
List II
1. Tomato
2. Lemon
3. Vinegar
4. Curd
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
113.x: Citric - lemon, oxalic - tomato, lactic - curd, acetic - vinegar: a-2, b-1, c-4, d-3.

113.s: Which of the following is a traditional remedy to alleviate the pain from sting of Nettle plant?
o: Rubbing the area with leaf of dock plant
113.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
113.x: The traditional remedy for a nettle sting (formic/methanoic acid) is rubbing the area with a dock leaf, which is basic (NCERT Class 7).

113.s: Tamarind contains:
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Tamarind contains tartaric acid.

113.s: Which of the following is the main acid present in Spinach?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
113.x: Spinach is rich in oxalic acid.

113.s: What is the scientific name of Ashwagandha?
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Ashwagandha is Withania somnifera (family Solanaceae). Withania coagulans is the 'paneer dodi' (Indian cheese-maker) and Solanum nigrum is black nightshade.

113.s: A flower is brightly coloured, scented and secretes nectar. It is most probably pollinated by
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: Bright colour, scent and nectar are adaptations that attract insects, so such a flower is insect-pollinated (entomophily). Wind- and water-pollinated flowers are small, dull and without nectar or scent.

113.s: Which of the following is pseudocereal
113.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
113.x: Buckwheat (kuttu) is a pseudocereal: its seeds are used like grain but it is not a grass (family Polygonaceae). Amaranth and quinoa are other pseudocereals.

113.s: Which part of the flower becomes the fruit?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: After fertilisation the ovary develops into the fruit and the ovules into seeds.

113.s: The magnitude of root pressure would be minimum during
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
113.x: Root pressure is lowest in summer, when heavy transpiration pulls water up and the positive root pressure largely disappears. It is highest in the rainy season, when absorption is high and transpiration low, so Rainy season was wrong.

113.s:
Match the following using suitable codes:
A (Plant):
a. Fennel
b. Ginger
c. Garlic
d. Touch me not
B (Botanical Name):
I. Mimosa pudica
II. Foeniculum Vulgare
III. Zingiber officinale
IV. Allium Sativum
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: Fennel – Foeniculum vulgare, ginger – Zingiber officinale, garlic – Allium sativum, touch-me-not – Mimosa pudica. Off-topic, moved.

113.s:
Match the following using suitable codes:
A (Medicinal Plant):
a. Sarpgandha
b. Isabgol
c. Arjuna
d. Sandal
B (Uses):
I. diuretic, refrigerant
II. nervous disorder
III. chronic constipation
IV. heart remedy
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: Sarpagandha – nervous disorders (hypertension), isabgol – chronic constipation, arjuna – heart remedy, sandal – diuretic, refrigerant. Off-topic, moved.

113.src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
113.x: Stomata – tiny pores on leaves, guard cells – open and close them, chloroplasts – contain chlorophyll, enzymes – biocatalysts. Off-topic, moved.

113.s:
Which of the following statements is correct with reference to sporopollenin?
i. The exine of pollen grains is made up of sporopollenin so that pollen grains can be preserved as fossils.
ii. It cannot withstand high temperatures.
iii. It is one of the most resistant organic materials.
iv. Enzymes can degrade it.
113.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
113.x: Sporopollenin forms the exine; it is one of the most resistant organic materials, withstands high temperatures and strong acids and alkalis, and no enzyme is known to degrade it – so only i and iii. Moved.

113.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are CORRECT for the processes involved in photosynthesis?
I. Absorption of light energy by chlorophyll
II. Oxidation of carbon dioxide to carbohydrates
113.src: APPSC Town Planning Building Overseers General Studies & Men
113.x: Photosynthesis begins with absorption of light by chlorophyll (I correct); carbon dioxide is reduced, not oxidised, to carbohydrate (II wrong) → Only I. Off-topic (biology), moved.

113.s: Apart from Sun light and Carbon Dioxide, the source for production of Oxygen through photosynthesis in plants is?
113.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
113.x: Plants split water in photosynthesis (photolysis); the oxygen released comes from water, not from CO2, air, chlorophyll or glucose. Off-topic (biology), moved.

113.s: What is the main role of photosynthesis in plants?
o: To absorb water from the soil
To take in carbon dioxide and release helium
To transport vitamins through the stem
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Photosynthesis lets green plants make their own food (glucose) from CO2 and water using sunlight; it releases oxygen, not helium. Off-topic (biology), moved.

113.s: Name the factor that does not require for photosynthesis
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Photosynthesis needs sunlight, water and carbon dioxide (and chlorophyll); oxygen is a product, not a requirement. Off-topic (biology), moved.

113.s: Transfer of pollen grains through wind is known as
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: Anemophily is pollination by wind; hydrophily is by water, entomophily by insects and ornithophily by birds.

113.s: Which part of Garlic plant is used?
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: The edible part of garlic is the bulb made of cloves (modified leaves). Off-topic (botany), moved.

113.s: Plants that complete their life cycle within one season are called
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Plants that complete their life cycle in one season are annuals, also called seasonal plants; biennials take two seasons/years and perennials live many years.

113.s: The following is generally used in bone healing in humans?
113.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
113.x: Cissus quadrangularis (hadjod, 'bone-setter') is the herb traditionally used for bone healing; garlic, black pepper and onion are not.

113.s: Which plants are called naked-seeded plants?
113.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
113.x: Gymnosperms (e.g. pines, cycas) bear naked seeds not enclosed in a fruit; angiosperms have seeds inside fruits. (Moved to general science.)

113.s: By self-pollination, the seeds formed are
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: Repeated self-pollination leads to inbreeding depression, so the seeds and progeny are weaker; cross-pollination gives vigour and new varieties. (Moved to general science.)

113.s: The study of grasses is known as:
113.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
113.x: Agrostology is the study of grasses; agronomy is crop science and anthology a collection of writings.

113.s: Which of the following seeds have wings that help in seed dispersal?
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Drumstick (Moringa) and maple seeds are winged and dispersed by wind; Xanthium and Urena have hooks, castor and balsam burst open.

113.s: The eyes of the potato tuber are
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
113.x: The 'eyes' of a potato tuber are axillary buds (in the axils of scale leaves), proving the tuber is a stem.

113.s: Which one of the following statements is not correct ?
o: The fibre length of cotton is 1-5 cm
Recommended dose of fertilizer (kg/ha) for Pusa
Edible part of apple is mesocarp
113.x: The edible part of an apple is the fleshy thalamus (receptacle), not the mesocarp, so 4 is wrong; cotton fibre of about 1-5 cm and boron as a micronutrient are correct.

113.s: What is the function of "stomata" in plants?
113.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: Stomata are leaf pores for gas exchange (CO2 in, O2 and water vapour out); xylem transports water.

113.s: Which of the following inputs is required for photosynthesis to occur?
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
113.x: Photosynthesis needs chlorophyll, light, CO2 and water; oxygen and glucose are its products.

113.s: Which of the following mechanisms help prevent cavitation in the xylem?
o: Negative pressure inside the vessels and the pores
End walls of the vessels and the pores
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
113.x: The end walls of xylem vessels and their pit pores (pit membranes) stop air bubbles spreading, preventing cavitation from blocking the whole water column.

113.s: Which Tissue helps in the transport of water in plants?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Xylem carries water and minerals from roots upward; phloem carries food.

113.s: Which cells control the opening and closing of stomata?
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Two kidney-shaped guard cells around each stoma swell or shrink and so open or close the pore; xylem and phloem conduct water and food.

113.s: Which plant is traditionally known as an antidote for snake bites?
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
113.x: Rauvolfia serpentina (sarpagandha) is the traditional snake-bite remedy; neem, teak and sal are not.

113.s: An example of a phosphoenol pyruvate carboxyl kinase (PEP-CK) type of C4 photosynthesis
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
113.x: Panicum (e.g. Panicum maximum) is the classic PEP-CK type C4 plant; sugarcane and maize are NADP-ME type, Amaranthus NAD-ME type.

113.s: Which of the following does NOT belong to the plant kingdom?
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer (FRO) Paper-I General Studies & M
113.x: Annelids (earthworms, leeches) are animals; algae, pteridophytes and angiosperms belong to the plant kingdom.

113.s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Transpiration is the loss of water from the plant through evaporation at the root surface.
II. Transpiration is the main driver of water movement in the root nodules.
III. Transpiration is caused by the evaporation of water at the leaf-atmosphere interface; it creates negative pressure (tension) at the leaf surface.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are CORRECT?
113.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
113.x: Only III is correct: transpiration is evaporation at the leaf-air interface creating tension that pulls water up; it is not loss at the root surface, and it does not drive water in root nodules.

113.s: Which of the following plant tissues contains starch grains and is known as the starch sheath?
113.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
113.x: The endodermis of dicot stems stores starch grains and is called the starch sheath.

113.s: In which of the following species is axile placentation commonly observed?
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
113.x: Hibiscus (family Malvaceae, e.g. China rose, roselle) has axile placentation, ovules on a central axis of a multi-chambered ovary. Legumes such as Delonix show marginal placentation.

113.s: The patterns of arrangement of leaves on the stem are called
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
113.x: The arrangement of leaves on the stem is phyllotaxy. Venation is the vein pattern, aestivation the arrangement of floral parts in a bud and placentation of ovules.

113.s: Pollination by birds is called
113.x: Pollination by birds is ornithophily. Anemophily is by wind, entomophily by insects and autogamy is self-pollination.

113.s: Which of the following ions is essential for the opening and closing of stomata in plants?
113.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
113.x: Potassium ions moving into and out of guard cells open and close the stomata. Carbon, iron and sulphur have no such role.

113.s: What is the function of Xylem in a plant?
o: Transport of food from leaves to rest of the plant
Transport of water from roots to leaves
113.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
113.x: Xylem carries water and minerals from the roots to the leaves. Phloem carries food from the leaves to the rest of the plant, and cambium makes new wood layers.

113.s:
The following item consist of two Statements:
Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
A: Spirogyra, Ulothrix, Cladophora and Chara are grouped under Thallophyta.
R: Spirogyra, Ulothrix, Cladophora and Chara lack roots, stem, leaves, and vascular system.
o: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
113.src: APPSC Executive Officer Gr-III Endowment Paper-I General Stu
113.x: Spirogyra, Ulothrix, Cladophora and Chara are algae, grouped under Thallophyta because the plant body is an undifferentiated thallus with no roots, stem, leaves or vascular tissue. R states that defining feature, so it correctly explains A.

113.s: Water and minerals are conducted upward in roots and stems through the
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: Xylem conducts water and minerals upward from roots through stems to leaves. Phloem carries food; cambium and cortex do not conduct water.

113.s: In a plant transports food from the leaves to the rest of the plant through a process known as translocation.
113.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
113.x: Phloem moves food (sugars) from the leaves to the rest of the plant; this is translocation. Xylem and tracheids carry water, and meristem is growing tissue.

113.s: According to Sach's, the body of the vascular plant is composed of the following three tissue systems
o: Dermal tissue system, vascular tissue system and fundamental tissue system
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
113.x: Julius Sachs grouped plant tissues into three systems: dermal (epidermal), vascular (fundamental conducting) and fundamental (ground) tissue systems. Parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma are simple tissue types, not Sachs' tissue systems.

113.s: Which of the following parts of the stem consists of xylem and phloem together?
113.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
113.x: A vascular bundle contains xylem and phloem together. The cortex, endodermis and pith are ground-tissue regions without both conducting tissues.

113.s: Which among the following is actually not a tree?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: The banana is a giant herb: its 'trunk' is a pseudostem of leaf sheaths, not wood. Neem, peepal and banyan are true trees. (Off-topic: botany.)

113.s: Which of the following seeds can benifit a patient of diabetes mellitus?
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
113.x: Fenugreek (methi) seeds are rich in soluble fibre and help lower blood sugar, so they benefit diabetics. (Biology item, moved.)

113.s:
Which of the following statements is correct about Angiosperms?
A. Seeds naked (not enclosed in ovary)
B. Xylem vessels usually absent
C. Bears flowers where reproductive spores (gametes) develop
113.src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
113.x: Angiosperms bear flowers, have seeds enclosed in an ovary (fruit) and usually have xylem vessels. Naked seeds and absent vessels describe gymnosperms, so only C is correct. (Biology item, moved.)

113.s: The seeds of the following plants are often called 'dust seeds'
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
113.x: Orchids produce minute, endosperm-less 'dust seeds' dispersed by wind. Lodoicea (double coconut) has the largest seed. (Botany item, moved.)

113.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Plant):
a. Potato
b. Carrot
c. Apple
d. Cabbage
List-II (Edible Part):
i. Swollen thalamus
ii. Vegetative bud
iii. Modified root
iv. Modified stem
113.src: TSLPRB SI Civil Preliminary Written Exam 2018
113.x: The potato is a modified stem (tuber), the carrot a modified root, the apple a swollen thalamus (false fruit) and the cabbage a vegetative bud.

113.s: What is the colour of Chlorophyll a?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: Chlorophyll a is blue-green, while chlorophyll b is yellow-green. (Moved to 5:1.)

113.s: Plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilisation, are called ......
113.src: APPSC Executive Officer Gr-III Endowment Paper-I General Stu
113.x: Gymnosperms (gymnos = naked, sperma = seed) have ovules not enclosed in an ovary, exposed before and after fertilisation. Angiosperms enclose ovules in an ovary.

113.s: Spirogyra is an example of:
113.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
113.x: Spirogyra is a green filamentous alga.

113.s: Which part of the plant is a potato?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
113.x: The potato is a tuber - a modified underground stem with eyes (buds).

113.s: Which of the following plants eats mosquitoes?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
113.x: The pitcher plant is insectivorous – its pitcher traps and digests insects such as mosquitoes. Cinchona gives quinine; lemon grass only repels.

113.s: The drug Rauwolfia, is obtained from ______ of Sarpgandha.
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: The drug from Sarpagandha (Rauvolfia serpentina), used for blood pressure, comes from its roots. (Off-topic: medicinal plants.)

113.s: The complete male flower of the following plant is transported to the female flower for pollination
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
113.x: In Vallisneria the male flowers break off and float up to the water surface, where water currents carry them to the female flowers raised on long stalks, so the whole male flower travels. In Zostera (a seagrass) only long pollen grains are released and carried under water; Nymphaea (water lily) is insect-pollinated.

113.s: The National Tree of India is
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
113.x: India's national tree is the Indian banyan, Ficus benghalensis. Ficus religiosa is the peepal (sacred fig), Ficus elastica the rubber fig and Ficus racemosa the cluster fig (gular).

113.s: Which enzyme present in the stomach breaks down the proteins into small peptides?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: Pepsin, from the chief cells of the stomach, breaks proteins into small peptides. Trypsin and peptidases act in the small intestine and lipase digests fats.

113.s: Kwashiorkor disease is a result of
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
113.x: Kwashiorkor results from protein deficiency in a diet that may have enough calories. Vitamin, carbohydrate or water deficiency do not cause it.

113.s: Which of the following diseases is caused in humans by a severe lack of proteins and calories in the diet?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Engineers General Studies & Mental Ability 2
113.x: Marasmus results from severe lack of both protein and calories. Scurvy is vitamin C deficiency, goitre iodine deficiency and mumps a viral disease.

113.s: Which of the following are only proteins?
113.x: Keratin (hair, nails) and myosin (muscle) are both proteins. Fructose, maltose and sucrose are sugars, so the other pairs are not only proteins.

113.s: Which of the following refers to a sticky film of protein that forms on top of dairy milk?
113.x: Lactoderm is the name of the sticky protein skin that forms on top of heated milk. The other options are made-up words.

113.s: Which of the following is an essential amino acid for the human body?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
113.x: Isoleucine is one of the essential amino acids that must come from food. Alanine, aspartic acid and cysteine are made in the body.

113.s: Which of the following is cause of main cause of the disease Kwashiorkor?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
113.x: Kwashiorkor is caused by protein deficiency. Water deficiency, pollution and viruses do not cause it.

113.s: Which of the following is a non-essential amino acid?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
113.x: Tyrosine is non-essential because the body makes it from phenylalanine. Methionine, tryptophan and threonine are essential.

113.s: Principle protein of Maize is:
113.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
113.x: Zein, a prolamin, is the principal protein of maize, as gluten is of wheat.

113.s: The building blocks from which proteins are synthesized are known as:
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
113.x: Proteins are synthesised from amino acids, their building blocks.

113.s: The egg proteins are known as high biological value proteins because they contain
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
113.x: Egg proteins have high biological value because they contain all the essential amino acids in the right proportion.

113.s: Which are the primary group of proteins present in Milk?
113.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: Caseins are the primary group of milk proteins (about 80% of cow's milk protein); whey proteins make up the rest. Lactoferrin and albumin are minor.

113.s: For muscle building, athletes require a
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
113.x: Muscle is built from protein, so athletes need a high-protein diet. Calories, vitamins and glucose give energy or regulation, not muscle tissue.

113.s: Nutrients that help in building the body
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Proteins are the body-building nutrients. Carbohydrates and fats give energy and vitamins regulate.

113.s: Which of the following is known as wheat protein?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
113.x: Gluten is the protein of wheat that gives dough its elasticity.

113.s: Which of the following diseases is caused due to deficiency of both proteins and calories in the human diet?
113.src: APPSC Combined Recruitment (Hostel Welfare Officer, Division
113.x: Marasmic kwashiorkor results from deficiency of both proteins and calories (wasting with oedema). Goitre is iodine, achondroplasia genetic and rickets vitamin D.

113.s:
Arrange the following food items in the increasing order of the protein content per 100 gm of food.
a. Egg white
b. Bengalgram dal
c. Fish
d. Skimmed milk powder
e. Groundnuts
Select the appropriate option
o: a, c, b, e and d
d, e, b, c and a
a, b, c, d and e
c, a, b, d and e
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
113.x: Protein per 100 g rises from egg white (~11 g) to fish (~20 g), Bengal gram dal (~21 g), groundnut (~25 g) and skimmed milk powder (~35 g). So a, c, b, e, d.

113.s: Which one of the following are the building blocks of proteins?
113.x: Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins. Ribosomes make proteins, glucose builds carbohydrates and fatty acids build fats.

113.s: Proline is a type of _______.
113.src: APPSC 2021 Medical Officer (Ayurveda) In Ayush Department
113.x: Proline is one of the 20 amino acids that make up proteins (a non-essential one). It is not a base, a bacterium or a virus.

113.s: Edema is a typical clinical feature of which disease?
113.src: APPSC 2018 Question Papers and Keys for Mains Exams
113.x: Kwashiorkor (protein deficiency) typically shows oedema (swelling). Marasmus is wasting without oedema, and hypertension and fever do not feature oedema as a typical sign.

113.s: Which one of the following is not a protein ?
113.x: Oxytocin is a small peptide hormone of nine amino acids, not a protein. Keratin (hair, nails), fibroin (silk) and collagen (connective tissue) are true fibrous proteins.

113.s: Which one of the following is the richest source of protein?
113.x: Groundnut has about 25 g protein per 100 g, far more than rice (~7 g) or apple (<1 g).

113.s: Hair is composed of protein called –
113.x: Hair is made of the fibrous protein keratin. Casein is milk protein, globulin a blood protein and mucin the protein of mucus.

113.s: Which one of the following food materials contains all essential amino acids?
113.x: Egg protein has the highest biological value and contains all essential amino acids in the right proportion, so it is the reference protein. Milk and soybean are good but are not the exam answer; rice lacks lysine.

113.s: Kwashiorkor, a form of malnutrition, is caused by deficiency of which of the following?
113.x: Kwashiorkor is protein deficiency with adequate calories (oedema, swollen belly). Selenium, chromium and carbohydrate lack do not cause it.

113.s: Silk fibre, hairs, nails and claw are made of –
113.x:
Most books and keys: keratin. Strictly, silk fibre is fibroin, not keratin; only hair, nails and claws are keratin (PMF General Science Part 7, animal fibres: keratin or fibroin).
Hair, nails and claws are made of keratin, the answer books and keys give. Strictly silk is fibroin (another fibrous protein), so keratin is the best of the four; fibrin is the clot protein, elastin and collagen are connective-tissue proteins.

113.s:
Assertion (A) : Human diet should compulsorily contain glycine, serine and tyrosin.
Reason (R) : Essential amino acids can not be synthesized in the human body.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
113.x: Glycine, serine and tyrosine are non-essential – the body makes them – so A is false. R is true: essential amino acids cannot be synthesised and must come from food.

113.s: Alpha-keratin is a protein, present in :
113.x: Alpha-keratin is the fibrous protein of the skin's outer layer, hair and nails. Blood and lymph carry albumin and globulins; eggs carry albumin.

113.s: The disease caused by deficiency of protein in children is–
113.x: Marasmus is protein-energy malnutrition of infants (severe wasting). Pellagra (B3), beri-beri (B1) and rickets (D) are vitamin deficiencies.

113.s: The substance responsible for bread-making quality in wheat is –
113.x: Gluten, the protein of wheat, makes dough elastic and lets bread rise. Globulin is another protein class; glycine and lysine are amino acids.

113.s: Which one of the following proteins is present in human hair and nails?
113.x: Keratin forms hair and nails. Oxytocin and vasopressin are peptide hormones; trypsin is a digestive enzyme.

113.s: Casein is milk :
113.x: Casein is the main protein of milk (~80% of milk protein); milk sugar is lactose.

113.s: Which compound present in D.N.A. does not form amino acid ?
113.x: Adenine, guanine and cytosine are nitrogen bases of DNA; tyrosine is an amino acid, not a DNA component – the odd one out the question intends.

113.s: Most of the enzymes are :
113.x: Almost all enzymes are proteins (a few are RNA ribozymes); they are not lipids, acids or alkalis.

113.s: Which of the following proteins is found in milk ?
113.x: Casein is the main milk protein. Myosin is muscle protein, haemoglobin blood protein and agglutinins are antibodies.

113.s: Which one of the following compounds is not stored in human body –
113.x: Amino acids are not stored – surplus is deaminated and passed as urea. Glycogen (liver, muscle), fat and tocopherol (vitamin E, fat-soluble) are stored.

113.s: Enzymes are basically –
113.x: Enzymes are basically proteins (e.g. pepsin, trypsin) acting as biological catalysts; they are not fats, sugars or vitamins.

113.s: Which of the following disease is caused by severe deficiency of proteins?
113.x: Kwashiorkor is caused by severe protein deficiency; anaemia (iron), osteoporosis (calcium) and goitre (iodine) are not.

113.s:
Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List I
I. Vitamin
II. Enzyme
III. Hormone
IV. Protein
List II
A. Pepsin
B. Carotene
C. Keratin
D. Progesterone
Codes:
o: I - A, II - B, III - C, IV - D
I - B, II - A, III - D, IV - C
I - B, II - A, III - C, IV - D
I - A, II - B, III - D, IV – C
113.x: Vitamin – carotene (provitamin A), enzyme – pepsin, hormone – progesterone, protein – keratin, which is code (b).

113.s: Protein requirement of young and old person are –
o: Higher in the young and lower in the old
Higher in the old and lower in the young
Very high in the young and very low in the old
113.x: Older people need more protein per kg than young adults (about 1.0–1.2 g/kg against 0.8 g/kg) because ageing blunts protein use and causes muscle loss, as the key says.

113.s: Choose wrong statement regarding proteins :
o: We obtain proteins from both animals and plants
Proteins are made of amino acids
About 30 percent of our body weight comes from
Proteins are called building blocks of our body
113.x: About 16–20% (NCERT: ~20%) of body weight is protein, not 30%, so (c) is wrong. Proteins come from plants and animals, are made of amino acids and are the body-building nutrients.

113.s: Tendons through which muscles are connected to bones are tightly compacted bundles of which one of the following long fibrous protein?
113.x: Tendons are made of collagen, a tough fibrous protein. Fibrin is for clotting, elastin is in elastic tissue and cellulose is not a protein.

113.s: An enzyme which helps in the digestion of protein is
113.x:
Most keys: trypsin. Strictly: 'protease' is the class of all protein-digesting enzymes, so it is also true.
Trypsin (pancreas) digests protein; urease breaks urea and sulfatase sulphate esters. 'Protease' is the general class name for all protein-digesting enzymes, not one enzyme.

113.s: Which one of the following processes in the bodies of living organisms is a digestive process?
o: Breakdown of proteins into amino acids
Breakdown of glucose into CO₂ and H₂O
Conversion of amino acids into proteins
113.x: Digestion is breaking large food molecules into small absorbable ones, such as proteins into amino acids. The others are respiration or synthesis.

113.s: Which of the following changes is catalyzed by the enzyme trypsin?
113.x: Trypsin (pancreatic juice) breaks proteins (and peptones) into smaller peptides; peptidases finish them to amino acids. Pepsin makes peptones.

113.s: Which one of the following enzymes convert proteins into amino acids?
113.x: Pepsin is the only protein-digesting enzyme among the options (lactase – lactose, urease – urea, zymase – sugar fermentation); strictly pepsin gives peptides, which other enzymes finish to amino acids.

113.s:
Assertion (A) : All the proteins in our food are digested in small intestine only.
Reason (R) : The protein-digesting enzyme from the pancreas are released into the small intestine.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are individually true and (R) is the
Both (A) and (R) are individually true, but (R) is not
113.x: Protein digestion starts in the stomach with pepsin, so A is false; R is true – pancreatic trypsin and chymotrypsin enter the small intestine.

113.s: Which of the following is used in beauty parlours for hair setting?
113.x: Hair setting and perming work on the sulphur (disulphide) bonds of hair keratin, which are broken and re-formed in the new shape with sulphur compounds (thioglycolates). Chlorine and phosphorus are not used.

113.s: The plant dye henna imparts orange-red colour to skin and hairs due to its reaction with which of the following?
113.x: Lawsone, the dye of henna, binds to the proteins (keratin) and amino acids of skin and hair, giving the orange-red stain. It does not react with lipids, carbohydrates or nucleic acids.

113.s:
Which of the following are correct with reference to proteins?
i. They are made up of nucleotides.
ii. They are linear chains of amino acids.
iii. They are heteropolymer.
iv. They are homopolymer.
113.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
113.x: Proteins are linear chains of amino acids and are heteropolymers (20 kinds of amino acids); nucleotides make nucleic acids. Off-topic (biology), moved.

113.s: Which of the following digestive enzymes acts in the stomach of humans?
113.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
113.x: Pepsin acts in the stomach (protein digestion in acid medium); amylase acts in mouth and intestine, trypsin and lipase come from the pancreas.

113.s: The "Iodine test" is used for testing the presence of?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: Iodine solution turns starch blue-black, so the iodine test detects starch. Sugars, fats and salt give no such colour (fat is tested with paper, sugar with Benedict's reagent).

113.s: Which of the following type of carbohydrate is present in starch?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
113.x: Starch is a polysaccharide, a long chain of glucose units. Mono-, di- and oligosaccharides are single sugars or short chains.

113.s: Which of the following is the major nutrient present in rice?
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
113.x: Rice is mostly starch, so carbohydrate is its major nutrient. Its protein is only about 7%, and vitamins and minerals are minor.

113.s: Arrange the following sugars in the descending order of their relative sweetness?
113.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: Fructose is the sweetest natural sugar, followed by sucrose, glucose and maltose. The other orders put glucose, maltose or sucrose first.

113.s: Out of the below, which sugar constitutes the largest component of Honey?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
113.x: Honey is mainly fructose (about 38%), with slightly less glucose; sucrose and maltose are minor. So fructose is its largest component.

113.s:
Which of the following matches of the sweetener and its explanation is correct?
Sweetener:
I. Ortho-sulphobenzimide (Saccharin)
II. Aspartame
III. Alitame
Explanation:
a. 100 times as sweet as cane sugar
b. High potency sweetener
c. The first popular artifical sweetening agent
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer (FRO) Paper-I General Studies & M
113.x: Saccharin was the first popular artificial sweetener, aspartame is (in NCERT's words) about 100 times as sweet as cane sugar, and alitame is a high-potency sweetener. So I-c, II-a, III-b.

113.s: What are the basic chemical units with which lipids are made?
113.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
113.x: Lipids (fats) are made of fatty acids joined to glycerol. Glucose and fructose build carbohydrates, and amino acids build proteins.

113.s: The major part in honey is
113.x: Honey is mainly fructose (about 38%) with slightly less glucose, so fructose is its major sugar. Sucrose and maltose are only minor components.

113.s: The cause of sweet taste in fruits is :
113.x: Fructose (fruit sugar) gives fruits their sweet taste. Maltose is malt sugar, lactose milk sugar and ribose a sugar of RNA.

113.s:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and other as Reason (R) :
Assertion (A) : Invert sugar is more sweet than sucrose.
Reason (R) : Invert sugar is obtained by the hydrolysis of sucrose.
Select the correct answer from the code given below:
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct
113.x: Invert sugar (glucose + fructose) is sweeter than sucrose because of its free fructose. It is made by hydrolysing sucrose, which is true but is not why it is sweeter.

113.s: In honey, which one among the following sugars predominates ?
113.x: Fructose predominates in honey, slightly ahead of glucose. Sucrose, galactose and maltose are minor or absent.

113.s: Which one of the following artificial sweetners is modified sugar?
113.x: Sucralose is made by replacing hydroxyl groups of sucrose with chlorine, so it is a modified sugar. Aspartame is a dipeptide, saccharin and alitame are not made from sugar.

113.s: Which of the following is a cereal grain product :
113.x: Oatmeal is made from oats, a cereal grain. Sago and arrowroot are starches from palm stems and roots, and soya flour comes from a legume.

113.s: Which of the following nutrients is known as the primary 'energy-giving' food for our body?
113.src: AP High Court Common Test for Multiple Posts 2026
113.x: Carbohydrates are the primary energy-giving food. Proteins build the body, and vitamins and minerals regulate it.

113.s: Which of the following is rich in all the three foods carbohydrates, proteins and fats?
113.x: Soybean has about 40% protein and 20% fat besides carbohydrate, so it is rich in all three. Rice is mainly carbohydrate, and mango and cabbage are poor in protein and fat.

113.s: Which of the following is NOT among the essential foods produced by plants each being of value in its own way to human and animal metabolism?
113.x: Plants make carbohydrates, fats and proteins as essential foods for human and animal metabolism. Nucleic acids (DNA, RNA) are genetic material, not a food group.

113.s: Which of the following is NOT a macronutrient required for livestock ?
113.x: Vitamins are micronutrients needed in small amounts, whereas protein, carbohydrates and fats are macronutrients.

113.s: Which of the following is mostly carbohydrate?
113.x: Rice has the highest carbohydrate share of the cereals given (~78% of the grain); wheat, barley and maize have more protein and fibre.

113.s: Which one of the following groups of diet provides maximum energy to human body?
113.x: Carbohydrate, fat and protein are the energy-giving nutrients (about 4, 9 and 4 kcal/g); vitamins, minerals and water give no energy.

113.s: The major food fuel during exercise of long duration is
113.x:
Printed key / most books: carbohydrate. Strictly, in prolonged low- to moderate-intensity exercise fat supplies about half or more of the energy (CSU Nutrition and Fitness 8.6; Nutrition Research Reviews 2003).
The key is carbohydrate: muscle glycogen and blood glucose fuel sustained, high-intensity endurance work, and running out of glycogen ends it. Fat's share rises in very long, gentle exercise, so fat is the tempting option; protein is a minor fuel.

113.s: Glucose is a source of energy, which one of the following types of molecule is glucose ?
113.x: Glucose is a monosaccharide – a simple carbohydrate – not a protein, fat or nucleic acid.

113.s: Which one among the following statements about a healthy diet is correct?
o: Regular eating of high energy snacks between meals is healthy, since it provides energy and vitamins in plenty.
Fruits and vegetables make a good choice because their energy content is high.
A balanced diet must contain plenty of fat and protein with little carbohydrates and fibre.
An optimal quantity of fat, protein carbohydrate with adequate amount of water and fibre makes a healthy diet.
113.x: A healthy diet has an optimal amount of carbohydrate, protein and fat with enough water and fibre. Frequent high-energy snacks, 'high-energy' fruits and a high-fat, low-carbohydrate diet are all wrong ideas.

113.s: Which of the following is known as energy currency for cellular process?
113.x: ATP stores and releases energy for all cell processes, so it is the energy currency. Glucose is the fuel, ADP the spent form and pyruvic acid a glycolysis product.

113.s: What taste do starchy substances have?
113.x:
APPSC key: sweet. Strictly, pure starch is nearly tasteless; it tastes sweet only as salivary amylase turns it into maltose (NCERT Class 7, Nutrition in Animals).
Starch is broken by salivary amylase into maltose, so starchy food tastes sweet on chewing – the key. Bitter, mint and sour are not carbohydrate tastes.

113.s: How do carbohydrates taste?
113.x: Carbohydrates (sugars such as fructose, sucrose, glucose) taste sweet; starch tastes sweet on chewing as amylase forms maltose.

113.s: Which of the following gives maximum energy in metabolic processes?
113.x: Fats give about 9 kcal/g, more than twice carbohydrates or proteins (~4 kcal/g); minerals give no energy.

113.s: In which category of food is the most amount of calories per unit –
113.x: Fats have the most calories per gram (~9 kcal), against ~4 kcal for carbohydrates and proteins; vitamins give none.

113.s:
Assertion (A) : Unsaturated fats are more reactive compared with the saturated fats.
Reason (R) : Unsaturated fats have only single bonds in their structure.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are individually true, and (R) is the
Both (A) and (R) are individually true, but (R) is not
113.x: Unsaturated fats are more reactive because they have carbon–carbon double bonds, so A is true and R (only single bonds) is false; single bonds only describe saturated fats.

113.s: Which of following is an artificial sweetening agent?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
113.x: Saccharin is an artificial sweetener; sucrose is natural sugar, glycine an amino acid and steviol glycosides a natural sweetener from stevia.

113.s: Which one of the following statements regarding starch and cellulose is not correct?
o: Both of them are of plant origin.
Both of them give colour with iodine
Both of them are made up of glucose molecules.
113.x: Starch gives a blue-black colour with iodine, but cellulose does not. Both are plant-origin glucose polymers.

113.s: Which of these is not a colloid?
113.x: Honey is a supersaturated sugar solution (true solution), not a colloid. Milk is an emulsion, blood and ice-cream are colloidal systems.

113.s: What is the formula of glucose ?
113.x: Glucose is C6H12O6; C6H10O5 is the starch/cellulose unit and C12H22O11 is sucrose.

113.s: Which one of the following is not considered as a macronutrient?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
113.x: Macronutrients are needed in large amounts and give energy or bulk: carbohydrates, proteins and fats. Minerals (and vitamins) are needed in small amounts and are classed as micronutrients.

113.s: Yellow and Orange fruits belong to the group of
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
113.x: Yellow and orange fruits are rich in vitamins (carotene/vitamin A, vitamin C) and minerals, so they are protective (regulatory) foods.

113.s: In which of the following season human beings require food with more fat content
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
113.x: In winter the body needs more energy to keep warm, so fat-rich (energy-dense) food is needed most then. Off-topic (nutrition).

113.s: Carbohydrates are organic compounds with the basic structure:
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
113.x: Carbohydrates have the general formula Cx(H2O)y – carbon with hydrogen and oxygen in the 2:1 ratio of water (e.g. glucose C6H12O6). A science question, moved to book 5.

113.s:
Living systems are made up of various complex biomolecules which include carbohydrates. Match the following Group of Carbohydrates with their examples.
Group of Carbohydrates:
I. Monosaccharides
II. Oligosaccharides
III. Polysaccharides
Examples:
a. Cellulose
b. Ribose
c. Maltose
113.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
113.x: Ribose – monosaccharide, maltose – oligosaccharide (disaccharide), cellulose – polysaccharide. Off-topic (biology), moved.

113.s:
A company marketing food products advertise that its items do not contain trans-fats. What does this campaign signify to the customers?
A. The food products are not made out of hydrogenated oils.
B. The food products are not made out of animal fats/oils.
C. The oils used are not likely to damage the cardiovascular health of the consumers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: 'No trans-fats' means no partially hydrogenated oils (A) and so less harm to heart health (C); animal fats may still be used (small natural trans fats aside), so B does not follow.

113.s: Which of the following contains high caffeine content per equal weight?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
113.x: By equal dry weight, tea leaves contain more caffeine (about 3-4%) than coffee beans (about 1-2%), though a brewed cup of coffee has more; chocolate has far less.

113.s: The sweetest sugar is
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
113.x: Fructose (fruit sugar, levulose) is the sweetest natural sugar, about 1.7 times as sweet as sucrose.

113.s: Honey is sweeter than cane sugar or corn syrup. Which one of the following carbon sugars is responsible for this?
113.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
113.x:
Levulose (option 2) is the same sugar as fructose, so both options are chemically right; keyed 'Fructose' as the standard name.
Honey is sweeter than cane sugar mainly because of fructose, the sweetest sugar. Levulose is only another name for fructose; dextrose (glucose) and sucrose are less sweet.

113.s: Which of the following forms of sugar is the main constituent of sugar cane juice?
113.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: Sugarcane juice is mainly sucrose (cane sugar), a disaccharide of glucose and fructose. Glucose, fructose and dextrose are only minor components.

113.s: After eating which of the following items, a person is likely feel more thirsty?
113.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: Salted chips add sodium, raising the salt concentration of body fluids and triggering thirst; the other foods have little salt.

113.s: Test used to detect starch adulteration in milk
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Starch in milk turns blue with iodine solution – the iodine test.

113.s: Why are roughages important in our food?
o: They help in expel of undigested food
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Roughage (dietary fibre) is indigestible plant carbohydrate: it gives no energy or nutrients but adds bulk and helps the body get rid of undigested food (prevents constipation). Energy comes from carbohydrates and fats, body building from proteins, and vitamins from food itself – not from roughage.

113.s: 'Volume of a given mass of a gas is inversely proportional to its pressure at a constant temperature'. This statement is associated with:
113.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
113.x: Boyle's Law: at constant temperature the volume of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure. Charles's Law relates volume and temperature.

113.s: Ignoring friction of air, if one brick and one feather are released to ground from top of a building, which one reaches ground first?
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
113.x: Without air resistance all bodies fall with the same acceleration g whatever their mass, so the brick and the feather reach the ground together (Galileo; shown on the Moon by Apollo 15).

113.s: Which liquid would boil last?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
113.x: Mercury boils at about 357°C, far above water (100°C), benzene (80°C) and ethyl alcohol (78°C), so it boils last.

113.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of friction?
o: Applying brakes to stop a moving car
Revolution of the planets around the sun
