113.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
113.x: Planets revolve round the Sun because of gravity in near-vacuum space, so there is no friction; brakes, striking a match and walking all depend on friction.

113.s: A Ball thrown outside from an artificial satellite revolving around the Earth will –
o: Revolve around the Earth in the same orbit with the
113.x: A ball released from an orbiting satellite already has the satellite's orbital speed, so it keeps falling round the Earth in the same orbit, like the satellite itself.

113.s: If a piece of wood and a piece of iron are placed in a fridge and taken out after 15 minutes, which one would feel more cold on touching?
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
113.x: Iron is a good conductor of heat, so it draws heat from the hand faster and feels colder, though both are at the same temperature. Wood is a poor conductor.

113.s: What is a change of position?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x:
Most keys: Motion. Strictly: the change in position (a vector) is displacement (NCERT Class 9 ch. 8).
In school physics, motion is the change of position of a body with time, which is the key the paper gives. Strictly, the size and direction of the change in position is displacement, and distance is the path length.

113.s: "An object at rest will remain at rest and an object moving at a constant velocity will continue moving at a constant velocity, unless it is acted on by an unbalanced force". This law is called as ____.
113.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
113.x: Newton's first law (law of inertia): a body stays at rest or in uniform motion unless an unbalanced force acts on it. The second law gives F = ma, the third deals with action and reaction, and there is no fourth law.

113.s: Which of these is the change of gaseous state directly to solid state without going through liquid state?
113.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
113.x: The change of a gas directly into a solid is deposition (desublimation); sublimation is the reverse, solid to gas. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: If two papers are kept very close to each other and wind is blown in between them, they would
113.src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
113.x: Air blown between the sheets moves fast and its pressure drops (Bernoulli's principle), so the higher outside pressure pushes the papers together. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: Which of the following principles is used in the process of cooling air in air-conditioners?
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
113.x: Air-conditioners cool a room by circulating air: cooled air sinks and warm air rises to the unit – a convection current. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: A person wonders how is it possible for insects to walk on water, human beings can't do it. In order to answer this question, we will have to refer to the concept of:
113.src: APPSC Town Planning Building Overseers General Studies & Men
113.x: Surface tension – the cohesive 'skin' of the water surface – supports light insects such as water striders. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: Amount of heat required to raise the temperature of one gram of substance by 1°C is called
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
113.x: The heat needed to raise the temperature of 1 g of a substance by 1°C is its specific heat. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: Why a glass bottle full of water breaks, if kept in a fridge?
o: The pressure in the fridge would be very high
When water solidifies, it expands in volume
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
113.x: Water expands by about 9% on freezing; the expanding ice exerts pressure that cracks the glass bottle. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: A corked bottle full of water when frozen breaks because
o: The Volume of the water decreases on freezing
The volume of the water increases on freezing
Glass material develops strain of freezing
113.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
113.x: Water expands by about 9% on freezing; the expanding ice pushes on the glass and breaks the bottle. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: If a person goes down into a deep mine, his weight?
o: Depends on location of the mine
113.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
113.x: g falls with depth below the surface, so a person's weight decreases slightly in a deep mine. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: When an air bubble at the bottom of a lake rises to the top, it will
o: Flattens into a dish like shape
113.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
113.x: Water pressure falls as the bubble rises, so the trapped air expands and the bubble grows (Boyle's law). Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: A corked bottle full of water when frozen breaks because
o: The volume of the water decreases on freezing
The volume of the water increases on freezing
Glass material develops strain on freezing
113.x: Water expands on freezing; the ice pushes on the glass and breaks the bottle. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: Super cooling stands for cooling of a liquid
113.x: Supercooling is cooling a liquid below its freezing point without it solidifying. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: After taking out from the fridge, compared to an apple, water melon would retain the coolness for more time because?
o: It is bigger in size and hene more volume
It contains more water which has higher specific heat
It is more green in colour which does reflects atmospheric heat
It has thicker skin which would not allow penetration of heat
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
113.x: Watermelon contains more water, which has a high specific heat, so it takes longer to warm up. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: What happens when salt is added to boiling water?
o: The water will boil more and temperature of the water would fall
The Water will stop boiling and the temperature of the water would fall
The water will stop boiling and temperature of the water would rise
The water will boil more and the temperature of the water would rise
113.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
113.x: Salt raises the boiling point, so the water stops boiling for a moment and its temperature rises to the new, higher boiling point before it boils again. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: Ice skating demonstrates that when ice is under pressure, its melting point
o: Melting point has no relation with pressure
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
113.x: Pressure lowers the melting point of ice (regelation); the skate's pressure melts a thin water layer. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: What is the result when we add salt in water?
o: The boiling point decreases and freezing point increases.
The boiling point increases and freezing point decreases.
Both the boiling point and the freezing point increase.
Both the boiling point and freezing point decrease.
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
113.x: A dissolved salt raises the boiling point and lowers the freezing point of water (colligative properties). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: During winter in cold countries, the following is mixed to melt the ice on the roads?
113.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
113.x: Salt (rock salt) spread on roads lowers the freezing point of water and melts ice. Off-topic (everyday chemistry), moved.

113.s: The triple point of pure water is at
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
113.x: The triple point of pure water – where ice, liquid water and vapour coexist in equilibrium – is 0.01 °C (273.16 K) at about 611.657 Pa. (Off-topic physics; moved.)

113.s: When ice is melting its temperature would?
113.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: While ice melts, the heat supplied goes into latent heat of fusion, so its temperature stays constant at 0°C. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: The shortest path between the initial and final position is known as
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: Displacement is the shortest straight-line path between the initial and final positions; distance is the actual path length. Physics, moved to book 5 row 1.

113.s: How much heat is required to increase the temperature of 1 gram kerosene by 1 degree centigrade?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: The specific heat of kerosene is about 2.1 J/g°C, i.e. about 0.5 cal per gram per °C (water = 1 cal). A physics question, moved.

113.s: What is the approximate value of 1 calorie in Joules?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: 1 calorie = 4.186 J, i.e. about 4.2 J (Joule's mechanical equivalent of heat). A physics question, moved.

113.s: Which liquid is represented by the Volume-Temperature Curve? (The curve shows volume falling from 0°C to a minimum at 4°C and rising again up to 10°C.)
113.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
113.x: Water contracts from 0°C to 4°C (maximum density) and expands above it – the anomalous expansion of water.

113.s: Which of the following is responsible for slowing down a moving object?
113.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
113.x: Friction is the force that opposes motion and slows a moving object.

113.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of gravity?
o: Revolution of planets around the sun
A rock rolling down a hill
Formation of tides in the ocean
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
113.x: Writing with a pencil works by friction, not gravity; planetary revolution, a rock rolling downhill and tides are effects of gravity.

113.s: A boat filled with heavy stones is in a lake. If the stones are thrown into the lake, the level of water with respect to the boat would?
113.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
113.x: A floating boat displaces water equal to the stones' weight; sunk, the stones displace only their volume, so the lake level falls (and the lighter boat rides higher).

113.s: If an object is thrown upwards, what will be its velocity, when it reaches its maximum height (neglect the air resistance)?
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
113.x: At the maximum height the vertical velocity of a body thrown upwards becomes zero (it then falls back).

113.s: Which of the following materials is not commonly used as sound-proof material?
113.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
113.x: Rockwool, wood and (double/laminated) glass are used for sound insulation; plain iron sheets reflect and transmit sound and are not a sound-proofing material.

113.s: Stainless steel pans are sometimes provided with copper bottom because?
o: Copper is not a harmful metal
Copper is better conductor of heat than steel
Oil stains on Copper are easier to clean
113.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
113.x: Copper conducts heat much better than steel, so a copper bottom spreads heat quickly and evenly.

113.s: How many classes of levers are there with reference to simple machines?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
113.x: Levers are of three classes (fulcrum, load or effort in the middle). Physics of simple machines, not ICT.

113.s: What is the density of water?
113.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
113.x: Pure water has a density of about 1 g/cm3 (1,000 kg/m3), highest at 4 °C.

113.s:
Assertion (A) : A man standing on a completely frictionless surface can propel himself by whistling.
Reason (R) : If no external force acts on a system, its momentum cannot change.
Code :
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
113.x:
Printed key: (b) both true, R not the explanation. Many solvers argue (a), since conservation of momentum (R) explains the recoil, and some call A practically false (general knowledge, not checked).
Both statements are true, and the printed key takes R as not the correct explanation of A. Blowing air out while whistling pushes the man the opposite way (third law), while R is the general conservation of momentum.

113.s: What should be the size of the burner of the gas stove to save the consumption of LPG?
o: Size of the burner does not matter
113.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: A small burner saves LPG because its flame stays under the vessel's base. A large flame spills heat around the sides. (Off-topic: energy saving in daily life.)

113.s: If a balloon filled with air is immersed in hot water, its volume would
113.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
113.x: Air expands when heated (Charles's law), so a balloon in hot water swells and its volume increases. (Off-topic: physics.)

113.s: If egg shell is carefully dissolved in acid and then immersed in salt water, then the shell?
113.src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
113.x: Acid dissolves the calcium carbonate shell, leaving the semi-permeable membrane; in strong salt water (hypertonic) water leaves the egg by osmosis, so it shrinks. Off-topic science, moved.

113.s: Temperature and time used to sterilise glassware in hot air oven
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: A hot air oven sterilises glassware at 160°C with a holding time of one hour (170°C for 30 min, 180°C for 20 min); shorter times at 160°C are not enough. Off-topic (microbiology).

113.s: Humans have ____ of chromosomes, or tightly wrapped strands of DNA, that provide the instructions for metabolic processes, building cellular and tissue components, as well as other body functions.
113.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
113.x: Humans have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs (22 pairs of autosomes + 1 pair of sex chromosomes). Off-topic (biology).

113.s: The outer shell of the egg is composed of
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
113.x: An egg shell is about 95% calcium carbonate (CaCO3). Off-topic (general science), moved.

113.s:
Match the types of following of asexual reproduction in Column A with correct example in Column B.
Column A:
A. Binary fission B. Budding
C. Regeneration
D. Spore formation
Column B:
i. Amoeba
ii. Yeast
iii. Rhizopus
iv. Planaria
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Binary fission – Amoeba, budding – yeast, regeneration – Planaria, spore formation – Rhizopus. Off-topic, moved.

113.s:
Match the given component of living tissues with the percentage of the total cellular mass.
Component:
I. Lipids
II. Proteins
III. Carbohydrates
IV. Nucleic acids
Percentage of the total cellular mass:
a. 5-7%
b. 10-15%
c. 3%
d. 2%
113.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
113.x: In a cell, proteins are 10–15%, nucleic acids 5–7%, carbohydrates 3% and lipids 2% of the mass (water 70–90%). Moved.

113.s: Aerobic respiration process requires
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: Aerobic respiration breaks down glucose using oxygen (giving CO2, water, energy). Off-topic (biology), moved.

113.s: Which is the correct statement about a genetic code?
o: UAC, UAG, and UGA are stop codons.
Initiation codon AUG codes for arginine.
113.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
113.x: The genetic code is a triplet (codon of three bases) and nearly universal; stop codons are UAA, UAG, UGA (not UAC); AUG codes for methionine. Off-topic (biology), moved.

113.s: ATP molecule releases about how much energy?
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Hydrolysis of ATP to ADP releases about 30.5 kJ/mol (7.3 kcal/mol) under standard conditions.

113.s: Normally how many number of Autosomes will be present in human beings?
113.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
113.x: Human cells have 46 chromosomes: 22 pairs (44) of autosomes and one pair of sex chromosomes.

113.s: The structural carbohydrates of vegetables and fruits are
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
113.x: Cellulose is the structural carbohydrate of plant cell walls in fruits and vegetables.

113.s: Genes controlling the body characteristics are found in
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: Genes for body characters are carried by both sperms and eggs, which each pass one set of chromosomes.

113.s: In Chlorophyll, the central metal ion is?
113.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
113.x: Magnesium is the central metal ion of chlorophyll. Off-topic (biology).

113.s: What is the full form of ATP?
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
113.x: ATP is Adenosine Triphosphate: adenosine (adenine + ribose) with three phosphate groups, the cell's energy currency. 'Adenine' alone lacks the ribose, and 'protease' is an enzyme class.

113.s: What is known as the 'energy molecule' in the living World?
113.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
113.x: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the energy currency of the cell. TNT is an explosive, ADP is its spent form and DNA is the genetic material.

113.s: Which of the following is the controlling centre of a cell?
113.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Village Agriculture Ass
113.x: The nucleus holds the cell's DNA and directs its activities, so it is the control centre of the cell. Chloroplasts make food, mitochondria release energy and the nucleolus only makes ribosomes.

113.s: Which organelle is called power house of the cell?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell: they release energy as ATP by cellular respiration.

113.s: Which of the following part of a cell is called power house of energy?
113.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell; the nucleus controls the cell and vacuoles store substances.

113.s: If mitochondria is removed from a living cell?
o: Energy metabolism of the cell gets extinguished
Cell fluid would not be transported
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
113.x: Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration and ATP production, so removing them stops the cell's energy metabolism. Reproduction and transport would only fail as a later result.

113.s: At what time respiration takes place in plants?
o: There is no need for respiration in plants
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: Plants respire all the time, day and night; only photosynthesis needs light. So respiration is a continuous process.

113.s: The occurrence of differences in characteristics among individuals of the same species is called
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Differences in characters among individuals of the same species are called variation. Inheritance is passing on traits, evolution the long-term change and adaptation a fit to the habitat.

113.s: Fermentation of Yeast is an example of?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
113.x: Yeast ferments sugar into alcohol and CO2 without oxygen, so fermentation is anaerobic respiration.

113.s: The limit of growth is fixed by which of the following factor?
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
113.x: The limit of growth is fixed by internal (genetic, hormonal) factors of the organism; nutrition and exercise only help reach it.

113.s: Sweating is an
o: Difficult to state, which type of process it is
113.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
113.x: Sweat cools the body because its evaporation absorbs heat from the skin, so sweating is an endothermic process.

113.s: Respiration is an
113.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
113.x: Respiration oxidises glucose and releases energy, so it is an exothermic process.

113.s: Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost is a/an?
113.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
113.x: Composting is microbial oxidation of organic matter and releases heat (compost heaps warm up), so it is exothermic.

113.s: What term describes the phenomenon in which a single species evolves into several different forms to exploit different ecological niches?
113.x:
Printed key: Adaptation (adaptive radiation). Strictly the phenomenon is adaptive radiation, a form of divergent evolution, so 'Divergence' is also defensible (general knowledge, not checked).
A single species evolving into many forms that exploit different niches is adaptive radiation (Darwin's finches), which the key reads as 'adaptation'. Strictly, adaptive radiation is a case of divergent evolution; convergence is the opposite process.

113.s: Out of the following, which is a product of the first stage of oxidation of Glucose?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: The first stage of glucose oxidation is glycolysis, which splits glucose into two molecules of pyruvic acid (pyruvate) in the cytoplasm; CO2, and ethanol (in fermentation) come later, and ATP is a by-product, not the product of glucose breakdown.

113.s: Identify the organisms that reproduce asexually by budding.
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Yeast and Hydra reproduce asexually by budding; Amoeba and Paramecium divide by binary fission.

113.s: In humans, which cells can perform anaerobic respiration during oxygen shortage?
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Skeletal muscle cells respire anaerobically in oxygen shortage, producing lactic acid.

113.s: Which of the following is present in plant cells but not cells of animals?
113.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall, which animal cells lack; both have vacuoles, plasma membrane and Golgi.

113.s:
Assertion (A): The amount of DNA present in somatic cell depends on the phase of the cell cycle.
Reason (R): Telophase and G1 phase nuclei contain only half (as 2c) the amount of DNA found in the prophase; G2 phase and metaphase cells represent 4c.
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct; (R) is correct explanation for (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct; (R) is not correct explanation for (A).
(A) is correct and (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct and (R) is correct
113.x: DNA content changes over the cell cycle: G1 and telophase nuclei are 2C, G2/prophase/metaphase 4C after S-phase replication - so R correctly explains A.

113.s: During the period of intense body exercise, which of the following increases in the blood of person?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: During intense exercise muscles respire anaerobically and lactic acid builds up in the blood; oxygen and glucose fall.

113.s: Which of the following is a homopolymer?
113.src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
113.x: Cellulose is a homopolymer of beta-glucose only; proteins and collagen are built from many different amino acids, and agarose has alternating galactose units (agarobiose). (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

113.s: The most abundant organic compound in world is?
113.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
113.x: Cellulose, the main component of plant cell walls, is the most abundant organic compound on Earth. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

113.s: The ATP production through respiration is called
113.src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
113.x: ATP made in respiration via the electron transport chain is oxidative phosphorylation; photophosphorylation is ATP formation in photosynthesis. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

113.s: In a mammal, what is the ratio of the number of chromosomes in a somatic cell to that in a gamete?
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Somatic cells are diploid (2n, 46 in humans) and gametes haploid (n, 23), so the ratio is 2:1.

113.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon, Group-IV and Other Posts Gene
113.x: Mitochondria - powerhouse, ATP (3); ribosomes - protein synthesis (1); cell membrane - regulates passage (4); nucleus - control centre with genetic material (2).

113.s:
Consider the following statements:
1.
Assertion (A): Amoeba is reproduced by fission.
2.
Reason (R): All unicellular organisms are reproduced by asexual methods.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both (A) and (R) are individually true and R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
113.x: Amoeba reproduces by binary fission (A true), but not all unicellular organisms are only asexual - Chlamydomonas, Paramecium (conjugation) and yeast show sexual reproduction (R false).

113.s:
Arrange the following events of "biogeny theory" in a sequence.
a. Formation of coacervates
b. Aerobic organisms came to existence
c. Heterotropic organisms began to form
d. Mycoplasmas are first formed cells
113.x: In the biogeny sequence, coacervates formed first, then the first cells (mycoplasma-like), then heterotrophs, and aerobic organisms came last: a, d, c, b. (Off-topic: origin of life.)

113.s: Recently the State of Tamil Nadu banned the sale of cotton candy due to the presence of which cancercausing agent in it?
113.x: Rhodamine B, a textile dye, was found colouring cotton candy; it is carcinogenic, so Tamil Nadu banned the sale (Feb 2024). Aristolochic acid comes from some herbal medicines, benzidine is a dye intermediate and 1,3-butadiene a rubber monomer.

113.s: Which of the following is used as an adulterant of a mustard seed?
113.x: Argemone (Mexican prickly poppy) seeds look like mustard seeds and are mixed with them; their oil causes epidemic dropsy. Papaya, cumin and coriander seeds are not the usual adulterants of mustard.

113.s: The chemical that is used to ripen mangoes is
113.x: Calcium carbide reacts with moisture to give acetylene, which acts like the ripening hormone ethylene, so it is (illegally) used to ripen mangoes. Calcium sulphide, carbonate and chloride release no such gas.

113.s: Improper handling and storage of cereal grains and oilseeds result in the production of toxins known as aflatoxins which are not generally destroyed by normal cooking process. Aflatoxins are produced by
113.x: Aflatoxins are made by moulds (Aspergillus flavus and A. parasiticus) that grow on badly stored grain and oilseeds. Bacteria, protozoa and viruses do not produce them.

113.s: Improper handling and storage of cereal grains and oilseeds result in the production of toxins known as aflatoxins, which are not destroyed by the normal cooking process? Aflatoxins are produced by:
113.x: Aflatoxins are poisonous, cancer-causing chemicals made by moulds such as Aspergillus flavus on stored grain; cooking does not destroy them. Bacteria, protozoa and viruses are wrong.

113.s: Which of the following chemicals is used for ripening?
113.x: Calcium carbide gives acetylene, which ripens fruit like ethylene, so it is the chemical used for (artificial) ripening. Sodium and potassium chloride have no ripening action.

113.s: Which of the following is the most common food preservative against mould, bacteria, fungus and yeast?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
113.x: Sorbic acid and its salt potassium sorbate are the commonest preservatives against moulds, yeasts and fungi. Tartaric acid is a food acid, acetylsalicylic acid is aspirin and formic acid only a limited preservative.

113.s: Sodium benzoate is used as a:
113.x: Sodium benzoate (E211) is a food preservative that stops bacteria, yeast and moulds in acidic foods and drinks. It is not a flavour, colour or antacid.

113.s: What causes ‘Blackheart’ in potato ?
113.x: Blackheart of potato is a storage disorder caused by oxygen deficiency in the tuber's centre. It is not caused by a copper, boron or potassium deficiency.

113.s: The substance employed for the food processing is
113.x: Benzoic acid (as sodium benzoate) is a standard food-processing preservative. Sodium carbonate, acetylene and sodium nitrate are not the usual answer.

113.s: Date of manufacture of food items fried in oil should be checked before buying because oils become rancid due to
113.x: Fats and oils turn rancid when they are oxidised by air, which is why the manufacture date of fried food matters. Reduction and hydrogenation do not cause rancidity.

113.s: Fruits stored in a cold chamber exhibit longer storage life because
o: concentration of carbon dioxide in the environment is increased.
there is an increase in humidity.
113.x: Low temperature slows the respiration rate of fruits, so they ripen and decay more slowly and keep longer. Darkness, CO2 or humidity are not the main reason.

113.s: Which of the following phytohormone is mainly responsible for fruit ripening ?
113.x: Ethylene is the gaseous plant hormone that promotes fruit ripening. Cytokinin promotes cell division and abscisic acid is a growth inhibitor.

113.s: Plants contain a variety of sterols like stigmasterol, ergosterol, sitosterol etc which very closely resemble cholesterol. These plant sterols are referred as
113.x: Plant sterols (stigmasterol, sitosterol, ergosterol) are called phytosterols; ergocalciferol is vitamin D2 and lumisterol a by-product of its synthesis.

113.s: Artificial chemicals are bio-chemically known as
113.x: Man-made chemicals that interfere with the hormone system (BPA, phthalates, some pesticides) are called endocrine disruptors. 'Facilitators', 'reactors' and 'inhibitors' are not the accepted term.

113.s: Which gas is used to ripen fruits?
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
113.x: Ethylene is the gaseous fruit-ripening hormone.

113.s:
Which of the following are symptoms of food allergy?
a. Nervousness
b. Fall in blood pressure
c. Atherosclerosis
d. Flushing of the skin
e. Difficulty in swallowing and speaking
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
113.x: Food allergy can cause a fall in blood pressure (anaphylaxis), flushing or hives, and swelling of the throat with difficulty in swallowing and speaking. Atherosclerosis is a chronic artery disease, and nervousness is not a typical allergic sign.

113.s: Which one of the following is the best example of desiccant?
113.x: Silica gel absorbs moisture and is the standard desiccant (in packets with shoes, medicines, electronics). Polystyrene is a plastic, and NaCl and Na2CO3 are not used as desiccants.

113.s: Which hormone is found in the gaseous form ?
113.x: Ethylene is the only plant hormone that is a gas (fruit ripening); abscisic acid, gibberellins and auxins are not gaseous.

113.s: "Triclosan', considered harmful when exposed to high levels for a long time, is most likely present in which of the following?
113.x: Triclosan is an antibacterial chemical in toiletries such as soaps, toothpaste and deodorants. It is not a food preservative or a ripening agent.

113.s: 'Triclosan', considered harmful when exposed to high levels for a long time, is most likely present in which of the following?
113.x: Triclosan is an antibacterial chemical in toiletries such as soaps, toothpaste and deodorants. It is not a food preservative or a ripening agent.

113.s: Sun drying is a method of:
113.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
113.x: Sun drying removes moisture so that microbes cannot grow; it is a traditional method of food preservation (dehydration).

113.s: To store potato chips for a longer period, the sealed packet of chips is normally filled with which gas?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
113.x: Chip packets are flushed with nitrogen, an unreactive gas, so the fats do not get oxidised (rancidity). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

113.s: What is the freezing temperature used for preserving pork for long period
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Meat such as pork is stored long-term frozen at about −18°C (0°F) or below; 3–5°C is only chilling. Off-topic (food science), moved.

113.s: Most of the artificial food colouring agents are derived from
113.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
113.x: Most synthetic food colours (tartrazine, sunset yellow) are coal-tar (petroleum-derived) dyes. Flowers, fruits and lichens give natural colours.

113.s: Why does open portion of a cut apple turn brown when exposed to air?
o: Due to presence of iron in apple
Due to settling of micro dust present in air
As the original inner colour is brown
Due to oxidation of an enzyme present in apple
113.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
113.x: A cut apple browns because its enzyme polyphenol oxidase, exposed to oxygen, oxidises the fruit's phenolic compounds (enzymatic browning); iron, dust or a brown inner colour are not the cause.

113.s: Retrogradation of starch is the prominent factor bringing about:
113.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Retrogradation (re-crystallisation of gelatinised starch) is the main cause of staling of bread.

113.s: The ideal temperature for storage of frozen foods is
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
113.x: Frozen foods are stored at about -18°C (0°F) or colder, where microbes cannot multiply. The printed '-180°C' is a slip for -18°C; no freezer works at -180°C.

113.s: Rancidity is a/an
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
113.x: Rancidity is the oxidation of fats and oils, which changes their smell and taste. Antioxidants are added to prevent it.

113.s: Which of the following chemical compound added to bread was banned in India
113.src: Technical Asst. (Hydrology), Laboratory Assistants in AP Gro
113.x: FSSAI removed potassium bromate from the list of permitted additives in 2016 after CSE found it in bread (possible carcinogen). Gluconate, sulphate and oxalate were not the banned bread additive.

113.s: Natural ripening of climacteric fruits (like apple) occurs due to?
o: Release of ethylene and increased rate of respiration
Release of ethylene and decreased rate of respiration
Release of acetylene and increased rate of respiration
Release of acetylene and decreased rate of respiration
113.x: Climacteric fruits such as apple ripen through a burst of ethylene release and a sharp rise in respiration (the climacteric rise). Acetylene is used only for artificial ripening, and respiration rises rather than falls.

113.s: Development of off odour in fats & oils when they are stored for a longer duration is known as
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
113.x: The off-odour and taste that develop in fats and oils on long storage, through oxidation, is called rancidity.

113.s: Primary methods to prevent food spoilage do NOT include:
113.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
113.x: Food spoilage is prevented by refrigeration, drying, salting, canning and preservatives; exposure to air, moisture and microbes causes spoilage, so it is not a method.

113.s:
A statement is given followed by two conclusions.
Select the correct response from the given options.
Statement: Aschelminthes are called roundworms.
Conclusion:
i. The body of the aschelminthes is circular in cross-section.
ii. Roundworms have organ-system level of body organisation.
113.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
113.x:
Printed key: only (i) follows from the statement. Strictly, both (i) and (ii) are true facts (PMF General Science p.89 / NCERT XI: organ-system level), so a fact-check reading gives 'both'.
The name 'roundworm' comes from the body being circular in cross-section, so conclusion (i) follows from the statement. Conclusion (ii) is a true fact (Aschelminthes have organ-system level of organisation) but does not follow from the statement about the name.

113.s:
Match the following columns I and II and choose the CORRECT answer from the given options.
Column I (Phylum):
A. Ctenophora
B. Porifera
C. Coelenterata (Cnidaria)
D. Echinodermata
Column II (Distinctive features):
1. Choanocytes
2. Bioluminescence
3. Water vascular system
4. Polyp and Medusa
113.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
113.x: Ctenophores show bioluminescence, sponges (Porifera) have choanocytes, Cnidaria have polyp and medusa forms, and echinoderms have a water vascular system: A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3. (Biology, filed under polity by mistake.)

113.s: Saurology is the
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Saurology (herpetology of lizards) is the study of lizards.

113.s: Which of the following features is NOT common in Chordates and non-chordates?
113.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
113.x: Printed key: bilateral symmetry – all chordates are bilaterally symmetrical, but many non-chordates (cnidarians, adult echinoderms) are radial, so it is not common to both groups. Off-topic (zoology), moved.

113.s: Skull of mammals is
113.src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
113.x: Mammals (and amphibians) have a dicondylic skull, joined to the vertebral column by two occipital condyles. Reptiles and birds have a monocondylic skull.

113.s:
Match the phylum in column A with their features in column B.
Column A (Phylum):
I. Porifera
II. Cnidaria
III. Arthropoda
Column B (Features):
a. Presence of Ostia and Osculum
b. Available in two forms- Polyp and Medusa
c. Have jointed appendages.
113.x: Porifera – ostia and osculum, Cnidaria – polyp and medusa forms, Arthropoda – jointed appendages. Off-topic, moved.

113.s:
Which of the following is a correct match of organisms and patterns of organisation of cells in it?
Organism:
I. Sponges
II. Coelenterates
III. Platyhelminthes
Pattern of organisation of cells:
a. Tissue level of organisation
b. Cellular level of organisation
c. Organ level of organisation
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer (FRO) Paper-I General Studies & M
113.x: Sponges – cellular level, coelenterates – tissue level, Platyhelminthes – organ level. Off-topic, moved.

113.s: The beak of an insect eating bird would be?
113.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: Insect-eating birds have long, sharp/pointed beaks to pick insects (woodpecker, kingfisher-type); short strong beaks crack seeds. Off-topic (biology), moved.

113.s: Which dog-breed and region-of-origin pair is NOT correctly matched?
113.x: The Chihuahua comes from Mexico, named after the Mexican state of Chihuahua, not China.

113.s: Which type of snake bite leads to neuroparalytic symptoms?
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
113.x: Krait (and cobra) venom is neurotoxic and causes neuroparalysis; Russell's and saw-scaled viper venom is mainly haemotoxic, and pythons are non-venomous.

113.s: Which one of the following is an animal belonging to the Marsupial category?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
113.x: The koala is a marsupial of Australia that carries its young in a pouch. Rabbit, porcupine and squirrel are placental mammals.

113.s: Respiration in grasshopper takes place through
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: Insects such as the grasshopper breathe through a network of tracheae opening at spiracles; gills and lungs belong to other animals.

113.s: In which of the following arthropods is the first pair of legs on the cranial segment modified into pincer-like forcipules?
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
113.x: Centipedes (Chilopoda) have their first pair of trunk legs modified into poison claws called forcipules. Millipedes have two pairs of legs per segment and no forcipules; cicadas and wasps are insects.

113.s: What is the primary purpose of a Wasp's sting?
o: To defend themselves or their colony
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
113.x:
Most books and keys: defence of self and colony. Strictly: in solitary wasps the sting is used mainly to paralyse prey (Britannica, "wasp").
Wasps chiefly use the sting (a modified ovipositor) to defend themselves and the colony. Solitary wasps also use it to paralyse prey, but stinging plays no part in pollination or marking territory.

113.s: Why chameleon changes its colours?
o: To tune its colour with temperature of the day
The colours automatically change on their own
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
113.x:
Most books and keys: to protect itself from predators (camouflage). Strictly: chameleons change colour mainly for social signalling and thermoregulation (Stuart-Fox & Moussalli 2008, PLoS Biology).
Most books say chameleons change colour mainly to camouflage themselves against predators. Strictly, colour change serves mainly social signalling and temperature control.

113.s: Which among the following does not contain crop
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: The emu, a flightless ratite, has no crop. Turkey, duck and quail store food in a crop. (Off-topic: zoology.)

113.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of class Amphibia?
113.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
113.x: Clarias is a catfish (class Pisces), not an amphibian. Bufo (toad), Rana (frog) and Hyla (tree frog) are amphibians. (Off-topic: zoology.)

113.s:
Match the following:
List-I:
a. Mycology
b. Palynology
c. Oncology
d. Paleontology
List-II:
i. study of pollen grains
ii. study of treatment of tumours
iii. study of fossils of animals and plants
iv. study of fungi
113.src: TSLPRB SI Civil Preliminary Written Exam 2018
113.x: Mycology is the study of fungi, palynology of pollen, oncology of tumours and palaeontology of fossils, so (a)-(iv), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iii).

113.s: Which of the following enzyme is elevated in Downer cow syndrome
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: In downer cow syndrome the recumbent cow suffers muscle damage, so serum creatine phosphokinase (CK) rises sharply; tryptophan and creatinine are not enzymes.

113.s: The foods of Protozoans is digested by
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: Protozoa such as Amoeba digest food with enzymes inside food vacuoles; contractile vacuoles remove water.

113.s: The postmortem sample collected during abortion is
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: After an abortion the aborted fetus (with placenta) is the key post-mortem sample for diagnosing the cause; blood, milk or serum are ante-mortem samples.

113.s: No. of lobes present in left lung of cow
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x:
Most keys: 3 lobes (apical/cranial, cardiac/middle, diaphragmatic/caudal). Strictly in current veterinary nomenclature the left lung has 2 lobes, the cranial lobe being split into two parts (general knowledge, not checked).
Classical veterinary anatomy divides the ox's left lung into three lobes (apical, cardiac, diaphragmatic); the right lung has four or five.

113.s: Mycology is the study of
113.x: Mycology is the study of fungi; entomology = insects, limnology = fresh waters, volcanology = volcanoes.

113.s: Which of the following is not used in lactic acidosis in cattle
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Rumen lactic acidosis is treated with alkalising agents - sodium bicarbonate, magnesium hydroxide, Ringer's lactate fluids; vinegar (acetic acid) is used for urea/ammonia poisoning, not acidosis.

113.s: Pneumatic bones are commonly present in
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: Birds have pneumatic (air-filled) bones that lighten the skeleton for flight; cattle, horses and pigs have solid marrow-filled bones.

113.s: The venom of Russell's Viper primarily affects the
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
113.x: Russell's viper venom is haemotoxic: it disrupts blood clotting (consumption coagulopathy, bleeding). Cobra and krait venoms are the neurotoxic ones.

113.s: Paste consisting of the drug mixed with either honey/jaggery and administered orally in large animals is called
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: An electuary is a drug mixed into a paste with honey, jaggery or treacle and given by mouth (smeared on the tongue). A bolus is a large pill, a drench a liquid dose, a pessary a vaginal insert.

113.s: The artery used for recording pulse in dog is
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: In dogs the pulse is recorded from the femoral artery on the inner thigh.

113.s: Site of recording pulse in dogs
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: The pulse of a dog is taken at the femoral artery (inner thigh); the coccygeal artery is used in cattle and the jugular is a vein.

113.s: What is the name of the process through which unicellular organisms eat food?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: Unicellular organisms like Amoeba engulf food by phagocytosis; pinocytosis is the intake of fluid droplets.

113.s:
Read the following statements in respect to difference between 'Poisonous and Venomous animals':
a. If you bite it and you die, it's Poisonous. If it bites and you die, it's Venomous.
b. If you bite it and you die, it's Venomous. If it bites and you die, it's Poisonous.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
113.x: Poisonous animals harm you when you bite or eat them (toxin passively delivered); venomous animals inject venom by biting or stinging. So only statement a is correct.

113.s: Which of the following has a open circulatory system?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: The cockroach, an insect (arthropod), has an open circulatory system: haemolymph is pumped into open sinuses (haemocoel) and bathes the organs. Fish, snakes and earthworms have closed circulatory systems with blood kept inside vessels.

113.s: Tracheal respiration occurs in which of the following organisms?
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: Insects such as the cockroach breathe through tracheae: air enters by spiracles and the tracheal tubes take it straight to the tissues. The earthworm breathes through its moist skin, the frog by skin and lungs, and fish by gills.

113.s: Identify the organisms that undergo cutaneous respiration.
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
113.x: Cutaneous respiration (gas exchange through moist skin) is seen in the earthworm and the frog; the frog also uses lungs. Fish breathe by gills and humans by lungs, so every other pair includes a non-cutaneous breather.

113.s: What is the main function of worker bees in a hive?
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
113.x: Worker bees are sterile females that do the colony's work: foraging for nectar and pollen, making honey and wax, nursing the brood and guarding the hive. Only the queen lays eggs, and the drones (males) mate with her, so guarding is only one of the workers' many tasks.

113.s:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: In a given medium, the speed of sound remains constant regardless of temperature changes.
Statement II: Sound waves are longitudinal waves, meaning the particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
o: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both Statement I and statement II are true.
Both Statement I and statement II are false.
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
113.x: Statement I is false – the speed of sound in a medium rises with temperature (about 0.6 m/s per °C in air). Statement II is true: sound waves are longitudinal.

113.s: Which of the following colours would have largest wavelength?
113.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
113.x: In the visible spectrum (VIBGYOR) wavelength rises from violet to red; of orange, yellow, indigo and violet, orange has the longest wavelength.

113.s: A sensitive magnetic field instrument can be effectively shielded from the external magnetic field by placing it inside which of the following materials?
113.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
113.x: Soft iron of high permeability draws the magnetic field lines into itself and so shields the space inside it (magnetic shielding); plastic, wood or a good conductor do not stop a steady magnetic field.

113.s: Rectifiers convert ____.
o: Low AC voltage to high AC voltage
113.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
113.x: A rectifier converts alternating current (AC) into direct current (DC). (Moved to science in daily life.)

113.s: Under what conditions the resistivity of the material does not change?
o: When the shape of the resistor is changed
When both the material and temperature are changed
113.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
113.x: Resistivity is a property of the material and its temperature, so it does not change when only the shape (length or area) of the resistor changes; resistance would change, resistivity would not.

113.s: Which of the following waves are used for common TV remote control?
113.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
113.x: Common TV remote controls use infrared (IR) light-emitting diodes. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: Which type of sound waves can propagate in solids?
113.x: Solids can carry both longitudinal and transverse mechanical waves (like seismic P- and S-waves); fluids carry only longitudinal waves. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: A louder sound is produced by a wave that has a greater
113.src: AP High Court Common Test for Multiple Posts 2026
113.x: Loudness depends on amplitude – a larger amplitude gives a louder sound; frequency decides pitch. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: Which of the following is incorrect about the ultrasonic waves?
o: These waves are can be used for imaging
It cannot be heard by normal human ears
The speed of ultrasonic waves is more in denser media
The ultrasonic waves can travel through vacuum
113.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
113.x: Ultrasonic waves are mechanical sound waves and cannot travel through vacuum; they are inaudible, used for imaging and travel faster in denser media. Moved.

113.s: The colour of an opaque object is due to the colour it
113.src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
113.x: An opaque object looks the colour of the light it reflects; the other colours are absorbed. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: When a semiconductor is heated, its resistance would
o: Resistance has no relation with temperature
113.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
113.x: A semiconductor has a negative temperature coefficient: heating frees more charge carriers, so its resistance decreases (a metal's would increase). Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: The electrical resistance of the insulators is
113.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
113.x: An ideal insulator offers (practically) infinitely high resistance to current, hence 'infinitely high' rather than merely 'high'. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: The lower limit of the aperture of a pinhole camera is set by?
113.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
113.x: Making a pinhole too small spreads the image by diffraction, which sets its lower limit. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: What is the cause of dispersion of light through a prism?
113.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
113.x: A prism disperses white light because each colour is refracted by a different amount. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: Twinkling of stars is due to?
113.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
113.x: Stars twinkle because of atmospheric refraction by turbulent air layers of changing density. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: The sun is seen little before it rises and for a short while after it sets. This is because of
o: apparent shift in the direction of sun
113.x: Atmospheric refraction bends sunlight over the horizon, so the Sun is seen about 2 minutes before sunrise and after sunset. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s:
Consider the following statements
I. The sky appears blue because of scattering.
II. The main cause of seven colors of the rainbow is scattering of light.
III. At the time of sunrise, the sun appears red, due to scattering of light.
Choose the correct statement/s from the given options
113.x: The blue sky and the red rising Sun are due to scattering (I, III true); the rainbow's colours come from dispersion, not scattering (II false). Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: When the sun is near the horizon during the morning or evening, it appears reddish. The phenomenon that is responsible for this observation is
113.x: Near the horizon sunlight crosses more air, blue is scattered away and the Sun looks red – scattering. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: When light passes from one medium to another, this phenomenon of change in its direction is called …… .
113.x: Change of direction of light passing from one medium to another is refraction. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: Bending of light rays in denser medium is termed as
113.x: Bending of light on entering a denser medium is refraction. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: Why does water tank appear shallower when viewed from the top?
113.x: Light from the tank bottom bends away from the normal on leaving water, so the bottom looks raised – refraction. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: When there is a short circuit what happens to the current in the circuit?
113.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
113.x: In a short circuit resistance falls almost to zero, so the current increases heavily. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: An electric fuse is used to prevent?
113.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
113.x: A fuse melts and breaks the circuit when an excessive (heavy) current flows, protecting appliances. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s:
Which of the following is/are correct about Galvanometer?
1. It is a device used to detect electric current in a circuit.
2. It shows the direction of current flows in the circuit.
3. The accuracy of the galvanometer is more as compared to the ammeter.
4. The Galvanometer is mostly used in bridge for knowing the zero current.
113.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
113.x: A galvanometer detects current and its direction and serves as the null detector in bridges (1, 2, 4); it is more sensitive but not more accurate than an ammeter (3 wrong). Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: At the time of short circuit, the current in the circuit
113.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
113.x: In a short circuit the resistance becomes almost zero, so the current rises very sharply (which blows the fuse). Physics, moved to book 5 row 1.

113.s: Grass appears green because
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
113.x: Grass looks green because chlorophyll reflects green light and absorbs the rest. Off-topic (physics/biology), moved.

113.s: What is the principle of working of transformer?
113.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: A transformer works on mutual induction: a changing current in the primary coil induces an emf in the secondary coil.

113.s: Which of the following coloured lights has the highest wavelength?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
113.x: Red light has the longest wavelength of visible light (about 620–750 nm); yellow, green and blue are progressively shorter.

113.s: What is the minimum distance required to hear an echo?
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
113.x: An echo is heard only if the reflected sound arrives at least 0.1 s later; with sound at about 344 m/s the reflector must be at least 344 x 0.1 / 2 = 17.2 m away.

113.s: The pitch of the voice of the women is in general –
o: marginally lower than that of men
much lower than that of men
the same as that of men
113.x: Women's vocal cords are shorter and thinner and vibrate faster, so their voice pitch (frequency) is generally higher than men's.

113.s: Splitting of white light into seven colors on passing through the glass prism is called
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
113.x: Splitting of white light into its seven colours by a prism is dispersion, because different wavelengths refract by different amounts.

113.s: Which of the following characteristics of a sound wave depends only on the source of sound and not on the medium through which it travels?
113.src: AP High Court Common Test for Multiple Posts 2026
113.x: Frequency is set by the vibrating source and stays the same in any medium. Speed and wavelength change with the medium. (Off-topic: physics of sound.)

113.s: Which of the following is not a primary colour?
113.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: Red, green and blue are the additive primary colours of light, so yellow is not one. (Moved to 5:1.)

113.s: What is the common name of Asafoetida (Ferula asafoetida) which is the dried sap or gum resin obtained from the roots of Ferula plants and used in several Indian dishes?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
113.x: Asafoetida is hing, the dried gum-resin from the roots of Ferula. Methi is fenugreek, saunf fennel and ajwain carom seed.

113.s: Turmeric powder is obtained from which part of turmeric plant ?
113.x: Turmeric powder is made from the dried rhizome, an underground stem, not a fruit, root or seed, so 'None of the above' is right. 'Dried root' tempts because the rhizome grows underground.

113.s: The chicory powder which is mixed with coffee powder is obtained from which of the following part of plant?
113.x: Chicory powder is made from the roasted, ground root of the chicory plant, so the answer is root.

113.s: What cooking methods involve a small amount of hot liquid, ideally at a temperature between 160 and 180 °F usually done with eggs, delicate grains and certain veggies?
113.x: Poaching cooks food gently in a small amount of hot liquid at about 160–180 °F, as for eggs. Blanching is a brief dip in boiling water, baking uses dry oven heat and broiling direct heat.

113.s:
Fruits such as papaya, mango, peaches and apricots are rich sources of:
a) Antioxidants
b) Proteins
c) Carbohydrates
d) Soluble fibre
e) Fats
113.src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
113.x: Papaya, mango, peaches and apricots are rich in antioxidants (beta-carotene, vitamin C), carbohydrates and soluble fibre; they are poor in protein and fat. So a, c and d.

113.s: The percentage of fat in double toned milk is:
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
113.x: Double toned milk has 1.5% fat (and 9% SNF); toned milk has 3% fat.

113.s: The colour of Cow's milk is slightly yellowish due to the presence of
113.x: Cow's milk is slightly yellow because of carotene (beta-carotene) in its fat; 'Carolin' is the paper's misprint of carotin (carotene). Riboflavin only gives whey a greenish-yellow tint, so the printed key (b) is wrong.

113.s: After parboiling, the nutritive value of rice
113.x: Parboiling drives water-soluble B vitamins and minerals from the husk and bran into the grain, so rice's nutritive value increases.

113.s: Lutein is a/an:
113.x: Lutein is a yellow xanthophyll pigment (marigold, egg yolk, the eye's macula). Blue/purple is anthocyanin, orange is carotene.

113.s: Which of the following accounts for the red colour of tomato?
113.x: The red colour of tomato is lycopene, a carotenoid. Capsaicin is chilli's pungent compound; carotene is orange and anthocyanin red-purple.

113.s: An example of modified underground stem is
113.x: Potato is a stem tuber, a modified underground stem with nodes ('eyes') that bear buds. Carrot and turnip are modified roots, and groundnut is a fruit that develops underground.

113.s: From which part of pant the ‘Asafoetida or heeng’ is obtained?
113.x: Asafoetida (heeng) is the dried latex (oleo-gum resin) exuded from the roots of Ferula plants.

113.s: Which is the most widely used method of cooking food?
113.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
113.x: Boiling is the most widely used cooking method in Indian homes (rice, dal, vegetables). Frying, barbecuing and tenderising are less common.

113.s: Name the scientific instrument to test the purity of milk
113.x: A lactometer measures the specific gravity of milk and so tests its purity.

113.s: The density of milk can be obtained by the use of :
113.x: A lactometer measures the density (specific gravity) of milk. A butyrometer measures fat content.

113.s: Flower colours of red, pink, blue and purple come mainly from the pigments called ………
113.x: Anthocyanins are water-soluble pigments that give red, pink, blue and purple colours to flowers. Carotenoids give yellow and orange.

113.s: Cloves are obtained from
113.x: Cloves are the dried unopened flower buds of the clove tree (Syzygium aromaticum).

113.s: ' Oryza sativa ' is the scientific name of:
113.x: Oryza sativa is cultivated rice. Wheat is Triticum, maize Zea mays and potato Solanum tuberosum.

113.s: With what is the banana plant propagated?
113.x: Banana is propagated vegetatively by suckers, the side shoots from the underground stem. Cultivated bananas are seedless, so seeds are not an option.

113.s: Ginger is a kind of
113.x: Ginger is a rhizome, an underground stem that stores food, so of these options it is a tuberous stem. It is not a root.

113.s: The storage organ of which of the following plants is not a stem ?
113.x: Sweet potato stores food in a tuberous root. Sugarcane, potato and ginger all store food in stems.

113.s: We obtain chilgoza from the seed of species –
113.x: Chilgoza is the edible seed of the pine Pinus gerardiana.

113.s: Which of the following underground produced vegetables is a modified root ?
113.x: Sweet potato is a tuberous (modified) root; potato is a stem tuber, and arbi (bandda) and jimikand (yam) are corms, i.e. stems.

113.s: In the following pairs of plants and their edible parts, which pair is not correctly matched ?
113.x: The printed options lost their edible parts; in the original 'Potato – root' is wrong, since the potato is a stem tuber. Ginger (rhizome), onion (bulb) and coconut (endosperm) were correctly matched.

113.s: The test in which the scorer is asked to rank samples in a decreasing or increasing order of same characteristics is:
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
113.x: In a ranking test (sensory evaluation) the judge arranges samples in increasing or decreasing order of one characteristic, such as sweetness.

113.s: The caramelization reactions require intense heat about
113.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
113.x: Caramelisation of sucrose needs about 170 °C (it begins near 160 °C); 100 °C only boils water and 200-240 °C burns the sugar.

113.s: The pH value of Curd as compared to that of Milk would be?
113.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
113.x: Curd contains lactic acid formed by bacteria from lactose, so it is more acidic than milk and its pH is lower (about 4-4.5 against 6.5-6.7).

113.s: Curd should not be kept in
113.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
113.x: Curd is acidic and reacts with brass (copper-zinc), forming toxic salts, so it should not be kept in brass vessels; glass, steel and earthen pots are safe.

113.s: Lycopene is a pigment present in:
113.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
113.x: Lycopene is the red carotenoid pigment of tomato (also watermelon).

113.s: Which of the following is an example of a Maillard reaction?
o: Burning of eyes while cutting onions
113.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
113.x: The Maillard reaction is the browning of food when sugars react with amino acids on heating - e.g. bread turning into toast; tears from onions, egg hardening (protein denaturation) and curd formation are other processes.

113.s: Viscosity is measured in:
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
113.x: Viscosity is measured in poise (CGS unit); the SI unit is the pascal-second (1 Pa·s = 10 poise).

113.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List-1 (Physicists):
A. WK Roentgen
B. Victor Francis Hess
C. Ernest Orlando Lawrence
D. CH Townes
List-2 (Major contribution/discovery):
1. Cosmic radiation
2. Maser
3. X-rays
4. Cyclotron
113.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
113.x: Roentgen discovered X-rays, Hess cosmic radiation, Lawrence invented the cyclotron and Townes the maser, so A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2. Off-topic science, moved.

113.s: A metric chain of 20 metre length consists of ____ links.
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
113.x: A 20 m metric chain has 100 links of 0.2 m (20 cm) each.

113.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I:
I. Hygrometer
II. Ammeter
III. Odometer
IV. Anemometer
List-II:
A. Current
B. Wind
C. Humidity
D. Speed
113.src: General Studies & Mental Ability (paper title page missing i
113.x: Hygrometer – humidity, ammeter – current, odometer – distance/speed of a vehicle, anemometer – wind. Off-topic, moved.

113.s:
Match the Name of Scientists in List-I to their fields of expertise Subject in List-II.
List-I:
A. Pier Antonio Micheli
B. George Cuvier
C. Rudolf Virchow
D. Stephen Hales
List-II:
i. Plant physiology
ii. Pathology
iii. Palaeontology
iv. Mycology
113.src: APPSC Executive Officer Gr-III Endowment Paper-I General Stu
113.x: Micheli – mycology, Cuvier – palaeontology, Virchow – pathology, Stephen Hales – plant physiology. Off-topic, moved.

113.s:
Match List I (Physical quantities) with List II (Units) and choose the correct option:
List I:
I. Electric current
II. Temperature
III. Luminous Intensity
List II:
a. candela
b. ampere
c. kelvin
113.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
113.x: SI units: current – ampere, temperature – kelvin, luminous intensity – candela. Off-topic, moved.

113.s: If Kilo is Thousand, then Deka is
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
113.x: Deka (deca) is the SI prefix for ten (10^1); kilo = 10^3, hecto = 10^2.

113.s: Who among the following determined the charge of electrons as 1.5924 x 10^-19 C?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
113.x: Robert Millikan's oil-drop experiment (1909-13) measured the electron's charge, about 1.59 x 10^-19 C in his 1913 result (now 1.602 x 10^-19 C).

113.s: Which instrument is used to measure speed?
113.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
113.x: A tachometer measures speed (rotational speed of an engine, rpm); an ammeter measures current, a venturimeter flow rate. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: The instrument used to measure high temperatures
113.src: APSLPRB SI Paper-IV Final Written Exam 2017
113.x: A pyrometer measures very high temperatures (furnaces) from emitted radiation; a pedometer counts steps. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: A projector for images of both opaque objects and transparencies is called an ______.
113.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
113.x: An epidiascope projects images of both opaque objects and transparencies (episcope + diascope); an anemometer measures wind speed. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: A hydrometer is used to measure?
113.src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
113.x: A hydrometer measures the relative density (specific gravity) of liquids; humidity is measured by a hygrometer. Off-topic (physics), moved.

113.s: ______ is an instrument for measuring the distance travelled by a vehicle.
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
113.x: An odometer measures the distance travelled by a vehicle (a speedometer measures speed).

113.s: Microsecond = x seconds; What is 'x'?
113.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
113.x: One microsecond = 10^-6 second (one millionth of a second).

113.s: The Least Count of a measuring instrument is the
o: Smallest change in the measured quantity that can be resolved
Error due to wrong zero setting
Largest value that the instrument can measure
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
113.x: The least count is the smallest value (smallest change in the measured quantity) that an instrument can resolve, e.g. 1 mm for a metre scale.

113.s: Who among the following wrote 'De Magnete' in the 1600s, which gave the first rational explanation of the compass needle's mysterious ability to point north-south?
113.src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
113.x: William Gilbert's De Magnete (1600) first explained the compass by treating the Earth as a giant magnet. Off-topic (physics), moved to book 5.

113.s: In which year did John Dalton present his atomic theory?
113.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
113.x: John Dalton put forward his atomic theory in the early 1800s and published it in 'A New System of Chemical Philosophy' (1808), the year usually asked.

113.s: Which device is used to measure current in a circuit?
113.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
113.x: An ammeter, connected in series, measures current; a voltmeter measures potential difference.

113.s: Steridian is unit of?
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
113.x: The steradian is the SI unit of solid angle; the radian measures a plane angle.

113.s:
The efforts to detect the existence of Higgs boson particle have become frequent news in the recent past. What is/are the importance/importances of discovering this particle?
a. It will enable us to understand as to why elementary particles have mass
b. It will enable us in the near future to develop the technology of transferring matter from one point to another without traversing the physical space between them
c. It will enable us to create better fuels for nuclear fission
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
113.x: The Higgs boson explains why elementary particles have mass (Higgs mechanism, confirmed at CERN 2012). It has nothing to do with teleporting matter or with fission fuels, so only statement a is right.

113.s:
Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched?
Inventor : Invention
A. Christopher Cockerell : Hovercraft
B. David Bushnell : Submarine
C. J.C. Perrier : Steamship
Select the correct answer by using the code given below:
113.x: All pairs match: Christopher Cockerell – hovercraft; David Bushnell – submarine (Turtle, 1775); J.C. Périer – steamship (1775).

113.s: An electric bulb is rated 11 W. What does W signify here?
o: Amount of electricity consumed in a day
113.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
113.x: The watt is the unit of power, i.e. energy consumed per unit time (1 W = 1 J/s); an 11 W bulb uses 11 joules each second. It does not measure light output or daily consumption.

113.s: Microscope was invented by
113.x:
Official key / most books: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek. Strictly: the compound microscope is credited to Zacharias Janssen (c. 1590); Leeuwenhoek perfected the simple microscope (general knowledge, not checked).
The usual key credits the microscope to Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, who built powerful single-lens microscopes (1670s). (Science item, moved.)

113.s: What is the range of mercury thermometer in Fahrenheit?
113.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
113.x:
Printed answer: -35 to 673 °F. Strictly mercury freezes at -38.8 °C (-37.9 °F) and boils at 356.7 °C (674 °F) (general knowledge, not checked).
A mercury thermometer works between mercury's freezing and boiling points, about -38 °C to 357 °C, i.e. roughly -37 °F to 674 °F; the printed answer gives the commonly quoted -35 to 673 °F.

113.s: How many square metres make one acre of area?
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
113.x: One acre = 4,046.86 square metres (about 0.4047 hectare); one hectare = 10,000 sq m. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

113.s: According to Kohlberg, which is the highest stage of moral reasoning?
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
113.x: Kohlberg's sixth and highest stage is the 'universal ethical principle' orientation (post-conventional). Law and order is stage 4, social contract stage 5 and punishment-avoidance stage 1.

113.s:
Consider the following actions :
1. Detection of car crash/collision which results in the deployment of airbags almost instantaneously
2. Detection of accidental free fall of a laptop towards the ground which results in the immediate turning off of the hard drive
3. Detection of the tilt of the smart-phone which results in the rotation of display between portrait and landscape mode In how many of the above actions is the function of accelerometer required?
113.x: All three use accelerometers: airbag crash detection, laptop free-fall detection and phone screen rotation by tilt.

113.s:
In which of the following are hydrogels used?
1. Controlled drug delivery in patients.
2. Mobile air-conditioning systems.
3. Preparation of industrial lubricants.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
113.x: Hydrogels are well established in controlled drug delivery, contact lenses and wound dressings. Mobile air-conditioning and industrial lubricants are not standard uses. UPSC official key (Set A Q.36): (a) 1 only.

113.s:
In which of the following are hydrogels used ?
1. Controlled drug delivery in patients
2. Mobile air-conditioning systems
3. Preparation of industrial lubricants
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
113.x: Hydrogels are well established in controlled drug delivery, contact lenses and wound dressings. Mobile air-conditioning and industrial lubricants are not standard uses. UPSC official key (Set A Q.36): (a) 1 only.

113.s:
Consider the following features of newer models of motor cars.
I. Radial tyres
II. Streamlined body
III. Multipoint fuel injection
IV. Catalytic converter with exhaust
Which of these features make the new models of motor cars more fuel efficient?
113.x:
Official key / most books: II and III. Strictly: radial tyres (I) also cut rolling resistance, so I, II and III improve efficiency (no such option).
A streamlined body (less drag) and multipoint fuel injection (better combustion) raise fuel efficiency. A catalytic converter only cuts emissions. Radial tyres also help through lower rolling resistance, but the standard key is II and III.

113.s: Where is the Black Box fitted in planes?
113.x: The black box (flight data and cockpit voice recorders) is fitted in the tail section, the part most likely to survive a crash.

113.s: From environmental considerations, which of the following is a better option to serve Tea or trains?
o: Serving in glass cups or metal glasses, which are reusable
113.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
113.x:
Printed key (APPSC): reusable glass or metal cups. Kulhads were also promoted by Indian Railways as the eco-friendly option (Wikipedia, Kulhar), but they are single-use and fired in coal/wood kilns.
Reusable glass or metal cups create no waste. Paper cups are plastic-lined, plastic glasses are single-use, and kulhads, though biodegradable, use topsoil and kiln fuel each time.

113.s:
Read the following statements about the impact of Science and Technology on the Environment and Society:
A. Technology misuse and its wrong implementation leads to the occurrence of environmental pollution
B. Scientists have proposed technology as a medium through which the environment can be sincerely helped if directed positively
Identify the INCORRECT statement/statements
113.x: Both statements are true (misused technology pollutes; well-directed technology can help the environment), so neither is incorrect.

113.s: Which of the following statements best reflects the impact of science and technology on society?
o: Science and technology have eliminated poverty and inequality worldwide
Advances in science and technology have led to significant improvements in healthcare and increased life expectancy
Science and technology have completely eliminated the risk of natural disasters
The development of science and technology has had no impact on economic growth and productivity
113.x: Science and technology have improved healthcare and life expectancy; the other options are absolute claims that are false.

113.s: In Pavlovian conditioning paradigm as developed originally which of the following was used as independent variable?
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
113.x: In Pavlov's original paradigm the experimenter varied the number of pairings of the conditioned stimulus (bell) with the unconditioned stimulus (food) – the independent variable; response magnitude and latency were the measured (dependent) variables.

113.s: Who among of the following is not an exponent of Humanistic Realism?
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
113.x: Humanistic realism is a 16th-century Renaissance school whose exponents were Erasmus, Rabelais and Milton; Aristotle is an ancient Greek philosopher, not one of its exponents. Off-subject (philosophy of education).

113.s: Who opined, "The world is continuously evolving towards greater degree of perfection that is God." It is the opinion of
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
113.x: The idea that the world is continuously evolving towards a greater perfection that is God (the Divine) is Sri Aurobindo's theory of spiritual evolution. Aristotle (the printed key) spoke of an unmoved mover, not of the world evolving into God; Plato and Russell do not hold this view. Off-subject (philosophy of education).
