113.s: New ideas (Eureka) suddenly come in the minds of the creative children in which of the following stage?
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
113.x: In Wallas's stages of creativity (preparation, incubation, illumination, verification) the sudden 'Eureka' insight comes at illumination. Off-subject (educational psychology).

113.s: The permissible percentage overload on DG sets for 1 hour in every 12 hours of operation is
113.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
113.x: Prime-rated diesel generator sets are allowed a 10% overload for 1 hour in every 12 hours of operation. Off-topic (electrical engineering).

113.s: Sum of exterior angles of a convex polygon is
113.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
113.x: The exterior angles of any convex polygon, one at each vertex, always add up to 360°. Off-topic (mathematics).

113.s:
Consider the following statements in respect of 'pi' (π):
a. Pi is the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter.
b. Pi is a rational number.
Which of the above statement/s is/are correct?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
113.x: Only a is correct: pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, and it is irrational (Aryabhata's 3.1416 is only an approximation), so statement b is false.

113.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I:
I. Owl
II. Horse
III. Eagle
IV. Bear
List-II:
A. Swoop
B. Lumber
C. Flit
D. Gallop
113.src: General Studies & Mental Ability (paper title page missing i
113.x: An owl flits, a horse gallops, an eagle swoops and a bear lumbers. Off-topic (vocabulary), moved.

113.s: Which among the following is appropriate Phrasal verb for 'Loiter Aimlessly'?
113.src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
113.x: 'Hang out' means to spend time idly or loiter; hold up = delay, keep on = continue, lay off = dismiss. Off-topic (English), moved.

113.s: If Mental Age of a Child is 6 and Physical Age is 10, the IQ of the child is?
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
113.x: IQ = mental age ÷ chronological age × 100 = 6 ÷ 10 × 100 = 60. Off-topic (psychology / mental ability), moved.

113.s: Wood neither gaining or losing moisture content is called:
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
113.x: Wood that neither gains nor loses moisture is at its equilibrium moisture content (in balance with the surrounding humidity); the fibre saturation point is the stage when cell walls are saturated but cell cavities empty. No printed key. Off-topic (wood science), moved.

113.s: 'Latent learning' is a concept enunciated by whom?
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
113.x: 'Latent learning' – learning that shows only when there is a reason to use it – was put forward by Edward Tolman (rats in mazes, cognitive maps). Off-topic (psychology), moved.

113.s: The function of the capacitor across the supply to the fluorescent tube is primarily to
o: Initiate the arc in the tube
Limit the current through the tube
113.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
113.x: The capacitor across the supply of a fluorescent tube corrects the lagging power factor caused by the choke.

113.s: In nominal scaling, if the observations in a group are not much different from each other but they can be ranked according to some criteria then they are said to be measured on:
113.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
113.x: Data that can be ranked but not measured in equal units are on an ordinal scale; nominal only names categories, interval and ratio need equal units. Off-topic (statistics), moved.

113.s: Out of the following, which type of graph is best suited for representing the outgo of a rupee in Budget?
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Mains Paper-I General Studies & M
113.x: The outgo of each rupee of the Budget is a share of a whole (paise per rupee), which a pie chart shows best; bar and line graphs compare amounts or trends and a histogram shows frequency. Off-topic (statistics), moved.

113.s: Who developed regression analysis?
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
113.x: Francis Galton introduced regression (regression toward the mean, 1880s); Karl Pearson developed correlation and Spearman rank correlation. (Moved: general science.)

113.s: When a synchronous motor is running at synchronous speed, the damper winding produces
113.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
113.x: At synchronous speed there is no relative motion between the rotor and the rotating field, so no current is induced in the damper winding and it produces no torque.

113.s: Pick up the correct pair among the following.
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
113.x: In chain surveying a ranging rod is set up to mark the position of stations and to range (align) survey lines; it does not measure distance or angles.

113.s: The purpose of child lock feature in a car/vehicle is to:
o: automatic closing of the door by the driver
113.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
113.x: A child lock disables the inside handle of a rear door so it cannot be opened from inside; it can still be opened from outside.

113.s: Which of the following is NOT the advantage of dumpy level over the wye level?
o: Simpler construction with fewer movable parts
Adjustment tested with greater rapidity and ease
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
113.x: The dumpy level's advantages are simpler construction, fewer adjustments and longer-lasting adjustments; quick and easy testing of adjustments is the advantage of the wye level.

113.s: For a transformer operating at constant load current, maximum efficiency will occur at
113.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
113.x: At constant load current the copper loss is fixed, so output and efficiency are highest at unity power factor. Off-topic here (electrical engineering).

113.s: In the fluorescent tube circuit the function of the choke is primarily to
o: Initiate the arc and stabilize it
113.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
113.x: The choke (ballast) gives a high-voltage kick to strike the arc in the tube and then limits the current to keep it stable.

113.s: What is the term for water contained within the cell wall of wood?
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
113.x: Water held within the cell walls of wood is bound (hygroscopic) water; free water fills the cell cavities. Wood-science texts call it bound water.

113.s: Maximum permissible earth resistance at large power stations is
113.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
113.x: Large power stations need earth resistance of no more than about 0.5 ohm (major substations 1 ohm, small substations 2 ohm).

113.s: A salient pole synchronous motor is running at no load. Its field current is switched off. The motor will
o: Continue to run at synchronous speed
Run at half the synchronous speed
113.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
113.x: A salient-pole motor at no load keeps running at synchronous speed even with its field switched off, because the reluctance torque of the salient poles holds it in step.

113.s: Designed power factor of a DG set is generally at:
113.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
113.x: DG (diesel generator) sets are rated at a power factor of 0.8 lagging, so their kVA rating is 1.25 times the kW rating.

113.s: No-load current in a transformer
o: Lags behind the voltage by about 15°
Is in phase with the voltage
Lags behind the voltage by about 75°
113.src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
113.x: At no load a transformer draws mainly magnetising current, so the power factor is very low (about 0.1-0.2) and the current lags the applied voltage by roughly 75-85°. Standard objective keys give about 75°.

113.s: How much water a dripping tap is likely to waste in a year (choose nearest figure)
113.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
113.x: A tap dripping once a second wastes on the order of 1,000+ litres a year, so 1,200 litres is nearest.

113.s: If a chain is too long, the corrections to the measured distances will be ____
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
113.x: A chain that is too long measures fewer chain lengths than the true distance, so the correction is positive (added).

113.s: The drum of a Photostat machine is made up of which one of the following elements?
113.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
113.x: The photocopier drum is coated with photoconductive selenium (or amorphous silicon/organic photoconductor) that holds charge in the dark and loses it when lit.

113.s: Holography is a technique which is now extensively used by:
113.x:
Printed/book key: Navigators. Strictly: holography is used widely by museum authorities (3D recording/display of artefacts) and in security; no source found stating 'navigators' (web search).
Printed key: navigators (holographic displays/head-up navigation aids). Holograms are also widely used to record and display museum artefacts, so the option is debatable.

113.s: The traits of Kalikak family of USA were studied by whom?
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
113.x: Henry H. Goddard studied the Kallikak family (1912) to argue that 'feeble-mindedness' was inherited; Galton studied hereditary genius.

113.s: Who is not a behaviorist from the following?
113.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
113.x: Kurt Lewin was a Gestalt/field-theory psychologist, not a behaviourist; Pavlov, Watson and Skinner are behaviourists.

113.s: Which type of fungi is most notorious for causing dry rot in wood?
113.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
113.x:
Most keys: 'Dry rot fungus'. Strictly, the dry rot fungus Serpula lacrymans is itself a brown-rot fungus (general knowledge, not checked).
The fungus notorious for dry rot of timber is the dry rot fungus (Serpula lacrymans), keyed as option 3; it decays wood as a brown rot. (Off-topic: wood decay.)

113.s: Who invented Television?
113.src: Pollution Control Board Steno Typist, Junior Assistant 2017
113.x: John Logie Baird demonstrated the first working television in 1926. Fleming discovered penicillin and Watt improved the steam engine.

113.s: Which of the following instruments is NOT used for setting out gradient?
113.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
113.x: The prismatic compass measures bearings (horizontal directions), not gradients. The clinometer measures slopes and the Ceylon ghat tracer locates points on a given gradient (hill-road surveys); the dumpy level gives levels from which gradients are set out.

113.s: Ripe avocado mainly contains ______ acid.
113.src: APPSC Lecturers in Government Degree Colleges (Notification No. 26/2018) - General Studies & Mental Ability (Paper-I), computer-based test, held 15-09-2020 · Q26
113.x: Ripe avocado fat is mainly oleic acid, a monounsaturated fatty acid.

113.s: Which of the following chromosomes is/are the sex chromosomes?
113.src: APPSC Lecturers in Government Degree Colleges (Notification No. 26/2018) - General Studies & Mental Ability (Paper-I), computer-based test, held 15-09-2020 · Q28
113.x: X and Y are the human sex chromosomes.

113.s: The digestive fluid bile is produced by which organ of the human body?
113.src: APPSC Lecturers in Government Degree Colleges (Notification No. 26/2018) - General Studies & Mental Ability (Paper-I), computer-based test, held 15-09-2020 · Q32
113.x: The liver makes bile, and the gall bladder only stores it.

113.s:
Match Table-I with Table-II and choose correct code.
Table-I:
A. Lipase,
B. Amylase,
C. Trypsin,
D. Lactase
Table-II:
1. Breaks lactose,
2. Breaks fat,
3. Breaks starch,
4. Breaks protein
113.src: APPSC Lecturers in Government Degree Colleges (Notification No. 26/2018) - General Studies & Mental Ability (Paper-I), computer-based test, held 15-09-2020 · Q36
113.x: Lipase breaks fat, amylase breaks starch, trypsin breaks protein and lactase breaks lactose.

113.s: What is a change of position ?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q14
113.x: A body is said to be in motion when its position changes with time.

113.s: The shortest path between the initial and final position is known as
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q15
113.x: Displacement is the shortest (straight-line) distance from the initial to the final position, with direction.

113.s: Grass appears green because
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q16
113.x: Chlorophyll in grass absorbs red and blue light and reflects green light, which reaches our eyes.

113.s:
Fill in the blanks:
Gunpowder, also known as black powder is made of Sulphur (S), Charcoal (C), and _________ .
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q38
113.x: Black powder is a mixture of sulphur, charcoal and potassium nitrate (saltpetre).

113.s: A process of deposition of calcium and other minerals on the surface of the cartilage is called
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q54
113.x: Ossification is the process in which calcium and other minerals are deposited in cartilage to form bone.

113.s: Aerobic respiration process requires
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q84
113.x: Aerobic respiration oxidises glucose using oxygen to release energy.

113.s: The gaseous exchange in humans takes place in
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q85
113.x: Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged across the thin walls of the lung alveoli.

113.s: The saliva helps in the digestion of
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q86
113.x: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) begins breaking starch into maltose.

113.s: Respiration in grasshopper takes place through
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q88
113.x: Insects such as grasshoppers breathe through a tracheal system opening at spiracles.

113.s: The food of Protozoans is digested by
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q89
113.x: Protozoans like Amoeba digest food inside food vacuoles using enzymes.

113.s: The tube that connects the pharynx with the stomach is the
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q90
113.x: The oesophagus (food pipe) carries food from the pharynx to the stomach.

113.s: Water and minerals are conducted upward in roots and stems through the
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q95
113.x: Xylem conducts water and minerals upward from roots.

113.s: A flower is brightly coloured, scented and secretes nectar. It is most probably pollinated by
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q97
113.x: Bright colour, scent and nectar attract insects, so such flowers are entomophilous.

113.s: Transfer of pollen grains through wind is known as
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q98
113.x: Anemophily is wind pollination.

113.s: By self-pollination, the seeds formed are
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q101
113.x: Repeated self-pollination leads to inbreeding depression, giving weaker seeds and plants.

113.s: The most malleable metal is
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q102
113.x: Gold is the most malleable metal; it can be beaten into very thin leaves.

113.s: Vinegar is a dilute solution of
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q104
113.x: Vinegar is about 5-8% acetic acid in water.

113.s:
Match the following using suitable codes:
A (Plant)
a. Fennel
b. Ginger
c. Garlic
d. Touch me not
B (Botanical Name)
I. Mimosa pudica
II. Foeniculum vulgare
III. Zingiber officinale
IV. Allium sativum
Codes:
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q109
113.x: Fennel is Foeniculum vulgare, ginger Zingiber officinale, garlic Allium sativum and touch-me-not Mimosa pudica.

113.s: The drug Rauwolfia, is obtained from ________ of Sarpgandha.
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q110
113.x: Reserpine and related drugs are extracted from the roots of Rauvolfia serpentina (sarpagandha).

113.s: Which of the following is not correctly matched (as per used plant part) ?
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q113
113.x: The useful part of turmeric is its underground rhizome, not the leaf.

113.s:
Match the following using suitable codes:
A (Medicinal Plant)
a. Sarpgandha
b. Isabgol
c. Arjuna
d. Sandal
B (Uses)
I. diuretic, refrigerant
II. nervous disorder
III. chronic constipation
IV. heart remedy
Codes:
113.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q114
113.x: Sarpagandha treats nervous disorders and hypertension, isabgol husk relieves constipation, Arjuna bark is a heart remedy and sandalwood is a cooling diuretic.

113.s: Free expansion of a system is
113.src: APPSC Group-I Services Preliminary (Screening) Test - General Studies & Mental Ability, held 20-04-2008 · Q132
113.x: Free expansion is expansion of a gas into a vacuum, against zero external pressure; examsnet's key marks the first option, which is wrong.

113.s: Which one of the following are the building blocks of proteins?
113.src: APPSC Group-I Services Preliminary (Screening) Test - General Studies & Mental Ability, held 20-04-2008 · Q137
113.x: Proteins are chains of amino acids.

113.s: Plants lose water through the process of
113.src: APPSC Group-I Services Preliminary (Screening) Test - General Studies & Mental Ability, held 20-04-2008 · Q141
113.x: Plants lose water vapour through stomata by transpiration.

113.s: Friction:
113.src: APPSC Group-I Services Preliminary (Screening) Test (Notification of 2008) - General Studies & Mental Ability, re-examination held 25-10-2010 · Q39
113.x: Friction opposes and so retards motion.
o: does not have any effect on motion

113.s: Cola type soft drinks contain
113.src: APPSC Group-I Services Preliminary (Screening) Test (Notification of 2008) - General Studies & Mental Ability, re-examination held 25-10-2010 · Q42
113.x: Cola drinks contain phosphoric acid.

113.s: 'Oryza sativa' is the scientific name of:
113.src: APPSC Group-I Services Preliminary (Screening) Test (Notification of 2008) - General Studies & Mental Ability, re-examination held 25-10-2010 · Q46
113.x: Oryza sativa is rice.

113.s: The chicory powder which is mixed with coffee is obtained from:
113.src: APPSC Group-I Services Preliminary (Screening) Test (Notification of 2008) - General Studies & Mental Ability, re-examination held 25-10-2010 · Q47
113.x: Chicory powder added to coffee comes from roasted roots.

113.s: Tomato belongs to the family of:
113.src: APPSC Group-I Services Preliminary (Screening) Test (Notification of 2008) - General Studies & Mental Ability, re-examination held 25-10-2010 · Q50

Android 6.0 is Marshmallow (2015); Lollipop is 5.x, KitKat 4.4, Jelly Bean 4.1-4.3 (now the latest is Android 17, June 2026).

118.x: MS-DOS has a command-line (command-based) interface, not a GUI.

118.s: Which of the following is not a hardware?
118.x: An operating system is software; printer, keyboard and mouse are hardware.

118.s: A Program that controls a computer's basic functions?
118.x: The operating system is the program that controls the computer's basic functions; motherboard, hard drive and CPU are hardware.

118.x: MS-DOS was first released in August 1981.

118.s: The operating system called UNIX is typically used for
118.x: UNIX is typically used on servers such as web servers; desktops and laptops mostly run Windows/macOS.

118.x: Booting loads the operating system, so without an OS a computer cannot boot; compiler, loader and assembler are not needed for it.

118.x: Windows is a GUI multi-tasking OS; batch and time-sharing describe other OS types.

118.x:
Bank exam keys / most books: Multi-tasking. Strictly OS texts call several programs sharing one CPU 'multiprogramming' (TechTarget).
Running two or more programs at once on a single processor is keyed as multi-tasking; multiprocessing needs more than one CPU.

118.s:
Consider the following statements.
I. Unix is a multitasking, multi-user computer operating system.
II. The Unix operating system is now entirely coded in C-language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x:
Most books: Both I and II. Strictly UNIX kernels keep a small part in assembly, so not 'entirely' C.
UNIX is a multitasking, multi-user OS and was rewritten in C, so both are keyed correct.

118.s:
Consider the following statements.
I. Soft reboot is also known as a warm reboot.
II. Warm reboot is the restarting of computer normally under software control without suddenly removing power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: A soft reboot is a warm reboot – restarting under software control without removing power; both correct.

118.s: Which process checks to ensure the components of the computer are operating and connected properly?
118.x: During booting the POST checks that components work and are connected; editing and processing are not checks.

118.s: Which is the programming tool in UNIX?
118.x: lint is UNIX's programming tool for checking C code; the kernel is the core and the C shell the command interpreter.

118.s: Which is not an operating system?
118.x: MS-Word is a word processor, not an OS; Mac, Linux and Windows are OSs.

118.s: What is not true about GNU operating system?
o: Its full form is 'GNU's Not Unix
It was started by Richard Stallman
It is not compatible with Unix
118.x: GNU ('GNU's Not Unix', Stallman, open source) is deliberately Unix-compatible, so 'not compatible with Unix' is the untrue statement.

118.s: Which of the following allows the processor to alternate between processing a user's active program and printing process?
118.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
118.x: The spooler program lets the processor alternate between the user's program and printing; a buffer only stores data, daisy-wheel and wire-matrix are printers.

118.s:
With reference to IT Jargon 'Daemon', which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. In multitasking computer operating systems.
2. A daemon is a computer program that runs as a background process, rather than being under the direct control of an interactive user.
3. The term was coined by the programmers of MIT's Project MAC.
Which of the above sentence (s) is/are true?
118.x: A daemon runs in the background in multitasking OSs, and the term came from MIT's Project MAC – all three are keyed true.

118.s: The nature of software applications can be characterized by their information
118.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Education and Data
118.x: Pressman: the nature of a software application is characterised by its information content and determinacy – both 2 and 3.

118.s: Word count option in Proofing dialog box of MS-Word displays the following information?
o: Pages, Words, Lines, paragraphs and characters with no spaces and characters with spaces
Pages, word count, characters with spaces and lines only
118.x: Word Count lists pages, words, characters without and with spaces, paragraphs and lines.

118.s: Which function key displays the print preview window in Microsoft Office?
118.x: Ctrl+F2 opens print preview in MS Office.

118.s: A word document, video or MP3 is a –
118.x: A Word document, video or MP3 is a file.

118.s: Which application in MS Office is used for audio visual presentations ?
118.x: MS PowerPoint makes audio-visual presentations; there is no 'MS Presenter'.

118.s: Drawings created with commercial software are typically saved as
118.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-II(B) VRO/Village Surveyor
118.x: Drawings made with CAD/commercial software are saved as electronic files. Off-topic, moved to software.

118.s: Which system allows multiple users to access a single computer system?
118.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
118.x: A time-shared system lets many users use one computer at the same time by giving each a short time slice; cluster and grid systems join many computers.

118.s: In computers, what does Yosemite, Mavericks, Mountain Lion, Lion, Snow Leopard, Leopard, Tiger, Panther, Jaguar, Puma and Cheetah stand for?
118.x: Cheetah, Puma, Jaguar, Panther, Tiger, Leopard, Snow Leopard, Lion, Mountain Lion, Mavericks and Yosemite are successive versions of Apple's Mac OS X. (Computer item, moved.)

118.s: Which of the following represents billion characters?
118.x: A gigabyte is about one billion bytes, i.e. a billion characters; a terabyte is a trillion.

118.x: One gigabyte holds about one billion characters (bytes).

118.s: Which of the following memory is embedded on CPU Chip?
118.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
118.x: Registers are embedded on the CPU chip; RAM and ROM are on the motherboard and auxiliary memory is external.

118.s: What is the portion of RAM that a computer microprocessor can access more quickly than it can access regular RAM?
118.x: Cache is the portion of memory the microprocessor can access faster than regular RAM.

118.s: Which one of the following would not be considered as a form of secondary storage?
118.x: RAM is primary memory; hard disk, optical disk, flash drive and floppy are secondary storage.

118.s: What is the smallest unit of information?
118.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
118.x: The bit (binary digit) is the smallest unit of information; a nibble is 4 bits and a byte 8.

118.s: Which of the following companies made the first commercially sold computer hard disk drive?
118.x: IBM sold the first commercial hard disk drive, the RAMAC 350 (1956).

118.s: One byte consists of
118.src: Technical Asst in Archaeology and Museum 2012
118.x: One byte consists of 8 bits.

118.s: Permanent memory built into computer
118.src: Asst. Director in A.P. Economics & Statistical Services 2011
118.x: ROM is the permanent memory built into the computer; RAM is volatile and the floppy is external.

118.s: We denote the time units taken by computer to execute instructions. Which of these time units is the smallest?
118.x: A picosecond (10^-12 s) is smaller than a nanosecond (10^-9 s) and a microsecond (10^-6 s).

118.s: In computers RAM stands for :
118.x: RAM stands for Random Access Memory.

118.s: What is the smallest unit of data represented in a computer ?
118.x: The bit is the smallest unit of data in a computer.

118.s:
Consider the following statements.

B. Primary Storage is slower as compared to Secondary Storage.

D. Von Neumann Architecture Uses Stored Program Digital Computer.
Choose the option in which all the statements are correct.
118.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
118.x: A is wrong (RAM is volatile) and B is wrong (primary storage is faster); C (SRAM faster than DRAM) and D (von Neumann = stored-program computer) are correct.

118.s:
Consider the following pairs;
Memory Device - Memory Type
A. RAM - Double Data Rate memory
B. Cache - Static random-access memory

D. Registers - Electronic Memory

118.x: RAM-DDR, cache-SRAM and registers-electronic memory are correct; a SATA hard disk is magnetic, not capacitive, memory, so A, B and D.

118.s: Which of the following is an example of Non-volatile Memory?
118.x: ROM is non-volatile; RAM is volatile and CPU is not a memory.

118.s: The decreasing order of storage capacities of external disks is
118.x: DVD (4.7 GB) > CD-ROM (about 700 MB) > floppy disk (1.44 MB).

118.s: Which among the following stores more data than a DVD ?
118.x: A Blu-ray disc (25 GB single layer) stores more than a DVD (4.7 GB); CD-ROM and floppy store less and 'Red Ray Disk' does not exist.

118.s: DVD technology uses an optical media to store the digital data. DVD is an acronym for
118.x: DVD = Digital Versatile Disc.

118.s: Which of the following is primary memory in Computer System?
118.x: RAM is primary memory; hard disk, compact disk and pen drive are secondary.

118.s: Which of the following memories has the shortest access time?
118.x: Cache memory has the shortest access time; RAM and magnetic memories are slower.

118.s: CD ROM stands for :
118.x: CD-ROM = Compact Disc Read Only Memory.

118.s: One byte equals to how many bits ?
118.x: A byte is 8 bits (a nibble is 4).

118.s:
Types of computer memory is/are –
(1) Semiconductor
(2) Magnetic
(3) Server
(4) Optical
Select the correct answer from the codes given below-
118.x: Computer memory is semiconductor (primary), magnetic or optical (secondary); 'server' is not a memory type.

118.s: Which of the following is not true about RAM?
o: RAM is a temporary storage area
RAM is like a hard disc storage
Information stored in RAM is gone when the computer
118.x: RAM is temporary and volatile, so it is not like hard-disc storage; that statement is the false one.

118.s: Which is not a type of secondary memory?
118.x: RAM is primary memory; SSD, hard disk and USB pen drive are secondary.

118.s: Which of the following memory of the computer is used to speed up the computer processing?
118.x: Cache memory speeds up processing by holding frequently used data next to the CPU.

118.s: The content of computer memory which is non-volatile, even when the power goes off is :
118.x: ROM is non-volatile and keeps its contents when power goes off; RAM is volatile.

118.s: In a computer, the permanent memory is called –
118.x: ROM is called the permanent memory of the computer.

118.s: Basic Input-Output system in computer resides :
118.x: The BIOS (Basic Input-Output System) is firmware stored in ROM.

118.s: Size of virtual memory depends on –
118.x: The size of virtual memory (virtual address space) is set by the number of CPU address lines; disc space only limits the swap file.

118.s: Which one of the following is not correct statement about 'Flash memory' ?
o: It is used for information storage in devices like digital
It can operate in extended temperature range of – 40 °C
It is cheaper than the normal mechanical disk drives
118.x: Flash memory is used in digital devices, works over a wide temperature range and uses little power, but it is costlier per GB than mechanical disk drives, so 'cheaper' is the wrong statement.

118.s: How many bits are there in a kilobyte?
118.x: 1 KB = 1024 bytes x 8 bits = 8192 bits.

118.s: How many bits are there in one byte?
118.x: One byte has 8 bits.

118.s: Which of the following is an extremely fast, small memory between CPU and main memory?
118.x: Cache memory is the extremely fast, small memory between the CPU and main memory.

118.s: 1024 bits is equal to how many bytes?
118.x: 1 byte = 8 bits, so 1024 bits ÷ 8 = 128 bytes; 1 MB is 1024 × 1024 bytes, far larger.

118.s: Multiple choice Questions makes us use of which form of retrieval of memory:

118.s: The memory of the computer is measured by –
118.x: Memory is measured in bits/bytes – the bit (binary digit) is the smallest unit; ohms, amperes and volts are electrical units.

118.s: Which of the following is the fastest memory ?
118.x:
Most keys: Cache memory. Strictly cache is made of SRAM, so 'Static RAM' is also fast (notes 0:6.2).
Cache is the fastest memory offered – shortest access time, between CPU and RAM. Static RAM is the material cache is built from, but 'cache memory' is the expected answer; disks are far slower.

118.s: Choose the smallest memory size unit –
118.x: Of the units offered KB is the smallest: KB < MB < GB < TB.

118.s: ROM is a memory –
118.x: ROM = Read-Only Memory: its contents can only be read, not written in normal use, and it is non-volatile.

118.s: The term bit is the short form of :
118.x: Bit is short for binary digit (0 or 1), the smallest unit of data.

118.s: Which one of the following is not a language of the computer ?
118.x: ROM is a memory, not a computer language; Java, C++ and Pascal are languages.

118.s: Computer hardware, which can store a very large quantity of data, is called :
118.x: Both magnetic tape and magnetic disk can store very large quantities of data, so 'both' is right.

Put the following units of storage into the correct order, starting with the smallest unit first and going down to the largest unit. I. Kilobyte

IV. Terabyte
V. Gigabyte
VI. Bit
Codes.
o: VI, II, I, III, V, IV
VI, II, I, IV, III, V
VI, II, I, III, IV, V
VI, II, I, IV, V, III
118.x: Bit < byte < KB < MB < GB < TB = VI, II, I, III, V, IV.

118.s: Which one of the following memories is not the primary memory of a computer?
118.x: CD-ROM is an optical disc – secondary storage; ROM, RAM and EEPROM are primary (semiconductor) memories.

118.s: Which of the following is a type of memory and is similar to RAM? It is used by computers to move data between the RAM and the CPU.
118.x: Cache is a RAM-like fast memory that moves data between RAM and the CPU; ROM is permanent, I-beam is a cursor and hypertext a link.

118.s: Which of the following is a storage device that uses rigid, permanently installed magnetic disks to store data or information?
118.x: A hard disk uses rigid, permanently installed magnetic platters; a floppy is flexible and removable, an optical disc uses laser.

118.s:
Consider the following statements.
I. Erasable programmable read only memory is a non-volatile memory that retains its data when its power supply is switched off.
II. EPROM can be erased by exposing it to the strong ultraviolet light.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: EPROM is non-volatile (keeps data without power) and is erased by strong ultraviolet light – both statements are correct.

118.s: Which of the following is equal to One Byte?
118.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
118.x: One byte = a string of eight bits; four bits is a nibble.

118.s:

2. Compared to a DVD, the BD format has several times more storage capacity.
3. Thickness of BD is 2.4 mm while that of DVD is 1.2 mm.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
118.x: BD supports HD video and holds several times more data than DVD, but both discs are 1.2 mm thick, so statement 3 is wrong.

118.s: What is full form of DVD?
118.x:
Most books: Digital Versatile Disk. Originally DVD was called 'Digital Video Disc', which is also printed.
DVD = Digital Versatile Disc (originally 'Digital Video Disc').

118.s: It is a plastic ribbon, usually half a inch wide that is coated on one side with an iron oxide material which can be magnetized. Identify this storage device.
118.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
118.x: Magnetic tape is a plastic ribbon, typically half an inch wide, coated on one side with magnetisable iron oxide.

118.s: A DVD is an example of
118.x: A DVD is an optical disc read by a laser; it is not a hard disc or a solid-state device.

118.s: Which of the following computer languages is used for artificial intelligence?
118.x: PROLOG (with LISP) is the classic language for artificial intelligence; C, FORTRAN and COBOL are general, scientific and business languages.

118.s: A computer program that converts assembly language to machine language is
118.x: Assembly language (2GL mnemonics) is converted into machine code by an assembler, not by a compiler; the other options are not translators.

118.s: The value of the variable having maximum frequency is known as:
118.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
118.x: The mode is the value that occurs most often (maximum frequency); the mean is the average and the median the middle value.

118.s: The C++ programming language is very popular because it is

118.x: C++ is popular for all three reasons: it is object-oriented, backward compatible with C and widely available.

118.s: Which of the following is a compiler?
118.x: Turbo C++ is Borland's compiler; Windows 98 is an OS and Java and BASIC are languages, not compilers.

118.s: A pictorial representation of sequence of steps of computation for a problem is known as
118.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
118.x: A flowchart is the pictorial form of the steps of an algorithm.

118.s: Which of the following languages is usually implemented with an interpreter?
118.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Education and Data
118.x: BASIC is the language usually implemented with an interpreter; assembly is translated by an assembler, Pascal and COBOL by compilers – the printed key 'Assembly' was wrong.

118.s: In the RAM of a computer, instructions and memory address are stored using
118.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Village Fisheries Asst.
118.x: Computers store instructions and addresses in RAM as binary digits (0 and 1); octal/hex are only shorthand for people, parity bits only check errors.

118.s: Which of the following is not a computer language?
118.src: Technical Asst in Archaeology and Museum 2012
118.x: Lotus (1-2-3) is a spreadsheet package, not a language; FORTRAN, BASIC and COBOL are languages.

118.s: The first high level computer language developed by I.W. Bekas in 1957
118.x: FORTRAN (IBM 1957, John Backus – 'I.W. Bekas' in the stem) was the first high-level language.

118.s: Computer language specially used in commercial activities
118.x: COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language) is for commercial work; FORTRAN is scientific.

118.s: The program language used in the computer is called as
118.x:
Printed key: C language. Strictly BASIC is also a programming language, so the stem has two language options.
C is a programming language; Windows is an OS and WordStar a word processor (BASIC is also a language, but C is the printed answer of the two).

118.s: The first computers were programmed using
118.x: The first computers were programmed directly in machine language; assembly and C came later.

118.s: Which of the following Languages is used for general purpose programs in early computers ?
118.x:
Printed key: BASIC (its name means 'all-purpose'). Strictly FORTRAN (1957) predates BASIC (1964).
BASIC (Beginner's All-purpose Symbolic Instruction Code) was the general-purpose language of early computers; FORTRAN was scientific, ALGOL algorithmic, PERL much later.

Arrange the following in increasing order of programming language generations?

118.x: Increasing generations: assembly (2GL), problem-oriented (3GL), query (4GL), application generator (4GL), natural language (5GL) = A, E, D, B, C.

118.x: A program expresses an algorithm in a specific language with strict syntax; a flowchart is pictorial and pseudo-code has no fixed syntax.

118.x: BCD stands for Binary Coded Decimal.

118.x: COBOL, PASCAL and BASIC are all high-level languages.

Convert high level language into machine language
Convert assembly language into machine language
Convert assembly language into high level language
118.x: An assembler converts assembly language into machine language; compilers handle high-level languages.

118.x: BASIC is a procedural language, not object-oriented.

118.s: Which one of the following is not the language of computer?
118.x: FAST is not a programming language; BASIC, C and FORTRAN are.

118.x: 7 = 0111 in 4-bit binary.

118.x: An OR gate gives 1 when any one input is 1; AND needs all inputs 1, NOR gives 0.

118.x: Machine language (0/1) is the only language the computer understands and runs directly.

2. Python

4. Java

118.x: Cobra, Python, Squirrel and Java are all computer languages.

118.x: FORTRAN (Formula Translation) is the scientific language; COBOL is for business.

118.x: The conditional operator (?:) is C++'s only ternary operator.

118.x: Function overloading is resolved at compile time (static polymorphism); virtual functions are the run-time case.

118.x: An assembler translates assembly language into machine language; a compiler handles high-level languages.

John George Kemeny and Dennis Ritchie

118.x: BASIC was developed by John G. Kemeny and Thomas E. Kurtz (Dartmouth, 1964); Ritchie made C and Hopper COBOL's forerunner.

118.x: C is the usual language of embedded computers; FORTRAN and COBOL are scientific and business languages.

118.s:

118.x: Adding an element to the top of a stack-style array is called push; pop removes it. Create and Evaluate are not insertion operations.

The overloaded operators follow the syntax rules of the original operator

119.x: A web server keeps information in web pages, and their text is marked up with HTML (HyperText Markup Language) tags.

119.s:
With reference to Web 3.0, consider the following statements:
A. Web 3.0 technology enables people to control their own data.
B. In Web 3.0 world, there can be blockchain based social networks.
C. Web 3.0 is operated by users collectively rather than a corporation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: All three are correct: Web 3.0 lets users control their own data, allows blockchain-based social networks, and is run collectively by users (DAOs) rather than by corporations (UPSC 2022 answer d).

119.s: Microsoft's new search engine launched in 2009 is called as
119.x: Microsoft launched the Bing search engine in 2009 (replacing Live Search). Buzz was a Google social tool.

119.s: The language of the world wide web is:
119.x: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the language of the WWW; the other options are misspellings.

119.s: The following is one of the world's most popular server-side scripting language of building dynamic and data-driven Web applications
119.x: PHP (Hypertext Preprocessor) is a widely used server-side scripting language for dynamic, data-driven websites. The other expansions are invented.

119.s: What is the use of <em> tag in HTML?
o: Indicate the importance of the text.
Increase the font size of the text.
119.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
119.x: The <em> tag marks emphasised text, i.e. it stresses the importance of the text (shown in italics). It does not create lists or change font size.

119.s: Which one of the following is not a search engine?
119.x: Chrome is a web browser (by Google), not a search engine. Google, Yahoo and Bing are search engines.

119.s: Which of the following is not a web browser?
119.x: Yahoo is a search engine and web portal, not a web browser. Internet Explorer, Firefox and Chrome are browsers.

119.s: In the field of Internet, W3C stands for :
119.x: W3C = World Wide Web Consortium, the international web standards body founded by Tim Berners-Lee in 1994.

119.s: Which of the following is a search engine?
119.x: Baidu is China's leading search engine. Packets are units of data and cookies are browser data.

119.s: Which of the following is not a search engine?
119.x: Orkut was Google's social networking site, not a search engine. Google and AltaVista are search engines, and ScienceDirect is a searchable research database.

119.s: DuckDuckGo is a
119.x: DuckDuckGo is a privacy-focused search engine that does not collect user information.

119.s: Which web browser was developed by Google?
119.x: Google developed the Chrome browser (2008). Internet Explorer is Microsoft's, Firefox is Mozilla's and Safari is Apple's.

119.s: The first page displayed by Web Browser after opening a Website is called :
119.x: The home page is the first page a browser shows when a website is opened.

119.s: Which of the following is not a Web browser?
119.x: Google Apps is a productivity suite, not a web browser. Opera, Vivaldi and Firefox are browsers.

119.s: Web Crawler is also known as :
119.x: A web crawler is also called a web spider (spiderbot): a bot that scans the Web for indexing.

119.s: Bing is a web search engine owned and operated by :
119.x: Bing is owned and operated by Microsoft.

119.s: JSP stands for :
119.x: JSP = Java Server Pages, a technology for dynamic web pages released by Sun Microsystems in 1999.

119.s: Which one of the following computer languages is used for displaying web pages and other information that can be displayed in a web browser?
119.x: HTML is the language used to build and display web pages in a browser. HTTP is the transfer protocol, not a display language.

119.s: Which one of the following is the small piece of data sent from a website and stored in a user’s web browser while a user is browsing a website?
119.x: A cookie is a small piece of data sent by a website and stored in the user's browser. A worm is malware, and a thumbnail is a small image.

119.s: In order to view pages on a website, the user needs to enter the site address called
119.x: A web page is opened by entering its URL (Uniform Resource Locator). A MAC address identifies hardware, and an e-mail address identifies a mailbox.

119.s: In information technology, what does HTML refers?
119.x: HTML = HyperText Markup Language.

119.s: Kurrently is a/an :
119.x: Kurrently is a real-time search engine for social-media content (Twitter, Facebook).

119.s: Yahoo, Google, and MSN are –
119.x: Yahoo, Google and MSN are internet sites (search engines/portals).

119.s: What is a homepage?
o: The last page of a website
119.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
119.x: A homepage is the main or introductory page of a website, from which its other pages are linked.

119.s: Solr is related to
119.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
119.x: Apache Solr is an open-source enterprise search platform (built on Lucene) used for full-text indexing and searching, e.g. in library discovery systems.

119.s: The search engine "Bing" is created and operated by
119.x: Bing is the search engine of Microsoft.

119.s: An online search in which all aspects of the records in natural language may be used as sought terms is known as ____.
119.src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
119.x: Free-text searching lets every word in the records, in natural language, be used as a search term (unlike controlled-vocabulary searching).

119.s: To reload a webpage, press the ____ button.
119.x: A web page is reloaded with the browser's Reload (Refresh) button, shortcut F5 or Ctrl+R. Ctrl alone does nothing. (Off-topic: ICT.)

119.s: All of the computers and printers on the network are called
119.x: Every device on a network, such as a computer or printer, is a node of the network.

119.s: The hardware unit required to connect a home computer to an internet is
119.x: A modem is the hardware that connects a home computer to the internet over the telephone or cable line. Wi-Fi only distributes an existing connection, and a switch or repeater works inside a LAN.

119.s: What is the function of a modem?
o: Voice to data conversion and data to voice conversion
Convert from analog signals to digital and from digital to analog signals
119.x: A modem (modulator-demodulator) converts digital signals to analog and analog signals back to digital. It does not encrypt, convert voice or check for viruses.

119.s: SMTP is the protocol of which OSI reference model Layer?
119.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
119.x: SMTP (e-mail sending) is an Application-layer protocol (layer 7), like HTTP, FTP and DNS.

119.s:
Arrange the following network devices used, starting from physical layer to application layer of OSI reference model: A. Router
B. Switch, Bridge
C. Gateway
D. NIC Card
E. Firewall
119.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
119.x: Going up the OSI layers: NIC (physical/data link) → switch and bridge (data link) → router (network) → firewall (network/transport and above) → gateway (up to application). So D, B, A, E, C.

119.s: A device used to convert Digital Data Signals into Analog Signals that can travel over standard telephone lines is called ___.
119.x: A modem converts digital data into analog signals that can travel on telephone lines, and back again. Repeaters, routers and switches do not modulate signals.

119.s: A device used for connecting a computer to Internet through a telephone line is :
119.x: A MODEM connects a computer to the internet through a telephone line. Switches, hubs and bridges join devices inside a network.

119.s: Which of the following performs, modulation and demodulation?
119.x: Modulation and demodulation are done by a modem. Coaxial cable, fibre and satellite are transmission media.

119.s: Which of the following is not a connecting device?
o: None of these (all are connecting devices)
119.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (None of these (all are connecting devices)); it is added as option 5.
Router, hub and switch are all connecting (networking) devices, so none of the printed options is 'not a connecting device' and the printed key (Router) is wrong. The original MPPSC 2014 question asked 'Which of the following is a connecting device?', answer 'All of these'.

119.s: In a network environment, which is not server?
119.x:
Official key (MPPSC 2021): Network Server. Strictly, a network server is a server too; it is just the generic term, while the other three are specific types.
File, print and application servers are named server types; 'network server' is the general name for any powerful central computer on a network, so the key treats it as 'not a server (type)'.

119.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Modem helps in stabilizing the voltage
Modem converts the analog signal into digital signal
119.x: A modem converts analog signals into digital signals (and digital to analog). It is hardware, not software or an operating system, and it does not stabilise voltage.

119.s:
Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the codes given below :
(1) Proxy server provides TCP/IP address.
(2) Proxy server processes clients requests by forwarding the requests to other servers.
Code :
119.x: A proxy server is a go-between that forwards client requests to other servers (statement 2 correct). It does not hand out TCP/IP addresses; DHCP does that (statement 1 wrong).

119.s: Which system or arrangement connects microcomputer with telephone ?
119.x: A MODEM connects a microcomputer to the telephone line. A VDU is a display, and UNIX is an operating system.

119.s: IP addresses are used on which layer of OSI reference model?
119.x: IP addresses are used at the Network layer (layer 3; the Internet layer of TCP/IP), where routers work. MAC addresses belong to the Data Link layer.

119.s:
Consider the following statements :
1. The most important technological application of liquid crystals is in digital display.
2. Modem is a device that is connected to a computer and to a phone line.
3. The National Institute of Oceanography is located at Coimbatore.
4. Virginis-70 is a system for recording video programmes. Of these statements :
119.x: 1 is correct (digital display, LCD) and 2 is correct (a modem connects a computer to a phone line). 3 is wrong because NIO is at Goa, and 4 is wrong because 70 Virginis is a star, not a video system. So only 1 and 2.

119.s: The layer between Physical and network layer is known as?
119.x: In the OSI stack the Data Link layer (layer 2) sits between the Physical (1) and Network (3) layers.

119.s: Such a device which convert data into impulses and transmitted it through terminal to computer or computer to terminal over telephone line, it is–
119.x: A modem converts data into signals sent over the telephone line between terminal and computer. Discs and CD-ROMs are storage.

119.s: A modem converts :
119.x: A modem converts both ways: digital to analog (modulation) and analog to digital (demodulation).

119.s: A modem is a hardware device that interfaces –
119.x: A modem interfaces telephone lines with computer equipment.

119.s: For sending and receiving data between computers around the world through telephone lines, we need:
119.x: A modem lets computers send and receive data worldwide over telephone lines. A fax sends images of documents, and a hub only joins devices locally.

119.s: The web browser 'World Wide Web' was invented by
119.x: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web (1989, CERN) and wrote the first web browser, itself named 'WorldWideWeb'. Crick (DNA) and Gould (palaeontology) are unrelated.

119.s: World Wide Web was discovered by
119.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-II(A) Engineering Assistant
119.x: The WWW was invented by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN in 1989. Ted Nelson only coined the word 'hypertext'; Gates and Page founded Microsoft and Google.

119.s: Personal Computers can be connected together to form a
119.x: Personal computers linked together to share data and resources form a network; a server is one machine on a network, not the linked whole.

119.s: Who is the founder of Internet?
119.src: Asst. Director in A.P. Economics & Statistical Services 2011
119.x: Leonard Kleinrock developed packet-switching theory and sent the first ARPANET message (1969), so he is credited as a founder of the Internet (Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn, the TCP/IP designers, are not among the options). Bill Gates founded Microsoft.

119.s: Internet allows to
119.src: Asst. Director in A.P. Economics & Statistical Services 2011
119.x: The Internet lets users send e-mail, view web pages and connect to servers, so all of the above.

119.s: Internet in India was started by VSNL in the year
119.x: VSNL launched public internet access in India on 15 August 1995. ERNET (1986) was only an academic network.

119.s: A network of networks is simply called –
119.x: The Internet is called a 'network of networks' because it interconnects millions of networks worldwide through TCP/IP. An intranet is one organisation's private network and an extranet extends it to partners.

119.s: The collection of linked information residing on computers which is available through internet is called
119.x: The World Wide Web is the collection of linked (hypertext) information on computers that is reached through the internet. A web server is only one computer that stores pages.

119.s: Who, among the following is considered as the inventor of the World Wide Web (WWW) ?
119.x: Tim Berners-Lee invented the WWW in 1989 at CERN. Vinod Dham is known for the Pentium chip and Edward Kasner for the word 'googol'.

119.s: WWW on the Internet stands for –
119.x: WWW (W3) stands for World Wide Web, the information system of linked documents on the internet.

119.s: World Wide Web (WWW) is a hypermedia system because –
o: It links to other computer resources
It can be used only to bring in video material
119.x: The WWW is a hypermedia system because its documents link to other computer resources (text, images, other pages). Its speed has nothing to do with the name, and it is not limited to video.

119.s: The full form of WWW is –
119.x: WWW = World Wide Web.

119.s: Who is the inventor of World Wide Web (WWW)?
119.x: Tim Berners-Lee invented the WWW at CERN in 1989. John Dalton gave the atomic theory.

119.s: In internet, the abbreviation WWW stands for
119.x: In internet usage WWW stands for World Wide Web.

119.s: Who is the inventor of WWW?
119.x: Tim Berners-Lee invented the WWW (CERN, 1989). Ray Tomlinson invented network e-mail.

119.s: Once the message is encoded in a desired format it is transferred through a medium called
119.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Education and Data
119.x: In the communication process (sender → encoder → channel → decoder → receiver), the encoded message travels through the channel.

119.s: Who is called the father of e-Mail?
119.x: Ray Tomlinson sent the first network e-mail on ARPANET in 1971 and chose the @ sign, so he is called the father of e-mail.

119.s: What does the letter "S" stand for in the Web terminology "HTTPS"?
119.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Education and Data
119.x: HTTPS = Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure; the S means Secure, because traffic is encrypted with SSL/TLS.

119.s: Standard protocol used for Internet surfing is
119.x: TCP/IP is the standard protocol suite on which all internet use, including surfing, runs. ARPANET was a network, while FTP and TELNET serve narrower tasks.

119.s: DNS stands for.....
119.x: DNS = Domain Name System. It translates domain names into IP addresses.

119.s: A database that contains the names and address of various hosts on internet is called :
119.x: The Domain Name System is the distributed database of names and addresses of internet hosts.

119.s: The set of protocols, which defines all transmission exchanges across the internet is called
119.x: TCP/IP is the protocol suite that defines all transmission exchanges across the internet. CSMA/CD is an Ethernet access method, and FDDI is a fibre ring LAN standard.

119.s: FTP stands for :
119.x: FTP = File Transfer Protocol, used to exchange files over the internet.

119.s: Which of the following protocol may be used for accessing World Wide Web?
119.x: HTTP is the protocol for accessing the WWW. SMTP sends e-mail, and SLIP is an old serial-line IP protocol.

119.s: A set of rules that governs data communication is called:
119.x: A protocol is a set of rules that governs data communication; RFCs are documents that publish such standards.

119.s: What is the full form of http?
119.x: http = Hypertext Transfer Protocol.

119.s: Which protocol is used for fetching web pages on the World Wide Web?
119.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
119.x: HTTP is the protocol for fetching web pages on the WWW. HTML is the markup language, and FTP transfers files.

119.s: Which of the following is a valid domain name extension?
119.x: .com, .gov and .net are all valid top-level domain extensions, so all of the above.

119.s: Which of the following countries represented by AU as its domain name?
119.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
119.x: .au is the country-code top-level domain of Australia (Austria .at, UAE .ae, Aruba .aw).

119.s: I.R.C. stands for :
119.x: IRC stands for Internet Relay Chat, an application-layer protocol for real-time text chat. Off-topic here; moved to networks and protocols.

119.s: HTTP refers to
119.x: HTTP = HyperText Transfer Protocol, the protocol of the World Wide Web.

119.s: What does PPTP stand for?
119.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
119.x: PPTP = Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol, a VPN protocol.

119.s: Which of the following is a computer network that is confined to a single building?
119.x: A LAN covers a limited area such as a home, office or single building. A MAN covers a city and a WAN countries; a PAN covers only personal devices within a few metres.

119.s: Which of the following is used to connect computers with in a small area ?
119.x: A LAN connects computers within a small area (room, building, campus). WAN and MAN cover wider areas, and IoT is not a network-size category.

119.s: Which network topology is the generalization of Bus topology?
119.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
119.x: Tree topology is a generalisation of bus topology: a branching cable with no closed loops (Stallings). Mesh, ring and star are separate layouts.

119.s: Which of the following is a network type?
119.x:
Printed key: MAN. Strictly, CAN (Campus Area Network) is also a network type (PMF S&T Part 5 p.30), so the stem has two right options; MAN is the standard textbook type.
MAN (Metropolitan Area Network) is a network type by area. Mesh and star are topologies, not types.

119.s: What is a "Virtual Private Network"?
o: It is a private computer network of an organisation where the remote users can transmit encrypted information
It is a computer network across a public internet that provides users access to their organisation's network while
It is a computer network in which users can access a shared pool of computing resources through a service provider.
None of the statements (a), (b) and (c) given above is the correct description of virtual private networks.
119.x: A VPN is a network across the public internet that gives users secure (encrypted) access to their organisation's network. (a) is too narrow, and (c) describes cloud computing (UPSC 2011 answer b).

119.s: ______ is not a common network topology.
119.x: The common topologies are bus, star, ring, mesh, tree and hybrid; 'grid' is not a network topology.

119.s: Ethernet is an example of
119.x: Ethernet is the wired technology (IEEE 802.3) used in LANs, e.g. office Ethernet. Wi-Fi is wireless LAN, not a network scope.

119.s: Internet system uses which of the following topology?
119.x:
Most books and keys: Tree. Strictly, the Internet is a hybrid, largely mesh, interconnection of networks (app notes 5:13: 'The Internet is the largest hybrid topology').
Exam keys say the Internet uses a tree topology, a hierarchical mix of bus and star.

119.s: In the context of the internet, what is the full form of MAN?
119.x: MAN = Metropolitan Area Network, which covers a city.

119.s: LAN stands for
119.x: LAN = Local Area Network, a network within a building or campus. Off-topic, moved to networks.

119.s: Which of the following best describes a private, company wide network, closed to public access?
119.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Intranet); it is added as option 6.
A private, company-wide network closed to public access is an intranet. The printed options repeat 'Internet' (option b is evidently a misprint of 'Intranet'); a VPN is a secure tunnel over a public network, cloud computing is remote services, and an extranet opens part of the network to outsiders.

119.s: The standard length of the MAC address is
119.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
119.x: A MAC address is 48 bits (6 bytes, 12 hex digits). IPv4 is 32 bits and IPv6 is 128 bits.

119.s: Which of the following is used to identify a computer uniquely on the internet?
119.src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
119.x: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on the internet. SMTP, TCP and UDP are protocols, not identifiers.

119.s: Which of the following is not class of IP address?
119.x: IPv4 has classes A to E only (A, B, C for networks, D multicast, E experimental). There is no Class F.

119.s: IPv4 and IPv6 are addresses used to identify computers on the Internet. Which statement is correct?
o: IPv4 and IPv6 require the same number of bits
Number of bits required for IPv4 address is less than number of bits required for IPv6 address
IPv4 requires more bits than IPv6
Both IPv4 and IPv6 are 32-bit addresses
119.x: IPv4 addresses are 32 bits and IPv6 addresses 128 bits, so IPv4 needs fewer bits than IPv6.

119.s: A MAC (Media Access Control) address is ________ bits long.
119.x: A MAC address is 48 bits long. 32 bits is IPv4 and 128 bits is IPv6.

119.s: A computer on internet is identified by
119.x: A computer on the internet is identified by its IP address.

119.s: Which of the following is not a valid IP address?
119.x: '192.23.350' is not a valid IPv4 address: it has only three octets, and 350 exceeds the maximum octet value of 255. The other three are valid dotted-decimal addresses.

119.s: What is the full form of IP?
119.x: IP stands for Internet Protocol, the addressing and routing protocol of the internet. Off-topic here; moved to networks and protocols.

119.s: Which of the following allows Internet access from cellular phones, portable and hand-held computers and other such portable gadgets?
119.x: 'Wireless web' means internet access from cellular phones, hand-held computers and other portable gadgets. Spaceweb, Astroweb and Cosmoweb are not standard terms.

119.s: Which of the following is a type of Internet connection that uses telephone lines?
119.x: DSL (Digital Subscriber Line) delivers internet over existing telephone lines. Cable uses coaxial TV lines, and fibre uses light in glass.

119.s: Slowest Internet connection service is –
119.x: Dial-up is the slowest connection (up to 56 Kbps). DSL, cable modem and leased lines are broadband and far faster.

119.s: The latest edition of Bluetooth (as of 2019) is
119.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
119.x:
Updated to the latest (Nov 2026): The latest Bluetooth Core specification is 7.0 (Nov 2026); 5.1 was latest in 2019. Source: https://www.bluetooth.com/
Bluetooth moved on to 5.2-5.4, 6.0 (2024, Channel Sounding), 6.1 (May 2025), 6.2 (Nov 2025) and 6.3 (May 2026) – now Bluetooth Core 7.0 (Nov 2026, High Data Throughput) (bluetooth.com blog 6 May 2026; audioxpress.com 4 Nov 2026).
When the paper was set (2019), Bluetooth 5.1 was the latest version (now Bluetooth Core 7.0, adopted Nov 2026).

119.s:
Consider the following:
1. Bluetooth device
2. Cordless phone
3. Microwave oven
4. Wi-Fi device
Which of the above can operate between 2.4 and 2.5 GHz range of radio frequency band?
119.x: All four work in the 2.4-2.5 GHz ISM band: Bluetooth, cordless phones, microwave ovens (2.45 GHz) and Wi-Fi, so the answer is 1, 2, 3 and 4.

119.s: What is the difference between Bluetooth and Wi-Fi devices?
o: Bluetooth uses 2.4 GHz radio frequency band, whereas Wi-Fi can use 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz frequency band.
Bluetooth is used for wireless local area networks (WLAN) only, whereas Wi-Fi is used for wireless wide area net-
When information is transmitted between two devices using Bluetooth technology, the devices have to be in the line
The statements (a) and (b) given above are correct in this context
119.x: Bluetooth uses the 2.4 GHz band, while Wi-Fi uses 2.4 or 5 GHz. (b) is wrong because Bluetooth is PAN, not WLAN; (c) is wrong because neither needs line of sight (UPSC 2011 answer a).

119.s: The first in the world, the Wi-Fi banking branch network was started by
o: State Bank of India and Windsor
119.x: Yes Bank, with Intel, launched the world's first Wi-Fi banking branch network.

119.s: Speed of internet is measured in
119.x: Internet speed is a data rate, measured in bits per second (Mbps, Gbps); GHz is frequency, GB is storage and dpi is print/scan resolution. Off-topic here; moved to networks.

119.s: Orbicom is the international network of
119.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
119.x: Orbicom is the international network of UNESCO Chairs in Communication, linking communication scholars and practitioners.

119.s: The 5th World Information Technology Forum was held during 17-18 April 2012 at
119.x: WITFOR 2012 (5th World IT Forum, IFIP) was held in New Delhi, 16–18 April 2012.

119.s: Who introduced 'www' to the world?
119.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test (2018 recruitment), held 28-05-2019 · Q38
119.x: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web at CERN in 1989.

119.s: IPv4 and IPv6 are addresses used to identify computers on the Internet.
119.src: APPSC Group-I Services Prelims (Screening Test) 2019, Notification No. 27/2018, Paper-II General Aptitude (GS/1G/101, Series A), Part B only (Science & Technology; Current Events), held 26-05-2019 · Q69
119.x: An IPv4 address has 32 bits and an IPv6 address has 128 bits, so IPv4 needs fewer bits.
o: Number of bits required for IPv4 address is more than number of bits required for IPv6 address
Number of bits required for IPv4 address is same as number of bits required for IPv6 address
Number of bits required for IPv4 address is less than number of bits required for IPv6 address
Number of bits required for IPv4 address is 64

119.s: What does PPTP stand for?
119.src: APPSC Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Group-III Services Screening Test 2019 (Notification No.13/2018), Part A General Studies, held 21-04-2019 · Q16
119.x: PPTP is the Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol, an older method for building VPNs.

119.s: Which of the following countries is represented by AU as its domain name?
119.src: APPSC Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Group-III Services Screening Test 2019 (Notification No.13/2018), Part A General Studies, held 21-04-2019 · Q38
119.x: .au is Australia's country-code top-level domain. Austria uses .at.

119.s: ARPANET, established in 1969, was developed under which organisation and is regarded as the forerunner of the Internet?
119.x: ARPANET was developed under the United States Department of Defense in 1969 and became the forerunner of the Internet.
xs: **ARPANET** (**1969**) was developed under the **US Department of Defense** — so option **(1)** is correct.
ARPANET is regarded as the **forerunner of the internet**.
**W3C** was founded by **Tim Berners-Lee** in **1994** — it sets web standards, it did not build ARPANET.
xa: The **WWW** was invented by **Tim Berners-Lee** in **1989** at **CERN**.
India's firsts: **ERNET** (**1986**, academic network) → **VSNL** public internet (**15 August 1995**) → **Satyam Infoway (Sify)**, first private ISP (**1998**).
⚠ Do not confuse the **internet** (ARPANET lineage, 1969) with the **WWW** (Berners-Lee, 1989).
119.tq: Link the historical network with its sponsoring organisation and legacy.

119.s: In which year did ERNET begin as India's academic network?
xs: **ERNET** began in **1986** as India's academic network.
119.x: ERNET began in 1986 as India's academic network.

119.s: On what date did VSNL launch public internet in India?
xs: **VSNL** launched public internet on **15 August 1995**.
119.x: VSNL launched public internet on 15 August 1995.

119.s: Which became India's first private ISP in 1998?
xs: **Satyam Infoway (Sify)** became the **first private ISP** in **1998**.
xa: The correct order is **ERNET → VSNL public internet → Satyam Infoway**
119.x: Satyam Infoway (Sify) became the first private ISP in 1998.

119.s: Cable internet uses which medium?
xs: 2 is wrong: **cable** internet uses **coaxial TV cable**; **light pulses** in optical fibre describe **fibre** internet.
119.x: 2 is wrong: cable internet uses coaxial TV cable; light pulses in optical fibre describe fibre internet.

119.s: In which year was NIXI established?
xs: **NIXI** (National Internet Exchange of India) was set up in **2003**.
119.x: NIXI (National Internet Exchange of India) was set up in 2003.

119.s: NIXI is a not-for-profit under which ministry?
xs: It is a **not-for-profit** under **MeitY**.

119.s: Which of the following represents the correct top-to-bottom order of the OSI model?
o: Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical
Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
Application, Session, Presentation, Network, Transport, Data Link, Physical
Presentation, Application, Session, Transport, Data Link, Network, Physical

xs: Top to bottom: **Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) is the bottom-to-top order; options (3) and (4) swap layers.
xa: Layer **7 Application**: **HTTP, FTP, SMTP, DNS**.
Layer **4 Transport**: **TCP, UDP**; layer **3 Network**: **IP**, router.
Layer **2 Data Link**: **MAC addresses**, switch, bridge, NIC; layer **1 Physical**: cables, hub, repeater.

A blanket ban for every person below 18 years
Graded limits based on age rather than a blanket ban
120.x: The proposed approach favours graded limits based on age instead of imposing a blanket ban on all persons below a specified age.

It is a separate law on **age-based social-media access**.
xa: **DPDP Act**: anyone **below 18** is a child; **verifiable parental consent** needed (**Sec 9**).
**Australia** = world's first nationwide **under-16** ban, effective **10 Dec 2025**.

120.s: Which e-mail field hides recipients from one another?
xs: **CC/BCC** send copies; only BCC hides recipients.
120.x: CC/BCC send copies; only BCC hides recipients.

120.s: A sender wants to send copies of an e-mail to several recipients without revealing the recipients' addresses to one another. Which field should be used?
120.x: BCC, or blind carbon copy, sends copies while hiding the recipients' addresses from one another.
xs: **BCC** sends copies while **hiding the recipients** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**CC** also sends copies but shows all recipients.
**SMTP** and **IMAP** are mail **protocols**, not address fields.
xa: **SMTP** sends mail; **POP3/IMAP** receive it.
An e-mail address = **username @ domain name**.

120.s: Which one of the following is NOT among the essentials of video conferencing?

Essentials: **camera, microphone, speaker/display, broadband link and conferencing software (codec)**.
xa: Multimedia components: **text, images/graphics, audio, video, animation**.
Telemedicine apps like **eSanjeevani** rely on such video links.
TV broadcasting methods: terrestrial, cable, satellite/**DTH**, IPTV/OTT.

15.s: The majority charge carriers in a p-type semiconductor are
15.x: In a p-type semiconductor, trivalent doping (e.g. boron) creates holes, which are the majority charge carriers; electrons are the minority carriers.

15.s:
In the context of digital technologies for entertainment, consider the following statements:

2. In Virtual Reality (VR), images generated from a computer are projected onto real-life objects or surroundings.

15.s:

15.s:
Monitoring of the crop field in conventional farming requires intensive labour, physical equipment, time, and effort. IoT provides an alternative to these traditional methods. An IoT device contains one or more sensors that collect data and provide accurate information via mobile applications or other means in real-time. Based on the passage presented and the following assertion and reason statements, which of the options is correct?
Assertion (A): Traditional methods of farming require intensive labour, physical equipment, time, and effort.
Reason (R): Internet of Things provides an alternative to traditional methods of farming.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
Both A and R are false
15.x: Both statements are true, but R does not explain A: farming is labour-intensive whatever IoT offers. R only names IoT as an alternative, not the cause of A.

15.s:

I. Location/identification of a person.
II. Sleep monitoring of a person.
III. Assisting the hearing impaired person.
Select the correct answer by using the codes given below.
15.x: Wearables track location (GPS) and sleep (motion and heart-rate sensors), and hearing aids assist the hearing impaired, so all three are correct (UPSC 2019 key d).

15.s:
With reference to RFID Technology, consider the following statements:
I. Passive RFID tags are powered by an internal circuit and utilize it to send response to the reader.
II. Semi-passive RFID tags comprise an internal circuit with power source but rely on radio waves received from the reader to transmit the response.
III. Active RFID tags acquire their power from the readers ' incoming radio waves.
IV. RFID Technology can scan a tag as long as it is within frequency range and it does not have any line-of-sight limitations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
15.x: I is wrong: passive tags have no battery and are powered by the reader's field. III is wrong: active tags carry their own battery. II (semi-passive: battery runs the chip, reply uses reader's waves) and IV (no line-of-sight needed) are correct.

15.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of defining technologies from Industry 1.0 to Industry 4.0?
o: Steam power — electricity — computers and electronics — cyber-physical systems
Electricity — steam power — cyber-physical systems — computers
Computers — electricity — steam power — artificial intelligence
Cyber-physical systems — steam power — electricity — computers
15.x: Industry 1.0 involved steam-powered mechanisation; Industry 2.0 electricity and mass production; Industry 3.0 computers and electronics; and Industry 4.0 cyber-physical systems.
xs: The sequence is **steam power → electricity → computers and electronics → cyber-physical systems** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Industry 1.0**: mechanisation, **steam power**, weaving loom; **2.0**: **electricity**, mass production, assembly line.
**Industry 3.0**: **automation, computers and electronics**; **4.0**: **cyber-physical systems**, IoT, AI, big data.
xa: **Industry 5.0** puts **human-machine collaboration** and people at the centre.
The term **Fourth Industrial Revolution** was coined by **Klaus Schwab** (WEF founder) in **2016**.
⚠ **3.0** = automation and computers; **4.0** = cyber-physical systems.
15.tq: Arrange the stages by their defining technological progression.

(When this paper was set, the answer was: Artemis III.) Source: https://www.theregister.com/2026/03/02/nasa_artemis_reshuffle/
NASA restructured Artemis in 2026 — now Artemis III is a 2027 low-Earth-orbit lander docking test and Artemis IV (2028) the first crewed south-pole landing (Rocket CA 2026 Part 2 p.93-94; Drishti IAS 15 Jun 2026)
Artemis III was announced as NASA's first crewed landing near the lunar south pole (then 2025); Pioneer 1-3 were 1958 probes. In 2026 NASA made Artemis III a 2027 Earth-orbit test, and the landing moved to Artemis IV (2028) (now Artemis IV).

121.s: At the International Space Summit in Paris on 10 September 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi advocated
o: national ownership of all orbital regions
competition over cooperation in outer space
121.x: The stated approach was 'cooperation over confrontation', with the aim of a safe, secure, peaceful and sustainable space domain anchored in international law.
xs: PM Modi called for "**cooperation over confrontation**" at the **International Space Summit, Paris** (**10 Sep 2026**) — option **(3)**.
He sought a **safe, secure, peaceful, sustainable** space domain anchored in **international law**.

Way forward includes **more SSA data-sharing**.
India signed the **Artemis Accords** in **2023**.
