121.s: Which of the following is identified as a major gap in the international governance of orbital activities?
o: Absence of international interest in space debris
Absence of any national licensing system for satellites
Absence of an international duty-of-care standard for orbits
Absence of all collision avoidance technology
121.x: There is no international duty-of-care standard for orbits. Differences in licensing conditions across countries can encourage operators to choose more permissive regimes.
xs: The gap is the **absence of an international duty-of-care standard for orbits** — option **(3)**.
Licensing conditions differ, so **operators pick permissive regimes** (**1 Apr 2026**).
xa: Treaties date from the **1960s-70s** and miss **cumulative harm** and **mega-constellations**.
India's **2026 re-entry rules** turn soft law into domestic rules.
CAMs exist — **18** in **2025** — so collision technology is not absent.
121.tq: Find the precise institutional gap and reject extreme claims such as absence of any licensing or technology.

33.s: Which maintains administrative and operational controls over the military?
o: Chiefs of the Army, Navy and Air Force

33.s: Which of the following is NOT a mission of DRDO?
o: Design, develop and lead to production state-of-the-art sensors, weapon systems, platforms and allied equipment for India's Defence Services
Provide technological solutions to optimise combat effectiveness and promote the well-being of troops
Develop infrastructure and committed quality manpower while building a strong indigenous technology base
Promote international collaboration in the development of defence technologies
33.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
33.x: DRDO's mission has three points: develop sensors, weapon systems and platforms; give technological solutions for combat effectiveness and troop well-being; build infrastructure, manpower and an indigenous technology base. International collaboration is not one of them.

33.s: DRDO was formed through the amalgamation of which of the following entities?
o: Technical Development Establishment (TDEs) of the Indian Army, Defence Science Organisation (DSO), and Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay (AEET)
Directorate of Technical Development & Production (DTDP), Defence Science Organisation (DSO), and Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay (AEET)
Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay (AEET), Technical Development Establishment (TDEs) of the Indian Army, and Directorate of Technical Development & Production (DTDP)
Technical Development Establishment (TDEs) of the Indian Army, Directorate of Technical Development & Production (DTDP), and Defence Science Organisation (DSO)
33.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
33.x: DRDO was formed in 1958 by amalgamating the Army's Technical Development Establishments, the Directorate of Technical Development & Production and the Defence Science Organisation. AEET Trombay (now BARC) was never part of it.

33.s: The motto of Defence Research and Development Organisation is :
33.x: DRDO's motto is "Balasya Mulam Vigyanam" – the source of strength is science. The other phrases are mottos of other services and bodies, not DRDO.

33.s: Which one of the following is not correct about the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)?

36.s: When a train is going away from a station, the frequency of the sound of train horn as heard by a person standing on the platform is?
o: Depends on goods train or passenger train
36.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
36.x: By the Doppler effect a source moving away is heard at a lower frequency than it emits, so the receding train's horn sounds lower.

36.x: The change in pitch of a sound when the source moves relative to the listener is the Doppler effect.

36.s: Stealth technology used in defence is for
o: Making an aircraft or a submarine invisible to the eye
Absorbing the electromagnetic waves produced by radars
Adding a nuclear capable missiles to aircrafts
36.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Education and Data
36.x: Stealth technology cuts a platform's radar signature by absorbing or deflecting radar waves (small radar cross-section, radar-absorbing material); it does not make objects invisible to the eye.

36.s: An artificial satellite can be tracked very precisely from the Earth by using :
36.x: A satellite's radial speed and position are tracked from the Doppler shift of its transmitter signal, so the Doppler effect is the answer.

36.s: The concept of expanding universe is based on –
36.x: The expanding universe rests on the Doppler (red) shift of light from galaxies moving away, which Hubble measured.

36.s: Which of the following statement is incorrect for Active Electronically Scanned Array Radar (AESA)?
o: It is not capable of tracking multiple targets
The radar features include wide band RF front end
It is solid-state active phased array fire control radar
It can be adapted for various types of fighter class of

36.s: What is the primary purpose of India's Surya VHF radar?
36.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
36.x: India's Surya VHF radar is meant to detect and track stealth aircraft; long VHF waves are hard for stealth shaping to defeat.

36.s: What is the name of the Weapon Locating Radar Developed in India?
36.x: Swathi (Swati) is India's weapon-locating radar (BEL/DRDO) that locates enemy guns, mortars and rockets. Rustom is a UAV, Dhanush a gun and Bhishm a tank.

36.s: RADAR is used for:
o: Detecting and fixing the position of objects
36.x: RADAR (Radio Detection And Ranging) detects objects and fixes their position, range and speed using reflected radio waves.

36.s: Researchers of which institute have created a 'metamaterial' that can protect soldiers from detection by enemy Radars?
36.x: IIT Kharagpur researchers developed a low-cost radar-absorbing metamaterial that can cloak soldiers and equipment from enemy radar.

36.s:
Which of the following statements with regard to stealth technology is/are correct?
1. Stealth objects have a very small radar cross-section and are coated with Radar Absorbing Material.
2. Stealth objects can be detected using specific frequencies.
3. Stealth objects are coated with metamaterials to increase the scattering of electromagnetic radiation. Select the answer using the code given below:
36.x: Stealth objects have a very small radar cross-section and radar-absorbing coatings (1 true) and can still be detected at specific frequencies (2 true); metamaterials are used to reduce scattering, not increase it (3 false).

36.s: 'Eye in the sky' is the name given to:

36.src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
36.x: Radar (Radio Detection And Ranging) detects and tracks objects, giving their range, direction and speed – not only distance or frequency.

36.s: AWACS is an:
o: air-based long-range radar surveillance and control system for air defence
instrument to measure wind speed in snow covered regions
air to air guided 2nd generation missile for air defence
36.x: AWACS (Airborne Warning and Control System) is a large airborne long-range radar surveillance and control system, e.g. India's IL-76-based Phalcon.

36.s: Andaman and Nicobar Command is

a regional command of the Indian Coast Guard.
an integrated theater command operating directly under the Chiefs of Staff Committee.
a joint command of the Indian Navy and the Indian Air Force.

The Andaman and Nicobar Command (2001) is India's first integrated tri-service theatre command, under the Chiefs of Staff Committee (now the CDS), not a single-service or Navy-IAF command.

the chain reaction in nuclear reactor is controlled
the chain reaction in nuclear reactor is not controlled
no chain reaction takes place in atomic bomb

49.x: I and III are correct: each fission releases more neutrons, and graphite slows fast neutrons so they cause further fission. II and IV are wrong: neutrons are not all absorbed at once and not every neutron causes a new fission.

the total mass of neutrons and protons
always more than the atomic weight
always less than its atomic number
49.x: Mass number is the number of protons plus neutrons (the nucleon count). It is a count, not the total mass, and it is not always more or less than other quantities.

49.s: The atoms, in which the number of protons is same but the number of neutrons is different, are known as –
49.x: Atoms with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons are isotopes. Isobars share the mass number, isotones the neutron number.

Number of protons is same but number of neutrons is

Atomic number and atoms mass both are same

49.x: The atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus (equal to the electrons only in a neutral atom).

49.x: Isotopes of an element differ in their number of neutrons. They have the same atomic number and the same chemical properties.

49.x: Electrons in the outermost (highest energy) shell are valence electrons. 'Valence' or 'orbital' protons do not exist.

49.x: The number of protons equals the atomic number, N. W is the mass number and W - N gives the neutrons.

49.x: The atomic mass (mass number) of an element is the sum of its protons and neutrons; electrons add almost nothing.

o: same atomic number and same electronic configuration.
different atomic number and same electronic configuration.
different atomic number and different number of valence electrons.
same number of electrons and neutrons.
49.x: Atoms of different elements have different atomic numbers and so different electronic configurations and numbers of valence electrons.

o: sum of number of protons and number of electrons
sum of number of protons and number of neutrons
49.x: Mass number is always the sum of protons and neutrons.

o: The atomic weight of an element is the sum total of the number of protons and neutrons present in the atom of an element.
Unlike mass number, the atomic weight of an element can be a fraction.
The atomic weight of an element is a whole number.
The atomic weight of all the atoms in an element is the same.
49.x: Atomic weight is the average mass of an element's isotopes, so it can be a fraction (chlorine 35.5), whereas the mass number is always a whole number.

49.s: The atoms of the elements having same difference between mass number and atomic number are called …………… .
49.x: Mass number minus atomic number gives the neutrons; atoms with the same neutron number are isotones.

different mass numbers but same atomic numbers.
49.x: Isobars have the same mass number but different atomic numbers (3H and 3He).

49.x: Most alpha particles passed through the gold foil but a few bounced back, showing a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus at the centre of the atom (Rutherford).

49.s: The most of the mass of the atom can be found in
49.x: Protons and neutrons in the nucleus carry almost all the atom's mass; electrons are about 1/1837 of a proton.

49.x: 7 electrons in the M-shell means 2 + 8 + 7 = 17 electrons, so 17 protons. Mass number = 17 + 18 = 35.

49.s: The force of attraction between an electron revolving around the nucleus and the nucleus is an … force.
49.x: The negatively charged electron and the positively charged nucleus attract by the electric (electrostatic) force; gravity is negligible at that scale.

o: a charge of + 1 and mass of 1 unit.
no charge and a mass of 1 unit.
a charge of - 1 and a mass of 1 unit.
49.x: A neutron has no charge and a mass of about 1 atomic mass unit (slightly more than a proton).

49.s: Charge on proton is equal to the charge on ………… .
49.x: A positron carries +1 charge, the same as a proton. The electron is negative, the neutron neutral and the alpha particle +2.

49.x: Isotopes have the same number of protons and electrons, so their chemical properties must be the same; only physical properties such as mass differ.

49.s: An atom of carbon has 6 protons. Its mass number is 12. How many neutrons are present in an atom of carbon?
49.x: Neutrons = mass number - protons = 12 - 6 = 6.

49.x: A neutral atom has as many protons as electrons (18), so the mass number = 18 + 20 = 38.

o: Neutron mass is almost equal to proton mass
Neutrons are located inside the atomic nuclei
Neutrons revolve around the atomic nuclei
49.x: Neutrons sit inside the nucleus; they do not revolve around it (electrons do). Their mass is almost equal to a proton's and they have zero charge.

49.s: The most common method Uranium enrichment is?

49.x: Uranium (as UF6 gas) is enriched mostly in gas centrifuges, which separate U-235 from the slightly heavier U-238. Distillation, ionisation and calcification are not used.

49.s: The fuel used in the nuclear reactors is
49.x: Uranium (U-235) is the fuel of nuclear reactors. Thorium is only fertile and must first be bred into U-233; radium is not a reactor fuel and 'nuclear water' does not exist.

49.s: Material most commonly used in nuclear power plants is
49.x: Uranium-235 is the fissile fuel most commonly used in nuclear power plants. Plutonium is used in fewer reactors, thorium is only fertile and radium is not a fuel.

49.s: Which of the following radio active elements is used to make nuclear fission reaction?
49.x: Uranium (its fissile isotope U-235) is the element split in nuclear fission reactors and bombs. Thorium is fertile and must first become U-233; barium is a fission product, not a fuel.

49.s: Which nuclear fuel is produced when thorium is bombarded with neutrons?
49.x: Th-232 is fertile; when it absorbs a neutron it turns into fissile Uranium-233. Hard water, hydrogen sulphide and heavy water are not nuclear fuels.

49.s: What nuclear fuel does bombarding Thorium with neutrons produce?
49.x: Bombarding Thorium-232 with neutrons converts it into fissile Uranium-233, the basis of India's thorium fuel cycle. The other options are not nuclear fuels.

49.s: Which one of the following elements is essential for the construction of nuclear reactors?
49.x: Zirconium alloys clad the fuel rods because they resist corrosion and absorb very few neutrons. Cobalt, nickel and tungsten are not essential reactor materials.

49.s: Which Uranium isotope is used in nuclear power plants to produce electricity?
49.x: U-235 is the fissile isotope burnt in nuclear power plants; natural uranium has only about 0.7% of it. U-233 is bred from thorium, while U-234 and U-239 are not used as fuel.

49.s: Identify the mineral not associated with atomic power –
49.x: Chromium has no role in atomic power. Monazite is the ore of thorium, thorium is a fertile fuel and beryllium (oxide) is a moderator and a prescribed atomic substance.

49.s: Which fuel is used by Nuclear reactors in India ?
49.x: Indian PHWRs burn natural uranium, which is about 99.3% U-238 with 0.7% U-235, so U-238 is the only printed option that fits. U-270 and U-500 do not exist and gasohol is a motor fuel.

49.s: Which of the following element is not included as a nuclear fuel–
49.x: Cadmium is not a fuel: it absorbs neutrons and is used in control rods. Thorium, plutonium and uranium are nuclear fuels (thorium after breeding).

49.s: Enriched Uranium is –
o: Uranium sticks laid in particular shell
Natural uranium in which radioactive U235 isotope is
mixture of natural uranium and thorium
49.x: Enriched uranium is natural uranium in which the share of the U-235 isotope has been raised by isotope separation. It is not a thorium mixture or coated sticks.

49.s: Which is not used as Atomic fuel?
49.x: Lead is not a nuclear fuel. Uranium and plutonium are fissile, and thorium is fertile and can be bred into U-233.

49.s: Which of the following is not a fuel element?
49.x: Helium is an inert gas and not a nuclear fuel element. Uranium and thorium are nuclear fuels; radium is radioactive but the clear odd one out is helium.

49.s: Which one of the following can not be used as a nuclear fuel?
49.x: Calcium is not a nuclear fuel. Uranium-235 and plutonium-239 are fissile, and thorium is bred into U-233.

49.s: Which metal can be used for producing electricity?
49.x: Uranium is the metal used to produce electricity, as nuclear fuel in power plants. Iron, copper and aluminium only carry or build things.

49.s: Which of the following uranium isotope is used in nuclear reactor for generation of electricity?
49.x: U-235 is the fissile uranium isotope used to generate electricity. U-233 is bred from thorium, while U-334 does not exist and U-239 is not a fuel.

49.s: Which one of the following is a good nuclear fuel?
49.x: Plutonium-239 is fissile, so it is a good nuclear fuel. U-238 is only fertile (it must first become Pu-239), neptunium is not a fuel and 'thorium-236' is not the fertile Th-232. (The old app notes said the APPSC 2007 key was U-238; that key was not verified and is factually wrong.)

49.s: The main element in the Ore Pitchblende is
49.x: Pitchblende (uraninite, UO2/U3O8) is the chief ore of uranium. Monazite, not pitchblende, is the thorium ore.

49.s: Which one of the following mineral is used as a fuel in nuclear power stations?
49.x: Pitchblende is the main uranium ore, and uranium is the fuel of nuclear power stations. Bauxite (aluminium), quartz and feldspar are not nuclear fuels.

49.s: Which one of the following is not radioactive ?
49.x: Zirconium (Z = 40) is not radioactive. Astatine and francium are heavy radioactive elements and tritium is a radioactive isotope of hydrogen.

49.s: Radioactive substance emits –
49.x: An unstable nucleus can emit alpha, beta and gamma radiation, so all three.

49.s: Emission of β-particle from an atom
o: increases the number of protons in the atom.
increases the number of neutrons in the atom.
decreases the number of proton in the atom.
does not change the number of neutrons and protons in an atom.
49.x: In beta-minus emission a neutron changes into a proton and an electron, which is emitted, so the number of protons rises by one.

49.s: What is end product of nuclear fission of Uranium?
49.x:
Printed key / books: Lead (end of the uranium decay series). Strictly, nuclear fission of uranium yields barium, krypton and other fission fragments, not lead (PMF S&T Part 4 p.24).
Lead is the stable end product of uranium's radioactive decay series (U-238 to Pb-206), which is the reading the key takes. Fission itself splits uranium into lighter nuclei such as barium and krypton; radium and thorium are intermediate decay products and plutonium is bred from U-238.

49.s: Which of the following is not a radioactive series?
49.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
49.x: There is no 'carbon series'. Thorium, actinium and uranium are natural radioactive decay series, and neptunium is an artificial series.

49.s: The alpha particle carries two positive charges. Its mass is very nearly equal to that of:
o: Sum of masses of two positrons and two neutrons
Two positrons, as each positron carries a single positive charge
49.x: An alpha particle is a helium nucleus (2 protons + 2 neutrons), so its mass is almost that of a helium atom; electrons weigh very little. Two protons alone would be only half that mass.

49.s: Which of the following particles has zero charge?
49.x: The neutrino has zero charge (and almost no mass). The positron is +1, the electron -1 and the alpha particle +2.

49.s: Which of the following is not a sub-atomic particle?
49.x: The basic sub-atomic particles are the neutron, proton and electron. A deuteron is the nucleus of deuterium (a proton plus a neutron), not a basic sub-atomic particle.

49.s: Which of the following carries a negative charge?
49.x: Beta particles are fast electrons and carry a negative charge. Alpha particles are positive, while X-rays and gamma rays are uncharged radiation.

49.s: The half-life of a radioactive substance is 10 days; it means there will be :
o: complete decay of substance in 20 days
complete decay of substance in 40 days
decay of 3/4 part of substance in 20 days
decay of 1/4 part of substance in 5 days
49.x: After one half-life (10 days) half remains, after two (20 days) a quarter remains, so 3/4 has decayed in 20 days. A substance never decays completely.

49.s: The half-life of a radioactive element is 5 years then the fraction of the radioactive substance that remains after 20 years is –
49.x: 20 years is 4 half-lives of 5 years, so (1/2)^4 = 1/16 of the substance remains.

49.s: The alpha particle carries two positive charges. Its mass is very nearly equal to that of –
o: Nucleus of an atom of helium
Sum of masses of two positrons and two neutrons
Two positrons, as each positron carries a single
49.x: An alpha particle is two protons and two neutrons, i.e. the nucleus of a helium atom, so its mass equals that of a helium nucleus.

49.s:
With reference to the radioactivity, which of the following statements is/are correct ?

2. Hydrogen bomb is prepared on the principle of nuclear fission.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
Codes :
49.x: Statement 1 is correct: radioactivity is a nuclear property. Statement 2 is wrong: the hydrogen bomb works on fusion, not fission.

49.s: Which particle is free of charge?
49.x: The neutron carries no charge. The alpha particle (+2) and proton (+1) are positive, the electron negative.

49.s: Radioactivity is measured by –
49.x: Radioactivity is detected and measured with a Geiger (Geiger-Muller) counter. A hydrometer measures density, a seismometer earthquakes and an ammeter current.

49.s: Which among the following is a positively charged particle emitted by a radioactive element?
o: More than one of the above
49.x: Alpha rays are positively charged helium nuclei emitted by radioactive elements. Beta rays and cathode rays are electrons (negative).

49.s: Which of the following is not a radio active element?
49.x: Zirconium (Z = 40) is not radioactive, whereas astatine and francium are heavy radioactive elements and tritium is a radioactive hydrogen isotope.

49.s: Beta rays emitted by a radioactive material are
o: the electrons orbiting around the nucleus.
49.x: Beta rays are electrons (or positrons) emitted from the nucleus, so they are charged particles. They are not orbital electrons, not neutral and not electromagnetic radiation (that is gamma).

49.s: Half-life of a radioactive element is 10 days. What does it mean?
o: Element will be completely disintigrate in 20 days.
Element will be completely disintigrate in 40 days.
3/4th part of element will disintigrate in 20 days.
1/4th part of element will distintigarate in 5 days.
49.x: After 10 days half remains and after 20 days a quarter, so 3/4 has disintegrated in 20 days. The element never fully disintegrates.

49.s: In an observation, α-particles, β-particles and γ-rays have same energies. Their penetrating power in a given medium in increasing order will be
49.x: Alpha is stopped by paper, beta by a few mm of aluminium and gamma only by lead or concrete, so penetrating power rises in the order alpha, beta, gamma.

49.s: In May, 2017, the Central Cabinet decided to launch 10 indigenous nuclear reactors of the following type as part of a mega project?
49.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
49.x: In May 2017 the Union Cabinet approved 10 indigenous 700 MWe Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors to be built in fleet mode. PWRs and FBRs were not part of that decision; Magnox is a British design.

49.s: A moderator is used in nuclear reactors in order to
o: slow down the speed of neutrons
49.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
49.x: A moderator slows fast neutrons to thermal speed so that U-235 can capture them and fission. It does not add, absorb or accelerate neutrons; absorbing is the job of control rods.

49.s: ___ is used as a moderator in nuclear reactors.
49.x: Heavy water (D2O) is a moderator: it slows neutrons while absorbing very few of them. Hydrogen peroxide, dihydrogen and CFCs are not moderators.

49.s: Which one of the following is used as moderator in a nuclear reactor ?
49.x:
Printed key / most books: (b) Heavy water. Strictly, (d) ordinary water is also a moderator, in light-water reactors (PMF S&T Part 4 p.38).
Heavy water slows neutrons without absorbing many, so it is the classic moderator. Ordinary (light) water is a moderator too, in PWRs and BWRs, which is why the book lists '(b) & (d)'. Thorium and radium are not moderators.

49.s: Which one of the following is used as a moderator in the nuclear reactor?
49.x:
Printed key / most books: (b) Graphite. Strictly, (d) ordinary water is also a moderator, in light-water reactors (PMF S&T Part 4 p.38).
Graphite slows neutrons and is a standard moderator. Ordinary water is also a moderator in light-water reactors, which is why the book prints '(b) & (d)'. Thorium and radium are not moderators.

49.s: Graphite is used in the nuclear reactor as –
49.x: Graphite slows fast neutrons, so it serves as a moderator; it is not the fuel. Its lubricant use is outside reactors.

49.s: The moderator used in nuclear reactor is :
49.x: Heavy water, D2O (deuterium oxide), is the moderator. U2O, Na2O and Cl2O are not moderators.

The printed list is garbled: 'e' (slows neutrons) describes a moderator, not a control rod, which absorbs neutrons, and 'd' repeats 'splitting'.

49.s: What is the function of moderator in a nuclear reactor?
49.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
49.x: A moderator slows down neutrons so that they can cause further fission. Absorbing heat is the coolant's job; control rods regulate the rate.

49.s: What happens if the control rods are not used in a nuclear reactor?
o: Chain process would go out of bounds
The reactor will be slow to act
The reactor will continue to work as it is
49.x: Control rods absorb surplus neutrons; without them the chain reaction would go out of bounds rather than stop or slow down.

49.s: The substance used as moderator and coolant both, in nuclear reactors is :
49.x:
Printed key / most books: (a) Ordinary water. Strictly, (b) heavy water is also both moderator and coolant, in PHWRs (PMF S&T Part 4 p.43-44).
Ordinary (light) water is both the moderator and the coolant in PWRs and BWRs. Heavy water does both jobs in PHWRs, which is why the book prints '(a) & (b)'. Liquid ammonia and liquid hydrogen are neither.

49.s: Heavy water is a type of –
49.x: Heavy water is chiefly a moderator that slows neutrons; in PHWRs it also acts as coolant. It is not an ore or a fuel.

49.s: Gas cooled reactor uses following materials as moderator and coolant.
49.x: Gas-cooled reactors such as Magnox use graphite as the moderator and carbon dioxide gas as the coolant.

49.s: Heavy water is used as a moderator in a nuclear reactor. The function of the moderator is
o: to control the energy released in the reactor.
to absorb neutrons and stop the chain reaction.
to slow down the neutrons to thermal energy.
49.x: A moderator slows fast neutrons down to thermal energy so that U-235 can fission. Absorbing neutrons and controlling the rate is the job of control rods.

49.s: If control rods are not used in the nuclear reactor, then
o: chain reaction will go out of control.
there will be impact on nuclear reactor.
49.x: Control rods absorb neutrons and regulate the rate; without them the chain reaction goes out of control. It would not stop or slow down.

49.s: The function of heavy water in a nuclear reactor is to?
o: Slow down the speed of neutrons.
49.x: Heavy water acts mainly as a moderator: it slows fast neutrons to thermal speed while absorbing very few. It does not speed neutrons up or stop the reaction. (In PHWRs it also cools, but 'cool down the reactor' is not the key.)

49.s: The function of heavy water in a nuclear reactor is to
o: Slow down the speed of neutrons
49.x: Heavy water is used as a moderator to slow down the neutrons produced in fission so that the chain reaction can be sustained. It does not increase their speed or stop the reaction.

49.x: A breeder reactor produces more fissionable material than it burns, as fast neutrons convert fertile U-238 into Pu-239.

49.x: The Kalpakkam fast breeders run on plutonium: FBTR on plutonium-uranium mixed carbide, PFBR on MOX (Pu-239 + U-238). Uranium-238 is only the fertile blanket; thorium is a Stage III fuel.

xa: APTRANSCO has **13** ongoing **400 kV** works worth **₹3,698 crore**.
AP opened **50,000 acres** barren land for solar leases.
67.tq: Identify the agency by its functional responsibility.

67.s: The agency primarily associated with energy conservation in Andhra Pradesh is:
67.x: APSECM is the agency associated with energy conservation.
xs: **APSECM** is AP's energy-conservation agency — option **(1)**.
**APGENCO** = generation; **NREDCAP** = RE nodal agency; **APTRANSCO** = transmission.
xa: APGENCO also runs the **Srisailam Right Bank** hydel plant.
APGENCO thermal: **4,210 MW**.
67.tq: Direct agency-role recall with closely related energy bodies as distractors.

67.s: Andhra Pradesh opened 50,000 acres of barren land for solar leases primarily to:
o: replace all wind projects with nuclear projects
restrict private participation in solar generation
67.x: The barren land was opened for solar leases to avoid diversion of farmland for renewable-energy projects.
xs: AP opened **50,000 acres** of barren land for solar leases to **avoid farmland diversion** (Apr **2026**) — option **(1)**.
It is a response to **food-vs-fuel** land conflicts.
xa: **NREDCAP** handles land, clearances and single window for RE.
SAEL **600 MW** Kadapa used **2,400 acres**.
PM-KUSUM in AP targets **2.93 lakh** farm pumps.
67.tq: Identify the policy rationale behind land-use decisions.

67.s: According to the Andhra Pradesh renewable-energy mix of 10,639.75 MW, which one of the following correctly represents the approximate shares of solar and wind energy, respectively?
67.x: Solar energy accounts for approximately 53% and wind energy for approximately 41% of Andhra Pradesh’s renewable-energy mix of 10,639.75 MW.
xs: AP RE mix: **solar ~53%** and **wind ~41%** of **10,639.75 MW** — option **(2)**.
Option (4) reverses them.
xa: AP's solar is ~**5.6 GW** vs India's **162.15 GW** (Jun **2026**) — a small share.
Major **2025** wind partnership in **Anantapur** (**APPSC 2025**).
Tata **800 MW** hybrid: **400 MW** wind at **Kanekallu**.
67.tq: Split the options by comparing the order and approximate shares of the two energy sources.

67.s: After the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, which factor contributed to increased coal-related difficulty in power generation?
o: Abolition of transmission charges for coal-based power
Excess availability of high-quality coal within Andhra Pradesh
Replacement of all thermal plants by nuclear plants
Loss of coal mines, resulting in long-distance coal haulage and poor coal quality
67.x: Andhra Pradesh lost its coal mines after bifurcation, causing long coal haulage and exposure to poor coal quality.
xs: AP **lost its coal mines** after bifurcation, leading to **long coal haulage** and **poor coal quality** — option **(4)**.
Transmission charges were not abolished — **CTU charges** are ~**₹3.4 lakh/MW/month**.
xa: APGENCO thermal: **4,210 MW** (NTTPS + RTPP).
**Krishnapatnam** SDSTPS (**APPDCL**): **2,400 MW**.
67.tq: Apply the stated cause-and-effect chain to an energy-sector situation.

67.s: With reference to PM-KUSUM in Andhra Pradesh, which one of the following figures represents the target number of farm pumps?
67.x: PM-KUSUM in Andhra Pradesh targets 2.93 lakh farm pumps. The figure of 32,000 refers to solar pumps installed earlier.
xs: PM-KUSUM in AP targets **2.93 lakh** farm pumps — option **(2)**.
**32,000** = solar pumps installed earlier; ~**5.6 GW** is AP's solar capacity.
xa: **123 MW** rooftop was installed earlier (**2024-25/2025-26**).
AP's 50,000-acre barren-land policy eases **food-vs-fuel** conflicts.
67.tq: Separate the target figure from the already-installed solar-pump figure before choosing the numerical option.

67.s: Which of the following correctly represents the national pumped-storage position?
o: 58 GW on-stream, 209 GW off-stream and approximately 7 GW installed
7 GW on-stream, 58 GW off-stream and 209 GW installed
267 GW on-stream, 7 GW off-stream and 58 GW installed
209 GW on-stream, 58 GW off-stream and 267 GW installed
67.x: The national potential includes about 58 GW on-stream and 209 GW off-stream components, while installed capacity is approximately 7 GW.
xs: PSP: **58 GW on-stream**, **209 GW off-stream**, ~**7 GW installed** — option **(1)**.
The other options jumble these numbers; total potential is **~267 GW**.
xa: ⚠ Off-stream potential (**209 GW**) far exceeds on-stream (**58 GW**).
67.tq: Separate potential categories from the installed-capacity figure.
