71.x:
APPSC key: (A) both true, R explains A. Strictly: 'second largest threat' is said of invasive species as a group; Parthenium is only one of them.
Invasive alien species are the second-biggest cause of biodiversity loss after habitat destruction, and Parthenium (congress grass) is one of India's worst invasive weeds; so A and R are true and R explains A.

71.s:
Which of the following is/are the reasons of extinction of species?
i. Loss of habitat
ii. Loss of genetic variation
iii. Loss of appetite
71.x: Loss of habitat and loss of genetic variation (which lowers a species' ability to adapt) both drive extinction. 'Loss of appetite' is not an ecological cause.

71.s:
Which of the following can be threats to the biodiversity of a region?
1. Global Warming
2. Fragmentation of habitat
3. Invasion of alien species
4. Promotion of Vegetarianism
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
Codes :
71.x: Global warming, habitat fragmentation and invasion of alien species threaten biodiversity, but promotion of vegetarianism does not, so the answer is 1, 2 and 3.

71.s: Vultures which used to be very common in Indian countryside some years ago are rarely seen now a days. This is attributed to
o: the destruction of their nesting site by new invasive species.
a drug used by cattle owners for treating their diseased cattle.
scarcity of food available to them.
a widespread, persistent and fatal disease among them.
71.x: Vultures declined because of diclofenac, a veterinary drug given to cattle that causes kidney failure in vultures feeding on carcasses (veterinary use banned in 2006). It was not disease, food scarcity or invasive species.

71.s:
While India’s Human population is growing at an astounding pace, the bird population is shrinking fastly mainly because
I. there has been an abnormal increase in the number of hunters.
II. bio-pesticides and organic manure are being used on an large scale.
III. there has been a large scale reduction in the habitats of birds.
IV. there has been a large scale use of pesticides, chemical fertilisers and mosquito repellents.
Select your answer correctly using the codes given below.
71.x: Birds are declining mainly through habitat reduction (III) and heavy use of pesticides, chemical fertilisers and mosquito repellents (IV). Bio-pesticides and organic manure are harmless, and hunting is not the main cause.

71.s: Which one of the following is not a major cause of Wildlife Extinction?
o: To make fire in the forest.
71.x: Habitat loss, forest fires and illegal wildlife trade kill wildlife directly. Population growth is treated as the exception because it acts only indirectly, through these other causes.

71.s:
Which of the following can be threats to the biodiversity of a region?
I. Global warming
II. Fragmentation of habitat.
III. Invasion of alien species.
IV. Promotion of vegetarianism.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
71.x: Global warming, habitat fragmentation and invasion of alien species threaten biodiversity, but promotion of vegetarianism does not, so I, II and III is correct.

71.s: Out of the birds given below, which bird is the most affected by cell tower radiation in India?
71.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
71.x: The house sparrow is the bird most often linked to cell-tower radiation in India, alongside loss of nesting sites. The link is popular rather than firmly proven, and the species is still Least Concern.

71.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Habitat loss and fragmentation are the most important cause driving animals and plants to extinction.
2. Human activities lead to over-exploitation of natural resources.
3. When a species becomes extinct, the plant and animal species associated with it do not become extinct.
Choose the correct answer using the following options:
71.x: Habitat loss and fragmentation are the most important causes of extinction (1), and humans over-exploit natural resources (2). Statement 3 is false: through co-extinction, obligately associated species die out too.

71.s: Which one of the following is not responsible for the extinction of a species?
71.x: A broad niche makes a species adaptable, so it does not cause extinction. Large body size, a narrow specialised niche and lack of genetic variability all raise extinction risk.

71.s: The disappearance of all members of a species is called
71.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
71.x: Extinction is the disappearance of every member of a species, i.e. the death of its last individual. Loss from one area only is extirpation.

71.s: The term "sixth mass extinction/sixth extinction" is often mentioned in the news in the context of the discussion of
o: Widespread monoculture practices in agriculture and large-scale commercial farming with indiscriminate use of
Fears of a possible collision of a meteorite with the Earth in the near future in the manner it happened 65 million
Large-scale cultivation of genetically modified crops in many parts of the world and promoting their cultivation in
Mankind's over-exploitation/misuse of natural resources, fragmentation/loss, natural habitats, destruction of ecosys-
71.x: The 'sixth mass extinction' is the present human-driven wave of extinctions caused by over-exploitation of resources, loss and fragmentation of habitats, ecosystem destruction, pollution and climate change. It is not about GM crops, monoculture or a meteorite.

71.s: The term ‘Sixth mass extinction/sixth extinction’ is often mentioned in the news in the context of the discussion of
o: Widespread monoculture practices in agriculture and
Fears of a possible collision of a meteorite with the
Large scale cultivation of genetically modified crops
71.x: The 'sixth extinction' refers to mankind's over-exploitation and misuse of natural resources, fragmentation and loss of habitats, destruction of ecosystems, pollution and climate change. Humans are the primary cause.

71.s: The theory that dinosaurs were driven to extinction by the aftermath of a large asteroid impact on Earth was given by .............. .
71.x: Physicist Luis Alvarez, with his son Walter Alvarez (1980), proposed that an asteroid impact about 66 million years ago caused the extinction of the dinosaurs.

71.s: A tree species in Mauritius failed to reproduce because of the extinction of a fruit eating bird. Which one of the following was that bird?
71.x: The dodo of Mauritius is the classic case of co-extinction. The tree whose fruit it ate and whose seeds it dispersed failed to reproduce after the bird went extinct.

71.s: A tree species in Mauritius failed to reproduce because of the extinction of a fruit eating bird. Which one of the following was that bird?
71.x: The dodo of Mauritius is the classic case of co-extinction. The tree whose fruit it ate and whose seeds it dispersed failed to reproduce after the bird went extinct.

71.s: Which of the following is NOT an extinct species?
71.x: The red panda is endangered but alive (Eastern Himalaya). The dodo, the West African black rhino (2011) and the Chinese river dolphin (baiji, functionally extinct 2006) are extinct.

71.s: The complete disappearance of a species from a specific area but not from the entire planet is
71.x: Extirpation is the disappearance of a species from one area while it survives elsewhere, e.g. tigers extirpated from Kawal TR. Extinction is global loss, and endemism means being confined to one region.

71.s: A species is considered to be extinct if it has not been seen in its natural habitat for
71.x:
Most books and keys: 50 years. Strictly: the IUCN sets no fixed period – a species is Extinct when there is no reasonable doubt that the last individual has died, after exhaustive surveys; the 50-year rule was only a 1980s suggestion (NextGen Environment APPSC 06 p.12; theconversation.com).
The traditional rule in books was that a species not seen in the wild for 50 years is considered extinct, so 50 years is keyed. The IUCN itself uses the 'no reasonable doubt after exhaustive surveys' test.

71.s: CR in IUCN red list refers to
71.x: CR stands for Critically Endangered, an extremely high risk of extinction in the wild, more severe than EN. There is no 'critically extinct' category, and EW is Extinct in the Wild.

71.s: The species which are in danger of extinction are known as?
71.x: Species in danger of extinction, whose numbers have fallen to a critical level, are called endangered. Vulnerable species face a high but lesser risk, and extinct species are already gone.

Reason (R): Nitric oxide (NO) and nitrogen dioxide (NO2) are formed during high-temperature combustion reactions, which later react with water to form nitric acid (HNO3), contributing to acid rain.
Which of the following is correct with respect to the above statements?
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
85.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
85.x: Rain with pH below 5.6 is acid rain; NOx from high-temperature combustion forms nitric acid in the air, which is one cause of acid rain, so R explains A.

85.s: Carbon monoxide breathing is harmful for human being because
o: It competes with oxygen in the blood
85.src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
85.x: CO binds haemoglobin 200-250 times more readily than oxygen, forming carboxyhaemoglobin, so it competes with and displaces oxygen in the blood.

85.s: Which of the following gases is primarily responsible for air pollution ?
85.x: Carbon monoxide is a major air pollutant; oxygen, nitrogen and helium are normal or inert components of air.

85.s: The odorless, poisonous gas that arises in the smoke from burning of coal is
85.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
85.x: Carbon monoxide is the colourless, odourless poisonous gas from incomplete burning of coal; CO2 is not poisonous at normal levels and H2S smells of rotten eggs.

85.s:
What is true about gaseous pollutants?
I. In humans, Sulphur Dioxide pollution causes headache, vomiting, irritation of eye and respiratory passages.
II. Nitrogen oxides are one source of photochemical smog, acid deposition and ozone depletion.
III. Mild Carbon Mono Oxide poisoning causes lung disorders like necrosis and emphysema.
IV. In humans Peroxyacetyl Nitrate (PAN) and Ozone cause irritation of eyes, coughing, headache, dry throat, respiratory problems and haemorrhage.
o: Only I and II are true
Only I and IV are true
Only I, III, and IV are true
85.x: I (SO2 irritates eyes and airways) and II (NOx drive photochemical smog, acid deposition and ozone depletion) are true; III is false because CO poisoning acts on blood oxygen, not lung necrosis/emphysema; IV overstates (PAN/ozone irritate eyes and airways, not haemorrhage). So only I and II.

85.s: The most injurious components of automobile exhaust for environment are
85.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Sanitation Secreta
85.x:
leaded petrol has been phased out in India (lead-free petrol) — now CO, NOx, hydrocarbons and PM are the main exhaust pollutants (PMF Environment Part 03 p.125).
Carbon monoxide (incomplete combustion) and lead (from leaded petrol) were the most injurious exhaust components; CO2 is not toxic, and EDC/EDB were only lead scavengers added to petrol (now: lead-free petrol, so lead is no longer emitted).

85.s: Pollutant produced by vehicles that reduces the Oxygen carrying capacity of Blood
85.x: Carbon monoxide from vehicle exhaust binds haemoglobin (carboxyhaemoglobin) and reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood; NOx and SO2 are irritants.

85.s: Excessive release of the pollutant carbon monoxide (CO) into the air may produce a condition in which oxygen supply in the human body decreases. What causes this condition?
o: When inhaled into the human body, CO is converted into CO₂
The inhaled CO has much higher affinity for haemoglobin as compared to oxygen
The inhaled CO destroys the chemical structure of haemoglobin
The inhaled CO adversely affects the respiratory centre in the brain
85.x: Inhaled CO has much higher affinity (200-250 times) for haemoglobin than oxygen, forming carboxyhaemoglobin and cutting oxygen supply; it is not converted to CO2 and does not destroy haemoglobin's structure.

85.s: Cigarette smoke contains –
85.x:
Most keys: CO and benzene. Strictly nicotine is also present in cigarette smoke, so 'CO and nicotine' is also true (PMF Environment Part 03 p.124).
Cigarette smoke contains carbon monoxide and benzene (also nicotine, HCN, arsenic, formaldehyde); 'dioxycine' is not a smoke component.

85.s: Combustion of petrol in automobiles pollutes the air by producing the following metal.
85.x:
leaded petrol (TEL) was phased out in India — now petrol is lead-free and vehicles no longer emit lead (PMF Environment Part 03 p.125).
Petrol combustion released lead from the anti-knock additive tetraethyl lead; mercury and cadmium are not petrol emissions and CO2 is not a metal (now lead-free petrol is used).

85.s: Pollutant emission gas in vehicle exhaust is mainly –
85.x: Carbon monoxide is the main pollutant gas in vehicle exhaust (incomplete combustion); CO2 is the normal combustion product and marsh gas is methane.

85.s: Which one of the following air pollutants can affect bloodstream leading to death?
85.x: Carbon monoxide enters the bloodstream as carboxyhaemoglobin and can cause death; asbestos dust affects lungs and cadmium the kidneys and bones.

85.s: Which of the following air pollutants get dissolved in the haemoglobin of the blood more rapidly than oxygen?
85.x: Carbon monoxide combines with haemoglobin more readily than oxygen (200-250 times affinity); PAN, CO2 and ozone do not.

85.s: 'Fly Ash', is an pollutant which generate by-
85.x: Fly ash is generated by burning coal (pulverised coal in thermal power plants) and is captured by electrostatic precipitators.

85.s: Which of the following air pollutants is most dangerous?
85.x: Carbon monoxide is usually rated the most dangerous air pollutant because it starves the body of oxygen and can kill; ozone and H2S are irritants and CO2 is not toxic at normal levels.

85.s: Which one of the following forms an irreversible complex with a hemoglobin of the blood?
o: A mixture of Carbon Dioxide and Helium
85.x:
Books and keys: CO forms an 'irreversible' complex. Strictly carboxyhaemoglobin is reversible but about 200-250 times more stable than oxyhaemoglobin, so CO is released only slowly (general knowledge, not checked).
CO forms carboxyhaemoglobin, a very stable complex that blocks oxygen transport, so CO is the answer; CO2, nitrogen and helium do not bind this way.

85.s: The incomplete burning of petrol and diesel produces :
85.x: Incomplete burning of petrol and diesel (too little oxygen) produces carbon monoxide; complete burning gives CO2 and water.

85.s: Which of the following is an inorganic gaseous pollutant of air?
85.x:
Printed key: hydrogen cyanide. Hydrogen sulphide is equally an inorganic gaseous pollutant, so option 3 is also defensible (app notes 5:99 sub 2; printed explanation names both).
Hydrogen cyanide is an inorganic gaseous pollutant; methane and phosgene are carbon compounds usually treated as organic.

85.s: Carbon monoxide poisoning affects mainly which one of the following?
85.x: CO poisoning mainly affects the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood by forming carboxyhaemoglobin, not digestion, liver or kidney function.

85.s: The chief source of Hydrogen Sulphide pollutant is :
85.x: Hydrogen sulphide (rotten-egg smell) is chiefly formed naturally by decay of vegetation and animal matter; refineries and sewage are smaller, anthropogenic sources.

85.s: Fly ash is a pollutive combustion product of burning
85.x: Fly ash is the combustion residue of coal burnt in thermal power plants; charcoal, diesel/kerosene and CNG do not produce it.

85.s:
Match List I (Air Pollutant) with List II (Part Affected) and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists.
List I
A. Asbestos Dust
B. Lead
C. Mercury
D. Carbon Monoxide
List II
1. Brain
2. Stomach
3. Lung
4. Blood Stream
Codes A B C D A B C D
85.x: Asbestos dust affects the lung (asbestosis), lead the brain, mercury the stomach (as keyed) and CO the blood stream, giving 3 1 2 4.

85.s: Which of the following gases reduces the oxygen carrying capacity of the blood?
85.x: Carbon monoxide reduces the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity by forming carboxyhaemoglobin; nitric oxide, CO2 and nitrous oxide are not the classic answer.

85.s: Colourless gases coming out from motor vehicle and cigarette due to incomplete combustion is
85.x: Carbon monoxide is the colourless gas from incomplete combustion in vehicles and cigarettes; CO2 is the product of complete combustion.

85.s: What is a particulate matter?
85.x: Particulate matter (dust, smoke, aerosols, PM10/PM2.5) is an air pollutant.

85.s: Which one among the following gases readily combines with the hemoglobin of the blood?
85.x: Carbon monoxide readily combines with haemoglobin (carboxyhaemoglobin); methane, NO2 and SO2 do not.

85.s: To prevent from knocking the substance employed in the car engine is
85.x: Tetraethyl lead (TEL) was the anti-knock additive in petrol; it is now phased out because of lead toxicity.

85.s: Colourless gas coming out from motor vehicle and cigarette due to incomplete combustion is –
85.x: Carbon monoxide is the colourless gas from incomplete combustion in vehicles and cigarettes.

85.s:
Magnetite particles, suspected to cause neurodegenerative problems are generated as environmental pollutants from which of the following?
1. Brakes of motor vehicles
2. Engines of motor vehicles
3. Microwave stoves within homes
4. Power plants
5. Telephone lines
Select the correct answer using the code given below
85.x: Magnetite comes from vehicle brakes, vehicle engines and coal-fired power plants (1, 2, 4); there is no evidence for microwave stoves or telephone lines.

85.s:
Match List-I (Pollutants) with List-II (Sources) and select the correct option.
List-I (Pollutants):
(a) Sulphur Dioxide (SO2)
(b) Nitrogen Oxides (NOx)
(c) Brown Carbon
(d) Volatile Organic Compounds
List-II (Sources):
(i) Incomplete combustion of fossil fuels and the smelting of mineral ores
(ii) Impure combustion of organic matter
(iii) High-temperature combustion from vehicles, power plants and lightning
(iv) Solvents, paints and emissions from industries producing chemicals, plastics, and fuel vapours
85.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
85.x: SO2 comes from fossil-fuel combustion and smelting of mineral ores, NOx from high-temperature combustion (vehicles, power plants, lightning), brown carbon from impure combustion of organic matter and VOCs from solvents, paints and fuel vapours: a-i, b-iii, c-ii, d-iv.

85.s: Tree useful for prevention of dust pollution –
85.x: Sita Ashok is the tree named in the key for preventing dust pollution; Mahua, Poplar and Neem are not the answer here.

85.s: Which of the following gases is not considered as polluting agent of air?
85.x: CO2 is a normal air constituent and greenhouse gas, the usual 'not a polluting agent' answer; CO, NO2 and SO2 are recognised air pollutants (in the AQI).

85.s: Which one of the following is not related to air pollution?
85.x: Eutrophication is nutrient enrichment of water bodies (water pollution); smog, acid rain and asbestosis (inhaled fibres) relate to air pollution.

85.s:
Assertion (A) During winter, air pollution in Delhi reaches to the maximum level.
Reason (R) Combustion process in motor vehicles increases during winter.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
85.x: Delhi's air pollution does peak in winter (A true), but the cause is temperature inversion, calm winds and farm-fire smoke, not more combustion in vehicles (R false).

85.s: What can be considered a natural source of air pollution?
85.x: Forest fires are a natural source of air pollution; factory emissions, power-station smoke and automobile exhaust are anthropogenic.

85.s: The combustion of coal, petrol and diesel etc is the basic source of
85.x: Burning coal, petrol and diesel (fossil-fuel combustion) releases CO, CO2, SO2, NOx and particulates into the atmosphere, the basic source of air pollution.

85.s:
Which of the following is/are air pollutant(s)?
(i) Ground level ozone
(ii) Nitrogen dioxide
(iii) Nitrogen gas
85.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
85.x: Ground-level ozone and nitrogen dioxide are air pollutants; nitrogen gas (78% of air) is a normal constituent, so only (i) and (ii).

85.s: As per the study by IIT Kanpur, which is the largest factor of pollution through fine particulate matter in Delhi which leads to heavy smog?
o: Burning of paddy straw in Punjab and Haryana
85.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
85.x:
Printed key: construction dust. Strictly the study names road dust (~38% of PM2.5 annually); in winter secondary particles, vehicles and biomass burning lead (IIT Kanpur 2016 study, governancenow.com).
IIT Kanpur's 2016 Delhi study found road dust (which includes construction dust) the largest annual source of fine particulates (~38% of PM2.5), ahead of vehicles (~20%); stubble smoke is a seasonal contributor.

85.s: During normal conditions, the gas which pollutes the atmosphere is
85.x: Carbon monoxide is a pollutant even under normal conditions; N2 and O2 are normal constituents of air and CO2 is a natural (quantitative) component.

85.s: Which one of the following statements about air pollution caused by diesel engines is correct?
o: It produces large quantity of carbon monoxide at lower and high temperatures.
It produces large quantity of nitrogen oxides at lower and high temperatures.
It produces large quantity of carbon monoxide at lower temperature and nitrogen oxides at high temperature.
It produces large quantity of nitrogen oxides at lower temperature and carbon monoxide at high temperature.
85.x: Diesel engines give much CO at low temperature (incomplete combustion) and much NOx at high temperature (nitrogen and oxygen combine in the hot cylinder).

85.s:
Which of the following are some important pollutants released by steel industry in India?
I. Oxides of sulphur
II. Oxides of nitrogen
III. Carbon monoxide
IV. Carbon dioxide
Select the correct answer using the codes given below
85.x: Steel plants (coke ovens, blast furnaces, coal burning) release oxides of sulphur and nitrogen, CO and CO2 – all four.

85.s: According to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), which one of the following is the largest source of sulphur dioxide emissions?
85.x: The US EPA says fossil-fuel combustion at power plants is the largest SO2 source (about 73%), followed by other industry; ships, locomotives and ore extraction are smaller.

85.s:
Which of the following are some important pollutants released by the steel industry in India?
1. Oxides of sulphur
2. Oxides of nitrogen
3. Carbon monoxide
4. Carbon dioxide
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
85.x: The steel industry releases oxides of sulphur and nitrogen, CO and CO2 – all four.

85.s:
Oxides of sulphur
2. Oxides of nitrogen
3. Carbon monoxide
4. Carbon dioxide Select the correct answer using codes given below.
85.x: In the steel furnace coke reduces iron ore giving CO and CO2, and coal burning adds oxides of sulphur and nitrogen – all four.

85.s: Which one of the following is an air pollutant gas and is released by burning fossil fuel?
85.x: Sulphur dioxide is the pollutant gas released by burning fossil fuels; hydrogen, nitrogen and oxygen are not pollutants.

85.s: The main air pollutant(s) in metropolitan cities is/are
85.x: The key takes CO and SO2 (from vehicles and fuel burning) as the main pollutants of metropolitan cities; particulates are also major.

85.s: Which is the main source of micro particulate Matter PM 2.5 in India?
85.src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
85.x: The printed key takes vehicular emissions as the main source of PM2.5; combustion (vehicles, coal, biomass) and secondary formation all contribute.

85.s: While cooking if bottom of the vessel is getting blackened on the outside, it means that
o: The food is not burning completely
The fuel is not burning completely
85.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
85.x: A blackened vessel bottom means soot (unburnt carbon) from incomplete burning of the fuel.

85.s: Which of the following contributes more to air pollution in Delhi?
o: Burning of Agriculture stubble in Rajasthan
Burning of Agricultural stubble in Punjab
Use of firewood for cooking in Punjab
Use of firewood for cooking in Rajasthan
85.src: APPSC Assistant Section Officer (ASO) Mains General Studies
85.x: Stubble burning in Punjab (and Haryana) contributes more to Delhi's air pollution; winter north-westerlies carry the farm-fire smoke to Delhi.

85.s: Which of the following is NOT a major primary air pollutant?
85.x: Silver oxide is not a major primary air pollutant; sulphur oxides, CO and nitrogen oxides are.

85.s:
Which of the following statements about technology and air pollution are correct?
1. Technological advancements have contributed to increased air pollution due to higher levels of travel and transportation.
2. The primary pollutants released from transportation include ozone, lead, nitrogen oxides, and carbon monoxide.
3. Burning fossil fuels for transportation has minimal impact on human health.
85.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
85.x:
Official key: 1 & 2. Strictly statement 2 is loose: ozone is a secondary pollutant formed from transport NOx and VOCs, not directly released (PMF Environment Part 04 p.3).
Statement 1 is true and statement 3 is false (transport fuel burning harms health), so the only usable code is 1 and 2.

85.s: The size of the Respirable Suspended Particulate Matter (R.S.P.M.) in air is :
85.x:
Older books and the UPPCS 2017 key: RSPM is less than 5 µm. Strictly CPCB treats RSPM as PM10 (particles below 10 µm) (PMF Environment Part 04 p.49).
The key takes RSPM as the fine fraction 'less than 5 µm'; the other options are all 'more than'.

85.s: According to National Ambient Air Quality Standards in India, what is the permissible limit in air for annual average of particulate matter of size less than 2.5 microns?
85.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
85.x: India's NAAQS annual limit for PM2.5 is 40 µg/m³ (24-hour 60 µg/m³); 20 is not a limit and 60 is the PM10 annual limit.

85.s:
In the context of WHO Air Quality Guidelines, consider the following statements :
1. The 24- hour mean of PM2.5 should not exceed 15μg/ m3 and annual mean of PM2.5 should not exceed 5μg/m3
2. In a year, the highest levels of ozone pollution occur during the periods of inclement weather.
3. PM10 can penetrate the lung barrier and enter the bloodstream.
4. Excessive ozone in the air can trigger asthma.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: WHO AQG 2021: PM2.5 24-hour 15 and annual 5 µg/m³ (1 true) and excess ozone triggers asthma (4 true); ozone peaks in sunny, not inclement weather (2 false) and PM2.5, not PM10, crosses into the bloodstream (3 false).

85.s: Which of the following pollutants is NOT covered under the National Air Quality Monitoring Programme that has been identified for regular monitoring at all locations?
85.src: APPSC Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences Mains Paper-II I
85.x: NAMP regularly monitors SO2, NO2, RSPM/PM10 and PM2.5 at all locations; carbon dioxide is not covered.

85.s: As per the colour code of National Air Quality Index maintained by Central Pollution Control Board, Yellow colour means that the air quality is
85.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
85.x: Yellow on the National AQI colour code means moderately polluted (101-200); good is dark green, satisfactory light green and poor orange.

85.s: A new National Air Quality Index (AQI) launched in October 2014 to disseminate the information on air quality in an easily understandable form for the general public is based on ____ pollutants which are measured up to 24-hourly averaging period.
85.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
85.x: The National AQI (launched October 2014 / April 2015) uses 8 pollutants: PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3 and Pb, measured up to 24-hour averages.

85.s: National Air Quality Index (AQI) was launched by Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change initiative under
85.src: APPSC Asst. Chemist (Ground Water), Asst. Director (Town & C
85.x: The National AQI was launched by the MoEFCC in April 2015 as an initiative under the Swachh Bharat Mission (NCAP came only in 2019).

85.s: If the Air Quality Index in a place in India is 100, the air quality in that place is?
85.src: AP Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in APBC W
85.x: An AQI of 51-100 is 'satisfactory', so 100 is satisfactory; 101-200 is moderately polluted.

85.s: How many pollutants are monitored in the National Air Quality index for measuring air quality?
85.src: AP Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in APBC W
85.x: The National AQI monitors 8 pollutants.

85.s: Which of the following countries does not have a global atmosphere watch station to collect data on world temperatures?
85.x: The key: India has no WMO Global Atmosphere Watch global station, while Algeria (Assekrem), Kenya (Mt Kenya) and Brazil do; India has only regional/contributing stations.

85.s: Who of the following inaugurated SAFAR (System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting) in July 2018?
85.x: The new SAFAR air-quality and weather forecast system for Delhi was unveiled in 2018 by Dr Harsh Vardhan, then Minister of Science & Technology, Earth Sciences and Environment.

85.s: Under Government of India's National Air Quality Monitoring Programme (NAMP) covering 312 cities/ towns in 29 States and 6 Union Territories of the country, which of the following combination has been identified for regular monitoring at all the locations?
o: CO, NO2, Oxygen Difluoride (OF2) and PM2.5
85.x: Under NAMP, SO2, NO2, suspended particulates (RSPM/PM10) and PM2.5 are monitored at all locations; CO and OF2 are not in the regular set.

85.s: Which one of the following is not included in the National Air Quality Index?
85.x: The National AQI covers PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3 and lead; methane is not included ('sulphur' means SO2).

85.s: The indigenously developed AUM Photonic system is used for real-time remote monitoring of _____.
85.x: The indigenous AUM (Air Unique-quality Monitoring) photonic system, developed at GVP-SIRC Visakhapatnam with DST support, does real-time remote monitoring of air quality.

85.s: The National Air Quality Index (NAQI) in India measures which key pollutants ?
o: PM2.5 , PM10 , CO , SO2 , NO2 , 03 , and NH ,
85.src: APPSC 2025 Forest Beat Officer and Assistant Beat Officer In
85.x: The NAQI measures PM2.5, PM10, CO, SO2, NO2, O3, NH3 (and lead); it does not measure all greenhouse gases or CO2.

85.s:
In the cities of our country, which among the following atmospheric gases are normally considered in calculating the value of the Air Quality Index?
1. Carbon dioxide
2. Carbon monoxide
3. Nitrogen dioxide
4. Sulphur dioxide
5. Methane
Select the correct answer using the code given below
85.x: Of the gases listed, only CO, NO2 and SO2 are in India's AQI; CO2 and methane are not.

85.s:
In the cities of our country, which among the following atmospheric gases are normally considered in calculating the value of Air Quality Index?
1. Carbon dioxide
2. Carbon monoxide
3. Nitrogen dioxide
4. Sulfur dioxide
5. Methane
Select the correct answer using codes given below:
85.x: India's AQI counts CO, NO2 and SO2 among its 8 pollutants; CO2 and methane are not included.

85.s: Which of the following is the mobile application launched by Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology to enable the citizens of India to know the city air quality (at present in 4 cities)?
85.src: APPSC Assistant Section Officer (ASO) Mains General Studies
85.x: SAFAR-Air is the IITM Pune (MoES) mobile app giving city air quality and forecasts (first for Delhi, Mumbai, Pune, Ahmedabad).

85.s: Smog is essentially caused by the atmospheric presence of :
85.x: Smog (smoke + fog) is essentially caused by oxides of nitrogen and sulphur in the air; oxygen and nitrogen are normal air constituents.

85.s: Which among the following is not a primary pollutant?
85.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
85.x: Ozone at ground level is a secondary pollutant formed from NOx and hydrocarbons in sunlight, so it is not a primary pollutant.

85.s:
Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched?
I. Classical smog - Mixture of smoke, fog and sulphur dioxide
II. Photochemical smog - High concentration of oxidizing agent
85.x: Classical (London) smog is smoke, fog and SO2; photochemical smog has a high concentration of oxidising agents (ozone, PAN), so both pairs are correct.

85.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of an air pollutant?
85.x: Ozone in the upper atmosphere (stratosphere) is a UV shield, not an air pollutant, whereas ground-level ozone, lead dust and unfiltered factory smoke are pollutants.

85.s: On the report of the UN Environment Programme, the Government of India launched a study on responsibility for the 'Asian Brown Cloud (ABC)'. Where is the ABC formed?
85.x: The Asian Brown Cloud is a dry-season layer of soot, black carbon and sulphate aerosols over South Asia (Indo-Gangetic plain) and the Indian Ocean.

85.s: Photochemical smog is a resultant of the reaction among
o: NO₂, 03 and peroxyacetyl nitrate in the presence of sunlight
CO, 02 and peroxyacetyl nitrate in the presence of sunlight
CO, CO₂ and N02 at low temperature
High concentration of N02, O₃ and CO in the evening
85.x: Photochemical smog results from NO2, ozone and PAN chemistry in sunlight (NOx + hydrocarbons + sunlight); it does not form at low temperature or in the evening.

85.s: Which among the following is the secondary pollutant?
85.x: Smog is formed in the air from other pollutants, so it is a secondary pollutant; CO2, CO and fly ash are emitted directly.

85.s: Which of the following is produced during the formation of photochemical smog?
85.x: Ozone (with PAN) is produced during photochemical smog formation; hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides are the inputs, not products.

85.s: Asian Brown Cloud, 2002 was mainly spared over –
85.x: The Asian Brown Cloud (2002 UNEP report) spread mainly over South Asia and the northern Indian Ocean.

85.s: Photochemical smog always contains :
85.x: Ozone is one of the primary components of photochemical smog, so it is always present; aluminium ions, phosphorus and methane are not defining components.

85.s: Smog is essentially caused by the atmospheric presence of
85.x: Smog is essentially caused by oxides of nitrogen (photochemical smog) and sulphur (classical smog); oxygen and nitrogen are normal air gases.

85.s: The term ‘brown air’ is used for
85.x: Photochemical smog gives a brownish haze, hence 'brown air'; sulphurous (London/industrial) smog is grey-black.

85.s: Which of the following diseases are not caused by smog?
85.x: Smog causes breathing problems and is linked to cancers; rickets is a vitamin D deficiency disease (heavy smog only reduces UV and vitamin D synthesis), so it is the one not caused by smog.

85.s: Which among the following is the secondary pollution?
85.x: Smog forms in the air from primary pollutants, so it is secondary; CO2, CO and fly ash are emitted directly (primary).

85.s: Which one of the following is produced during the formation of photochemical smog?
85.x: Ozone (with PAN) is produced during photochemical smog formation; hydrocarbons and NOx are its precursors.

85.s: Among the following greenhouse gases, which does not cause ozone pollution in the troposphere?
85.x: Tropospheric ozone forms from NOx, CO and methane/VOCs in sunlight; water vapour is not a precursor, so it does not cause ozone pollution.

85.s: In which city/State was air pollution control system 'VAYU' installed n September 2018?
85.x: WAYU, the CSIR-NEERI air-purifying unit for traffic junctions, was installed in Delhi (ITO, Mukarba Chowk) in September 2018.

85.s: Electrostatic precipitator is used to remove
o: Poisonous gases present in the smoke released from the industry
Carbon dioxide present in the smoke released from the automobiles
Particulate matter present in the smoke released from the industry
Oxides of nitrogen present in the smoke released from the automobiles
85.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
85.x: An electrostatic precipitator removes fine particulate matter (fly ash) from industrial flue gases using electrostatic forces, not gases like CO2 or NOx.

85.s: Carbon monoxide, emitted by vehicles which turn to carbon dioxide by the catalyst converter, whose ceramic disc is controlled by?
85.x: Catalytic converters convert CO to CO2 using precious-metal catalysts – platinum, palladium and rhodium; of the options, palladium.

85.s:
Consider the following features of newer models of motor cars :
1. Radial tyres
2. Streamlined body
3. Multipoint fuel injection
4. Catalytic converter with exhaust Which of these features make the new models of motor cars more fuel efficient ?
85.x:
Most books/keys: 1, 3 and 4. Strictly a catalytic converter cuts exhaust emissions, not fuel use, and a streamlined body (less drag) does improve fuel efficiency (general knowledge, not checked).
The book key takes radial tyres, multipoint fuel injection and the catalytic converter as the features of newer, fuel-efficient cars (1, 3 and 4).

85.s: Which of the following metals are used as catalyst in the Catalytic converters to eliminate poisonous gases?
85.x: Rhodium (with platinum and palladium) is the catalyst metal in catalytic converters; sodium and thorium are not.

85.s: Which one of the following is not an instrumental device to check air pollution?
85.x: Bag filters and cyclone separators/collectors are real particulate-control devices; 'cyclone divider' is not a device.

85.s:
How CNG is a cleaner fuel?
I. It produces oxides of Sulphur and Nitrogen in very smal amounts.
II. It makes environment less polluted.
III. It emits less greenhouse gases.
85.x: CNG (mainly methane) gives very little SOx and NOx, makes the environment less polluted and emits fewer greenhouse gases, so all three are correct.

85.s: CNG used in automobiles to check pollution mainly consists of –

13.x: Pseudomonas putida (A.M. Chakrabarty's oil-eating 'superbug') degrades hydrocarbons of oil spills; E. coli, yeast and Rhizobium do not.

13.x: Yeast and mushrooms are fungi (no chlorophyll).

13.x: Milk becomes curd through bacteria (Lactobacillus), which make lactic acid.

B. Vinegar has acetic acid.

D. Vinegar is used as a preservative.
Code :
13.x: A (vinegar from fermented sugarcane juice), B (acetic acid) and D (preservative) are right; C is wrong - benzoic acid is not vinegar's acid.

13.s: Which bacteria cause milk to spoil ?
13.x:
Most books and keys: Lactobacillus (souring). Strictly: refrigerated milk is spoiled mostly by psychrotrophic Pseudomonas (general knowledge, not checked).
Lactobacillus sours milk by turning lactose into lactic acid - the usual book answer for milk spoilage.

13.s: Vinegar is the solution of which of the following?
13.x: Vinegar is a solution of acetic acid, produced by fermentation of ethanol.

13.s: Which acid is found in Vinegar?
13.x: The acid in vinegar is acetic acid.

13.s: Sour taste of vinegar is due to :
13.x: Vinegar's sourness is due to acetic acid, which is not among tartaric, lactic or citric acid, so 'None of these'.

13.s: Which one of the following acids, is formed during the change of milk into curd?
13.x: Lactobacillus in curd/whey turns lactose into lactic acid, which gives curd its sour taste; acetic acid is vinegar, citric is lemon.

13.s: The wine is prepared by the process of
13.x: Wine is made by fermentation: yeast (Saccharomyces) converts grape sugar into ethanol and CO2 anaerobically.

13.s: Which of the following is the major component of vinegar?
13.x: Vinegar is a 5-8% solution of acetic (ethanoic) acid made by Acetobacter from ethanol; lactic acid is curd, citric acid lemon.

13.s: Biogas is formed through
13.x: Biogas (mainly methane) forms by anaerobic fermentation (digestion) of biomass by methanogenic bacteria; it is not an oxidation or aerobic process.

13.s: Which bacteria is helpful in making curd from milk?
13.x: Lactobacillus (lactic acid bacterium) curdles milk; yeast is a fungus used for bread and alcohol, E. coli and Mycobacterium are not used.

13.s: Enzyme involved in the hydrolysis of starch to glucose is
13.x: Amylase (e.g. salivary amylase/ptyalin) hydrolyses starch to maltose/glucose; invertase acts on sucrose, dehydrogenases and anhydrases on other reactions.

13.s: Scientifically, fermentation means
o: Incomplete oxidation of sugar in oxygen
Complete oxidation of sugar without oxygen
Incomplete oxidation of sugar without oxygen
Complete oxidation of sugar in oxygen
13.x: Fermentation is the incomplete oxidation (breakdown) of sugar in the absence of oxygen, giving alcohol or lactic acid and little energy; complete oxidation in oxygen is aerobic respiration.

13.s: Curd making is an ancient “Biotechnological” process involving :
13.x: Curd is made by the bacterium Lactobacillus - a traditional biotechnological process; yeast (fungus) is used for bread and wine.

13.s: Yeast is an example of :
13.x: Yeast (Saccharomyces) is a unicellular fungus, without chlorophyll; it is not a bacterium or alga.

13.s: Oil spills can be cleaned by using this genetically engineered bacteria?

13.x: Pseudomonas (P. putida 'superbug', A.M. Chakrabarty) was genetically manipulated from natural isolates to degrade oil hydrocarbons.

13.s: Genetics deals with–
13.x: Genetics is the study of genes, heredity and variation; Mendel's laws and DNA structure are only parts of it.

13.s: What is the main function of nucleic acids in human beings?
o: Storage and expression of genetic information
13.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
13.x: Nucleic acids (DNA, RNA) store and express genetic information; oxygen transport is by haemoglobin and energy mainly from carbohydrates and fats.

13.s: The information in DNA is stored as a code made up of chemical bases. Which of the following are those chemical bases found in DNA?
13.src: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
13.x: DNA bases are adenine, guanine, cytosine and thymine; uracil replaces thymine only in RNA.

13.s: DNA is present in
13.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
13.x: Besides the nucleus, DNA is present in mitochondria and chloroplasts, which carry their own small circular DNA.

13.s:
The characteristics features of genetic code are :
i. It is always universal
ii. It is triplet of nucleotides bases corresponding to 20 amino acids
iii. It is non-overlapping, non-ambiguous and commaless.
iv. It has start and stop codon Which of the statements given above are true?
13.x:
Most books and keys: all four statements true. Strictly: the code is only nearly universal - mitochondria and some protists use a few different codons, so 'always universal' overstates it (general knowledge, not checked).
The code is a triplet code for 20 amino acids; it is non-overlapping, unambiguous and commaless, and has start (AUG) and stop codons; books treat it as universal, so 'all of the above'.

13.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Histone proteins is correct?
o: Histones are proteins that are present in mitochondrial membrane.
Histones are proteins that are present in nucleus in association with DNA.
Histones are proteins associated with lipids in the cytosol.
Histones are proteins associated with carbohydrates in the cytosol.
13.x: Histones are basic proteins in the nucleus around which DNA wraps to form nucleosomes and chromatin; they are not mitochondrial or cytosolic.

13.s: Change in basic sequence of Gene is known as
13.x: A change in the base sequence of a gene is a mutation; transversion is only one type of base substitution, conjugation is gene transfer between bacteria.

13.s: RNA differs from DNA in having
13.x: RNA has uracil in place of thymine; adenine and guanine occur in both DNA and RNA.

13.s: The unit of heredity in our body is called
13.x: The gene, a DNA segment coding for a trait, is the unit of heredity; chromosomes and the nucleus only carry genes.

13.s:
At present, scientists can determine the arragement or relative position of genes or DNA sequence on a chromosome. How does this knowledge benefit us?
I. It is possible to know the pedigree of livestock.
II. It is possible to understand the causes of all human diseases.
III. It is possible to develop disease resistant animal breeds.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
13.x: Gene mapping helps trace livestock pedigree and breed disease-resistant animals (I, III); it cannot explain the causes of all human diseases, many of which are not genetic.

13.s: Which of the following is responsible for controlling hereditary characters of the living cells?
13.x: DNA is the genetic material that controls hereditary characters; RNA mainly carries the message for protein synthesis, and enzymes and hormones carry no hereditary information.

13.s: Which of the following features of DNA make it uniquely suited to store and transmit genetic information from generation to generation?
o: Number of base pairs per turn
13.x: The complementarity of the two strands (A-T, G-C) lets each strand act as a template, so DNA can be copied and passed on exactly.

13.s: Change in the base sequence within the gene is called :
13.x: A change in the base sequence within a gene is a mutation; cloning, breeding and fusion are not.

13.s: What is the structure of RNA?
13.src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
13.x: RNA is usually single-stranded - a 'single helix' in exam language - while DNA is a double helix.

13.s: The major contribution of the well-known scientist Har Govind Khorana is
o: Invention of helix model of DNA

Khorana shared the 1968 Nobel Prize for interpreting the genetic code and its function in protein synthesis, and made the first artificial gene. The helix model was Watson and Crick's, so the printed key is wrong; 'gene transformation' (Griffith), new cells and plant mutation are not his work either.

13.s: In which year and by whom the double-helical structure of DNA was discovered?
13.x: Watson and Crick proposed the double helix in 1953; Sanger sequenced proteins/DNA, Mendel and Leeuwenhoek worked earlier.

o: The amino acid sequences of proteins

13.x: The double helix is credited to Watson and Crick (1953); Franklin and Wilkins supplied X-ray data, Pauling proposed a wrong triple helix.

13.x: The double-helical model of DNA was given by Watson and Crick; Jacob and Monod gave the operon, Khorana the genetic code.

13.s: Who is the father of modern genetics?
13.x: Mendel is the father of modern genetics (pea hybridisation, laws of inheritance).

Statement 2: Carbohydrates are composed of carbon, hydrogen, and nitrogen atoms

13.x: The first human heart transplant was done by Christian Barnard in South Africa (1967).

13.x: Christian Barnard (South Africa, 1967) did the world's first heart transplant; William Harvey described blood circulation.

13.s:

I. They are man-made proteins.
II. They stimulate immunological function due to their ability to bind to specific antigens.
III. They are used in treating viral infections like that of Nipah virus.

13.x: Monoclonal antibodies are lab-made proteins (I); they bind a specific antigen and so trigger immune functions (II); they are used against viral infections such as Nipah (m102.4) (III).

fertilisation takes place in uterus while development takes place in test tube.
development of ova takes place in test tube without fertilisation.

13.x: Stem cells can develop into any type of cell; endodermal, ectodermal and muscle cells are already committed.

13.s: Which one of the following is a hereditary disease?
13.x: Haemophilia is an inherited (X-linked) bleeding disorder; cataract, pellagra (niacin deficiency) and osteoporosis are not classic hereditary diseases.

13.s:
RNA interference (RNAi) technology has gained popularity in the last few years. Why?
I. It is used in developing gene silencing therapies.
II. It can be used in developing therapies for the treatment of cancer.
III. It can be used to develop hormone replacement therapies.
IV. It can be used to produce crop plants that are resistant to viral pathogens.

13.x: RNAi silences genes, so it is used for gene-silencing therapies (I), cancer therapies (II) and virus-resistant crops (IV); it is not used for hormone replacement (III).

13.s: Haemophilia is a genetic disease carried by –
13.x: Haemophilia is X-linked recessive: women are usually carriers and the disease appears in men, who have only one X.

13.s: Which one of the following genetic disease is sex-linked?
13.x: Royal haemophilia is X-linked; Tay-Sachs and cystic fibrosis are autosomal recessive and hypertension is not a single-gene disease.

13.s: Haemophilia is :
13.x: Haemophilia is a hereditary clotting-factor defect, not caused by bacteria, viruses or pollutants.

13.s: India's first genetically engineered vaccine is:
13.x: India's first genetically engineered vaccine was Shanvac-B (Shantha Biotechnics, 1997) against hepatitis B virus.
